o-platforme:
PILOT is a monitoring system that collects data from sensors and shows the location and status of objects.

The system runs on protected servers, and only authorized users can access the information.

PILOT works with different types of sensors and video cameras and combines them into a single network. The system analyzes the data it receives, helps you make decisions, and warns you about possible problems.

With PILOT you can:

— track objects in real time

— view reports at different levels of detail

— study the history of events

— view photos and videos from objects

Access levels

The system has two access levels: the user account and the admin panel.

The user account is the basic interface without administrator rights. In this account, users can track vehicles, equipment, people, and other objects.

The admin panel provides full access to the system settings. Administrators manage accounts, users, system objects, and the overall structure of the system, configuring the platform for the company's tasks.

Modular architecture

PILOT is built on a modular architecture. Modules are separate components of the system, each responsible for specific functions.

Thanks to the modular design, you can:

— configure the system for your company's specific tasks

— pay only for the features you actually need

— add new modules as your needs change

You can enable the modules you need through the contract administrator or by contacting technical support.

PILOT under your company's brand

PILOT can be used with your company's own domain and branding. The preparation procedure is described in the article “Setting up PILOT under a partner's brand”
chto-novogo-v-pilot-7-10:
August 2026

PILOT 7.10 expands reports, automation, and integrations, updates the admin panel, and adds new features to the mobile app.

PILOT web version

New AI assistant features

We continue to develop the PILOT AI assistant: we have updated its design and expanded its capabilities. It answers questions about working with the platform, helps you find the right features and documentation materials, and suggests solutions to common tasks. If there is no ready answer, the assistant helps you prepare a request to technical support.

Developers now get hints on working with the API and creating extensions. The AI assistant is still being tested and refined, so its capabilities and the quality of its answers will improve gradually.

Detecting hidden fuel drains

The fuel sensor settings now include the “Drain via return line” function. It helps detect thefts in which fuel is drained through the return line to the tank.

The system analyzes abnormal fuel consumption while driving, calculates the volume of a possible drain, and marks the location of the event on the map.

Controlling stop visits by RFID

Bus visits to stops can be controlled with RFID tags. You can link one or more tags to each stop of a bus line. When the vehicle reads a linked tag, the system registers a visit to the corresponding stop.

Relative odometer

We added a sensor that calculates mileage from pulses from the speedometer or other connected equipment. You can use it when GPS/GLONASS data is unavailable or not accurate enough. You can set a separate number of pulses per kilometer for each vehicle.

Managing downtime data

The “Downtime” tab of the “Service” module now has filtering, import, and export of records. You can select data by object, dates, duration, and downtime reason, and export it to a file and load it back into the system. It is easier to find the information you need and work with a large number of records.

Video upload progress

While a video file is uploading, the system shows the amount of data transferred, the percentage complete, the current speed, and the estimated time to completion. This makes it easier to estimate when the video will be ready and to notice a drop in transfer speed.

Reports

Updated report scheduler

We reworked the creation of schedules for automatic reports. The report parameters, the data period, and the generation schedule are separated into individual blocks, so you can independently specify what data should go into the report and when it should be sent.

The scheduler lets you generate reports for the entire previous day, set the start and end time of the period, and configure intervals that cross midnight. Before saving, you can check the data period for the next report, and in the schedule you can select specific days of the week for generating it.

Filter by drivers

You can now generate reports only for selected drivers. The “By drivers” parameter is available for the following reports:

  • “Downtime report”

  • “Mileage report (by drivers)”

  • “Mileage report (with drivers)”

When you enable the parameter, the “Drivers” panel opens. In it you can select one or more drivers or a whole group. The report will include only the events related to them.

Selecting geofences for a report

Before generating the “Movement between zones” report, you can select the geofences you need. The report will include only movements between them.

Report builder

More sensor data in reports

“Work” type reports can include values of discrete, two-position, and multi-position sensors. To output the data, just select the label of the sensor you need when configuring the column.

Merging report rows

The report builder has a new setting, {"merge": true}. It suits reports where, instead of a detailed list of events, you need a single summary row for the selected breakdown period.

When the setting is enabled, the records for the period are merged and the intermediate rows are hidden.

For example, in a report broken down by day, you can output one row per driver: with total mileage and driving and idle durations, as well as the start time of the first trip and the end time of the last trip. This makes the report more compact and the summary figures easier to compare.

Filtering numeric data

For columns with numeric values you can set the conditions >, <**, or **=**. For example, the condition **> 25 in the “Maximum event speed” column leaves in the report only the rows where the maximum speed exceeds 25 km/h.

Configuring rows in geofence reports

For “Geofences” type reports you can choose how the rows are generated:

  • Geofence visits — a separate row for each visit to a geofence

  • Equipment work periods — a separate row for each work period of the selected sensor inside the geofence

For example, the Equipment work periods mode helps determine how long equipment worked in a given area. If the equipment was switched on before entering, the period starts at the moment of entry. If the object left the geofence before the equipment was switched off, the period ends at the moment of exit. The report includes only the intervals during which the object was in the geofence and the equipment was working.

Work shift reports

We added data breakdown by work shifts. A separate interval with calculated indicators is generated for each shift, so you can analyze day and night work separately.

In the report configuration you can set the shift boundaries, output one or all shifts, and choose whether to keep the night shift whole or split it at midnight.

Integrations and API

Sending statuses and media files via Telegram

Employees can send work statuses, photos, and videos to PILOT through the Telegram bot. The available statuses are configured separately for each account, so the employee only needs to choose the right option in the bot.

You can view and download the photos and videos that were sent in the PILOT web interface. The dispatcher can track the stages of work, and the supporting materials are stored together with the work data.

Sending events to external systems

“Situation center” algorithms now have a Webhook block. It lets you automatically send event data to external services.

Place the block in the branch of the algorithm you need, and when linking the algorithm to a notification, specify the recipient's address and the data to send.

Access to event media files via API

We added an API for getting photos and videos associated with ADAS and DMS events. You can request data for selected objects for the period you need and get links to view the media files in a browser. The resulting materials can be used in external systems to analyze and verify events.

Admin panel

Updated design

The admin panel has a new design and a higher-contrast color palette. The dark side menu is separated from the light work area, selected rows and statuses are more noticeable, and large tables are easier to view.

Search, filters, and actions on records are placed directly above the tables, next to the data.

The user panel has moved to the bottom of the side menu. It shows the user profile and offers quick actions:

— switching between the light and dark themes

— choosing the interface language

— going to the news

— logging out of the account

— collapsing the side menu

We also updated the internal components of the admin panel. The interface displays correctly in modern browsers, and tables, forms, and controls work consistently in all sections.

Managing Comms Cloud SIM cards

We added support for Comms Cloud SIM cards. In a single section you can check the SIM card's data and status, go to the linked vehicle, and, if necessary, block or unblock the card.

Mobile app

Vehicle operation analytics

The mobile app now has an “Analytics” tab for monitoring key indicators of vehicle operation. It shows statistics for the last 24 hours: idle and working time, mileage, and the number of vehicles.

Vehicle statuses, connection state, mileage, violations, geofences, and other indicators are presented in charts. You can assess the situation and spot deviations right from your smartphone.

AI assistant

The PILOT AI assistant is now available in the mobile app. It helps you find the right features and explains how to perform common tasks: build a report, configure an object, create a geofence, or connect a device. Answers may contain links to the relevant documentation sections.

Chats are saved in the history, so you can return to a previous conversation to continue the discussion or view an answer again.

Additional login protection

The app supports login with two-factor authentication. After entering your username and password, confirm the login with a one-time code from an authenticator app or from e-mail.

The additional check protects the account even if someone else learns the password.

Topping up the balance via Stripe

We added the ability to top up the organization's balance via Stripe. In the “Finance” tab, enter the amount, proceed to payment, and choose an available method on the Stripe page.

The function is available for accounts that have Stripe payment connected. You can check the account status after the payment right in the app.

Viewing events and notifications

The “Events” section now has separate “Notifications” and “Events” tabs. The first collects the triggers of configured rules, and the second shows changes in the state of objects and sensors.

For each tab you can separately select objects, data types, and the viewing period. You can open the place where a notification or event was registered on the map.

PILOT 7.10 offers more tools for data analysis, process automation, and working with the platform from a smartphone. The new features help you get the information you need faster and monitor vehicle operation.

We continue to develop the platform and are preparing new tools for monitoring and managing your fleet.

This section contains all the updates and changes that have appeared in PILOT. It lists new features, improvements, and bug fixes for the latest versions.

Each version has a separate article describing its changes. Choose a version to find out what was added, changed, or fixed.
pilot-7-9:
In version 7.9 we focused on ease of use, flexible settings, and expanded analytics. In this section we have gathered and described in detail all the key changes and improvements included in both releases.

There are new tools for driver monitoring, access and notification management, expanded reporting and integration capabilities, and improvements to existing system modules.

Access and security management

Two-factor authentication by e-mail

The system now supports two-factor authentication by e-mail. At login, in addition to your username and password, you must enter a one-time code sent to your e-mail. This method increases account security and helps protect data from unauthorized access.

Two types of tokens for accessing the monitoring service

The system now has two types of tokens: special links for secure access without sharing a username and password. You can choose the access format depending on the task: view only or full login to the system.

A view token lets you open monitoring without revealing credentials, for example to show a map to a client or to give temporary access for observation.

A login token lets you log in via a link without entering a password. The user is automatically logged in with the same rights as with regular authorization. The token's validity period can be limited or left unlimited.

Interface settings for a user

We added the ability to manage the display of system sections and modules for each user in the “Interface” tab.

Now you can:

— show or hide individual modules

— turn off the display of the main tabs

— configure the workspace for a specific role

Even if a module is enabled at the contract level, you can hide it for a selected employee.

Expanded integrations

Telegram bot configuration

We added the ability to quickly go to the Telegram bot from the user account.

In the account settings, specify the bot configuration and add its address. After saving, a separate tab with a link to the bot appears in the user account.

Links Field integration

We integrated the Links Field platform for managing SIM cards.

When working with the Links Field provider, you can now:

— specify the SIM card ICCID for each vehicle

— configure API access

— get SIM card data directly in the system

— use the provider to send SMS notifications

LBS connection

We added the ability to enable Yandex base station (LBS) positioning yourself from the account's admin panel.

A new key, LBS Config, has appeared in the account configuration section. Enter your Yandex API key in it, and the account will be able to determine device locations from the nearest cellular base stations (GSM/LTE).

Weather layer integration

The map now has a Windy.com weather layer. Weather conditions are displayed right in the system, on top of routes and monitored objects, which helps you take conditions into account when planning and analyzing routes.

In the map settings you can turn on the weather layer, choose a forecast model (depending on your plan), and select the display type: wind, precipitation, cloud cover, and other parameters. A time panel with animation is available for viewing the forecast over time.

Weather data is synchronized with the map and updates automatically when you pan and zoom.

Integration of equipment with Wirepas support

The system now supports equipment with Wirepas technology for indoor navigation. You can track the movement of objects indoors, where the GPS signal is unavailable or unstable.

The technology uses a network of wireless devices that form a self-configuring mesh network and transmit location data inside the building.

The solution is suitable for monitoring equipment, machinery, and personnel in warehouses, production premises, and other enclosed spaces, and also helps control internal logistics and movements inside facilities.

Admin panel

Account cloning

We expanded account cloning and made it easier to create a new account based on an existing one.

When cloning in the admin panel, you can now choose which data to transfer to the new account:

— sensor templates

— individual prices per object

— payment e-mail templates

— user assignments

— users with their rights and display settings

— reports from the report builder

— geofences linked to the contract

“Vehicles by sensor name” report

We added a new administrative report, “Vehicles by sensor name”. It helps you view sensors by contract, check that their names are correct, and put the records of installed equipment in order. The report simplifies auditing and makes data control more transparent and convenient.

Module updates

“Composite objects” module in the new interface

The “Composite objects” module is now available in the new interface. It lets you combine in a single logical scheme:

  • stationary and mobile tanks

  • inlet flow meters (fuel receiving)

  • outlet flow meters (fuel dispensing)

  • related sensors

Now you can:

 — describe the complete fuel flow chain, from receipt at the “inlet” part to dispensing to the consumer

 — account for storage, receiving, and dispensing within a single scheme

 — analyze fuel receipts, consumption, balances, and possible losses across the whole system

Create and configure composite objects, use them in monitoring and reports, and analyze the indicators.

Expanded capabilities of the “Service” module

We expanded the “Service” module to make planning and control of maintenance more convenient and transparent.

The tables now include new indicators: current engine hours, mileage to the next maintenance, and engine hours to the next maintenance.

You can now attach files to service records: photos, work completion reports, documents, or instructions. All materials are stored with the record and are always available for viewing and downloading.

An access rights system has also been added. You can separately configure who can add, edit, or delete records, and define access to the module's sections.

Quick adding of downtime

You can now add downtime directly from the object's context menu in the “Online” tab, without going to the “Service” module. Just right-click the object and select “Add downtime”, and the record is created automatically.

Updated “Object analytics” chart

We updated the analytics overview chart in the object card so that you can clearly evaluate the cost of owning equipment and make management decisions based on actual and planned data.

Now, when you go to the “Object analytics” section, you see a combined “Analytics overview” chart that shows by year:

— planned and actual maintenance costs for each year

— planned and actual fuel costs

— the total cost of owning the object, planned and actual

— changes in the object's value over time

— the cost of one kilometer of mileage, planned and actual

Event processing interval in the “Situation center” module

We added a new setting to the “Situation center” module: the event processing interval. It defines how long an event remains relevant and available for processing.

Previously, unprocessed events were deleted automatically after 24 hours. Now you can increase the interval to 72 or 120 hours. Events will stay in the list longer so that you can process them later.

Linking tags in the “Routes” module

You can now link BLE tags to route points and count trip completion by their signal.

If a vehicle detects a BLE tag, the point is considered visited, even if GPS is inaccurate or jammed.

As a result:

— routes are counted correctly even during satellite signal failures

— a visit to a point is confirmed by the vehicle's actual presence

— the system automatically records arrival and departure

Updated fuel analysis algorithm

The new data processing logic for fuel sensors detects refuels and fuel drains more accurately, reduces the effect of sensor noise, and excludes false events.

The algorithm analyzes changes in the fuel level taking into account several factors: volume thresholds, vehicle speed, the rate of fuel level change, and sensor data quality. This helps the system tell real fuel operations from normal consumption or random fluctuations in readings.

The fuel sensor settings now include advanced analysis parameters: event volume thresholds, a speed filter, a speed accounting mode, a filter by the rate of fuel level change, sensor data smoothing, and a mechanism for removing symmetric events.

Report builder

We expanded the “Report builder” so that you can analyze equipment operation in more depth and get more useful data in a familiar format.

Service downtime accounting

The Service Downtime table has been added.

Now you can:

— see the downtime of each vehicle

— calculate the total downtime for a period

— analyze service downtime over time

This way, you can evaluate the effect of maintenance on fleet operation and make management decisions based on actual data.

Eco summary reports by event type

For the Eco type, summary analysis by event type has been added.

New fields are available:

— Eco event type

— number of events

— average speed

— maximum speed

Now you can generate reports in the form of an active safety summary and analyze driving style more systematically.

Speed at the time of violation

Reports have a new parameter: speed at the time of violation. You can now see the vehicle's actual speed at the point where the violation was triggered.

Detailed fuel report

A new report type has been added: fuel refuels and drains.

Each operation is shown in a separate row with the time, volume, location, and fuel level. You get a complete log of operations and a transparent picture of fuel handling.

Loss of communication

We added a new “Loss of communication” report type to the builder. It helps you understand when and under what conditions a device loses its connection to the system.

The report shows the start and end time of the disconnection, its duration, where it happened, the vehicle's state at the moment of signal loss, and the possible cause, for example power disconnection or network loss.

With this report you can not only record the fact of a disconnection but also understand the situation and tell short-term interference from real problems.

Driver monitoring

Face ID for automatic driver assignment

The system now supports face recognition through on-board cameras. A driver can be assigned automatically based on the Face ID result.

The check is performed when the ignition is switched on and periodically during the trip. The system determines who is behind the wheel, even if different drivers use the vehicle, records the recognition results, and passes the data to reports.

Driver working hours

We added a new “Working hours” tab to the driver card. You can now configure the driver's schedule: select working days of the week and set time intervals separately for weekdays, Saturday, and Sunday. If necessary, the system can restrict assigning the driver outside the set schedule.

Accounting for drivers' working hours in the PTM module

The PILOT Task Manager module now checks drivers' working hours when assigning tasks.

When creating a task, the system can now analyze the driver's work schedule. If the selected interval falls on rest time or non-working hours, the system shows the user a warning.

To enable the check, activate the “Check working hours” parameter, available for Datetime and Address fields.

The function allows dispatchers and logistics specialists to take drivers' work schedules into account when planning tasks and reduces the risk of assigning tasks to non-working time.

Updated Eco Driving and rating calculation logic

The logic for calculating Eco Driving scores has been updated. The score is now generated for each driver, taking into account all the vehicles they drove.

You can build ratings by both vehicles and drivers and analyze data in different breakdowns. Violations are attributed to a specific driver rather than to the equipment, so the score reflects real driving style and helps you make better-founded management decisions.

Notifications

Command templates in notifications

The notification create and edit form has two new fields:

  • Command — for entering text manually

  • Command template — select a ready-made template from the list

When configuring a notification, you can now enter a command yourself or choose a previously saved template.

Account ID in Webhook notifications

Webhook notifications now include additional information: Account ID. Along with the event data, the system now sends the identifier of the account from which the notification was sent.

New notification type: “Event media files”

The system has a new notification type: “Event media files”. The notification is sent when a device successfully uploads to the server a media file related to an event, for example a photo or video.

Unlike regular notifications, it is triggered not at the moment of the event but after the file is uploaded successfully. This notification type gives you immediate confirmation and lets you go straight to viewing materials for events such as violations or ADAS/DMS triggers.

Notifications in the object card

The object card has switches for managing notifications about the limits of each vehicle.

For the “Speed control”, “Loss of communication”, and “Downtime” parameters you can turn notifications on or off separately.

For the “Downtime” parameter an ignition icon is available. It defines whether the ignition state is taken into account when calculating downtime.

Limits continue to be recorded in the system even when notifications are turned off, so control is maintained without unnecessary alerts.

New API: rental contracts

A new API method has been added for getting the list of rental contracts from the Rent Car module.

With it you can get data on all types of contracts:

— active (open)

— booked

— completed

For each contract, the method returns data about the renter, the rental start and end points, the planned issue and return dates, and the contract and vehicle numbers.
pilot-7-8:
In PILOT 7.8 we made the platform even more convenient and functional. We added useful tools, expanded reports, and improved data accuracy so that you can find the information you need faster and solve work tasks easily.

Interface and data improvements

New access rights in the report builder

You can now manage access to reports flexibly: set rights to view, edit, and delete separately. For example, you can give an employee view-only access, without the ability to change or delete reports. This protects reports from accidental changes and deletion.

Choosing the speed source

In the object settings you can now choose the speed source: use GPS by default or specify another field, for example a CAN bus value. This function helps calculate mileage and driving time more accurately and take into account the specifics of different vehicle types. When choosing the speed source, you can also set the units of measurement right away.

Tracking temperature along the route

When you click the temperature chart in a report, you immediately see where the vehicle was on the map at that moment. This makes it easy to trace the relationship between temperature changes and the route.

Displaying sensor values in the mobile app

The sensor settings now have an option that lets you choose whether to show sensor values in the mobile app. If the option is on, the sensor value is visible on the smartphone. If it is off, the value is not shown in the mobile version.

Displaying the “Under maintenance” status

Vehicles with the “Under maintenance” status are now more noticeable in the system: such objects appear in the general list with a wrench icon. When you click it, you see information about the dates of the current maintenance.

Sending location via Telegram

You can now use the updated function for sending coordinates via Telegram. It works on the new version of the Telegram API and is even more stable and accurate.

The updated Telegram bot can be used as a mobile tracker: send your location straight from the app, and the system receives this data in real time.

Downloading a video segment

You can now export only the segment you need from videos received from connected devices. Open the recording, set the start and end time, and download a separate clip without unnecessary minutes.

Choose the exact interval and get a separate file, save time and traffic by not downloading the whole video, and prepare incident materials faster.

New “Points of interest” module

We added “Points of interest” so that you can mark important places on the map: offices, warehouses, parking lots, customer addresses, and other sites. For each point you can specify coordinates, choose a suitable icon, add a description, and combine it with others into a group by purpose.

Analytics update

Connection status chart with percentages

The vehicle connection status chart in the analytics section of the dashboard has been updated. The chart shows the percentage breakdown by connection status, so you immediately see what part of the fleet is currently online and which vehicles have not connected for a long time.

Grouping the rating by models

In the vehicle rating you can now group data by vehicle model. You can compare indicators not only for individual vehicles but also by model.

New features and integrations

AI bot: your technical assistant

We created a smart assistant that acts as a technical consultant. With it you can find answers to questions faster and get help right inside the system.

The bot is available in all languages and is always ready to tell you:

  • how to use the platform's capabilities

  • where to find the information you need

  • how to solve technical tasks more easily

Like any AI-based system, the bot can sometimes make mistakes. It is best to double-check important details or confirm them with the support team. Your feedback will help make it even more useful.

Toll roads: expense control and route planning

Use the “Toll roads” function in the “Geofences” module to take toll road sections into account. With it you can:

  • control expenses and see when and how much your objects drove on toll roads

  • take toll sections into account when planning routes

  • analyze trips: toll road data is saved and available in reports

For details on how to work with toll roads and set up entry and exit sections, read this article.

Yandex LBS integration

Object locations can now be determined with the Yandex LBS service: coordinates are available not only from GPS but also from cellular network and Wi-Fi data. As a result, the system keeps tracking vehicles even without a GPS signal, for example in underground parking lots or dense urban areas.

Jimi video recorder support

You can now connect and use the Jimi JC400 video recorder to record and transmit video.

CMSV6 passenger counter integration

We added support for CMSV6 passenger counting cameras. Based on data from these devices, two reports are now available:

  • the number of boardings and alightings in each departure and arrival geofence

  • overall passenger flow statistics for the selected period across all routes

These reports will help you better understand route load and plan vehicle operation more accurately.

Wialon data migration wizard

Transferring objects and events from Wialon to PILOT is now easier. We created a separate module: the “Import from Wialon” migration wizard.

With the migration wizard you can:

  • create data transfer tasks

  • select the objects to transfer

  • see the status of each migration stage

Two-way communication through the camera

If a video device is connected, you can talk to the driver through the camera as if on a call. Open the camera and click the intercom icon: the driver will hear you through the device's speaker and can reply.

With the intercom you can get in touch quickly without extra calls: right in the camera window you can clarify the situation on site, give instructions, and immediately get a voice confirmation.

Saving zones together with toll sections

You can now save and transfer geofences together with toll section and scheduler settings. Use the export and import buttons, and all parameters will be saved.

Sending coordinates from the “Situation center”

The “Situation center” module has a button for quickly copying a link to the vehicle's current location. You can copy the link with one click and send it to emergency services, colleagues, or other recipients, for example in case of theft, an emergency, or to clarify a route.

Improved bus arrival forecast

In the “Bus line management” module, the bus arrival forecast has been improved: the time is now calculated taking into account the actual road route.

Three new columns have appeared in the “Online” tab:

  • bus line name

  • next stop

  • scheduled arrival time at it

You immediately see which bus is running on which route, where it is heading, and when it will reach the next stop.

Driving and rest time control in the “Eco driving” module

In the “Eco driving” module you can set up rules for controlling drivers' driving and rest time.

You define:

  • how long a driver can be behind the wheel

  • how long they must rest between trips

  • daily and weekly rest periods

The system automatically monitors these parameters and warns you if the limits are exceeded. The function is based on tachograph logic, helping you comply with work and rest regulations and look after drivers' safety.

Notification about repeated iButton use

A new notification type has been added. It is triggered if the same iButton is used on several vehicles within a set period of time. This way you can notice a driver change in time and avoid errors in the “driver – vehicle” assignment.

For the notification to work, objects must have an iButton sensor installed, and the “Drivers” and “Notifications” modules must be enabled.

Reports and automation

Custom intervals in the report scheduler

In the scheduler you can now set any report sending interval, for example every 5 minutes, every hour, or another period. Reports are generated for completed periods. For example, if a report is set to be sent every 15 minutes, at 10:00 you receive data for the interval from 9:45 to 10:00. You can set up the schedule for your tasks and receive exactly the data you need.

New report for managing waste bins

The system has a new report on waste container management that helps analyze and optimize waste collection. It consists of two blocks:

Service chart

Shows how many times each container was serviced during the selected period. Based on this data you can:

  • assess compliance with the collection schedule

  • identify containers with high or low load

  • compare zones and bin types

Fill map

Shows on the map the points where containers were full. Each circle shows how many times the bin was full during the selected period. The map helps you:

  • identify areas with regular overflow

  • identify districts where collection frequency needs to be increased

  • adjust routes and send vehicles to the busiest zones

Sensor templates for partner accounts

You can now create a sensor template for the entire partner account and apply it at once to all the objects you need with a particular device type. In the interface you can select and apply such a template to all objects; you don't have to configure each object separately.

Fuel report update

The fuel report, which calculates consumption based on sensor readings, now includes tables of refuels and fuel drains. In one report you now see both consumption and all refuel and drain events with dates and volumes.

Extended sensor reports

The report builder can now generate sensor reports with support for new parameters. You can configure a report to include:

  • geofence name

  • ignition status

  • door status

  • temperature

  • humidity

In one report you can see all vehicle and sensor parameters, as well as the geofence in which events were recorded. All the columns you need can be added flexibly through the report builder.

Notification templates

You can now create notification templates and transfer them between accounts. You can save notification settings from one account and apply them in another. This function helps you set up notifications for new or similar accounts faster and saves time.

Coordinates in the speeding report

Each record in the report now has exact coordinates. You immediately see where the violation occurred, can discuss the situation with the driver in specific terms, and can identify “dangerous” road sections to adjust routes.

PILOT mobile app updates

In the new version of the mobile PILOT we updated the interface, brought back the dark theme, and added useful functions. We fixed bugs and made the app more stable. Using the mobile PILOT is now even more convenient.

Interface updates

We updated the color palette and synchronized it with the web version. Colors are now the same on all platforms.

We increased contrast and refreshed the shades so that the interface is easier to read and more comfortable to use on any screen. Working in the system has become visually cohesive and pleasant.

We updated markers and icons to make them more noticeable and clearer, so elements are readable at a glance and navigation is easier.

We moved some elements so that the data you need is found faster in familiar scenarios.

Dark theme

Updated user interface

New design

Color update

We reworked the palette and refreshed the interface colors to make it more readable and comfortable to work with on different screens. Improved contrast and updated aesthetics make working with the system smoother and more engaging.

New settings menu

All rarely used functions, such as choosing the language, switching the theme, viewing news, and contacting technical support, are now gathered in one menu. This frees up screen space for the main functions and keeps the interface simple and clear.

Optimized map tools

All map tools are now gathered in one place: a special panel in the lower right corner of the screen. You no longer need to spend time looking for tools in different parts of the screen; everything you need is at hand.

Improved navigation with a new menu structure

We moved the second-level menu to the left. The main sections are located at the top, as before, and the section tabs are on the left. This layout simplifies navigation and helps you find the information you need faster.

Module

“Scales”

   — add new weighing stations

   — track weighing history

   — export weighing data for reports

Updates in the

“Service” module

  • Answer checklist questions

  • Attach photos and supporting documents

  • Mark the condition of parts

ICCID field for identifying SIM cards

Notifications with an exact timestamp

We added the time to every notification. When you come back after a period without connection, you will see the exact sequence of all events. SMS and push messages will show what happened and when.

Recalculating driver performance data

Deleting objects through the admin panel

The admin panel can now hide confidential retransmission data (tokens, passwords, user names) from partners. New API for moving objects to new contracts

You can now move vehicles between accounts quickly with the new API. Just specify the vehicle ID and the new account in the API request, and the object is moved.

Extended API for adding vehicles

Before you start working in PILOT, we recommend getting familiar with the basic concepts and terms:

Authorization

— determining a user's access rights to the functions and data of the system after a successful login.

Administrator

— a user of the admin panel who is responsible for configuring and managing the monitoring system.

Account

— a person's personal account in the monitoring system. Through the account, the user gets access to their data and the system's features. The account stores the user's personal data, login, password, contact information, and individual interface settings.

Alerts

— system notifications about important events or deviations from set parameters, sent to the user by e-mail, SMS, or messengers.

Authentication

— confirming a user's identity at login with a username and password.

Software version

— the release number of the software, which shows which variant of the program is currently in use. Each new version contains updates, fixes, or new features.

Geofence

— a virtual bounded area on a geographic map.

Geocoder

— a system tool that converts GPS coordinates into ordinary addresses.

Sensor

— a device that collects and transmits data about a specific parameter or state of an object.

Dashboard

— a control panel that presents the main working information in a clear form. The dashboard shows key indicators, charts, and quick access to important functions.

Contract

— the main element of the system, which combines all monitored objects, users, and available features for one client or company. The contract specifies which devices the system tracks and who can access them.

History

— the history of an object's movement or the history of a sensor's operation.

Object card

— the place where you can edit information about an object and configure its parameters.

Cache

— a place for temporary data storage.

Mapping contract

— a type of contract in the system that combines data from several accounts or contracts in one interface. It acts as a “mirror”, reflecting information from other accounts without changing them directly. With it, a user can track information from different user accounts without switching between them. A mapping contract does not contain physical data; it only reflects data from other accounts. For example, a company's security service can create such a contract to track all of the company's vehicles in one place without logging in to each account separately.

Object menu

— a list of available actions you can perform with the selected object.

Module

— a separate part of the system with a set of specific functions. Modules connect to the main system and can work independently or together with other modules.

Object

— a vehicle, equipment, person, animal, or other moving or stationary object that is being monitored.

Report

— collected information about monitored objects for a selected period of time.

Data transmission

— the process of collecting and transporting information from devices installed on objects to the central server over mobile networks. Data on location, speed, and other parameters is processed, filtered, and stored in a database for further analysis and use.

User

— a person who works with the PILOT monitoring system. Each user has a certain level of access, which depends on their role in the system. Some users can see only basic information, while others have access to system settings.

Push, push notification

— a notification about an event sent to a phone.

Events

— changes in a vehicle's parameters, for example speeding, leaving a geofence, start of movement, or fuel drain.

Tag

— a special label for searching for objects.

Token

— a unique access code.

Tracker

— a compact electronic device for tracking the movement of an object. Once switched on, it automatically determines its current location and establishes an internet connection to transmit data. A tracker is configured by connecting it directly to a computer and using special software to set all the device's operating parameters.

API

— a set of rules and tools for programs to interact with each other. The API is used to exchange data between systems, services, applications, and the PILOT platform.

AccountID

— a unique identifier of a user's account in the system. The system uses it to identify a specific user at login and during work in the system.

AgentID

— a unique number of a device or monitored object in the system, for example a GPS tracker on a car.

Device ID

— the unique number of the device installed on an object.

SMS tracker setup

— a method of configuring a tracker remotely with SMS commands. A text message with a specific instruction is sent to the number of the SIM card installed in the device. Each SMS changes only one tracker parameter. After executing the command, the device sends a reply message confirming the change.

Unixtimestamp

— a numeric time format that shows the number of seconds since January 1, 1970.

PILOT has a hierarchical structure of roles and access rights. The role hierarchy separates the rights of different users.

For example, a company employs drivers, logistics specialists, managers, and a director. They all need access to information about vehicles, objects, and routes, but not to all of it at once.

A driver only needs to see their own vehicle and route. A director needs to see all vehicles, assign drivers, and configure the system for the company.

Everyone sees only what their job requires. Drivers don't get unnecessary data, and the director has everything at hand.

This is why PILOT has several types of users with different access rights.

Roles in the user account:

Administrator

This is a user with full access to all features of the user account.

User

This is a regular user of the system. They work through the user portal, but their rights are limited. The administrator decides which actions a user can and cannot perform.

Roles in the admin panel:

Main administrator

These are usually technical support employees who have unrestricted access to all data and settings. They can perform any action in the system, including managing roles and rights.

2. Administrator

This is a PILOT partner who configures and integrates the monitoring system for various companies and fleets. Their rights are limited, but they can see all the fleets they work with, all contracts, vehicles, and all the necessary information.

3. User

A partner in the administrator role can create additional users in the admin panel, for example for their employees, and assign them specific access rights within their own limits.

Master status

In addition to roles, the system has a special user attribute: master. It is assigned when logging in through the admin panel. A user with master status has unrestricted rights in the system.

PILOT can be used under your company's brand, with your own domain and branding. To prepare for launch you will need:

— a domain name

— access to DNS settings

— an SSL/TLS certificate

— a logo and brand materials

— contact details of the employee who will approve the final design

If your company has an IT administrator, we recommend involving them in setting up DNS and preparing the SSL/TLS certificate.

1. Prepare a domain name

Choose the domain your customers will use to open the platform. For example: app.company.com or company.com. Register the domain with an accredited domain registrar.

The domain must be registered to your company. To keep control of the domain, we recommend that you:

  • register the domain through a corporate account

  • enable two-factor authentication

  • keep the e-mail address on the account up to date

  • enable automatic domain renewal

Do not register the domain through the personal account of an employee, contractor, or third party, because access to it may later be lost.

What to send to PILOT technical support

Tell us the exact domain name you want to use.

PILOT technical support will tell you which IP address the domain must point to and which additional DNS records, if any, are needed.

2. Set up the domain connection to PILOT

After you receive the IP address from PILOT technical support, change the DNS settings of your domain. They are usually available in the domain registrar's or DNS provider's panel.

What to do

1. Open the DNS settings of the domain

2. Create or edit an A record

3. Fill in the Name / Host field:

   Platform address
  Field value
 Main domain, for example company.com
  @
 Subdomain, for example app.company.com
  app

4. In the Value / IP Address field, enter the IP address you received from PILOT technical support

5. Check whether there are other A or AAAA records for the same domain or subdomain. If they point to a different server, you may need to delete them

6. Save the changes

Do not delete DNS records if you are not sure what they are for. They may be required for e-mail, domain ownership verification, or other services.

If you use a CDN, a proxy, or a web application firewall (WAF) such as Cloudflare, enable proxying for the new domain or subdomain only after agreeing it with PILOT technical support.

DNS changes may take effect within a few minutes or take up to 24 hours.

What to send to PILOT technical support

Send one of the following:

— a screenshot of the DNS records

— a text copy of the records you configured

PILOT technical support will check whether the domain is configured correctly.

3. Prepare an SSL/TLS certificate

An SSL/TLS certificate is required for secure access to the platform over HTTPS.

The certificate must cover every domain name that users will use to open the platform. For example, if both company.com and www.company.com must work, the certificate must include both names.

You can use:

  • one certificate with both names in the SAN field (the list of alternative names)

  • separate certificates, if agreed with PILOT technical support

If you have not worked with SSL/TLS certificates before, pass this section to your IT administrator, hosting provider, or certificate vendor.

1) Agree on the certificate parameters

Before buying a certificate, agree the required domain names and the CSR parameters (certificate signing request) with PILOT technical support.

2) Purchase a certificate

Purchase a publicly trusted SSL/TLS certificate from a reliable certificate authority or its authorized reseller. Browsers recognize a publicly trusted certificate as trusted.

You can use the following types of certificates:

  • DV — with domain ownership validation

  • OV — with organization validation

  • EV — with extended organization validation

If you have no special requirements, a DV certificate is usually enough.

3) Create a CSR and a private key

When ordering a certificate, you usually need to create:

  • CSR (Certificate Signing Request) — a request to issue a certificate

  • a private key

Keep the private key in a secure place. If it is lost, the certificate authority cannot recover it.

4) Confirm domain ownership

The certificate authority may offer one of these ways to confirm domain ownership:

  • add a DNS record

  • upload a file to the website

  • confirm by e-mail

If confirmation through DNS is required, PILOT technical support can help with this step if needed.

5) Download the certificate files

After the certificate is issued, download the full set of its files.

What to send to PILOT technical support

Send the files in PEM/Base64 format. These files usually have the extensions .pem, .crt, or .cer.

As a rule, the following set is required:

  File
  What it contains
  Server certificate
  The certificate issued for your domain
  Intermediate certificates / certificate chain
  All intermediate certificates of the certificate authorities, in the order provided by the certificate authority
  Root certificate
  The root certificate authority's certificate that matches the certificate chain
  Private key
  The key created together with the CSR

If the certificate authority provides all the files in one archive, you can send the original archive and explain the purpose of each file.

If the root certificate is not in the set, download it from your certificate authority's official repository.

Before sending, make sure that:

— the certificate was issued for the agreed domain

— it includes all the required domain names

— the private key matches the certificate

A certificate issued for a different domain, or one that does not contain the required name in the SAN field, cannot be used.

The private key is confidential information. Do not send it over an unprotected public channel. Use a secure transfer method agreed with PILOT technical support.

4. Send the brand materials

Send your current brand book in PDF format, if you have one, and the source files of your brand materials.

It is best to include in the set:

  • the logo in a vector format: SVG, AI, or EPS

  • the logo in PNG format with a transparent background

  • logo variants for light and dark backgrounds

  • brand colors

  • requirements for the minimum logo size and the clear space around it

  • a favicon (the site icon)

  • mobile app icons, if needed

  • contact details of the employee who will approve the final design

If you don't have a brand book

You can prepare the materials without a brand book. In this case, send at least:

  • the logo

  • the main brand colors

  • the company or product name you want to use

  • a favicon, if you have one

  • contact details of the employee responsible for approving the design

PILOT technical support will tell you whether additional materials are needed.

5. Agree on the launch

After receiving the materials, PILOT technical support will check:

  • the domain name

  • the DNS settings

  • the SSL/TLS certificate files

  • the brand materials

Based on the results of the check, technical support will confirm whether everything is ready to set up the platform under your brand. If any data or files are missing, you will be told what to add or correct.

After the check is complete, PILOT technical support will perform the setup and agree the launch date with you.

After the configuration is agreed, notify PILOT technical support in advance if you plan to:

— change the DNS records used to connect the platform

— reissue or replace the SSL/TLS certificate

An object is a vehicle, machine, person, animal or any other moving or stationary item you monitor.

To add an object

  1. Click the “Add object” (+) button above the object list.
  2. Fill in the required fields in the object card:
    • Vehicle number: the license plate or the object’s name;
    • Device ID: the unique ID of the device. You can use the device’s IMEI, which is usually printed on its case;
    • Device type: the type of device installed on the object.
  3. Click “Save”, and the object appears in the object list in the workspace.

The GPS device installed on the object must be on the list of supported hardware.

To add a different kind of object, choose it in the “Vehicle type” field: animal, special machinery, trailer or another type.

You can fill in the rest of the object’s details later, whenever it suits you. To learn how, see the “Objects” section.

A sensor is a device that collects and transmits data about a specific parameter or state of the monitored object.

To add a sensor

  1. Open the object menu: right-click the object in the object list on the “Online” tab.
  2. Go to the “Sensors” tab in the object menu.
  3. In the window that opens, click the button to add a sensor.
  4. Choose the type of sensor to add, for example an ignition sensor.
  5. Fill in the required fields: enter a name and choose the device field that carries the values for this sensor. Set thresholds, the update rate and other parameters.
  6. Click “Save”. Check that the sensor appears in the list of active sensors and reports data correctly.

History is information about an object’s past movements and states, including its routes, stops and sensor readings over a chosen period.

A track is a line on the map that shows the object’s path. A track is made of points marking where the object was at different times.

To view an object’s movement history

  1. Open the “History” section in the top bar.
  2. Choose an object from the list.
  3. Set the time range by clicking the calendar icon.
  4. Click “Search”.
  5. In the search results, tick the object’s track records you want to view.

Once you select track records, the screen shows:

  1. The list of selected tracks.
  2. The player, a tool for playing back tracks and controlling the playback.
  3. The “Events” window with significant events or changes related to the object.
  4. Routes on the map.
  5. A chart with the object’s sensor readings over the selected period.
kak-postroit-otchyet-1:
A report is the information collected about monitored objects over a chosen period.

To view a report

  1. In the main menu, open “Reports” and select an object by ticking it in the object list.
  2. Choose the time range for the report by clicking the calendar icon.
  3. Choose the report type.
  4. Set how the report is split: by day, by week or not split into intervals.
  5. Choose the grouping: by date, to see how values change over time, or by object, to compare objects with each other.
  6. Choose the sensor groups the report will use.
  7. Click “Build report”.

After you click “Build report”, the report appears in the chosen format. You can save it as CSV, Excel or PDF, or print it.

If you used the password recovery function by accident, delete the e-mail you received and use your previous login details.

Logging in to the user account with two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is an additional level of account protection.

In addition to the username and password, a one-time code is used to log in. This reduces the risk of unauthorized access, even if third parties learn the password.

PILOT offers two 2FA methods:

  • TOTP authentication: through an authenticator app

  • E-mail authorization: with confirmation by e-mail

The contract administrator must enable the use of two-factor authentication.

TOTP two-factor authentication

This is an additional level of protection for your account. In addition to your regular password, you will use a temporary code to log in.

How to enable TOTP two-factor authentication:

1. Before your first login

install a two-factor authentication app for iOS or Android

Google Authenticator for Android Google Authenticator for iOS

Microsoft Authenticator for Android Microsoft Authenticator for iOS

Twilio Authy for Android Twilio Authy for iOS

2. Find the “Two-factor authentication” section in the “Privacy” tab

  1. Click the “Connect” button next to “TOTP authorization”

4. Scan the QR code with the installed app

5. Enter the code from the app

How to log in with TOTP:

1. Open a browser and go to https://pilot-gps.com/

2. Enter your credentials: username and password

3. Click the “Log in” button

4. In the window that appears, enter the six-digit code from the app. To do this, open the authenticator app on your smartphone, find the six-digit code displayed, and enter it in the required field on your computer screen.

The code refreshes every 30 seconds. If you didn't manage to enter the code before it refreshed, just wait for a new code to appear and enter it.

5. Click the “Log in” button

E-mail two-factor authentication (Email 2FA)

This is an additional level of protection for your account. After you enter your username and password, the system additionally asks for a code that is sent to your personal e-mail. You can log in only after entering this code.

How to enable Email 2FA

1. Find the “Two-factor authentication” section in the “Privacy” tab

2. Click “Connect” next to “E-mail authorization”

3. Select a confirmed e-mail from the list

4. Click “Send code”. An e-mail with a confirmation code will be sent to the selected address

5. Enter the code from the e-mail and confirm the connection

How to log in with Email 2FA

1. Open a browser and go to https://pilot-gps.com/

2. Enter your credentials: username and password

3. Click the “Log in” button

4. Enter the one-time code sent to your e-mail

5. Click “Log in”

verkhnyaya-panel:

navigatsionnoe-menyu:
The navigation menu helps you find the tools you need and move between PILOT sections.

The menu has two levels: the main menu in the top panel and the menu of the selected section on the left side of the screen.

Main menu

The main menu contains the main sections of the system: “Main”, “History”, “Reports”, and others.

The available sections depend on the modules connected to your account.

You can change the order of sections in the top panel by dragging them with the mouse. This way you can arrange the sections to suit you: place the sections you use often at the beginning of the menu for quick access.

For example, after you select “Main”, the left side shows the tabs for working with objects and other features of this section.

statusy-obektov:

Which statuses are displayed

All objects: the total number of objects

Moving: the number of moving objects

Parked: the number of parked objects

Idle in zone: the number of objects that are idle in a zone

Inactive: the number of objects that are not sending current data

You can customize the status colors in the top panel. To learn how, see here.

Click a status indicator and the object list is filtered automatically.

imya-polzovatelya-i-balans:

ai-pomoshchnik:
The AI assistant helps you explore PILOT's capabilities, find instructions, and get recommendations on configuring the system. The assistant opens in a separate window inside the user account.

Ask your question in your own words in the language you prefer. If you need to clarify something, continue the conversation in the same chat.

In the interface the assistant is called AI Support. In the documentation it may also be called the AI assistant or the AI bot; it is the same assistant.

In this article you will learn:

  • How to enable the AI assistant

  • What questions it helps with

  • How to ask a question and refine an answer

  • How to return to a conversation, rename or delete a chat

  • How to rate an answer and leave a comment

  • How to collapse the chat list and change the theme

How to enable the AI assistant

For the assistant to work, AI must be enabled for your account. Technical support performs the initial setup.

After it is enabled:

1. In the top panel of PILOT, open the additional actions menu and select “Extensions”

2. Find AI Support in the list

3. Turn on the switch to the left of the name. A green switch means the extension is enabled

4. Click the AI Support icon in the top panel to open the assistant

If the extension is missing from the list or does not open, contact support. Specialists will check the connection.

What the AI assistant helps with

  • Working with PILOT: setting up devices and objects, reports and templates, geofences, routes, events, notifications, users, and access rights

  • API and integrations: API methods, authorization, request parameters, response handling, and code examples

  • Pilot Extension: extension structure, required files and components, examples, and local testing

The assistant can suggest links to the official documentation. If the information is not enough, it will help you prepare a request to technical support.

How to ask a question

1. Go to the AI assistant

2. In the field at the bottom of the window, describe your question or task

3. Click the button to send the message

4. Read the answer. Follow the links to the documentation if you want to see detailed instructions

For example, you can ask:

  • How do I set up daily report sending?

  • Why is the object online but no new points appear?

  • Show an example API request for getting the list of objects

  • Which files are needed to create an extension?

To help the assistant understand the task better, say which section you are working in, what you want to do, and at which step the difficulty arose.

If you need to refine an answer, ask a follow-up question in the same chat. For a different task, click “New chat” on the left side of the window.

Chat history

The “Recent chats” list on the left shows your conversations. Click a chat name to return to the messages and continue the discussion.

How to rename a chat

To change the name of a chat you have already worked with:

1. Click next to the chat

2. Select “Rename”

3. Enter the new name

4. Click “Save”

How to delete a chat

Click next to the conversation name and select “Delete”.

Rating an answer

Below the assistant's answer there are positive and negative rating buttons . Use them to mark whether the answer was helpful.

If you want to explain what should be clarified or improved:

1. Click “Comment” below the answer

2. Enter your remark in the “Comment on the answer” window

3. Click “Save”

Display settings

The arrow at the top of the left panel collapses or expands the chat list.

The theme button in the upper right corner of the chat switches between light and dark themes.

The cross in the upper right corner of the window closes the AI assistant.
menyu-dopolnitelnykh-nastroek:

Interface theme

rabochaya-oblast:

Divider

karta:
The map is a tool that clearly shows what is happening with objects.

The map displays:

  • Monitored objects

  • Their current location

  • Movement routes

  • Significant geographic points and places

  • Geofences

  • Additional information about objects, for example status, speed, and direction

The map is available when you work with tabs and sections. Most often it takes up most of the screen.

If you want the maximum view of the map, you can hide the work area. To do this, click the screen divider.

If you want to see only the map and remove all panels, titles, and browser buttons, press F11, and the screen expands to the full size of the monitor.

Searching for objects on the map

When you select objects in the list, they are displayed on the map automatically.

1 — Selecting an object in the list. To select an object, select the checkbox next to it

2 — The object on the map

Moving around the map

instrumenty-karty:
All map tools are gathered in one place: a special panel in the lower right corner of the screen.

Zooming

There are several ways to change the map scale:

1. Buttons on the map toolbar and

In the upper left part of the map there are buttons for quick zooming in and out. When you click the buttons, the map zooms in or out, but the point that was in the center stays in place.

2. Mouse scroll wheel

Turn the mouse wheel: away from you to enlarge the map, toward you to reduce it. The cursor points to the area you want to examine in more detail.

3. Mouse double click

Double-click the left mouse button at any point on the map, and it zooms in immediately.

The current coordinates are always visible in the lower right corner and are updated as you move the mouse cursor over the map.

Printing the map

This function prints the current view of the map. When you click the print button, three print orientation options are offered:

1. Landscape: the map is printed in horizontal orientation. This orientation is convenient for displaying extended areas or objects arranged horizontally.

2. Portrait: the map is printed in vertical orientation. This format suits areas that extend vertically.

3. Auto: the system automatically chooses the best print orientation depending on the current map view and its proportions.

Measuring area

This tool helps you calculate the area of a section you select on the map.

How to use it:

1. On the map, mark the corners of the shape you want to measure one after another

2. When you finish drawing the shape, the program calculates and shows its area automatically

Measuring the distance between points

This tool helps you easily calculate distances between any points on the map.

How to use it:

  • Click on the map to mark the first point

    2. Click again to mark the second point

    3. A line showing the distance appears between the points

    If you need to measure several segments, keep clicking on the map to add new points. The length of each segment is shown next to it.

Choosing a map

To change the map, click the map type selection button .

Measuring distance along roads

With this tool you can determine the distance along roads between selected points on the map.

How to use it:

1. Click the first point on the map

2. Mark the intermediate points of the route one after another

3. Finish building the route with a second, final click

4. The system automatically calculates the path along existing roads. The total length and duration of the route are shown on the screen.

Distance to the nearest vehicle

This tool helps you quickly find the nearest vehicle and find out the distance to it from a selected point on the map.

How to use it:

1. Click any point on the map for which you want to find the nearest vehicle

2. The system automatically determines the nearest vehicle and displays:

— the vehicle number or object name

— the distance from the selected point to the vehicle

— the time it will take the vehicle to reach the point

Geocoder

The geocoder lets you find a point on the map by a specified address.

How to use it:

1. Enter an address or coordinates in the geocoder field

2. A hint with a refined address appears below the input field

3. Click the hint with the exact address in the drop-down list

4. View the point you need on the map

Coordinates

: the current coordinates, updated as you move the mouse cursor over the map.
tipy-kart:

PILOT offers several map types for displaying space in the user interface. The choice of a specific map type depends on your needs and preferences. Some maps are better suited for navigation, others for studying terrain or finding infrastructure objects.

To change the map, click the map selection button .

In the menu that opens, select the map type you need. It becomes the main one and will be loaded by default when you open the system.

sloi-i-dopolnitelnye-funktsii-karty:
In the upper right part of the map there are additional functions that help display more contextual information on the map: connect custom layers, view streets, assess road conditions, and see GPS jamming zones.

In this article:

• Object layers: display of additional geographic data from KML/KMZ files

• Street view: go to panoramic images of the area

• Traffic view: display of road congestion on the map

• GPS jamming: display of zones with different levels of GPS interference

Object layers

The “Object layers” function turns the display of additional geographic data from uploaded KML/KMZ files on the main map on and off.

How to use the function:

1. Find the “Object layers” panel in the upper right corner of the map

2. Expand the list of available layers and select the checkboxes next to the layers you want to see

You can enable several layers at the same time or turn off the additional data completely, leaving only the main map.

To learn how to upload and work with KML/KMZ files, see the “KML settings” section.

Street view

The street view function lets you see panoramic photos of the area.

Three viewing options are available:

  • GSV: panoramic images from Google with high image quality and wide territory coverage

  • YR: street panoramas from “Yandex”. They have good coverage in Russia and some neighboring countries

  • OSC: panoramas created by a community of users. They may contain more recent images in some areas

To enable street view:

1. Select the checkbox for this option in the upper right part of the map

2. Drag the yellow figure on the map to the place you need

3. Choose the viewing option you want: GSV, YR, or OSC

4. After you choose one of the options, the corresponding panorama service opens, where you can view interactive panoramas of the selected area.

Traffic view

The traffic view function shows current road congestion using color indication:

  • Green: free-flowing traffic

  • Yellow: moderate congestion

  • Red: heavy traffic jams

To turn on traffic display, select the checkbox for this option in the upper right part of the map.

GPS jamming

The “GPS jamming” function shows zones where GPS signal interference was recorded on the selected date. This data helps you assess areas where object coordinates may be determined less accurately because of an unstable GPS signal.

The function is available on the map as a separate checkbox in the upper right part of the map. After you enable it, colored cells with the interference level are displayed on the map.

A legend is displayed in the lower left corner:

green: low interference level, 0–2%

yellow: medium interference level, 2–10%

red: high interference level, more than 10%

You can also select the date for which to display data. To do this, use the “Date” field in the layer panel.
pogoda-na-karte:
The system has built-in weather visualization from Windy.com, an online platform with interactive weather maps and forecasts.

Weather data is displayed on top of the map and is automatically synchronized with its panning and zooming.

How to connect the weather layer

  • Getting an API key

    1. Register on the Windy API portal

    2. Create an API key

    3.) You will receive a key in this format: 4epwZKT8erOIe6Boq2gfdhffs50ky

By default, a trial (test) key is issued

Trial limitations:

— the GFS model is available

— available layers: wind, temperature, pressure

2. Setting up the key in PILOT

To make the weather layer available:

1.) The Windy configuration must be connected in the contract

2.) In the admin panel, add the following parameter in the contract settings:

windy_api_key = your_key

After you save the settings, the weather functionality becomes available to the contract's users.

How to enable weather

1. Open the map

2. A “Weather” checkbox appears in the list of layers

3. Select the checkbox

4. After you enable it, the weather layer appears on top of the map, and the forecast time panel is displayed at the bottom

To turn weather off, just clear the checkbox.

How to choose a forecast model

Click the globe icon in the weather panel and select a model.

The availability of models depends on the plan.

Free

  • GFS: a global model with basic detail. Suitable for a general understanding of the weather situation around the world

Pro

  • ICON: high detail for Europe

  • NAM: an accurate model for North America

  • AROME: very high detail (especially for France and nearby regions)

  • GEOS5: a NASA model for global analysis

  • CAMS: an air quality monitoring model

  • HRRR: frequent hourly updates for the USA

ECMWF (with a separate subscription)

  • ECMWF: one of the most accurate global forecast models, used for professional analysis

The system automatically detects the plan and shows only the available models.

How to choose the weather layer type

Click the drop-down arrow and select the data type.

Free:

  • Wind

  • Temperature

  • Pressure

Pro (additionally):

  • Humidity

  • Precipitation

  • Thunderstorms

  • Cloud cover

  • Visibility

  • Satellite images

  • Weather radar

    and other professional parameters.

    After you make a selection, the map updates automatically.

How to work with the time panel

When the weather layer is on, a time panel appears at the bottom of the map. It helps you view the forecast by hours and days.

  • Play: starts the forecast animation. The map shows how the weather changes over time

  • Pause: stops the animation at the selected moment

  • Time slider: drag it manually to go to the date and time you need

The panel is shown only when the weather layer is on. If you turn weather off, the panel is hidden automatically.
