primenenie-formul:
A conversion formula is a mathematical expression applied to the data received from a sensor.

Why apply a formula:

  • To correct sensor readings, for example, a formula lets you fix inaccuracies in sensor readings

  • To bring raw sensor data to real physical quantities. For example, a sensor outputs numbers from 0 to 1000, and the formula converts them into the real liters of fuel in the tank

  • To convert units of measurement, for example, kilometers to miles or liters to gallons

  • To combine data, for example, a formula can use values from different sensors to produce new indicators

In the sensor settings window, the formula is entered in a special field

The formula is applied to the data immediately after it is received from the sensor, before the calibration table is used.

The formula must start with one of the following characters:

• arithmetic signs: +, -, *, /

• the equals sign: =

In a formula you can use:

• mathematical operations: addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), division (/)

• parentheses ( ) to specify the order of operations

Simple formulas

Used for simple operations such as multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction. The original sensor value is substituted into the formula automatically.

Let's look at an example of applying a formula.

Suppose we have a battery charge sensor that transmits the value in millivolts. In the raw points, we find the sensor value: Vsource = 9246.

To display the familiar sensor value in volts, the raw value must be divided by 1000. In the sensor settings window, in the “Formula” field, we write the formula: /1000.

The final sensor value is calculated by the formula Vbattery/1000:

  • The system takes the current sensor value in the raw points

2. Divides this value by 1000

3. The result becomes the new sensor value

The final value of the battery sensor in volts is shown in the object tooltip — 9.25 V.

Examples of simple formulas

 Formula
  Result
   *10
  Multiply the original value by 10
 /1000
  Divide the original value by 1000
   /25.5+7
  Divide the value by 25.5 and add 7 to it
  /100+(7*3-2)*4
  A more complex example using parentheses
In formulas, decimal fractions are written with a period, not a comma. For example: 25.4, 1.75

Variables in a formula

Data from sensor fields and standard variables can be substituted into a formula.

All values to be substituted into the formula are enclosed in %% characters

Standard variables used in a formula:

%S% — speed

%A% — altitude

%D% — direction

%P% or %satsinview% — number of satellites

%ts% — time of the current packet

%ts1% — time of the previous packet

Time is used in Unix timestamp format — the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970.

%value% — value of the current sensor

All other values are taken directly from the names in the raw points data packet sent by the sensor.

For example:

%Vbattarey% — battery charge sensor value

%GSM% — mobile signal level value

%HDOP% — horizontal dilution of precision

Enclose the required parameter name in %%, and during the formula calculation it is replaced with the corresponding value from the data packet.

Examples of formulas with variable substitution

 Formula
  Result
   *%GSM%
  Multiply the original value by the data from the GSM field
 /%HDOP%
  Divide the original value by the data from the HDOP field
   %ts1%-%ts%
Get the time difference between the current and the previous packet
   %ts%/86400
  Convert time from seconds to days

Complex formulas

Complex formulas always start with the = sign. In such formulas the original sensor value is not used automatically. If you need to use the original value, specify it through %value%.

These formulas let you perform more complex operations, including using variables, parentheses, and mathematical functions.

Examples of complex formulas

 Formula
  Result
   =%value%*2+10
  Multiply the current sensor value by 5 and add 10
 =%S%*3.6+%value%
  Convert speed to km/h and add the original value
   =(%DIN1%+%DIN2%)/%value%
  Divide the sum of the digital inputs by the original value
  =7/%value%
  Divide the number 7 by the original sensor value

Conditional operators

Conditional operators are a way to set selection logic in a formula. They let a formula take different values depending on whether a certain condition is met. It is similar to a query: “If the condition is true, do one thing, otherwise do another”.

A conditional operator is written like this

condition ? value_if_yes : value_if_no

This expression can be explained as follows:

— condition — the expression that is checked, for example, the temperature is above 30

—value_if_yes — the value returned if the condition is true

— value_if_no — the value returned if the condition is false

Comparison operators

The following operators can be used in conditions:

Operator
  Meaning
  Description
   ==
  equal to
  checks for exact equality
   !=
  not equal to
  checks for inequality
   >
  greater than
  checks whether the left value is greater than the right one
   <
  less than
  checks whether the left value is less than the right one
   >=
  greater than or equal to
  checks whether the left value is greater than or equal to the right one
  <=
  less than or equal to
  checks whether the left value is less than or equal to the right one
  &&
  and
  checks that all conditions are true
   ||
  or
  checks that at least one condition is true

Example 1

Suppose we have a digital input sensor field DIN1, and we want to set a condition:

  • If DIN1 equals 1, the result is 22

  • If DIN1 does not equal 1, the result is 33

The formula looks like this: =(%DIN1% == 1) ? 22 : 33

The system checks the condition: %DIN1% == 1 (whether the DIN1 value equals 1). If the condition is true, 22 is returned. If the condition is false, 33 is returned.

Example 2

Suppose we have a temperature sensor field temp, and we want to set a condition:

  • If the temperature is above 30, the result is: temperature * 10.

  • If the temperature is less than or equal to 30, the result is: temperature * 20.

The formula looks like this: =(%temp% > 30) ? %temp% * 10 : %temp% * 20.

The system checks the condition: %temp% > 30 (whether the temperature is above 30). If the condition is true, temperature * 10 is returned. If the condition is false, temperature * 20 is returned.

Example 3

Suppose we have a temperature sensor with the field temp and a humidity sensor humidity, and we want to set the following condition:

  • If the temperature is above 25 AND the humidity is below 60%, the result is 100

  • Otherwise, the result is 50

The formula looks like this: =(%temp% > 25 && %humidity% < 60) ? 100 : 50

%temp% > 25 is the first condition (the temperature is above 25), %humidity% < 60 is the second condition (the humidity is below 60%). The && operator means that both conditions must be met. The system checks the conditions and, if both conditions are true, returns 100; if at least one condition is false, it returns 50.

PHP functions

PHP functions are ready-made tools of the PHP programming language for processing, converting, and formatting data. With PHP functions, apply complex transformations by simply specifying the function name and the value in the formula.

All you need to do:

1. Write the function name in the formula

2. Specify in parentheses the value you want to convert

3. And the system automatically takes your data, processes it the required way, and shows the result

For example, if you write round (45.78) in a formula, you get the rounded number 46.

   Functions
  Description
   Example
   substr
  Extracts part of a string
   =substr('%Data%', x, y) — returns “y” characters from the Data value starting at position “x”
   =substr('%FIELD%', 1, 2) — returns 2 characters from the FIELD value starting at position 1
   round
  Rounds a number
=round(%AIN1%/1000) — divides the AIN1 value by 1000 and rounds the result
   hexdec
  Converts a hexadecimal number to decimal
  =hexdec('%Param%'), if Param=0A, the function returns 10
   dechex
  Converts a decimal number to hexadecimal
  =dechex('%Param%'), if Param=255, the function converts 255 to 'FF'
   decbin
  Converts a decimal number to binary
  =decbin('%Param%'), if Param=10, the function returns 1010 
   hex2bin
  Converts a hexadecimal notation to binary data
  =hex2bin ('%Param%'), if Param=4142, the function returns the binary representation
  'AB'
   strrev
  Reverses a string
=strrev('%value%'), if value=0123d848010000e5, the function converts the value to      
5е000010848d3210
   bytesrev
  Reverses hexadecimal bytes
  =bytesrev('%value%'), value=0123d848010000e5, the function converts the value to
  e500000148d82301
   explode
 
  Splits a string into parts by the specified delimiter and returns an array of strings
 
=explode(',','%value%')[2]
Suppose the sensor transmits a string of comma-separated values: 90.5,3450,112,43,215
In this case the formula =explode(',','%value%')[2] takes the current sensor reading and splits it into an array: '90.5', '3450', '112', '43', '215', and then extracts the element with index 2 — '112'
An array of strings is  a list of separate strings numbered from zero.
',' is the delimiter, in this case a comma. The string is split at this character.
'%value%' is the string to split.
[2] — square brackets are used to access an array element. [2] means “give me the third element”, numbering starts at 0.
   max
  Compares several values and returns the largest
=max('%value%', 90), if value=85, the function returns 90
   min
  Returns the smallest value
=min('%value%', 90), if value=85, the function returns 85
   abs
  Returns the absolute value of a number
=abs('%value%'), if value = -15, the function returns 15
   str_replace
Replaces some characters or words with others
 
str_replace(search, replace, subject)
  • search — what to look for
  • replace — what to replace it with
  • subject — where to look (the string)
 For example, we need to replace commas with periods in numbers
=str_replace(",", ".",'%value%'), if value = 1,234,567, the function outputs — 1.234.567
  sqrt
  Calculates the square root
  =sqrt('%value%'), if value = 25 , the function returns 5
  pow
  Raises a number to a power
  =pow('%value%', 3), if value =2, the function returns 8 (that is, 2³)
  sin
  Calculates the sine of an angle (in radians) 
  =sin('%value%'), if value= 1.57, the final value is ≈ 1
  cos
  Calculates the cosine of an angle (in radians)
  =cos('%value%'), if value = 0, the final value is 1
  asin
  Calculates the arcsine (in radians)
  =asin('%value%'), if value=1, the function returns 1.57
  acos
  Calculates the arccosine (in radians)
  =acos('%value%'), if value= 0, the function returns 1.57
  number_format
  Formats a number with separators
  =number_format(1234.56, 2, ',', ' ') the function returns 1 234,56
   time
  Returns the current time in UNIX format — in seconds since January 1, 1970
   =time('2023-12-20 12:00:00')
   array_sum
  Adds up all numbers in an array
   =array_sum([1,2,3,4]) — the function returns 10
   pack
Packs data into a binary format
   =pack('H*', '4142') — packs 'AB' into binary data
   unpack
Unpacks binary data
   =unpack('H*', 'AB')[1] — returns '4142'

Examples of complex conversions

  Description
  Example
Converting an unsigned number to a signed number
 =((%BLE_T1%>3000)?((%BLE_T1%-65535)/100):(%BLE_T1%/100)) 
 
  • If the number is greater than 3000 — subtract 65535 from it and divide by 100
  • If it is less than or equal to 3000 — divide by 100
    This formula is often used for temperature sensors, where negative values are encoded as large positive numbers.
  Converting a byte sequence
  (little endian to big endian)
 =strtoupper(substr(unpack('H*',strrev(hex2bin(%value%)))[1],2,12)) — 1500000124286b01 → 6B2824010000
  • hex2bin(%value%) — converts a hex string to binary data
  • strrev(...) — reverses the bytes
  • unpack('H*', ...) — converts back to hex
  • substr(..., 2, 12) — takes the required part of the string
  • strtoupper(...) — converts to upper case

Division by zero

When a formula contains division, be careful with the divisor — the number you divide by. If the divisor is zero, an error occurs, because division by zero is mathematically impossible.

For example, the formula =1000/%DIN1% causes an error if the DIN1 sensor value is 0 or undefined.

In this case, use a conditional operator to check the divisor: =(%DIN1%==0) ? 0 : 1000/%DIN1%. The system checks the condition: %DIN1% == 0 (whether the DIN1 value equals zero). If the condition is true, the result is 0. If the condition is false, 1000 is divided by the DIN1 value.

How to check that a formula works

When you apply a formula, make sure it converts the data correctly.

Check the formula using the “Test” button:

  • Click the “Test” button in the “Formula” field.

  • The system shows values you can use to check the formula specified in the handler. You can select ready-made values or enter your own.

    3. After that, click the “Test” button again, and the system shows the result of applying the formula: correct or incorrect.

Where else formulas are used

Formulas in PILOT can be used not only for processing sensor data. You can use formulas in the “Object card” or when working with the “Notifications” module. The principle of how they work is the same everywhere — the same writing rules and the same mathematical operations.

Transferring sensor settings to a new object
Before importing sensors, make sure you are working with the right object.  To do this, check the object's AgentID in the sensors window.
3. AgentID
The unique identification number of the object.

  • Open the sensors window for the object you want to copy the settings to

    2. Click the “Import” button

istoriya:
History is information about an object's past movements and states, including its routes, stops, and sensor readings for a certain period of time.

With “History” you can see where an object was, analyze its route and driving speed, as well as sensor data.

In this section you will learn:

— how to view the movement history of objects

— how to work with the track list

— how to use the history player

— how to display a track on the map

— how to view an object's actions

— how to work with speed and sensor reading charts
kak-prosmotret-istoriyu:
The “History” section helps you track the movements of vehicles and other monitoring objects. Here you can view routes, analyze events, track sensor readings, and get detailed information about trips for a selected period.

How to view an object's movement history:

1. Go to the “History” section on the top navigation panel

The “Last report” button opens the most recently built history.

  1. Select an object from the list by checking its checkbox

  2. Specify the time period in one of the following ways:

1 — Use the calendar to select specific dates

2 — Use the quick buttons: “Yesterday”, “Today”, “Week”

3 — Select working days only, if necessary

4 — Add parking information to the history

4. Click the “Search” button

5. In the search results, select with checkboxes the track records of the object that you want to view

A track is a line on the map that shows the path of an object's movement. A track consists of points marking the places where the object was at different times.

After you select the tracks you are interested in, the following elements are displayed on the screen:

1 — List of selected tracks

2 — Player — a tool for playing back and controlling the viewing of tracks

3 — Events — significant events or changes related to the object

4 — Route on the map

5 — Chart showing the speed or sensor readings of the object during the selected period
kak-rabotat-s-istoriej:
In this article we look at the history functions that help you track an object's movement and parameters and work with the obtained data.

Track list

After you select the time period and the parameters for building the history, the list of tracks is displayed in the search results.

A track is a line on the map that shows the path of an object's movement. A track consists of points marking the places where the object was at different times.

The list consists of track records with the following parameters: track date, start, stop, duration, distance, and the object's maximum speed.

To configure the parameters that affect how a track is built, go to “Object settings”

Configure the track list the way you like. Select which parameter columns to display, for example, the duration of parking or stops.

How to configure the list of track records:

1. In the header of any column, click the arrow . A menu with the column settings appears, where you can:

• Sort the data in ascending or descending order

• Select which columns to show on the screen

• Group the records by the selected parameter

2. To configure which columns to show:

  • Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display in the list opens

  • Select the checkboxes next to the parameters you want to see

Buttons below the track list

“Follow” — tracks the object on the map in real time
“Return to ‘Online’” — returns to the “Online” tab but keeps the player and the track on the map
“Close” — removes the records of the selected tracks from the list

Player

Use the player to view how the object moved in the past.

Click the “Start” button to start viewing.

Watch the object's movement on the map and on the speed chart at the bottom of the screen.

Next to the player you see the date, time, and current speed of the object at a given moment.

To speed up viewing, click the speed-up button — it helps you review long routes faster.

Track on the map

When you select a record in the track list, the system displays the object's route on the map. You can add several tracks to the map at once, for example, to compare the routes of one or several objects over different periods.

Tracks can be displayed in different colors depending on the selected parameters.

Track color by speed

The speed color is configured in the “Speed in color” section on the “Map and geocoding” tab. Sections of the route are colored depending on the driving speed.

Track color by sensor readings

The track is colored according to the readings of the selected multi-position sensor along the entire route.

To display a track with color indication of sensor readings:

1. Make sure the sensor is configured and has colors set in the calibration table

2. Build the object's movement history by selecting tracks in “History”

3. After the track is displayed, find the panel with the list of sensors at the bottom of the map

4. Select the required sensor from the list

5. Click the palette button that appears

6. The track on the map is colored according to the sensor readings at each point of the route

To enlarge the map area, collapse the bottom panel with the chart by clicking the button

Event markers

Important events that occurred during movement, such as fuel drains, speeding, and parking, are marked on the map with special icons. For detailed information about an event, simply click the corresponding marker on the map.

Events

Events in “History” are actions that occurred with the object. They are displayed on the “Events” tab.

On the “Map and geocoding” tab you can configure which types of events are displayed in “History”.

To view events in “History”:

1. Build the object's history and select tracks

2. Go to the “Events” tab. All the object's actions on the selected track are displayed here

3. Select the checkboxes next to all the events in the list that you want to see on the map

4. Go to the map to view the selected events on the track

Chart

The chart shows the driving speed and sensor readings.

When you select a track, only the speed is displayed on the chart automatically.

To add sensor readings, select the required sensors in the sensor panel. Their values then appear on the chart.

To temporarily hide the data of a sensor, click its name to the left of the chart. The name becomes crossed out, and the line with this parameter disappears from the chart. Clicking again restores the display.

Click the “Select all sensors” button to display all available readings.

To clear the chart of all selected readings, click the “Clear” button .
otchyety-1:
A report is information collected about monitored objects for a selected period of time. Reports help you track vehicle operation, monitor task completion, find deviations, and make decisions.

In this section you will learn:

— how to configure access to reports

— how to build a report

— how to configure report parameters

— how to download or print a finished report

— which report types are available and what they are for
kak-nastroit-dostup-k-otchyetam-1:
To set up access to the reports you need, complete three main steps:

  • Select the available reports in the admin panel

2. Assign report rights to specific users

3. Configure how reports are displayed in the general list

Setting up reports through the admin panel

If you have administrator access:

1. Sign in to the admin panel

2. Go to the “Contracts” tab

3. Select a contract

4. Right-click the selected contract — the context menu opens

5. In the context menu, select “Report list”

6. In the list that appears, select with checkboxes the reports that you want to make available to the contract's users

If necessary, change the report name. To do this, click the field in the “Alternative name” column and enter a more familiar name.

Setting up reports in the user account

Now it is important to specify which reports are available to specific users:

1. In the contract configuration, go to the “Staff and groups” tab

2. Select a user in the list and click the icon

3. A window with the list of reports opens

4. Select with checkboxes the reports you are assigning access to for this user

You can either grant access to all reports or limit the list to only the ones needed.

Displaying reports in the list

To configure which report types are available when creating a new report:

  • In the contract configuration, go to the “Report list” tab

  • Select the report types — select the checkbox next to the required report name

3. Click the “Save settings” button

After you configure report display and access rights, you will be able to:

  • View reports in the list

  • Select the report you need to view

  • Work only with the reports you have access to
kak-postroit-otchyet-2:
To build a report:

  • In the main menu, go to the “Reports” section and select an object by checking it in the object list

2. Select the time interval for the report by clicking the calendar icon

3. Select the report type

Specify the report parameters:

4. Report breakdown by days, weeks, or no breakdown into intervals

5. Report grouping by dates, to analyze changes in indicators over time, or by monitoring objects, to compare indicators between different objects

6. Sensor groups the report is generated for

7. Click the “Build report” button
kak-rabotat-s-otchyetom:
After the report is built, you see the results online right away.

1 — Map in the report

2 — Area divider

Interactive map

Some reports contain an interactive map that helps you see the report data visually.

To enlarge the map area, click the screen divider.

For example, the map is useful in reports on object movement. In the trip report, you can select a specific record, and the map shows the corresponding route with marks for the start and end of the movement.

When viewing an idle report, select the required record, and a stop marker appears on the map. Click it to get all the details about this idle period.

1 — Marker on the map

2 — Report settings

When you finish working with the map, click the “Clear” button in the upper right corner of the map to remove all displayed data.

Additional parameters

Some reports support additional parameters. They help display more data or filter the results when building. The set of parameters depends on the selected report type.

Where to set the parameters:

  • Open the “Reports” tab and select the report type

    2. A block with additional settings appears below. Set the required parameters and click “Build report”.

Which parameters exist:

1. Switches (checkboxes)

Show or hide additional columns and report elements. To show the information, select the checkbox. To hide it, clear the checkbox.

For example, the “Trips and parking” report has the following additional parameters: columns with drivers and vehicle type, and a chart.

If you do not select any parameters, the report is built with the default settings.

2. Numeric parameters

Used for filtering by values and setting a range. Enter numbers; the units of measurement are shown next to the field (sec, min, temperature, etc.).

If you do not need an upper threshold, in some reports you can leave it empty or set it to 0.

For example, in the parking report, specify “Minimum time (sec)” and, if necessary, “Maximum time (sec)” — the parking duration in seconds.

Report settings

Most reports can be customized:

  • After the report is built, click the button

2. Select the required parameters with checkboxes — for example, object, geofences, sensors, etc.

3. Click “Build report” to update the report with the selected parameters

Example

In the “Idle events on the route” report, all parameters are displayed by default.

But you can select the settings you need and get the report only for the selected parameters. This way you get only the information you need.

Downloading and printing a report

A built report can be downloaded in CSV, Excel, or PDF format, and also sent to print. To do this, click the button for the required format or the printer icon at the bottom of the report.

Downloading as PDF

When you select PDF, the PDF export window opens, where you can configure the page size and orientation:

1. In the Page size field, select the page size: A5, A4, A3, or A2

2. In the Orientation field, select the orientation:

  • Portrait — vertical page layout

  • Landscape — horizontal page layout

3. Click “Export” to download the file

For reports with many columns, select landscape orientation and, if necessary, a larger page size — this makes the table easier to read.

Report scheduler

Use the report scheduler to set up automatic sending of reports to your e-mail.

The report scheduler is a tool that sends reports automatically on a schedule.

How to work with the report scheduler:

  • Configure which reports you need

    2. Select the time when it is convenient for you to receive them

    3. Reports are sent to your e-mail automatically

For more information about setting up the scheduler, read this article.
tipy-otchyetov:
In PILOT, all reports are divided into types depending on what they are for and what data they use.

Each report is generated as a table. Tables are the main way of displaying data in reports. Each report type has its own set of columns, calculation logic and separate display settings.

The system provides basic reports used to analyze standard monitoring data: trips, mileage, time in motion, events and other universal indicators. These reports are available regardless of the connected modules.

The system also has reports for modules. They are designed to work with specific system modules (for example, “Drivers”, “Fuel”, “Geofences”, etc.) and use additional data and settings available only when the module is active.
administrator:
This section contains reports related to user management and monitoring of users' actions in the system. They help you track account changes, logins, password resets, blocks, and other user actions.

With the reports you can:

— view the history of administrative actions

— monitor the creation, modification, disabling, and blocking of accounts

— track successful and failed login attempts

— analyze the number and duration of user sessions

— find out which user, under which login or with which role, performed an action
administrativnye-dejstviya:
The “Administrative actions” report shows the history of user actions in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out who made which changes to the data, and when.

Each row of the report corresponds to one registered user action.

What the report displays

  • User name — the name of the user who performed the action

  • Role — the user's role in the system, for example “Administrator”

  • User activity — the action performed and information about the changes

  • Date — the date and exact time the action was performed

The data in the report may be split by days. The names of some actions are displayed using system designations. For example, UPDATE means a data change.
zablokirovannye-polzovateli:
The “Blocked users” report contains information about users whose access to the system was blocked during the selected period. It lets you find out the date and method of blocking, and also check the number of allowed and incorrect login attempts.

What the report displays

  • Role — the role of the blocked user in the system

  • Login — the user's login for signing in to the system

  • Block date — the date and time the account was blocked

  • Block method — the way the user was blocked, for example blocking by an administrator

  • Allowed login attempts — the permitted number of login attempts

  • Incorrect attempts — the number of failed attempts to sign in to the system
sozdannye-polzovateli:
The “Created users” report contains information about the accounts created in the system. It lets you check the user's creation date, role, account status, and validity period.

What the report displays

  • Login — the user's login for signing in to the system

  • Creation time — the date and time the account was created

  • User role — the user's role in the system, for example “Administrator” or “User”

  • Display name — the user name displayed in the system

  • Last password set — the date and time the password was last set

  • Account expires — the account expiration date. If no period is set, the value “unlimited” is displayed

  • Status — the current state of the account, for example active or blocked

  • Created by — the user who created the account
otklyuchyennaya-uchyetnaya-zapis-polzova:
The “Disabled user account” report contains information about accounts whose access was disabled during the selected period.

After blocking, the user cannot sign in to the system with their account. Access remains closed until the administrator unblocks the account.

What the report displays

  • Login — the login of the user whose access to the system was disabled

  • Changed date — the date and exact time the account state was changed

  • Current status — the current state of the account. The value “block” means the user is blocked and cannot sign in to the system

  • Changed by — the name of the user or administrator who changed the account state
nedejstvuyushchie-polzovateli:
The “Inactive users” report contains information about accounts that were disabled during the selected period. It lets you find out when the account was created and disabled, who disabled it, and what state it is in now.

What the report displays

  • User name — the user's login for signing in to the system

  • Display name — the user name specified in the account settings

  • User creation date — the date and time the account was created

  • User disable date — the date and time the account was disabled

  • Disabled by — information about the initiator or method of disabling, for example by the system administrator

  • Account state — the current status of the user's account
neudachnye-popytki-vkhoda-v-sistemu:
The “Failed login attempts” report contains information about unsuccessful authorization attempts during the selected period.

What the report displays

  • User name — the name or login of the user on whose behalf the login attempt was made

  • Number of attempts — the number of registered login attempts

  • Failed attempt time — the date and time of the unsuccessful authorization

  • Possible login attempts — the number of login attempts

If the system could not identify the user or obtain certain details of the login attempt, the corresponding fields may remain empty.
istoriya-vkhoda-v-sistemu:
The “Login history” report contains information about users' logins to the system for the selected period. It lets you find out who signed in to the system and when, from which IP address, and how long the session lasted.

What the report displays

  • Name — the user's display name

  • Login — the user's login for signing in to the system

  • Email — the user's e-mail address

  • Date — the date and time of login to the system

  • Role — the user's role in the system

  • IP — the IP address from which the user signed in

  • Duration — the length of the registered user session
svodka-po-vkhodu-v-sistemu:
The “Login summary” report contains summarized information about users' logins for the selected period. It lets you find out the number of logins of each user, the time of the last login, and the total and average session duration.

What the report displays

  • Name — the user's display name

  • Email — the user's e-mail address

  • Last login — the date and time of the user's last login in the specified period

  • No logins — the number of registered logins of the user

In the current version, the name of the “No logins” column is displayed incorrectly and will be clarified in one of the following versions of the system.

  • Total duration — the total duration of all of the user's sessions

  • Avg Duration — the average duration of one session
izmenyennye-polzovateli:
The “Modified users” report contains information about account changes for the selected period. It lets you find out which account was changed, when it happened, what data changed, and who made the changes.

What the report displays

  • User name — the login of the user whose account was changed

  • Modified time — the date and time the changes were made

  • Modified attributes — the name of the changed account parameter, for example lang — interface language

  • Modified by — the login of the user who made the changes

  • User role — the user's role after the changes

  • Old role — the user's role before the changes
sbros-parolya:
The “Password reset” report contains information about user password changes for the selected period. It lets you find out for which account the password was changed, when it happened, and who performed the action.

What the report displays

  • User name — the login of the user whose password was changed

  • Password change date — the date and time the password was reset or a new one was set

  • Changed by — the login of the user or administrator who changed the password
otchyet-ob-aktivnosti-polzovatelej:
The user activity report contains the history of actions performed by users in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out which user, with which role, performed a certain action, when it was performed, and from which IP address.

What the report displays

  • User name — the display name of the user who performed the action

  • Role — the user's role in the system

  • User activity — the action performed and information about the object it relates to

  • Date — the date and exact time the action was performed

  • IP — the IP address from which the action was performed

  • Location — the user's location
otchyet-o-dejstviyakh-polzovatelya:
The user actions report contains information about actions performed by users in the system for the selected period. It lets you find out which user, under which login, performed an action and when it was performed, and also determine the user's IP address and location.

What the report displays

  • Name — the display name of the user who performed the action

  • Login — the user's login for signing in to the system

  • Description — the action performed and information about the object it relates to

  • Date — the date and exact time the action was performed

  • IP — the IP address from which the action was performed

  • Location — the user's location, determined by the IP address
agro:
This section contains reports related to the “Agro” Module.

With these Reports you can:

— monitor the progress of field work

— analyze the duration and distance of completed work

— calculate the area treated based on the working width of the equipment

— track fuel and working fluid consumption

— compare results across different fields and Geofences

— assess the efficiency of agricultural machinery use
selskokhozyajstvennyj-otchyet:
The Agricultural Report contains information about the field work of the selected monitored Objects and their attached implements over the specified period. Use it to determine the duration and distance of completed work, calculate the area treated, and analyze fuel or working fluid consumption.

Data is grouped by Object, trailer, and zone. For each zone, separate work periods are displayed, and the “Zone total” row shows the summary figures.

What the report shows

• Start — date and time the work in the zone began

• Stop — date and time the work ended

• Duration — length of the corresponding work period

• Distance — distance traveled by the Object during the work

• Width — working width of the trailer or implement per pass

• Area treated — area calculated from the distance traveled and the working width of the implement

• Fuel consumption — volume of fuel used during the corresponding period

• Fuel consumption/ha — fuel consumption per hectare of area treated

• Start location — address where the work began

• End location — address where the work ended

The “Zone total” row shows the summary figures for all work periods in the corresponding zone:

• total work duration

• total distance traveled

• total area treated

• total consumption of fuel or working fluid

Selecting a trailer

Before generating the report, you can select the trailer the Object worked with.

After you click “Generate report”, the “Report parameters” window opens, showing:

• Trailer — the selected attached implement

• Width — the working width of the implement used to calculate the area treated

If needed, you can change the width before generating the report. After you confirm, the system recalculates the area treated using the specified value.

Report settings

By default, the report shows fuel consumption figures.

Use the “Report settings” button to choose the consumption type:

• Fuel consumption (Fuel Consumption) — shows the volume of fuel used and consumption per hectare

• Fluid consumption (Fluid Consumption) — shows the volume of working fluid used and consumption per hectare

Preparing the report

The Agricultural Report is available when two Modules are connected and configured:

• Geofences — used to create and define the boundaries of the fields to be treated

• Trailers — used to register agricultural equipment, link it to monitored Objects, and set the working width

The report is generated when the vehicle is inside a field Geofence and a trailer with the “Agro” option enabled is attached to it. If the Modules are not connected or are configured incorrectly, the area treated is not shown in the report.
bazovye:
This section contains the main Reports for analyzing the operation of vehicles and other monitored Objects. They help you monitor Mileage, Trips and Parking, working time, engine hours, fuel consumption, equipment utilization, fleet status, and the performance of specialized tasks.

With these Reports you can:

— analyze Mileage based on GPS, CAN bus, and odometer data

— view Trips and Parking, their duration, addresses, and coordinates

— monitor movement time, engine operating time, and ignition-on time

— compare equipment operation during working and non-working time

— track fuel consumption, refuels, and fuel drains

— analyze travel speed, equipment utilization, and axle load

— monitor Driver performance and the completion of assigned routes

— view routes, Parking, and Events on charts and Maps

— generate waybills and monitor document validity periods

— assess the composition and changes of the fleet over the selected period

The specific set of indicators, filters, and additional parameters depends on the selected Report, the Object’s hardware, and the system settings.
otchyet-po-tochkam:
The Points Report contains information about the location and status of vehicles at each recorded route point. Use it to trace vehicle movement and find out its speed, heading, coordinates, and status at a specific moment.

Before generating the report, you need to select:

— a period of no more than one day

— no more than three vehicles

A separate data block is generated for each selected vehicle. Each row of the report corresponds to one point received from the GPS tracker.

What the report shows

  • № — sequence number of the point since the start of the selected period

  • GPS date/time — date and time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker

  • Driver — name of the Driver assigned to the vehicle

  • Speed — vehicle speed at the moment the point was recorded

  • Heading — direction of vehicle movement in degrees

  • Distance — distance traveled during the interval between points

  • Travel time — duration of movement during the corresponding interval

  • Latitude — geographic latitude of the point

  • Longitude — geographic longitude of the point

  • Place — address or description of the vehicle location

  • Status — vehicle state at the moment the point was recorded, for example “Stop”

  • Geofence — name of the Geofence the vehicle was in

  • Received date/time — date and time the point was received by the system from the GPS tracker
otchyet-brag-po-bezopasnosti-vozhdeniya-:
The BRAG Report is designed to assess driving safety and assign Drivers to BRAG categories. The Report was developed to meet QatarEnergy requirements for IVMS vehicle monitoring systems.

The system analyzes recorded violations: speeding, harsh acceleration, braking, and cornering, as well as seat belt violations. Based on the results, each active Driver is given an overall score and a color category.

Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles or a vehicle group. Drivers for whom data was received during the selected period are included in the calculation.

General information

The top of the report shows:

  • Contractor — contractor name

  • Project — project name

  • Department — the unit the report was generated for

  • Report period — start and end of the analyzed period

  • Generated — date and time the report was generated

  • Report type — report type, for example Weekly/Monthly

Fleet Overview

The Fleet Overview block contains general information about the fleet:

  • Total Vehicles — total number of selected vehicles

  • Active Drivers — number of Drivers with recorded activity during the selected period

  • Total Distance (km) — total vehicle mileage in kilometers

  • Total duration — total vehicle operating time

The number of active Drivers may be lower than the number of vehicles: only Drivers for whom the system received the necessary data are included in the BRAG distribution.

BRAG Performance Distribution

The BRAG Performance Distribution block shows the distribution of active Drivers across four categories. For each category, the number of Drivers and their share of the total number of active Drivers are displayed:

  • BLUE — Outstanding — outstanding driving performance

  • GREEN — Acceptable — acceptable performance

  • AMBER — Attention Required — performance requires attention

  • RED — Action Required — action must be taken

The category color is also used to highlight the Driver’s name in the detailed table:

  • blue — BLUE category

  • green — GREEN category

  • yellow — AMBER category

  • red — RED category

The higher the overall score and the number of violations, the more attention the driving style requires.

Fleet Performance Summary

The Fleet Performance Summary block contains summary indicators for the selected fleet:

  • Fleet Average Score — average overall score of the Drivers

  • Total events — total number of recorded events and violations

  • Events per 100 km — average number of events per 100 km of mileage. This indicator lets you compare the results of Drivers and units with different mileage.

Individual Driver Performance

The Individual Driver Performance block gives detailed results for each Driver.

The table shows:

  • Driver ID — Driver identifier

  • Driver Name — Driver name

  • Duration HH:MM:SS — total Driver working time

  • Distance (km) — distance traveled

  • Overspeed 120 kph — number of speeding events in the 120 km/h category

  • Overspeed 100 kph — number of speeding events in the 100–119 km/h category

  • Overspeed 80 kph — number of speeding events in the 80–99 km/h category

  • Overspeed 60 kph — number of speeding events in the 60–79 km/h category

  • Overspeed 40 kph — number of speeding events in the 40–59 km/h category

  • Overspeed 30 kph — number of speeding events in the 30–39 km/h category

  • Harsh Accel — number of harsh accelerations

  • Harsh Braking — number of harsh braking events

  • Harsh Cornering — number of harsh cornering events

  • Seatbelt Violation — number of seat belt violations

  • Driver Score — the Driver’s overall score, which determines the Driver’s BRAG category

Preparing data for the report

Violation data comes into the report from the Notifications configured for the vehicles. Therefore, before using the report, you need to create the required Notifications and assign them to the corresponding vehicles.

The algorithm identifies the Event type by the Notification name. The names must strictly match the established template:

  • BRAG Harsh Braking

  • BRAG Harsh Acceleration

  • BRAG Harsh Cornering

  • BRAG Overspeed

  • BRAG Overspeed 30-39

  • BRAG Overspeed 40-59

  • BRAG Overspeed 60-79

  • BRAG Overspeed 80-99

  • BRAG Overspeed 100-119

  • BRAG Overspeed 120

  • BRAG Seatbelt Violation

Assign the Notifications to the vehicles whose data should be included in the report.

If the Notification name has been changed, the Notification is missing, or it is assigned to the wrong vehicle, the algorithm may not recognize the Event. In this case, the violation will not appear in the report and the overall figures may be calculated incorrectly.
poterya-svyazi:
The “Connection Loss” report contains information about the periods when the system did not receive data from monitored Objects. Use it to find out which vehicle lost its connection, when it happened, how long it lasted, and where the Object was according to the last data received.

Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles and enter a value in the “Min. time (sec)” field.

The “Min. time (sec)” field sets the minimum duration of a connection loss for the Event to be included in the report. The value is specified in seconds.

For example:

  • 120— the report shows intervals of two minutes or longer

  • 300— the report shows intervals of five minutes or longer

Short intervals shorter than the specified value are not included in the report. This setting helps filter out brief connection interruptions and keep only significant Events.

What the report shows

  • Object — name of the vehicle or other monitored Object

  • Folder — the folder containing the Object in the Object list

  • Start — date and time the interval began during which the system did not receive data from the Object

  • Stop — date and time the interval ended or data transmission was restored

  • Duration — total duration of the connection loss

  • Address — address or location of the Object according to the last available data
otchyet-o-podklyuchenii-tarifa-akkaunta:
The Report contains information about plan activation for the monitored Objects in the account. Use it to check the activation cost of each Object, the billing start date, the hardware identifier, and information about the installed SIM cards.

What the report shows

  • № — row sequence number

  • License plate (fleet number) — the state registration or fleet number of the Object specified in the system

  • IMEI — unique identifier of the installed hardware

  • SIM card 1 — number of the first SIM card

  • SIM card 2 — number of the second SIM card, if installed

  • Plan installation date — date the plan was activated and billing for the Object began

  • Price — activation cost with the currency
svodnyj-otchyet:
The Summary Report contains key information about the operation of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to check mileage and travel time, refuels and fuel drains, speeding, and parking.

Before generating the report, select the period and the vehicles, and check the boxes for the data you want to include:

  • Refuels

  • Drains

  • Speed

  • Parking

  • Distance

You can select all parameters or only the ones you need. A separate data block is generated for each selected vehicle.

What the report shows

The beginning of the block shows the Object — the name of the vehicle the figures are calculated for.

Distance

If the “Distance” box is checked, the following is shown:

  • Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period

  • Travel time — total duration of movement

  • Max. speed — maximum recorded speed

  • Average speed — average travel speed

Refuels

If the “Refuels” box is checked, recorded increases in fuel level are shown:

  • date and time of the refuel

  • volume of fuel added, in liters

Drains

If the “Drains” box is checked, recorded decreases in fuel level are shown:

  • date and time of the drain

  • volume of fuel drained, in liters

Refuel and drain data is shown when a fuel level sensor is present and correctly configured.

Speed

If the “Speed” box is checked, the “Speeding” section shows cases of exceeding the set speed:

  • date and time the speeding began

  • recorded speed

  • duration of the speeding in seconds

Parking

If the “Parking” box is checked, the following is shown:

  • date and time the parking began

  • parking duration
rabota-transporta:
The “Vehicle Operation” report contains summary indicators of vehicle operation for the selected period. Use it to assess mileage and travel time and to identify trips outside working hours, speed limit violations, travel outside Geofences, and idling.

Data can be split by day. Each row corresponds to one vehicle for the specified time interval. The “Total” row shows the summary figures for all vehicles.

What the report shows

  • № — row sequence number

  • Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Total distance (km) — total mileage for the reporting period

  • Travel time (hh:mm) — total duration of movement

  • Distance traveled outside working hours (km) — distance traveled outside the set working hours

  • Number of speed limit violations — number of recorded speeding cases

  • Distance outside Geofences (km) — distance traveled outside monitored Geofences

  • Time outside Geofences — time the vehicle spent outside Geofences

  • Fuel consumption (norm) (l) — calculated fuel consumption according to the set norm

  • Idling during working hours — total duration of idling within the set working hours
kachestvo-dannykh-data-quality:
The “Data Quality” report is designed to check the quality of the telematics data received from monitored Objects over the selected period. Use it to identify missing or delayed data, gaps between packets, GPS problems, sudden coordinate jumps, and other anomalies.

The Report helps you assess how suitable the received data is for building Tracks, calculating Mileage, processing Sensor readings, and performing subsequent recalculations. It takes into account not only the loss of connection with the Object but also the quality of the data already received.

The indicators are calculated separately for each Object for each day of the selected period.

What is analyzed

When assessing data quality, the system checks:

— delay in packets arriving at the server

— intervals between adjacent packets

— sudden coordinate jumps

— GPS signal quality, including the number of satellites and the HDOP value

— invalid packets and packets without coordinates

— packets with identical timestamps

— exceeding the maximum speed set for the Object

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Start — start of the analyzed period

  • Stop — end of the analyzed period

  • Score — overall data quality score on a scale from 0 to 100. The higher the value, the better the data quality

  • Status — overall state of data quality:

  • ok— the data meets the set requirements

  • warning— deviations requiring attention were detected

  • bad— significant data quality problems were detected

  • no_data— there is no data for the analyzed period

  • Points — number of telematics packets received during the period

  • Problems — total number of detected deviations

  • Delay max — maximum delay of a packet arriving at the server

  • Gaps — number of significant gaps between adjacent packets

  • Longest gap — duration of the longest gap

  • GPS problems — number of problems caused by an insufficient number of satellites or an HDOP value above the allowed limit

  • Coord jumps — number of detected sudden coordinate jumps

Threshold values

The analysis uses allowed data transmission intervals, delays, gaps, the rate of coordinate change, and other threshold values. They can be configured individually for each Object.

If some parameters are not set, the system uses default values and the Object’s existing settings, including the minimum number of satellites, maximum HDOP, maximum speed, and allowed time without connection.
podrobnyj-otchyet-po-poezdkam:
The Detailed Report shows how a vehicle moved over the selected period. It lets you view the time and route of Trips, the vehicle location, Driver data, and travel speed.

The report can be generated for only one vehicle at a time. The selected period must not exceed three days.

What the report shows

  • Object — the vehicle the report was generated for

  • Date and time — date and time of the Event

  • Location — the address where the vehicle was at the given moment

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip

  • Travel speed — vehicle speed at the given route point

  • Max. speed — maximum speed on the corresponding segment

  • Status — Trip type, for example, Trip start or Parking end

For each Trip, summary information is also provided:

  • Trip number

  • duration

  • average speed

  • maximum speed

  • distance traveled
ustrojstva-oflajn:
The “Offline Devices” report contains a list of selected Objects with which there is no connection at the time the report is generated. Use it to find out which device is not transmitting data, how long the connection has been missing, and when the last Event was received from it.

The Report shows the current state of the Objects and is built for the current day only. If you select several vehicles, only those that are offline at the time of generation are included in the report.

What the report shows

  • Group — the group the monitored Object belongs to

  • Object — name or number of the vehicle

  • Message — connection status information, for example, how long the connection has been missing or a message that the device has never connected

  • Device type — type of the monitored Object, for example, car or bus

  • Last event — date and time of the last Event received from the device

The “Total” row shows the total number of Objects that are offline.
rabota-tekhniki-po-dnyam-1:
The “Equipment Operation by Day” report is designed to monitor the daily operation of monitored Objects. Use it to assess the duration of movement and Parking, working time on the line, ignition-on time, daily Mileage, and average speed.

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the monitored Object;

  • Time moving — total duration of the Object’s movement during the day. The minimum speed at which an Object is considered to be moving is set in its settings

  • Parking time — total time during which the Object was not moving; set in the Object card on the “Settings” tab

  • Working time on the line — the sum of moving time and stop time during working hours

  • Stop time during working hours— total duration of stops included in working time. The minimum duration of such a stop is determined by the “Min. parking time” parameter in the Object settings

  • Ignition on — total time the ignition was on

  • Time off duty — the part of the day not included in working time on the line. Calculated as the difference between 24 hours and working time;

  • Distance — the Object’s Mileage for the day

  • Avg. speed — the Object’s average speed for the day
otchyet-po-sobytiyam:
The Events Report contains information about the Events recorded by the system for the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Use it to find out which Event occurred, when and where it was recorded, how fast the Object was moving, and which Driver was assigned to it.

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Date and time — date and time the Event was recorded

  • Event — Event type and additional details

  • Speed — the Object’s speed at the time of the Event. If speed is not determined for the Event, the field may be empty

  • Drivers — the Driver assigned to the Object at the time of the Event

  • Geofences — the Geofence where the Event was recorded

  • Place — address or description of the Object’s location at the time of the Event

The content of the report depends on the Events, Sensors, and Notifications configured for the selected Objects.
sobytie-prostoev-na-marshrute:
The “Route Idling Events” report contains information about cases when a monitored Object remained stationary for longer than the allowed time. Use it to find out where and when the idling occurred, which Driver was assigned to the Object, and which Geofence it was in.

How idling is determined

The allowed idling duration is set in the Object card in “Settings” in the “Idling, sec.” field.

The Event is generated as follows:

1. The vehicle stops

2. The countdown of the set idling time begins

3. If the vehicle does not start moving before this time expires, the system records the Event

4. Idling continues until movement resumes or the ignition is turned off, if the ignition state is taken into account

For example, if the idling time for an Object is set to 00:10:00, the Event appears after the vehicle has been stationary for more than 10 minutes.

If needed, you can enable ignition tracking in the Object settings. In this case, an idling Event is recorded only when the vehicle is not moving with the ignition on.

1 — Set the idling time

2 — Enable ignition tracking

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Date and time — date and time the idling Event was recorded

  • Event — information about exceeding the allowed idling time, for example “Idling for more than 00:10:00”

  • Drivers — the Driver assigned to the Object at the time of the Event

  • Geofences — the Geofence where the idling was recorded

  • Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the place where the Object was during the idling
otchyet-po-prostoyam:
The Idling Report is designed to monitor the duration of vehicle idling. It lets you determine when and where idling occurred, how long it lasted, which Driver was assigned to the Object, and how much fuel was used during this period.

How idling is determined

Idling is a period during which the vehicle did not move for longer than the allowed time set in the Object settings.

The allowed duration is set in the Object card in the “Idling” field. If needed, you can enable ignition tracking. In this case, idling is recorded only if the vehicle is not moving with the ignition on.

1 — Set the idling time

2 — Enable ignition tracking

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle or identified by the system, for example, by iButton

  • Department — the group the vehicle belongs to

  • Vehicle type — type of vehicle, for example, passenger car or truck

  • Start — date and time the idling began

  • Stop — date and time the idling ended

  • Duration (hh:mm:ss) — idling duration, calculated as the difference between the start and end times

  • Address — the address where the vehicle was during the idling

  • Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the idling location

Excessive fuel consumption

Before generating the report, you can check the “Excessive fuel” box. If a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is configured for the Object, an additional column appears in the report:

  • Excessive fuel — the amount of fuel used by the vehicle during idling.

Filter by Drivers

If you enable the “On Driver” option, an additional “Drivers” panel opens to the right of the Object list.

1 — Enable the Driver filter

2 — Select a Driver from the list

In this panel you can select one Driver, several Drivers, or a group of Drivers. The report will show only Events related to the selected Drivers.
otchyet-o-razmere-avtoparka:
The Fleet Size Report contains information about the number of vehicles in the User’s groups and about changes in the fleet during the reporting period. Use it to assess the initial fleet size, track new arrivals and vehicles taken out of service, and determine the current number of Objects.

What the report shows

• Object or User group — name of the User group the figures are calculated for

• Existing fleet — number of vehicles in the group at the start of the reporting period

• Removed from fleet — number of vehicles removed from the group or taken out of service during the reporting period

• New deliveries — number of vehicles added to the group during the reporting period

• Current fleet — number of vehicles in the group at the end of the reporting period

The bottom total row shows the total number of vehicles in the existing fleet, the total number of removed Objects and new deliveries, and the current size of the entire fleet.
otchyet-po-sboru-otkhodov-garbage-collec:
The Garbage Collection Tracking Report contains information about garbage truck visits to waste collection points over the specified period. Use it to monitor the completion of assigned routes, check vehicle arrival and departure times, and identify the collection points actually visited.

Data is grouped by vehicle and date. For each vehicle, the list of collection points visited during the corresponding day is shown.

What the report shows

• Vehicle ID — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Vehicle Type — type of vehicle

• Driver Name — the Driver assigned to the vehicle

• Assigned Route — the route assigned to the vehicle

• Notes — additional notes

• Collection Point — name or full address of the waste collection point

• Location — the actual location of the visited point; shown as a link together with geographic coordinates

• Arrival — date and time the vehicle arrived at the collection point

• Departure — date and time the vehicle left the collection point

• Comment — additional information about the visit to the collection point

The links in the “Location” column take you to the corresponding point on the Map. Comparing the Collection Point with the actual location helps you check whether the required point was actually visited.

The Report helps you:

— monitor compliance with waste collection routes

— check the sequence in which points were visited

— determine how long the vehicle spent at each point

— identify missed points or deviations from the assigned route

— analyze vehicle and Driver performance by day
otchyet-po-glonass:
The GLONASS Report contains summary information about organizations’ vehicles for the selected period. Use it to compare the number of registered vehicles with their actual deployment, and to identify Objects with zero Mileage, missing navigation data, or repair status.

What the report shows

  • Organization name — the organization the vehicles belong to

  • Registered in GLONASS — number of vehicles registered in the GLONASS system

  • Actual deployment — number of vehicles that actually operated on the given day

  • Zero mileage — number of vehicles with no Mileage recorded for the day

  • No navigation — number of vehicles from which no navigation data was received

  • Vehicles under repair — number of vehicles marked as under repair

At the bottom of each block, the totals are shown:

  • Total table count — total number of records in the table

  • Total vehicles — total number of vehicles

If there is no data for the selected day, 0 is shown in the corresponding columns.
otchyet-o-zapravkakh-iman-group:
The Report contains information about changes in fuel level for the selected vehicles over the specified period. In addition to refuels, the report also shows fuel drains.

Use it to find out when and where the fuel level changed, determine the volume of a refuel or drain, and compare the Sensor readings at the beginning and end of the Event.

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the vehicle

  • Date — date and time the fuel Event was recorded

  • Fuel start — fuel level at the beginning of the Event

  • Refuel — volume of the fuel level change. For a refuel, this is the amount of fuel added; for a drain, the amount drained

  • Fuel end — fuel level after the Event ended

  • Type — kind of fuel Event:

  • Refuel — the fuel level increased

  • Drain — the fuel level decreased

  • Geofence — the Geofence where the Event occurred

  • Address — address or description of the refuel or drain location

The data is generated from fuel level sensor readings. For Events to be displayed correctly, the Sensor must be installed and configured for the corresponding vehicle.
detali-poezdki:
The “Trip Details” report contains detailed information about the movement and state of the selected Object over the specified period. Use it to trace the route by individual GPS points, find out the Object’s speed, heading, coordinates, and location, and check the readings of connected Sensors.

Before generating the report, you need to select a period of no more than three days and no more than three monitored Objects.

A separate data block is generated for each selected Object. Each row corresponds to one point recorded by the GPS tracker.

What the report shows

  • № — sequence number of the point

  • GPS date/time — date and time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker

  • Speed — the Object’s speed at the moment the point was recorded

  • Heading — direction of the Object’s movement in degrees

  • Distance — distance traveled during the interval between points

  • Travel time — duration of movement during the corresponding interval

  • Latitude — geographic latitude of the point

  • Longitude — geographic longitude of the point

  • Place — address or description of the Object’s location at the moment the point was recorded

  • Status — state of the Object, for example “Stop” or “Moving”

  • Geofence — name of the Geofence the Object was in

  • Received date/time — date and time the data was received by the system from the GPS tracker

  • Temperature — temperature Sensor reading

  • Humidity sensor — humidity Sensor reading

  • Battery — battery charge level

  • Door — door state, for example, open or closed

The columns with temperature, humidity, charge level, and door state are filled in when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured.
pomesyachnyj-otchyet-po-probegu:
The Monthly Mileage Report contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles in each month of the reporting period. Use it to compare Mileage by month and find out the total Mileage of each vehicle over the entire selected period.

Before generating the report, select the vehicles and a period that may cover one or more months. The system automatically splits the data by calendar month and creates a separate column for each month.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Month — the vehicle’s Mileage for the corresponding month

  • Total — the vehicle’s total Mileage for the entire selected period.
otchyet-po-probegu:
The Mileage Report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place each Trip started and ended, its duration, the distance traveled, and the average and maximum speed.

The “Total” row shows the total duration, total distance, and maximum speed for the corresponding Object.

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Begin — date and time the Trip started

  • End — date and time the Trip ended

  • Start — address or description of the Trip start location

  • Stop — address or description of the Trip end location

The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location.

  • Duration — Trip duration, calculated as the difference between the start and end times

  • Distance — the vehicle’s Mileage for the Trip

  • Avg. speed — average travel speed during the Trip

  • Max. speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

Fuel data

Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box.

In this case, fuel level and consumption information for each Trip is added to the table:

  • Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip

  • Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading at the end of the Trip

  • Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip, in liters

  • Fuel consumption — average fuel consumption during the Trip, calculated in liters per 100 km

The figures are generated when a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is present and correctly configured. If there is no Sensor or no data was received from it, the corresponding columns may show zero values.
otchyet-po-probegu-2:
Mileage Report No. 2 contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place each Trip started and ended, the assigned Driver, odometer readings, duration, distance, and travel speed.

What the report shows

  • Begin — date, time, and place the Trip started

  • End — date, time, and place the Trip ended

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip

  • Odometer at start, km — odometer reading at the start of the Trip

  • Odometer at end, km — odometer reading after the Trip ended

  • Next maintenance, km — remaining Mileage until the next maintenance

  • Duration — Trip duration

  • Distance, km — distance traveled during the Trip

  • Avg. speed, km/h — average travel speed during the Trip

  • Max. speed, km/h — maximum speed recorded during the Trip
otchyet-po-motochasam:
An engine hour is a unit for measuring the operating time of an engine or other equipment. In the simplest case, one engine hour corresponds to one hour of engine operation. In some systems, the calculation may also take engine speed and load into account. Engine hours help determine the actual operating time of machinery, monitor its use, and plan maintenance by operating time rather than by Mileage alone.

The Engine Hours Report contains information about the operating time of the selected Objects over the specified period. Operating periods are determined from the readings of the Sensor configured for calculating engine hours.

The “Total” row shows the total operating time and total fuel consumption for the corresponding Object.

What the report shows

  • Sensor — the Sensor whose state is used to calculate operating time, for example, an ignition Sensor;

  • Start — date and time the Sensor switched to the active state and engine hour counting began;

  • Stop — date and time the Sensor switched to the inactive state and counting ended;

  • Duration — operating time during the corresponding interval;

  • Fuel — amount of fuel used during operation.

For engine hours to be calculated correctly, you need to configure the corresponding Sensor for the Object. Fuel data is shown when a fuel level or fuel consumption sensor is present and correctly configured.
otchyet-netstar:
The Netstar Report is an electronic trip sheet (e-Trip Sheet) with detailed information about the vehicle’s operation over the selected period. The report shows, in sequence, the movement and Parking intervals, speed indicators, Mileage, violations, and fuel consumption.

Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicle. In the “Report parameters” window you can specify:

  • Crew Member 1–4 — crew members

  • Controller — the responsible controller

The information you enter is used to generate the electronic trip sheet.

General information

The top of the report shows:

  • Trip Sheet Number — the electronic trip sheet number generated by the system

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle

  • Crew Members — the crew members specified before generating the report

  • Vehicle — name or number of the monitored Object

  • Period — the dates the trip sheet was generated for

What the report shows

Each row corresponds to a separate movement or Parking interval.

  • Status — state of the vehicle: moving or a numbered Parking

  • Start — date and time the interval began

  • End — date and time the interval ended

  • Duration — duration of the movement or Parking

  • Distance — distance traveled during the movement interval

  • Max. — maximum speed during the interval

  • Average — average speed during the interval

  • Driver ID — Driver identifier

  • Speeding — information about recorded speeding

  • Harsh Braking — information about harsh braking

  • Harsh Acceleration — information about harsh acceleration

  • Over Idle — duration of exceeding the allowed idling time

  • Started at — start time of the recorded action or Event

  • Ended at — end time of the recorded action or Event

  • Work — type of activity during Parking, for example Rest/Sleep/Eat/Other

  • Work — working time category, indicated by the codes NT/OT/DT

If a particular Event was not recorded, a dash is shown in the corresponding column.

Summary indicators

The bottom of the report shows summary information:

  • Total distance — total Mileage

  • Driving time — total duration of movement

  • Parking time — total duration of Parking

  • Number of Stops — number of Parking stops

  • Average speed — average travel speed

  • Max. speed — maximum recorded speed

  • Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption according to the set norm

  • Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption according to Sensor readings

  • Average by norma — average normative consumption per 100 km

  • Average by sensor — average consumption per 100 km according to Sensor readings
net-dvizheniya:
The “No Movement” report is designed to find vehicles that did not move for a set amount of time or traveled less than a set distance over the selected period.

Use it to determine which vehicles have been stationary for a long time, when data was last received from them, and where they are.

Before generating the report, you can set the following parameters:

1 — Vehicle not moving time (hours) — the minimum number of hours the vehicle has not moved. The report includes Objects whose time without movement is equal to or greater than the specified value

2 — Vehicle has traveled less than (km) — the maximum distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period. The report includes Objects whose Mileage is less than the specified value

For example, if you enter 2 in the first field and 5 in the second, the report shows the vehicles that meet these conditions: those that have not moved for at least two hours and have traveled less than five kilometers.

What the report shows

  • Group — the group or folder the vehicle belongs to

  • Registration — registration or fleet number of the vehicle

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle

  • Last movement date — date and time when the vehicle was last moving

  • Last update time — date and time the last data was received from the Object

  • Status — current state of the Object and Parking duration

  • Location — the vehicle’s last known location

  • Difference — interval between the date of the last movement and the time of the last data update
otchyet-po-parkovkam:
The Parking Report contains information about the Parking of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where a vehicle was parked, how long the Parking lasted, and which Geofence the Object was in.

Before generating the report, you need to select the period and the vehicles. You can also set the duration of the Parking to be included in the report:

1— Min. time (sec.) — minimum Parking duration. Shorter Parking is not included in the report. For example, with a value of 120, Parking of two minutes or longer is shown.

2— Max. time (sec.) — maximum Parking duration. Parking longer than the specified value is not included in the report. A value of 0 means the maximum duration is not limited.

These parameters help you exclude Parking that is too short or too long and keep only the intervals needed for analysis.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle number — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

  • Start — date and time the Parking began

  • Stop — date and time the Parking ended

  • Duration — total Parking duration

  • Place — address or description of the place where the vehicle was

  • Lat — geographic latitude of the Parking location

  • Lon — geographic longitude of the Parking location

  • Geofence — the Geofence where the Parking was recorded

The “Total” row shows the total duration of all Parking of the corresponding vehicle over the specified interval.
otchyet-ob-iskhodnoj-skorosti:
The Raw Speed Report contains raw speed and coordinate data for the selected Object over the specified period. Use it to view the sequence of recorded measurements, find out the vehicle’s speed, and determine its location at each moment.

What the report shows

  • Date — date the measurement was recorded

  • Time — exact time the measurement was recorded

  • Speed — vehicle speed at the moment the data was received

  • lat — geographic latitude of the Object’s location

  • Lon — geographic longitude of the Object’s location
otchyet-o-refrizheratore:
This report shows information about the operation of the Sensors installed on the refrigerator unit, as well as its location and speed over the selected period.

When generating the report, you can set the minimum recording interval (in seconds).

The minimum recording interval (in seconds) is a parameter that determines how often the system records the state of the refrigerator unit and adds new rows to the report.

For example, if you set the interval to 900 seconds (15 minutes), the temperature, door state, ignition, and other parameters are shown in the report at 15-minute steps over the selected period.
