To track the parameters of specific Sensors and get their readings in the report, you need to configure them on the Object. For example, if temperature and humidity Sensors are installed on the refrigerator unit, their readings are shown in the report.

What the report shows

  • Gps Date & Time — date and time within the reporting period

  • Geographic latitude and longitude coordinates to determine the Object’s location

  • Place — place where the movement began

  • Speed — speed of the Object

  • Ignition sensor — state of the ignition Sensor

  • AC unit status — Sensor showing whether the refrigerator unit is on or off

  • Back door, Left door, Right door — door states (rear, left, right)
otchyet-o-refrizheratore-2:
The report is designed to monitor refrigerator unit operation while the vehicle is moving and parked.

It helps you track temperature, equipment state, speed, and Object location over the selected period.

When generating the report, you can set the minimum recording interval (in seconds). This parameter determines how often the system records data and adds rows to the report. For example, if you set the interval to 900 seconds (15 minutes), information about temperature, ignition, and other parameters is shown in the report at 15-minute steps over the selected period.

What the report shows

GPS date/time — date and time the data was recorded

Latitude / Longitude — coordinates of the Object at the time of recording

Place — address or detected location of the Object

Speed — travel speed at the time the data was recorded

Ignition sensor — ignition state (on / off)

AC unit status — Sensor showing whether the refrigerator unit is on or off

Back door — rear door state (open / closed)

Ground — state of the connection to the “ground” of the vehicle’s on-board network (power circuit monitoring)

RFID — radio-frequency identification data (if tag-based authorization is used)
otchyet-o-pogruzkakh-i-razgruzkakh:
The Report contains information about loading and unloading operations of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where the cargo weight changed, determine the operation type, and compare the weight Sensor readings before and after the operation.

An increase in the recorded weight is treated as loading, and a decrease as unloading. Each row of the report corresponds to one detected operation.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle number — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

  • Date — date and exact time the operation was recorded

  • Weight at start (kg) — weight Sensor reading before the operation began

  • Weight difference (kg) — amount of weight change during loading or unloading

  • Weight at end (kg) — weight Sensor reading after the operation ended

  • Operation type — kind of recorded change:

  • Load — the vehicle weight increased

  • Unload — the vehicle weight decreased

  • Address — address or description of the place where the operation took place

The address is shown as a link that takes you to the corresponding location.

Summary indicators

The bottom of the report shows:

  • Total weight load — total weight of cargo loaded

  • Total weight unload — total weight of cargo unloaded

  • Max weight load — maximum weight of a single loading

  • Min weight load — minimum weight of a single loading
otchyet-po-datchikam-vrashcheniya:
The Rotation Sensors Report contains graphical information about the vehicle’s speed and the operation of rotating mechanisms over the selected period. Use it to compare the Object’s movement with the intensity of connected equipment, for example, loading and unloading mechanisms.

A separate chart is generated for each selected Object. The horizontal axis shows the date and time, and the vertical axes show travel speed and the rotation speed of the mechanisms.

What the report shows

  • Speed, km/h — travel speed of the Object

  • Loading, rpm — rotation speed of the loading-related mechanism

  • Unloading, rpm — rotation speed of the unloading-related mechanism

Each indicator is shown in a separate color on the chart. This lets you determine periods of movement, when the mechanisms start and stop working, and compare their activity over time.

Rotation data is shown when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured on the Object.
poezdki:
The “Trips” report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out when and where each Trip started and ended, its duration, the distance traveled, the speed, and the coordinates of the start and end points.

To view individual Trips, click the icon to the left of the Object name. After it expands, detailed data for each Trip appears under the summary row. To collapse the list, click the icon.

What the report shows

  • Object — name or number of the vehicle

  • Begin — date and time the Trip started

  • Start — address or description of the Trip start location

  • End — date and time the Trip ended

  • Stop — address or description of the Trip end location

  • Duration — Trip duration

  • Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip

  • Avg. speed (km/h) — average travel speed

  • Max. speed (km/h) — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

  • Start coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip start location

  • End coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip end location

Fuel data

Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box.

In this case, the following columns are added to the table:

  • Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip

  • Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading after the Trip ended

  • Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip

  • Average fuel consumption per 100 km — fuel consumption based on Sensor readings, converted to 100 km

  • Fuel consumption by norm — calculated fuel consumption according to the norm set for the Object

  • Fuel consumption by norm/100 km — the set fuel consumption norm per 100 km

The actual fuel level and consumption figures are generated when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured.

Viewing a Trip on the Map

You can expand the “Map” block above the report. To see the route of a specific Trip, first expand the Trip list using the icon, and then click the row you need.

The Map shows:

— the vehicle’s route

— the start and end points of the Trip

— the direction of movement along the route

— the vehicle’s position

— the sections of the route corresponding to the selected Trip
probegi-plyus:
The “Mileage Plus” report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to find out the time and place movement started and ended, the Trip duration, the distance traveled, the speed, and the coordinates of the start and end points.

What the report shows

• Object/Event — name of the vehicle or the Event associated with it

• Begin — date and time the Trip started

• Begin/Message — address or description of the place where movement started

• End — date and time the Trip ended

• Stop — address or description of the place where movement ended

• Duration — Trip duration

• Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip

• Avg. speed (km/h) — average travel speed

• Max. speed (km/h) — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

• Start coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip start location

• End coordinates — latitude and longitude of the Trip end location

• Agent ID — identifier of the monitored Object

The total row shows the duration, distance, and average and maximum speed for the corresponding interval.

Fuel data

Before generating the report, you can check the “Fuel” box.

In this case, the following columns are added to the table:

• Fuel level at start — fuel Sensor reading at the start of the Trip

• Fuel level at end — fuel Sensor reading after the Trip ended

• Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the Trip

• Average fuel consumption per 100 km — actual fuel consumption converted to 100 km

• Fuel consumption by norm — calculated consumption according to the norm set for the Object

• Fuel consumption by norm/100 km — the set fuel consumption norm per 100 km

The actual fuel level and consumption figures are shown when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured.
tochki:
The “Points” report contains information about the telematics points received by the system from the GPS tracker of the selected Object. Use it to check the recording and receipt time of each point, the coordinates, speed, heading, ignition state, and other transmitted parameters.

Before generating the report, you need to select:

— one vehicle

— a period of no more than one day

What the report shows

  • № — sequence number of the point

  • Gps Date — date the point was recorded by the GPS tracker

  • Gps Time — time the point was recorded by the GPS tracker

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle at the time the point was recorded

  • Speed — the Object’s speed determined from GPS data

  • Latitude — geographic latitude of the Object’s location

  • Longitude — geographic longitude of the Object’s location

  • GPRS Received Date — date the point was received by the system

  • GPRS Received Time — time the point was received by the system

  • Ignition — ignition state at the time the point was recorded

  • Heading — direction of the Object’s movement indicated by a compass point, for example N, SE, or W

  • Acceleration/Deceleration — recorded value of the Object’s acceleration or deceleration

Downloading the report

Next to the “Generate report” button there is a download button. Use it to download the report in XLSX format for viewing and further processing in a spreadsheet program.
otchyet-po-smenam:
The Shifts Report is designed to monitor vehicle operation against a shift schedule in the “Time Control” Module. Use it to compare the actual departure and return times of vehicles with the set shift boundaries, identify late arrivals, and view movement and Parking intervals.

One shift per day is counted for each vehicle. The day boundary is determined by the time zone specified in the Object settings.

How a shift is determined

  • The start of a shift is when the vehicle leaves the specified Geofence

  • The end of a shift is when the vehicle returns to that Geofence

  • Allowed start and end times are set for the shift

  • If the vehicle left later than the set time, the system may record a “Late departure” Event

  • If the vehicle returned later than the set time, the system may record a “Late return” Event

The report shows, in sequence, the vehicle’s movement and Parking intervals during the shift

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

  • Departure/Return — shift start or end Event: leaving the specified Geofence or returning to it

  • Working time violation — detected deviation from the set schedule, for example, late departure or late return

  • Status — state of the vehicle in the corresponding interval, for example Movement or Parking

  • Date — the date the shift belongs to

  • Start time — actual start time of the displayed movement or Parking interval

  • End time — actual end time of the interval

  • Shift start — set shift start time

  • Shift end — set shift end time

  • Duration — duration of the corresponding interval.

  • Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the interval. For Parking, a zero value is usually shown.

  • Start place — address or description of the Object’s location at the start of the interval.

  • End place — address or description of the Object’s location at the end of the interval.

For the start and end of a shift to be determined correctly, first configure the working Geofence and the vehicle’s schedule:

1. In the Geofence settings, assign the required Object and check the “Working” box for it. Leaving this Geofence is treated as the start of a shift, and returning to it as the end of the shift.

2. In the Object card, open the “Working time” tab, select the working days, and set the schedule for weekdays and days off.

3. Check the Object’s time zone: it determines the day boundaries and is used to match actual Events against the set schedule

4. Check the minimum parking time in the Object settings. This parameter determines how long a stationary Object must remain still before it is counted in the report as Parking.
svodka-po-smenam:
The “Shifts Summary” report contains summary information about vehicle operation relative to a base working Geofence, for example “Office”. Use it to find out when the vehicle started work and first arrived in the base Geofence, how long it stayed there, the number of departures, daily Mileage, and odometer readings.

For each vehicle, data is generated by day for the selected period.

For the report to be generated correctly, you need to assign one base Geofence to the vehicle and set the “Working” option for it. The system uses this Geofence to record entries and exits.

What the report shows

• Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Start date — the date the figures are calculated for

• Start time — time the vehicle began work

• Arrival time in the “Office” base Geofence — time of the vehicle’s first arrival in the working Geofence

• Idle duration in the base Geofence during the day — total time the vehicle was stationary in the working Geofence

• Number of departures from the base Geofence during the day — number of recorded exits from the working Geofence

• Time of last entry into the base Geofence during the day — time of the last recorded entry

• Time of last exit from the base Geofence during the day — time of the last recorded exit

• Odometer reading at start of day — odometer value at the start of the counted period

• Odometer reading at end of day — odometer value at the end of the counted period

• Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle during the day

Idle duration is determined according to the Parking settings of the corresponding vehicle.

An image with an example of the report will be added to the guide in one of the upcoming versions.
svodka-po-smenam-2-shifts-summary-2:
This is a summary report for analyzing vehicle operation by shift. It shows how Mileage and working time are distributed between the first shift, the second shift, and time outside shifts.

The report is built based on the working time settings in the Object card.

For example, two shifts are set in the Object’s working time:

  • Shift 1 — from 06:00 to 17:00

  • Shift 2 — from 18:00 to 05:00

  • Friday — day off

The system uses this schedule to split data into time intervals:

  • movement from 06:00 to 17:00 falls into Shift 1

  • movement from 18:00 to 05:00 falls into the second shift

  • movement between shifts and on days off falls outside shifts

What the report shows

  • 1st Shift (km) — Mileage in the first shift

  • 2nd Shift (km) — Mileage in the second shift

  • After Duty (km) — Mileage outside shifts

  • Total (km) — total Mileage

  • 1st Shift Hours — driving time in the first shift

  • 2nd Shift Hours — driving time in the second shift

  • After Duty Hours — driving time outside shifts

  • Ignition On (hh:mm) — total ignition-on time

  • Running (hh:mm) — driving time

  • Idling (hh:mm) — idling time

  • Sensor (hh:mm) — operating time of the selected Sensor

  • Trips — number of Trips

  • Average speed — average speed of Trips

  • Avg Km / Trip — average Mileage per Trip

  • Avg Time (hh:mm) / Trip — average Trip duration

  • Fuel Consumption — fuel consumption
otchet-dlya-sky-favorit:
The Report for Sky Favorit contains information about vehicle movement and Parking over the selected period. Use it to find out when and where a vehicle was moving or parked, assess the duration and distance of Trips, and check the operation of the door, air conditioner, and heater.

What the report shows

• Status — state of the vehicle: moving or a numbered Parking

• Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began

• End — date and time the movement or Parking ended

• Dur. — duration of the corresponding interval

• Distance (km) — distance traveled during the movement interval

• Start — address where the movement or Parking began

• Stop — address where the movement or Parking ended

• Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the start and end points of the interval

• Door open (count) — number of recorded door openings

• Air conditioner (Duration) — air conditioner operating time

• Heater (Dur) — heater operating time

The door, air conditioner, and heater indicators are shown when the corresponding Sensors are present and correctly configured.

Summary indicators

The bottom of each Object’s block shows:

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle

• Driving time — total duration of movement

• Parking time — total duration of Parking

• Average speed — average travel speed

• Max. speed — maximum recorded speed

• Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated consumption according to the set norm

• Fuel consumption (by sensor) — consumption according to the fuel Sensor readings

• Average l/100 km (by norm) — normative fuel consumption per 100 km

• Average l/100 km (by sensor) — actual consumption per 100 km based on Sensor data

Actual fuel consumption data is generated when a fuel Sensor is present and correctly configured.
upravlenie-sborom-otkhodov-smart-waste-m:
The Smart Waste Management Report is designed to analyze waste container servicing over the selected period. Use it to assess the intensity of waste collection, identify areas where containers fill up regularly, and adjust collection schedules and routes.

The Report consists of two blocks.

Collections Chart

The chart shows the number of recorded servicing operations for each selected Object. Object names or numbers are shown on the left, and the values on the bars show the number of servicing operations during the reporting period.

The chart lets you:

— assess the intensity of work for each Object

— compare the number of servicing operations

— identify Objects with high or low workload

— check compliance with the waste collection schedule

Bins Statistics Map

The Map shows the places where the system recorded waste containers being full. The number on a marker shows the number of such Events at the corresponding point.

When you select a marker, the Bins Statistics window opens with the following information:

  • Coordinates — latitude and longitude of the point

  • Address — address or description of the location

  • Total full alerts — total number of fullness Notifications

  • Bin full alerts list — list of Objects for which Notifications were recorded, and the number of Events for each

The Map lets you identify zones where containers regularly fill up or overflow, determine areas that may need more frequent collection, and plan vehicle routes based on the actual load.

The Report data is generated from recorded servicing Events and container fullness Notifications. For the information to be displayed correctly, the corresponding Sensors and Notifications must be configured for the selected Objects.
otchyet-po-spetsdatchikam:
The Special Sensors Report contains charts of Sensor readings for the selected Objects over the specified period. Use it to trace how parameters change over time, identify sharp deviations and periods with no data, and compare the readings of several Sensors.

A separate block of charts is generated for each selected Object. The content of the report depends on the hardware and Sensors installed on the Object.

What the chart shows

— the horizontal axis shows the date and time the data was received

— the vertical axis shows the Sensor values in the corresponding units

— individual Sensors or indicators are shown in different colors

— when you hover over a line, you can see the exact time and the recorded value

The example report shows:

  • Fuel level sensor signal level, dB — signal level of the fuel level sensor

  • GSM/GPRS network level, units — indicator of the device’s mobile network connection quality

  • Satellite signal level, units — indicator of satellite signal reception quality

  • CAN speed, km/h — vehicle speed received from the CAN bus

  • On-board network, Volts — voltage of the vehicle’s on-board network

Sharp rises and drops in the lines show a change in the corresponding parameter. Horizontal sections mean the value stayed relatively constant.

To display readings, the special Sensors must first be added and correctly configured on the Object. If a Sensor is missing, configured incorrectly, or did not transmit data during the selected period, the corresponding chart may not be displayed.
otchyet-po-skorosti:
The Speed Report contains charts of speed changes for the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to trace speed dynamics, determine periods of movement and stops, and identify sudden changes or high speed values.

A separate chart is generated for each selected Object and time interval.

What the chart shows

  • Horizontal axis — date and time the data was recorded

  • Vertical axis — vehicle speed in km/h

  • Blue line — change in the Object’s speed over time

  • Zero value — no movement at the corresponding moment

  • Gaps in the chart may mean there is no data for that period

When you hover over the line, a pop-up window appears with the date, time, and the Object’s speed at the selected point on the chart.
svodnyj-otchyet-po-oborudovaniyu:
The Equipment Summary Report contains daily indicators of the operation of machinery and the equipment installed on it over the selected period. Use it to assess the duration of operation, idling, operation under load, and downtime, and to check the number of recorded actions, fuel consumption, and distance traveled.

What the report shows

• Object — name of the monitored Object

• Vehicle number — registration, fleet, or other vehicle number specified in the system

• Date — the date the figures are calculated for

• Operating time (ignition sensor) — operating duration determined from the state of the ignition Sensor

• Idling — duration of equipment operation without load

• Under load — duration of equipment operation under load

• Downtime — duration of the period during which the machinery or equipment was not operating

• Number of actions — number of recorded work operations or equipment activations

• Fuel consumption — amount of fuel used during the corresponding day

• Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle during the day

The duration of the modes is shown in the “hours:minutes:seconds” format. The content and accuracy of the data depend on the presence and correct configuration of the ignition, load, equipment operation, and fuel consumption Sensors. If the required data was not received, some fields may be empty or contain zero or incorrect values.
summarnyj-otchyet-po-probegu:
The Total Mileage Report contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles over the specified period. Use it to compare the daily Mileage of Objects based on GPS and CAN data, and to find the total Mileage for the entire reporting period.

Data is grouped by date: each row corresponds to one day, and a separate column is generated for each selected vehicle. The top of the report shows the list of selected Objects and the analyzed period.

What the report shows

• № — row sequence number

• Date — the date the Mileage is calculated for

• Total — total Mileage of all selected vehicles for the corresponding date

• Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

• GPS — Mileage calculated from GPS coordinates

• CAN — Mileage calculated from CAN bus data

The bottom total row shows the total Mileage based on GPS and CAN data for the entire selected period — both for all Objects together and for each vehicle separately.

CAN data availability depends on the hardware and Object settings. If no data is received from the CAN bus, the corresponding value may be missing or equal to zero.
svodnyj-otchyet-o-probege-2:
Summary Mileage Report No. 2 contains information about the distance traveled by the selected vehicles on the specified date. Use it to compare the Mileage of monitored Objects based on GPS and CAN data, and to find the total Mileage of all selected vehicles.

What the report shows

  • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

  • Date — the date the Mileage is calculated for

  • GPS — Mileage calculated from GPS coordinates

  • CAN — Mileage calculated from CAN bus data.

The bottom “Total” row shows the total Mileage of all selected vehicles for the specified date — separately for GPS and CAN data

CAN data availability depends on the installed hardware and Object settings. If no data is received from the CAN bus, the corresponding value may be missing or equal to zero.
summarnyj-otchyet-po-motochasam:
The Total Engine Hours Report contains information about engine operating time and the distance traveled by the selected vehicles over the specified period. An engine hour is a unit for measuring engine operating time.

The Report helps you monitor vehicle use and plan maintenance based on engine operating time, not just the distance traveled.

What the report shows

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Period — date and time the period began and ended for which the data is calculated

• Engine hours — engine operating time over the specified period

• Distance — distance traveled by the vehicle over the specified period

The bottom “Total” row shows the total engine operating time and the total distance traveled by all selected vehicles over the specified period.
poezdka-i-parkovki-s-kartami:
The “Trips and Parking (with Maps)” report contains information about the Trips and Parking of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to analyze the time and place movement started and ended, the duration of operation and Parking, the distance traveled, and speed indicators.

The Report includes summary indicators for the selected period and detailed information for each Trip. When Maps are enabled, the vehicle’s route is displayed graphically.

What the report shows

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Work start time — date and time the vehicle began work

• Work start place — address where the work started

• Work end time — date and time the vehicle ended work

• Work end place — address where the work ended

• Duration — duration of the counted Event

• Operating duration — total vehicle operating time

• Parking duration — total Parking time for the corresponding period

• Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip

• Mileage — distance traveled by the vehicle

• Maximum speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

• Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed during the Trip

Report parameters

Before generating the report, you can select the Map type and configure additional display options:

• Show odometer — adds the odometer readings at the start and end of the Trip to the table

• Show maps — adds a Map with the vehicle’s route to the report

• Show parking — shows Parking locations on the Map; this option becomes available after Maps are enabled

Show odometer

If you enable the “Show odometer” option, additional columns appear in the summary and detailed parts of the report:

1 — Odometer at start — odometer reading at the moment work or the Trip began

2 — Odometer at end — odometer reading at the moment work or the Trip ended

Show maps

If you enable the “Show maps” option, a Map with the vehicle’s route for the selected period appears below the table part of the report.

Before generating the report, you can select in the “Map type” field the base map to be used to display the route.

Show parking

If you enable both “Show maps” and “Show parking”, Parking location markers are shown on the Map along with the route.

When you select a Parking marker, a tooltip opens with the following data:

• Start — date and time the Parking began

• End — date and time the Parking ended

• Duration — total Parking duration
otchyet-o-poezdke:
The Trip Report contains information about the Trips of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to determine the time and place each Trip started and ended, check odometer readings, and find the distance traveled.

What the report shows

• Type — the data source used to calculate Trip indicators, for example CAN

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the Trip

• Start time — date and time the Trip started

• Start Odo — odometer reading at the start of the Trip

• Start address — address recorded at the Trip start location

• End time — date and time the Trip ended

• End Odo — odometer reading at the end of the Trip

• End address — address recorded at the Trip end location

• Total Odo — distance traveled during the Trip, calculated as the difference between the final and initial odometer readings

The bottom “Total” row shows the total distance traveled by the vehicle over the selected period.
poezdki-i-stoyanki:
The “Trips and Parking” report contains information about the movement and Parking periods of the selected monitored Objects. Use it to determine when and where a vehicle started and finished moving, how long it was on the road or parked, how far it traveled, and how fast it moved.

Events are shown in chronological order. Each row corresponds to a separate Trip or Parking. The top of the report shows the monitored Object and the analyzed period.

What the report shows

• Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”; Parking is also assigned a sequence number

• Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began

• End — date and time the movement or Parking ended

• Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking

• Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking

• Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location

• Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may not be shown

• Coordinates — geographic coordinates of the start and end of the Trip, or the coordinates of the Parking location

The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location.

Summary indicators

The bottom of the report shows summary indicators, first for the current data block, for example for one Object for a day, and then for the entire selected reporting period.

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object within the current report block

• Track Time — total Track duration, which includes moving time and short Parking recorded within the Track

• Moving time — total time the Object was moving

• Track Parking Time — total duration of Parking included in the Track; together with moving time it makes up the Track Time value

• Parking time — total duration of all Parking of the Object, including Parking before the first Trip, between Trips, and after the last Trip within the reporting period

• Average speed — the Object’s average speed while moving

• Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded while moving

Totals for the entire reporting period

Below the divider line, similar indicators calculated across all report blocks are shown:

• Total mileage for the period — total distance traveled by the Object over the entire selected period

• Tracks Time for the period — total duration of all Tracks in the period, including movement and Parking within Tracks

• Moving time for the period — total time the Object was moving over the entire selected period

• Track Parking Time for the period — total duration of Parking included in Tracks over the selected period

• Parking time for the period — total time the Object was parked within the selected period

• Average speed for the period — the Object’s average speed over the entire selected period

• Maximum speed for the period — the highest speed recorded over the entire selected period

How Parking time is counted

The Report covers the entire selected time interval, including the periods before the first and after the last Trip:

• If the vehicle was not moving at the start of the reporting period, the system adds Parking from the start of the period to the first recorded movement

• If the Object remained stationary after the last movement, Parking is shown until the end of the reporting period

• If the end of the selected period is in the future, the last Parking is shown up to the current moment

In this way, the report accounts not only for Trips but also for the gaps between them, so that the sequence of Events within the analyzed period remains continuous.

Trips and Parking display filter

At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options.

They let you change which rows are shown without selecting the reporting period again:

• “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — all Events are shown

• only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown

• only “Parking” enabled — only periods when the Object was parked are shown

To show or hide an Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box.

Report parameters

Before generating the report, you can configure additional parameters:

• Drivers — adds a “Driver” column to the table with information about the Driver assigned to the Object during the Event

• Vehicle type — adds a “Vehicle type” column to the table with the vehicle category

• Chart — adds a graphical representation of movement and Parking periods to the report

The chart appears above the table part and shows the sequence of Events on a timeline:

  • “Parking” — periods when the Object was not moving

  • “Movement” — periods of the Object’s Trips

The chart lets you visually compare the duration of Trips and Parking and determine when the state changes. For a detailed view, you can zoom in on a selected part of the timeline. The Reset zoom button restores the original chart scale.
poezdki-i-stoyanki-s-grafikami-i-kartami:
The “Trips and Parking with Charts and Maps” report (Trips and Parkings (charts & maps)) contains summary and detailed information about an Object’s movement and Parking over the selected period.

It helps you find out the number and duration of Trips and Parking, the places where movement started and ended, Mileage, and maximum and average speed. The chart shows changes in speed and Mileage, and the Map shows the route and Parking locations.

Report summary

The Report Summary section shows the overall indicators of the Object’s operation for the selected period:

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Start time — date and time the first recorded movement began

• Start location — address where the first movement began

• Departure time — date and time the last recorded movement ended

• End location — address where the last movement ended

• Trips — total number of Trips

• Movement duration — total time the Object was moving

• Parking — number of recorded Parking stops

• Parking duration — total duration of Parking counted between Trips

• Mileage — total distance traveled by the Object

• Duration — additional total indicator of the duration of recorded Events

• Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded over the selected period

• Average speed — the Object’s average speed

The “Total” row shows the total values for the number of Trips and Parking stops, movement duration, Parking duration, and Mileage.

Trip details

The Trips details section contains a separate row for each Trip:

• Start time — date and time the Trip started

• Start location — address where the movement began

• Departure time — date and time the Trip ended

• End location — address where the movement ended

• Duration — Trip duration

• Parking duration — duration of the Parking associated with the Trip

• Engine hours — engine operating time during the Trip

• Mileage — distance traveled during the Trip

• Maximum speed — maximum speed recorded during the Trip

• Average speed — average travel speed during the Trip

The Trip start and end addresses are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location.

Parking details

The Parkings details section contains information about recorded Parking:

• Start time — date and time the Parking began

• Departure time — date and time the Parking ended

• Duration — total Parking duration

• Location — address where the Object was located

Chart

Below the tables there is a chart of speed and Mileage changes over time.

• Horizontal axis — time within the selected reporting period

• Left vertical axis — vehicle speed in km/h

• Right vertical axis — accumulated Mileage value in kilometers

• Speed / “Speed” — change in the Object’s speed over time

• Mileage / “Mileage” — change in accumulated Mileage

Sections where the speed is zero correspond to periods with no movement. A rising Mileage line shows an increase in the distance traveled.

When you hover over a point on the chart, a tooltip appears with the date, time, and recorded speed value.

Map and Parking

To add a Map to the report:

1. In the “Map Type” field, select the base map on which the route will be shown. For example, OSM or Google Sat

2. Check the “Show maps” box

A static Map with the route for the corresponding period is added to the report. It may show the start and end points of the route.

3. To mark Parking locations, also check the “Show parking” box.

The “Show parking” option becomes available after Show maps is enabled.

If Parking display is enabled, Parking locations are marked with the icons.

Odometer readings

To include odometer readings, check the “Show odometer” box before generating the report.

Additional columns with the odometer readings at the start and end of the Trip appear in the table part.
poezdki-i-parkovki-dlya-aramco:
The “Trips and Parking for Aramco” report contains information about the movement and Parking periods of vehicles over the selected period. The Report lets you reconstruct the sequence of Trips and Parking, and determine their time and duration, start and end addresses, distance traveled, and summary operating indicators.

What the report shows

• Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”, as well as the Event sequence number

• Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began

• End — date and time the movement or Parking ended

• Duration — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking

• Distance (km) — distance traveled during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking

• Start — address where the Trip began or the Parking location

• Stop — address where the Trip ended; for Parking the value may not be shown

• Coordinates — coordinates of the start and end of the Trip, or the coordinates of the Parking location

For a Trip, the “Coordinates” column shows two pairs of coordinates: the first corresponds to the start of movement, the second to its end. For Parking, the coordinates of the Object’s location are shown.

The addresses in the “Start” and “Stop” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding location.

Trips and Parking filter

At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options. Use them to change which data is shown:

• “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — the full sequence of Events is shown

• only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown

• only “Parking” enabled — only Parking periods are shown

To show or hide an Event type, check or uncheck the corresponding box.

Summary indicators

Below the table, summary indicators are shown, first for the current Object or report block, and then for the entire selected period:

• Trips — total number of Trips

• Movements — number of recorded movement periods

• Parking — number of recorded Parking stops

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle

• Moving time — total duration of all movement periods

• Parking duration — total time the Object was parked

• Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed over the selected period

• Maximum speed — the highest speed recorded over the selected period

• Fuel consumption (by norm) — calculated fuel consumption based on the set norm

• Fuel consumption (by sensor) — fuel consumption calculated from Sensor readings

• Average consumption, l/100 km (by norm) — calculated average fuel consumption per 100 km

• Average consumption, l/100 km (by sensor) — average fuel consumption per 100 km calculated from Sensor data

In a separate summary block, the values are repeated with the “for the period” label and are calculated from all the data included in the report.

The “Chart” option

Before generating the report, you can enable the “Chart” option.

In this case, a timeline appears above the table part that graphically shows the sequence of movement and Parking.

The chart shows:

• horizontal axis — date and time within the reporting period

• “Parking” — periods when the vehicle was not moving

• “Movement” — periods when the vehicle was moving

The chart helps you determine when the Object was moving or parked, compare the duration of Events, and see long periods without movement.
poezdki-i-parkovki-mc-trips-and-parkings:
The “Trips and Parking MC” report (Trips and Parkings MC) contains information about the movement and Parking periods of the selected monitored Object. It lets you reconstruct the sequence of Events, determine the time and duration of Trips and Parking and their start and end addresses, and calculate Mileage and other operating indicators.

What the report shows

• Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”

• Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began

• End — date and time the movement or Parking ended

• Dur. — duration of the corresponding Event

• Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object while moving; no value is shown for Parking

• Start — address where the Trip began or the Parking location

• Stop — address where the Trip ended; for Parking the value may not be shown

Summary indicators

Below the table, summary indicators are shown, first for the current report block, then for the entire selected period:

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object

• Track Time — total duration of the generated Tracks

• Moving time — total time the Object was moving

• Track Parking Time — duration of Parking counted within Tracks

• Parking time — total duration of all Parking within the reporting period

• Average speed — the Object’s average speed

• Max. speed — the highest recorded speed

The “for the period” block shows similar indicators calculated from all the data included in the report.

Trips and Parking filter

At the top of the generated report there are the “Parking” and “Trips” options:

• “Parking” and “Trips” enabled — all Events are shown

• only “Trips” enabled — only movement periods are shown

• only “Parking” enabled — only Parking periods are shown

The checkboxes let you change which rows are shown without regenerating the report.

Parameters before generating the report

Before generating the report, the following additional parameters are available:

• Show debug

• Auto reset [Beta]

• Show max/avg speed

• Reset milage

• Update milage

• Drivers

• Vehicle type

• Fuel

• Chart

Show debug

The “Show debug” option is intended for diagnosing the calculation of Trips and Mileage.

After you enable it, a “Debug menu” panel appears at the top of the generated report.

The panel contains additional parameters:

• Type

• Mileage

• Show TS

• Show Lat/Lon

These parameters let you view the internal data from which the Trips and Parking were generated.

1 — Type

If you enable the “Type” option in the Debug menu, a “Type” column is added to the table.

It shows the internal type or identifier of the Event used by the system to generate the row. For example:

• renderStart — Event generated at the start of the reporting period

• render_LP_tracks — Parking generated between movement segments

• one_[…], m_start_[…], m_last_[…] — internal identifiers or methods of generating movement segments

These values are intended primarily for diagnostics. They help determine from which Event or algorithm stage a Trip or Parking was generated.

2 — Mileage

If you enable the “Mileage” option in the Debug menu, columns with detailed odometer data are added to the table:

• Odo type — source or type of odometer data, for example CAN

• Start — odometer reading at the start of the Trip

• Stop — odometer reading at the end of the Trip

These columns let you check which readings the value in the “Distance, km” column is calculated from. Odometer readings may be missing for Parking.

3 — Show TS

If you enable the “Show TS” option, the values in the “Begin” and “End” columns are shown as timestamps — numeric timestamp values.

The system uses a timestamp to store the exact time of an Event. This mode is intended for technical data checks. When the option is disabled, the time is shown in the usual date and time format.

4 — Show Lat/Lon

If you enable the “Show Lat/Lon” option, geographic coordinates are shown in the “Start” and “Stop” columns instead of addresses:

• lat — latitude

• lon — longitude

For a Trip, the coordinates of the start and end of movement are shown. For Parking, the coordinates of the Object’s location are shown.

Auto reset [Beta]

The “Auto reset [Beta]” option is used when calculating Mileage from odometer readings. The system automatically tries to detect resets or breaks in the sequence of readings, for example when a new odometer value is lower than the previous one, and takes them into account when calculating the distance.

Reset milage

The “Reset milage” option enables processing of Events related to resetting the Mileage readings. It is used to exclude an incorrect difference between the readings before and after a detected reset.

Update milage

The “Update milage” option enables the use of updated Mileage readings when generating the report. It affects the odometer values used and the calculated distance.

The changes can be seen in the following data:

• initial and final odometer readings

• distance for individual Trips

• total mileage

Show max/avg speed

If you enable the “Show max/avg speed” option, additional columns appear on the right of the table:

• Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the Trip

• Avg. speed — the Object’s average speed during the Trip

Drivers

If you enable the “Drivers” option, a “Driver” column is added to the table.

It shows the Driver assigned to the Object during the corresponding Trip or Parking. If no Driver was assigned or no data was received, the cell may stay empty.

Vehicle type

If you enable the “Vehicle type” option, a column of the same name is added to the table.

It shows the category or type of the vehicle specified in the Object settings.

Fuel

If you enable the “Fuel” option, additional indicators are shown in the summary part of the report:

• Total consumption, l/100 km — calculated fuel consumption

• Balance at start, l — amount of fuel at the start of the reporting period

• Balance at end, l — amount of fuel at the end of the reporting period

• Total consumption for the period — total calculated fuel consumption over the entire selected period

The availability and accuracy of these values depend on the presence of a fuel level sensor and its settings.

Chart

If you enable the “Chart” option, a timeline showing the sequence of Events appears above the table:

• “Parking” — periods when the Object was not moving

• “Movement” — periods of the Object’s movement

• horizontal axis — date and time within the reporting period

The chart helps you visually compare the duration of Trips and Parking, determine when each movement started, and detect long periods without movement.
poezdki-i-stoyanki-rabochee-vremya:
The “Trips and Parking (Working Time)” report contains information about the movement and Parking of the selected vehicles according to the work schedule. Use it to determine how an Object was used during working or non-working time: when it was moving, where it was parked, how far it traveled, and how much time it spent in each state.

What the report shows

• Status — state of the Object: “Movement” or “Parking”

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the vehicle

• Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the corresponding Event

• Day of the week — the day of the week on which the movement or Parking took place

• Begin — date and time the movement or Parking began

• End — date and time the movement or Parking ended

• Dur. — duration of the corresponding Trip or Parking

• Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object during the Trip; no value is shown for Parking

• Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location

• Stop — address where the movement ended; for Parking the value may not be shown

Summary indicators

Below the table, summary indicators for the current Object or report block are shown:

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the Object during the counted time

• Moving time — total duration of all movement periods

• Parking time — total duration of all Parking

• Average speed — the Object’s average speed while moving

• Max. speed — the highest speed recorded while moving

Below that, a separate summary block with indicators for the entire selected period is shown:

• Total mileage for the period

• Moving time for the period

• Parking time for the period

• Average speed for the period

• Max. speed for the period

Working time parameters

Before generating the report, you can select which data to include:

• Working time only — the report counts Events that fall within working time according to the configured schedule

• Non-working time only — the report counts Events that fall within non-working time

Working and non-working time is determined by the Object’s work schedule settings.

Working time only

When you enable the “Working time only” option, the report lets you analyze vehicle use during the hours set by the work schedule.

The report shows:

• Trips made during working time

• Parking between Trips

• Parking from the start of the working interval to the first movement

• Parking from the last movement to the end of the working interval

Non-working time only

When you enable the “Non-working time only” option, the report shows movement and Parking outside the set work schedule.

It helps you identify:

• Trips after working hours end

• vehicle use on weekends or non-working days

• movement before the start of the work shift

• long Parking outside working hours
otchet-o-poezdkakh-i-parkovkakh-rabochee:
The “Trips and Parking (Working Time) No. 2” report contains summary information about the movement of the selected vehicles according to the work schedule. Use it to determine when a vehicle was used, who drove it, where it traveled from and to, and to find out the movement duration, Mileage, and speed indicators.

What the report shows

• Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

• Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle during the movement

• Day — the day of the week on which the Trips were made

• Start — date and time the first movement began in the counted interval

• End — date and time the last movement ended in the counted interval

• Duration — total movement duration in the report row

• Distance — total distance traveled by the vehicle

• From — address where the movement began

• To — address where the movement ended

The addresses in the “From” and “To” columns are shown as links that take you to the corresponding locations.

Totals by date

Below each daily block, the indicators calculated from all rows for the corresponding date are shown:

• Total mileage — total distance traveled by the vehicle during the day

• Moving time — total movement duration for the day

• Average speed — the vehicle’s average speed for the day

• Max. speed — the highest speed recorded during the day

Totals for the entire period

The bottom of the report shows indicators for all data included in the selected reporting period:

• Total mileage for the period — total distance traveled by the vehicle

• Moving time for the period — total movement duration

• Average speed for the period — average travel speed over the entire period

• Max. speed for the period — the highest speed recorded over the entire period

Working time parameters

Before generating the report, you can select which data to include:

• Working time only — Trips made within the Object’s work schedule are counted

• Non-working time only — Trips made outside the Object’s work schedule are counted

Working and non-working time is determined by the vehicle’s work schedule settings.

Working time only

When you enable the “Working time only” option, the report shows vehicle use during the hours set by the work schedule. This mode lets you assess:

• the number and duration of working departures

• Mileage during working time

• the start and end points of movement

• average and maximum speed

• the assigned Driver’s work

Non-working time only

When you enable the “Non-working time only” option, the report shows Trips made outside the set work schedule. This mode lets you identify:

• Trips on weekends and non-working days

• vehicle use outside permitted hours

If a Trip crosses the boundary of the working interval, the report counts the part of the movement that corresponds to the selected mode.

poezdki-i-stoyanki-s-urovnyami:
The “Trips and Parking with Levels” report contains information about the movement and Parking of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Data is grouped by Object and date and shown as summary rows that you can expand to view the detailed sequence of Events.

The summary row shows the time and place the counted period started and ended, its total duration, and the total distance. To view the Trips and Parking it includes, click the button to the left of the Object name.

What the report shows

• Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

• Type — Event type: “Movement” or “Parking”

• Begin — date and time the Trip or Parking began

• Start — address where the movement began or the Parking location

• End — date and time the Trip or Parking ended

otchyet-po-zagruzhennosti-tekhniki:
The Equipment Utilization Report contains information about the use of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. It lets you compare the time machinery spent idling and under load, and determine the total engine hours and the distance traveled.

Use the Report to assess the efficiency of equipment operation, identify long operation without useful load, reduce downtime, and allocate resources more efficiently.

Report structure

The information is presented in several sections:

  • “Totals for the period” — summary indicators for all selected Objects

  • “Equipment use for the period” — a pie chart showing the ratio of Parking, idling, and operation under load

  • Breakdown by Object — indicators for each Object, split by date

Totals

  • Object — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

  • Description — additional information about the Object. If no description is set, the field stays empty

  • Days — number of calendar days included in the analyzed period

  • Idling — engine operating time without recorded useful load. The indicator is shown in two columns:

  • % — the share of idling calculated by the system

  • hh:mm — idling duration in hours and minutes

  • Operation under load — time during which the equipment performed useful work. The indicator is shown in two columns:

  • % — the share of operation under load calculated by the system

  • hh:mm — duration of operation under load in hours and minutes

  • Total engine hours — total engine operating time for the corresponding period in “hh:mm” format

  • Distance, km — distance traveled by the Object over the specified period

Equipment use chart

Below the totals table, in the “Equipment use for the period” section, a pie chart is shown. It shows the ratio of the main equipment states:

  • Parking — time when the equipment was neither working nor moving

  • Idling — time the engine ran without useful load

  • Operation under load — time the equipment performed useful work

The chart lets you visually compare the states and determine what part of the selected period was actual work, idling, and Parking.

Breakdown by Object

Below the chart, separate blocks split by date are shown for each Object. Each daily block contains:

  • Description — additional description of the Object

  • Idling — percentage and duration of idling

  • Operation under load — percentage and duration of operation under load

  • Total engine hours — total engine operating time for the day

  • Distance, km — the Object’s Mileage for the corresponding date

This breakdown lets you compare the indicators of one Object by day and find periods of high load, long idling, or no work.

This breakdown lets you compare the indicators of one Object by day and find periods of high load, long idling, or no work.
srok-dejstviya-litsenzii-na-transportnoe:
The “Vehicle License Expired” report is designed to monitor the validity periods of vehicle registration documents. It lets you identify in advance the Objects whose vehicle registration certificate (STS) has already expired or expires within the selected period.

Check period

Before generating the report, you need to specify the check range in months. The system calculates the checked interval starting from the current date and selects the vehicles whose STS validity falls within this range.

For example, if a period of 3 months is selected, the report includes vehicles:

  • whose STS has already expired

  • whose STS expires within the next three months

The larger the selected range, the more future expiration dates the check covers.

For the report to be generated correctly, open the “Info” tab in each vehicle’s card and fill in the following data:

  • STS number — series and number of the vehicle registration certificate

  • Validity period — STS expiration date

The system compares the specified date with the check period and adds the vehicle to the report if the document has already expired or expires within the selected range.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

  • Group — the group the vehicle is in

  • Description — additional description of the vehicle

  • Year — the vehicle’s year of manufacture specified in the Object card

  • STS number — the document number specified in the Object card

  • Validity period — STS expiration date
summarnyj-otchyet-po-rabote:
The Total Work Report contains time indicators of the operation of the selected monitored Objects over the specified period. Use it to compare the duration of movement and Parking, ignition-on time, and Maintenance periods, and to determine the time actually worked.

What the report shows

• Vehicle — name, registration, or fleet number of the monitored Object

• Date — date and time the interval began and ended for which the indicators are calculated

• Information — additional information about the monitored Object; if no information is specified, the field stays empty

• Total time — total duration of the corresponding reporting interval

• Movement duration — total time the Object was moving

• Parking time — total duration of the Object’s Parking

• Ignition on — total time during which the ignition was recorded as on

• Ignition off — total time during which the ignition was off

• Non-working time — the part of the reporting interval that falls within non-working time according to the configured Object schedule

• Maintenance time — duration of the periods during which the Object was under Maintenance

• Time worked — time within the work schedule minus Maintenance periods. Calculated as the total time minus non-working time and Maintenance time

The “Working time only” option

Before generating the report, you can enable the “Working time only” option. In this case, the indicators are calculated only within the working intervals set in the Object’s schedule.

The option lets you exclude nighttime, weekends, and other non-working intervals from the analysis.
putevye-listy:
The “Waybills” report is designed to generate vehicle waybills according to the established standard forms. Some fields are filled in automatically based on the selected Object, the assigned Driver, the reporting period, and the data specified in the system.

The Report lets you prepare a document for recording the operation of the vehicle and Driver, check the generated information, save the waybill to a file, or print it.

Selecting the vehicle type

Before generating the report, you need to select the vehicle type.

The waybill form depends on the selected type:

• Passenger car — a passenger car waybill is generated using standard interindustry form No. 3, approved by Resolution of the State Statistics Committee of Russia of 28.11.1997 No. 78

• Truck — a truck waybill is generated using standard interindustry form No. 4-P, approved by Resolution of the State Statistics Committee of Russia of 28.11.1997 No. 78

What the waybill shows

The content of the document depends on the selected form. The waybill may include:

• organization details

• date, series, and number of the waybill

• make and state registration number of the vehicle

• fleet and personnel numbers

• Driver details

• driver’s license number and Driver class

• license details

• actual departure and return times

• data on the Driver’s and the vehicle’s work

• information on movement and fuel consumption

• the Driver’s assignment

• fields for marks, signatures, and technical inspection results

The presence and completion of individual fields depends on the selected form and on what information has been entered in the organization, vehicle, and Driver cards.

Saving and printing

You can preview the generated waybill in the report. The following actions are available at the bottom of the window:

• Download in Excel format — saves the waybill as a spreadsheet

• Download in PDF format — saves the document in PDF format

• Print — opens the waybill for printing
rabochee-vremya-2:
The “Working Time No. 2” report contains information about the Mileage and working time of the selected vehicle over the specified period. Use it to compare odometer readings with the calculated Mileage, determine the number of Trips, and split working time into categories: regular, overtime, holiday, and Sunday.

What the report shows

• Date — the day the indicators are calculated for

This section contains reports related to the “Trips” Module. They help you monitor vehicle movement along bus lines, stop visits, the completion of loop trips, and schedule adherence.

With these Reports you can:

otchyet-po-poseshcheniyu-ostanovok:
The Stop Visits Report is designed to monitor visits to bus stops by vehicles assigned to routes. Use it to determine which stops a vehicle visited, and to find out its actual arrival and departure times.

Before generating the report, you need to select the vehicles and the bus line for which you want to check stop visits.

What the report shows

Each row of the report corresponds to one recorded visit to a stop by a vehicle.

The report shows:

  • Order — the position of the stop in the sequence of the route

  • Route number — name or number of the route on which the stop was visited

  • Stop — name of the visited stop

  • Address — address of the stop

  • Date — date of the stop visit

  • Arrival time — time the vehicle arrived at the stop

  • Departure time — time the vehicle left the stop

  • Vehicle — number of the monitored Object that visited the stop

If an RFID tag is linked to the stop, PILOT can determine a visit from the data of the RFID reader installed on the vehicle. The recorded visit is shown in the report in the same way as a visit determined by the Object’s coordinates.
kontrol-poseshcheniya-ostanovok:
The “Stop Visit Control” report helps you monitor how vehicles actually follow the set routes. Use it to check which stops a vehicle visited, when it arrived and departed, and how long it stayed at the stop.

When generating the report, select the stops whose visits you want to check. If several stops are selected, the report shows all recorded visits to these stops by the selected vehicles during the specified period.

What the report shows

Each row is one recorded visit to a stop by a vehicle.

The report shows:

  • Stop sequence number — the position of the stop in the sequence of the route

  • Route — name or number of the route the vehicle was following

  • Stop name — name of the visited stop

  • Address — location of the stop

  • Date — day of the stop visit

  • Arrival time — time the vehicle arrived at the stop

  • Departure time — time the vehicle left the stop

  • Parking — length of time the vehicle was at the stop

  • Vehicle number — vehicle number
otchyet-po-krugorejsam:
The Loop Trips Report is designed to analyze vehicle operation on routes. It shows how long the vehicle operated, as well as the number of completed full and incomplete loop trips.

The system determines whether a loop trip is complete based on the visits to the stops assigned to the Trip and the set direction of movement. If the vehicle completed the route according to the specified conditions, the loop trip is counted as full. If the route conditions were not fully met, the loop trip is counted as incomplete.

Each row of the report contains information about the operation of one vehicle on the route on the specified date.

What the report shows

  • Trip number — number of the Trip assigned to the monitored Object

  • Vehicle number — vehicle number

  • Date — date the Trips were performed

  • Route arrival time — time the vehicle entered the route

  • Departure time — time the vehicle left the route

  • Time on route — total duration of the vehicle’s operation on the route, calculated as the difference between the arrival time and the departure time

  • Number of Trips — number of full loop trips completed on the route

  • Number of incomplete Trips — number of loop trips during which not all anchor stops were visited
otchyet-po-soblyudeniyu-raspisanij:
The Report is designed to monitor actual schedule performance on the selected bus line.

It compares the planned stop times (from the schedule matrix) with the actual stop visit times and clearly shows how closely the actual movement matched the plan.

What the report shows

The Report is built for one selected bus line and is generated as a table where:

  • The first column is the schedule name

  • Each following column is a stop on the route

  • Each cell contains data for a specific stop for a specific Trip

Each cell shows:

  • Plan — planned arrival time at the stop

  • Actual — actual arrival time at the stop

  • Difference — deviation of the actual time from the planned time

  • Object — the vehicle (license plate) that actually made the stop

If no actual visit was recorded, the cell is marked “Missed” (not performed)

How the report is generated

1. The selected bus line and its list of stops are taken

2. The history of schedule versions in effect during the specified period is loaded

3. For each day in the reporting interval, the schedule table to apply is determined:

  • by specific date

  • by day of the week

  • or daily

    4. For each planned Trip and each stop, the nearest actual visit to that stop is searched for

    5. If an Event is found within the allowed deviation window, Plan / Actual / Difference / Object are shown in the cell

    6. If no Event is found, the cell is marked “Missed”

Comparison logic

  • The Report checks schedule adherence not for a specific bus but by whether the stop was made on the line.

  • If several buses operate on the line at the same time, the report counts any bus that actually made the stop at the right time.

  • No more than one actual Event is used for each planned time.

  • One actual Event is not reused to confirm several planned stops.

  • If the schedule changes within the reporting period, the schedule version that was in effect at the time of the specific planned Trip is applied.

Report color coding

  • Green — minimal deviation, the stop was made close to the plan

  • Yellow — acceptable deviation from the schedule

  • Orange — noticeable time deviation.

  • Red — large deviation or missed stop (no actual visit)

otchyet-o-ezhednevnoj-poezdke:
This report shows how each vehicle and Driver worked during the day.

It lets you see:

— when the first Trip started and the last one ended

— how long the vehicle was moving, parked, and idling

— the Mileage and speed for the day

— how many Trips were made

What the report shows

The report is built by day: one table row = one working day of one vehicle

  • Date — date the first Trip of the day started

  • Object — vehicle

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle on that day (if no Driver is assigned, no driver is shown)

  • First Trip start time — date and time the vehicle first started moving during the day

  • Hours between the start of the first Trip and the end of the last (hh:mm:ss) — the vehicle’s total “working time” for the day: from the first Trip to the last, including movement and stops

  • Driving time % — the share of working time spent moving

  • Travel time (hh:mm:ss) — total movement time for the day

  • Parking time (hh:mm:ss) — total time of stops and Parking between Trips

  • Duration (hh:mm:ss) — total duration of the vehicle’s operation for the day (movement + Parking)

  • Idling time (hh:mm:ss) — time when the vehicle was on but not doing work (for example, the engine was idling)

  • Distance (km) — the vehicle’s Mileage for the day.

  • Average speed (km/h) — average speed for the day

    (distance divided by moving time).

  • Max. speed (km/h) — maximum recorded speed for the day

  • Number of Trips — how many separate Trips were made during the day

At the bottom of the table there is a “Total” row, which automatically calculates:

— total working time

— total Mileage

— average indicators across all rows for the selected date

kachestvo-vozhdeniya:
Driving Quality

Driving quality is a measure of how well a driver operates a vehicle safely, economically and comfortably.

Reports for the Eco-driving module.
otchyet-po-kachestvu-vozhdeniya:
The Driving Quality Report helps you understand how carefully and safely Drivers drive.

The system records Events (harsh acceleration, braking, speeding, and others), converts them into penalty points, and generates a summary table.

What the report shows

Each row is the data for one vehicle on the selected date and the assigned Driver.

The report shows:

  • Object — the vehicle for which violations were recorded

  • Group — name of the group the vehicle belongs to

  • Date — the day the indicators are calculated for

  • Driver — the Driver assigned to the vehicle at the time of the violation

  • Distance — the section of the route (in km) on which Eco Driving Events were recorded

  • Duration — total time of violations

Types of violations

For each Event type (acceleration, braking, cornering, speed, seat belt), the following is shown:

  • number of violations / penalty points

  • Total penalty — total number of points for all violations

  • Penalty / 100 km — average number of penalty points per 100 km of Mileage

The lower the value, the calmer and safer the driving style.

At the bottom of the report there is a “Total” row — these are the summary indicators for all rows of the table.

When generating the report, you can choose which data to use for the analysis:

  • By Objects — to see which vehicles have more violations

  • By groups — to compare indicators between vehicle groups

  • By Drivers — to identify the most careful Drivers and those who break the rules most often

If you do not select Objects, the report is built for all vehicles driven by the selected Drivers

If you do not select Drivers, the report includes all Drivers, as well as periods when no Driver was assigned to the vehicle

When generating the report, you can also take into account the eco weights settings . These settings let you define which violations are considered more serious and which are less significant.

The penalty points and the overall score of Drivers and vehicles depend directly on the selected weights.

The weights settings icon in the report is shown:
— only to Users with administrator rights
— only if the Eco Driving Module is enabled in the Contract

  • Penalty — number of penalty points assigned for the Event

  • Place — address where the violation occurred — a link that lets you open the point on the Map

When you select a specific violation, its type and the place on the Map where it occurred are shown.

Reports in this section can be presented as tables and charts.

Two-State Sensors Report

A two-state sensor is a type of sensor that can be in one of two states: active or passive. Such sensors are commonly used to monitor liquid level, pressure, temperature and other parameters. They can be mechanical, optical, magnetic, capacitive or inductive.

The report contains:

raskhod-topliva-po-can:
The “Fuel Consumption by CAN” report shows fuel consumption based on CAN data for the selected period. Use it to compare the amount of fuel consumed with the Object's mileage and to calculate the average consumption per 100 km.

Sensor configuration requirements

For data to appear in the report, a CAN fuel consumption sensor must be configured on the Object.

In the sensor settings, specify:

• Purpose — Fuel consumption

• Type — Discrete integral

• Save history — the checkbox must be enabled

The sensor must transmit the cumulative fuel consumption value. To calculate the report, the system takes the initial and final values for the day and calculates consumption as the difference between them.

If the sensor is configured with a different purpose or type, or if history saving is disabled, the data may not appear in the report.

What the report shows

• Object — the name of the monitored object for which the report was generated

• Date — the date for which the data is shown

• Consumption — the amount of fuel consumed on the specified date

• Distance — the Object's mileage on the specified date

• Fuel consumption — the average fuel consumption per 100 km

Fuel consumption is calculated using the formula: (Consumption × 100 km) / Distance

sostavnye-obekty-1:
This section contains reports related to the “Composite Objects” module. They help you control fuel movement and see receipts, consumption and balances across the entire fuel scheme that combines several tanks and sensors.

With these reports you can:

— track the fuel balance by day

— analyze consumption and identify discrepancies between level and flow meter readings

— control balances and fuel deliveries across the entire scheme

sensors.

For the reports to be generated correctly, the related elements and sensors must be configured on the composite object: the main tank, input or output flow meters, additional tanks and the links between them. The set of required sensors depends on the scheme of the particular composite object.

Diesel Logbook

The “Diesel Logbook” report shows the fuel balance of the selected composite object for the period. The report displays the opening balance, receipts, consumption, dispensing via outputs, discrepancy and closing balance.

The report is built for one composite object only. For the calculation to be correct, tanks, flow meters and the links between the elements of the composite object must be configured on the Object.

Fuel Movement

The “Fuel Movement” report shows fuel movement across a composite object for the selected period. It can be displayed as a table or a chart.

In table view, the report shows the fuel balance: opening balance, receipts, consumption, output readings and discrepancy. In chart view, you can view the sensor reading series and fuel level change events.

To build the report, select a composite object and the required sensors. If necessary, you can use a breakdown by days and grouping by dates or Objects.
sostavnye-obekty-2:
The “Composite Objects” report shows the daily fuel balance across the entire fuel scheme configured in the “Composite Objects” module. It helps you see how much fuel there was at the start of the day, how much was received, how much was consumed and how much remained overall for the composite object.

What the report shows

Each row of the table corresponds to one day of the scheme's operation and contains:

  • Date — the day for which fuel movement was calculated

  • Fuel at start — the estimated balance at the start of the day

  • Delivery — the volume of fuel received by the composite object during the day

  • Fuel consumption — the actual consumption based on the fuel level in the tanks

  • Consumption by flow meters — the total consumption recorded by the dispensing flow meters

  • Consumption difference — the difference between the consumption by level and the consumption by flow meters

  • Fuel at end — the estimated balance at the end of the day

At the bottom of the report there is a total row for the selected period with the total values of delivery, consumption and balances.

The report is built for one composite object only. For the calculation to be correct, tanks, flow meters and the links between the elements of the composite object must be configured on the Object.

• Consumption — the volume of fuel consumed during the period

• Dispensed via outputs — the volume of fuel dispensed through output elements or flow meters

• Discrepancy — the difference between calculated and actual values

• Closing balance — the fuel balance at the end of the selected period

A screenshot of the report will be added in the next version of the documentation.
