The “Fuel Movement” report shows fuel movement across a composite object for the selected period. Use it to analyze receipts, consumption, fuel balances, output readings and fuel level changes based on sensor data.

The report can be displayed as a table or a chart. To build the report, select a composite object and the required sensors. If necessary, you can use a breakdown by days and grouping by dates or Objects.

What the report shows

• Start — the fuel balance at the start of the selected period

• Receipts — the volume of fuel received by the composite object

• Consumption — the volume of fuel consumed during the period

• By outputs — the volume of fuel dispensed through output elements or flow meters

• Discrepancy — the difference between calculated and actual values

• End — the fuel balance at the end of the selected period

• Sensor readings — the values of the selected fuel sensors in chart mode

• Fuel level change events — events related to changes in the fuel level

A screenshot of the report will be added in the next version of the documentation.
situatsionnyj-tsentr-1:
Reports of the “Situation Center” module help you view the events that occurred in the system during the selected period. They let you understand what happened to Objects, when it happened and whether the event was processed.

The reports show who processed an event, when it was done and what comments the operator added.
sobytiya:
The “Events” report shows all events recorded by the system during the selected period. It helps you understand what happened, when, and how operators handled these events.

The main part of the report is a table. It displays the following fields:

  • Group — the group of Objects the Object belongs to.

  • Object — the monitored object that generated the event

  • Time — the date and time the event occurred

  • Type — the event description (for example, speeding, Alarm → Lane deviation, etc.).

  • Group (on the right) — the event category (for example, Alarms).

  • Status — the event processing state: unprocessed or processed

  • Operator — the system user who processed the event

  • Processing time — the date and time when the operator finished processing the event

  • Comments — additional notes the operator added during processing
geozony-1: This section covers reports related to the Geofences module.
oborudovanie-po-geozonam:
This report displays data on hardware operation within a zone.

The report contains:

  • Hardware - the sensor name;

  • Start - the time and date the sensor started operating;

  • End - the time and date the sensor stopped operating;

  • Duration - the operating time;

  • Distance - the monitored object's mileage in km on the specified date;

  • Start location - where operation in the zone started;

  • Stop location - where operation in the zone ended;

  • Driver - the driver's name in the system.
otchety-po-sobytiyam:
This report displays actions of an Object over a specific period of time.

The report contains:

  • Event - the sensor event type;

  • Event start - the time and date the sensor started operating;

  • Event end - the time and date the sensor stopped operating;

  • Duration - the operating time;

  • Distance - the monitored object's mileage in km on the specified date;

  • Address of event start - the event address;

  • Address of event end - the event address at the end;
otchyet-po-prostoyam-v-geozone:
Geofence Idling Report

The geofence idling report is used to monitor idling of monitored objects in geographic zones. It is available when the additional Geofences module is enabled.

The report contains:

  • Date - the time period for which the idling table is generated for the specified Object.

  • Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated.

  • Geofence - the geographic zone in which idling was recorded.

  • Start - the date and time idling recording started.

  • End - the date and time idling recording ended.

  • Time in geofence - the time the monitored object spent in the specified geofence.

  • Idling setting - the permitted idling time in the geofence (set in the Object settings on the “Geofences” tab, in the idling control field).

  • Idling - the idling time of the monitored object in the geographic zone. Equal to the difference between the start and end of idling minus the permitted idling time.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
poezdki-v-geozone:
The trips report is used for monitoring in geographic zones. The report contains data on the trip start and end date, duration, mileage, the zone recorded at the start and at the end, as well as coordinates.

The report contains:

  • Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated.

  • Zone - the geographic zone in which idling was recorded.

  • Start - the date and time the trip started.

  • End - the date and time the trip ended.

  • Duration - the trip duration during the reporting period;

  • Mileage - the distance in km over the specified period of time.

  • Start location - where the trip started in the zone;

  • Stop location - where the trip ended in the zone;

  • Coordinates - coordinates are used to determine a location by latitude and longitude.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchyet-po-geozonam:
Geofences Report

The geographic zones report (1) displays data as a table showing the Object name, mileage, time, the message about arrival in or departure from a particular zone, and the duration of stay in the zone at a given moment in time.

The report contains:

  • Vehicle - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated.

  • Mileage - the distance traveled at the given moment in time.

  • Start - the start time of the event in the geofence.

  • Stop- the end time of the event in the geofence.

  • Geofence - the geofence name.

  • Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence.

  • Driver - the name of the driver linked to the Object in the system.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchyet-po-geozonam-2:
Geofences Report No. 2

The geographic zones report 2 displays data as a table showing the Object name, time, the message about arrival (entry) in and departure (exit) from a particular zone, and the duration of stay in the specified zone, with the option of setting a time filter (set in the Object settings on the “Geofences” tab, in the idling control field).

The report contains:

  • Object - the monitored object for which the idling table is generated.

  • Date - the time period for which the idling table is generated for the specified Object.

  • Zone- the geographic zone in which idling was recorded.

  • Start - the date and time the monitored object entered the geographic zone.

  • End - the date and time the monitored object exited the geographic zone.

  • Duration - the time the monitored object spent in the geographic zone, equal to the difference between the entry and exit times.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchet-po-geozonam-3:
Geofences Report No. 3

Geofences report #3 is used to account for the Object's starting and ending geofences, with additional parameters on mileage and time.

The report contains:

  • Date - the date of the event.

  • Vehicle type - the type of vehicle.

  • License plate - the monitored object;

  • Start time - the trip start time;

  • Start zone - the starting geofence;

  • Trip duration - the duration of the trip.

  • Trip distance - the distance traveled during the selected period of time.

  • Arrival time - the time of arrival in the zone;

  • End zone - the ending geofence.

  • Departure time - the time of departure from the zone;

  • Duration in zone - the length of time spent in the zone**;**

  • Drum sensor work - sensor operation**;**

  • Drum sensor duration - the sensor operating duration**;**

  • Drivers - the driver assigned to this monitored object.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchet-po-geozonam-4:
Geofences Report No. 4

Geofences report #4 is used to account for time spent in a geofence.

It is available when the additional Geofences module is enabled.

The report contains:

  • Object - the monitored object;

  • Zone - the zone the Object arrived in;

  • Entry - the time of entering the geofence;

  • Exit - the time of exiting the geofence;

  • Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence.

  • Mileage (km) - the distance traveled.

  • Total - the total values for duration and mileage.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchet-po-geozonam-6:
A brief report on a trip through geofences showing the zone name, start, end and mileage for the specified period.

The report contains:

  • License plate - the monitored object;

  • Zone - the zone the Object arrived in;

  • Start - the date and time movement started;

  • Stop - the date and time movement ended;

  • Mileage (km) - the distance traveled.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
svodnyj-otchet-po-geozonam:
Geofences Summary Report

This report is used to account for geofence visits by Objects.

The report contains:

  • Vehicle - the monitored object;

  • Geofence - the geofence in which visits were recorded;

  • First entry - the Object's first entry into the geofence;

  • Last exit - the Object's last exit from the geofence;

  • Number of visits - the number of visits during the specified period of time;

  • Total duration - the total length of time spent in the geofence.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
svodnyj-otchet-po-geozonam-2:
This report is used to account for geofence visits by Objects, with trip details.

The report contains:

  • Object - the vehicle of the monitored object;

  • Zone - the geofence in which visits were recorded;

  • Start - the Object's first entry into the geofence;

  • End - the Object's last exit from the geofence;

  • Duration - the length of time spent in the geofence.

  • Start location - the zone at the start;

  • Stop location - the zone at the end;

  • Coordinates - coordinates are used to determine a location by latitude and longitude.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
prostoi-vne-gezony:
This report displays data on Objects that are outside geofences during the specified period.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — the vehicle or monitored object

  • Driver — the driver assigned to the vehicle at the time of idling

  • Department — the group the Object belongs to

  • Object type — the type of vehicle (passenger car, truck, trailer, etc.)

  • Start — the date and time idling started

  • Stop — the date and time idling ended

  • Duration — how long the idling lasted (hh:mm:ss)

  • Address — the address of the idling location (according to the geocoder). The value is shown as a hyperlink: clicking it opens a map with the idling point

  • Coordinates — the exact latitude and longitude of the point
probeg-v-geozonakh:
The report shows how many kilometers a vehicle drove inside each selected geofence during the specified period, and how long it spent there, both in motion and parked.

When building the report, select one or more geofences. The system calculates the mileage, driving time and parking time inside the selected zones for the specified period.

You can also use checkboxes to refine the calculation.

 

Movement in geozones

This checkbox turns on accounting for movement inside geofences.
If the checkbox is selected:
— the report counts and displays only the mileage recorded inside the selected geofences
— data outside these zones is not counted

Outside geofences

This checkbox controls the display of mileage outside the selected geofences.
If the checkbox is selected:
— the system additionally calculates the mileage and time when the Object was outside the selected zones
— separate rows with the distance and time outside the zones appear in the report

What the report shows

Each row is one vehicle in one geofence for the selected period.

The report shows the following data:

  • Date — the period for which the indicators are calculated

  • Object — the vehicle for which the report is built

  • Zone — the name of the geofence inside which movement was recorded

  • Mileage (km) — how many kilometers the vehicle drove inside this zone

  • Time — the total time spent in the zone

  • Time in motion — how long the vehicle was moving inside the geofence

  • Parking duration — how long the vehicle stood in the zone without moving

At the bottom of the report there is a “Total” row that sums up:

— the total mileage across all selected geofences

— the total time spent

— the total time in motion

— the total parking duration
probeg-vne-geozon:
The report displays data on an Object's mileage outside geofences.

If an Object did not leave the geofences and has no mileage outside geofences, such mileage values are cut off and are not displayed in the report.

The report contains:

  • Object - the monitored object;

  • Duration - the duration of the mileage;

  • Mileage - the mileage in km for the reporting period.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
peresecheniya-v-geozonakh:
Intersections in Geofences

This report displays information on Objects intersecting in geofences.

The report contains:

  • Geofence - the geofence name;

  • Quantity - the number of Objects that intersected in the geofence;

  • List of vehicles - the list of Objects that intersected in the geofence;

  • Start - the start time of the intersection in the geofence;

  • Stop - the end time of the intersection in the geofence.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
parkovki-v-geozonakh:
The report contains data on parking in geofences.

The report contains:

  • Object - the vehicle of the monitored object;

  • Zone - the zone where parking was recorded;

  • Start - the time and date parking started;

  • Stop - the time and date parking ended;

  • Duration - the parking duration;

  • Address - the idling address;

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
poezdki-s-geozonami:
This report displays information on trips between geofences.

The report contains:

  • Direction - the direction of travel between geofences.

  • Number of loads (number of trips) - the number of trips between zones.

  • Trip duration - the duration of a trip from one zone to another.
otchyet-o-peremeshchenii-mezhdu-zonami:
The report shows vehicle movements between the selected geofences during the specified period. Use it to find out which zone a vehicle left and which zone it arrived in, how long the movement took, what distance was covered and how many stops occurred along the way.

Before building the report, you need to select:

— the period

— one or more vehicles

— the geofences whose movements you want to include in the report

If the data is split by day, a separate block is generated for each day. The “Total” row shows the totals for the corresponding period.

What the report shows

  • Vehicle — the name or number of the monitored object

  • Driver — the driver assigned to the vehicle

  • Start time — the date and time the movement between zones started

  • End time — the date and time the movement between zones ended

  • Zone start — the geofence from which the vehicle started moving

  • Zone end — the geofence in which the vehicle finished moving

  • Number of stops — the number of stops recorded during the movement

  • Travel time — the total duration of movement between zones

  • Idling time — the total duration of idling

  • Stop time — the total duration of stops

  • Distance — the distance traveled by the vehicle between zones

  • Time in zone — how long the vehicle stayed in the geofence

Preparing geofences

For the report to be generated correctly, create the necessary geofences in the “Geofences” module, then link them to the vehicle in the Object settings and set the type to “Working”.

A working geofence is a territory where the vehicle is supposed to be or to perform tasks, for example a warehouse, a construction site, a production site or a section of a route.
otchet-o-spiske-zon:
A list of the account's geofences with addresses.

The report contains:

  • Zone name - the zone name in the system;

  • Zone shape - the shape of the zone;

  • Zone address - the geographic location of the zone;

  • Zone group - the name of the zone group.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
svodnyj-otchyet-po-platnym-dorogam:
This report works provided that toll roads are configured in the Geofences module.

The report contains:

  • Toll Road Name - the name of the toll road.

  • Entrance Time - the entry time.

  • Entrance Location - the entry location.

  • Exit Time - the exit date and time.

  • Exit Location - the exit location.

  • Price - the price per kilometer. The cost may vary depending on several factors, including the vehicle type, time of day, day of the week and the specific toll road.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
logistika-1: This section contains reports for the Logistics module.
dostavka-plan-i-fakt:
This report compares planned delivery parameters with actual results, letting you identify deviations and improve processes

.

The report contains:

  • Number - the order number from the Logistics module;

  • Customer - the customer name;

  • Receipt number- the receipt number from the list in the Logistics module;

  • Status - the request status;

  • Group - the customer group;

  • Start address - the starting address of dispatch;

  • End address - the end address.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
otchet-po-uvedomleniyam:
This report informs you of any changes to a monitored object, according to the settings in the Notifications module.

The Notifications module provides conditions such as speed notification, ignition event, sensor malfunction and others.

The report contains:

  • Object - the monitored vehicle;

  • Driver - the driver assigned to the vehicle;

  • Time - the date and time the notification was received;

  • Notification type - the notification name;

  • Notification name - the name of the notification;

  • Message- the notification message;

  • Latitude - the geographic coordinate that defines the position of a point on the map.

  • Longitude - the geographic coordinate that indicates the position of a point on the map.

  • Location - the location of the notification;

  • Speed - the recorded speed**.**

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
podrobnyj-otchet-ob-uvedomleniyakh:
The detailed report contains data on drivers, type, date, time and speed at the moment the notification was triggered.

The report contains:

  • Driver - the driver assigned to the vehicle;

  • Object - the monitored vehicle;

  • Notification name - the name of the notification;

  • Notification type - the notification name;

  • Message- the notification message;

  • Date - the date of the event;

  • Start time - the date and time of the notification status;

  • End time - the date and time of the notification status;

  • Number of occurrences - the number of notifications;

  • Event value - the value;

  • Speed control - the speed value for the notification;

  • Max speed - the maximum speed recorded in the notification;

  • Duration - the duration.

If necessary, you can hide certain parts of the report by clicking the icon . A menu opens in which you can turn individual fields on or off.
ptm: Reports related to the PILOT Task Manager module.
summarnyj-probeg-po-zayavkam:
The summary report displays data on total mileage by requests.

Driver requests are located in the PTM module.

The report contains:

  • Date - the date and time the request was created;

  • Vehicle - the monitored object;

  • Folder - the location of the Object in the system;

  • Distance - the distance value for requests and outside requests.
kontrol-marshrutov:
Route Control

This section covers reports related to the Routes module.
avtobusnye-marshruty:
Bus Routes

This report displays information on visits to specified stops (geofences).

The report contains:

  • Between geofences - trips between zones;

  • First departure - the time of departure onto the route;

  • Last arrival - the time of arrival from the route;

  • Quantity - the number of visits.
svodka-po-avtobusnym-marshrutam:
This report displays general information on visits to specified stops.

The report contains:

  • Between geofences - trips between zones;

  • First departure - the time of departure onto the route;

  • Last arrival - the time of arrival from the route;

  • Quantity - the number of visits.
marshruty-1: This section covers reports related to the Routes module.
vypolnenie-rabot-po-soderzhaniyu-dorog:
This report belongs to the Routes module.

After linking an Object to a route, build the Road Maintenance Work Completion report.

A recalculation is available for this report.

If a route is configured and linked to an Object and the report then turns out to be empty, you will need to recalculate it.

If recalculation through the interface does not recalculate the data and resets the recalculation, contact support to have it recalculated.

The report contains:

  • License plate (garage number) - the Object in the system**;**

  • Vehicle type - the vehicle type in the system;

  • Start time - the date and time work started;

  • End time- the date and time work ended;

  • Route name - the route name;

  • Route length - the route length;

  • Mileage (Work cycle), km - the work cycle is a parameter showing how long, in km, the machine can work without a break.

  • Area (Work cycle) ㎡ - the total area treated during one work cycle of the machine.

  • Mileage (Idle cycle) km - the distance in km that the vehicle drives without a load.

  • Mileage on other roads, km - the mileage on other roads.
spetsialnaya-tekhnika-marshruty:
This report belongs to the Routes module. It displays data on the operation of special equipment.

The report contains:

  • Vehicle - the Object in the system;

  • Route- the route set for the equipment;

  • Start - the date and time work started;

  • Start address - the address where the equipment started work;

  • End - the date and time work ended;

  • End address - the address where the equipment ended work;

  • Actual duration - the duration value;

  • Reference duration - a standard or normative time value used as a benchmark for comparison and calibration**.**

  • Route length - the length of the route traveled;

  • Distance outside the route - the distance traveled outside the route;

  • Number of violations - the number of violations on the route.

For a report built for an Object with a map, when you click a row in the report, the track is highlighted in color.
marshruty-gps-route-gps:
The Route GPS report helps you monitor the execution of scheduled trips: visits to checkpoints, driving time, trip duration, distance traveled and unplanned stops.

The report includes only those routes on which the Object made a trip during the selected period. If there were no trips on a route, the route is not displayed.

The report is designed for circular routes consisting of three checkpoints:

1. the starting point — the company premises

2. the intermediate point — the customer's location

3. the end point — the same company premises

What the report shows

  • Vehicle No (vehicle number) — the Object number

  • Customer Name (customer name) — the name of the second-to-last checkpoint of the route

  • Actual Start Time (actual start time) — the date and time the trip along the route started

  • Time arrived at customer location (time of arrival at the customer) — the date and time the Object arrived at the second checkpoint of the route

  • End Time (end time) — the date and time the trip finished, when the Object returned to the final checkpoint. For a circular route, the end point is the same as the starting point

  • Actual Route (actual route) — the route along which the trip was made

  • Trip Status (trip status) — the result of the route execution. The status shows whether the driver visited all the planned checkpoints:

  • Finished (completed) — all checkpoints were visited

  • Unfinished (not completed) — one or more checkpoints were not visited or the trip is not yet finished

  • Time In Transit (travel time) — the Object's driving time during the trip

  • Trip Duration (trip duration) — the time from the start to the end of the trip

  • Distance Travelled (distance traveled) — the distance the Object covered during the trip

  • Number of Stops Outside Planned Geofence (number of stops outside planned geofences) — the number of stops made outside the route checkpoints

  • Number of planned stoppage (number of planned stops) — the number of checkpoints provided for by the route

Viewing the route on the map

To study the Object's movement in more detail, expand the “Map” panel and click the required report row. The map shows data for the selected day:

  • the Object's trips — as lines with arrows showing the direction of travel

  • parking — as P markers

  • the planned route — as a dashed line

  • route checkpoints — as numbered markers

If there were several trips during the day, their lines may overlap.

A collapsible “Trips” panel appears on the left side of the map. For each trip it lists the start time, date and distance traveled. Click the required trip to keep only its route on the map.

Click a checkpoint marker to see

  • the point name

  • the coordinates

  • the address

Accounting for parking

The map shows all parking events related to the selected day. The last parking event is also counted if it started on the selected day and ended on the next one.

For example, if the Object stopped at 17:00 and resumed moving at 09:00 the next day, the time of this parking event is included in Trip Duration (trip duration). Therefore, the duration value can sometimes exceed 24 hours.
to: This section contains reports for the Service module.
otchyet-o-dostupnosti:
The “Availability Report” shows the availability of vehicles during the selected period, taking registered breakdowns into account. Use it to determine the fleet size, the number of unavailable vehicles, the total downtime and the availability percentage.

To build the report, you need to configure the “Service” module. If breakdowns and downtime periods were registered for vehicles, the fleet availability percentage decreases.

What the report shows

  • Object or user group — the name of the Object or group for which the indicators are calculated

  • Fleet size report — the total number of vehicles in the group

  • Vehicles Down — the number of vehicles that were unavailable during the selected period

  • Total number of downtime days — the total duration of vehicle unavailability

  • % availability based on breakdowns — the share of time during which vehicles were available for operation, taking registered breakdowns into account
sostoyanie-parka:
The Fleet Status report displays general information about an Object.

The report contains:

  • Make - the make of the Object in the system;

  • Model- the model of the Object in the system**;**

  • Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;**

  • Mileage- the total mileage of the Object;

  • Driver name - the driver's name in the system;

  • Driver change history - the history of drivers during operation;

  • Next maintenance - data on maintenance completion;

  • Comment- additional information.
otchyet-ob-inspektsiyakh:
The inspections report helps you monitor all completed service operations for each vehicle during the selected period.

It is convenient for tracking both completed work and scheduled services.

When building this report, you can choose which services are displayed:

  • All — all service events: completed and scheduled

  • Completed — the report displays only work that has already been done

  • Scheduled — services that have been assigned but not yet performed

The report shows:

  • Which vehicle

  • The service name, for example: oil change, brake check, cleaning

  • When the service was performed

  • Difference in days — how much time has passed since the service

  • The mileage or distance at the time of the service

  • Status — done, completed or pending

  • Condition — one-time or recurring service

  • Next service

  • Costs — separately for parts and labor

  • Comments — additional notes
plan-to:
A maintenance plan is a technical maintenance plan that defines the frequency and scope of inspection, adjustment, lubrication, replacement and repair work on equipment and vehicles.

A maintenance plan is necessary to ensure reliable and safe operation of Objects, extend their service life and improve performance, and reduce repair and operating costs.

A maintenance plan is drawn up on the basis of technical documentation, norms, standards and recommendations

from manufacturers.

The report contains:

  • Make - the make of the Object in the system;

  • Model- the model of the Object in the system**;**

  • Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;**

  • Mileage- the total mileage of the Object;

  • Driver name - the driver's name in the system;

  • Average monthly mileage - mileage data for the reporting period;

  • Interval between maintenance, km - the set interval after which scheduled maintenance of the vehicle must be performed**;**

  • Date of last maintenance - the maintenance date;

  • Last maintenance No. - the maintenance number;

  • Date of next maintenance - the date of the next maintenance.
zatraty-na-ehkspluatatsiyu:
Operating costs are the total expenses associated with keeping equipment and vehicles operational and reliable.

Technical characteristics, operating mode, operating conditions and other factors should be taken into account.

The report contains:

  • Make - the make of the Object in the system;

  • Model- the model of the Object in the system**;**

  • Year of manufacture- the year of manufacture of the Object in the system**;**

  • Driver name - the driver's name in the system;

  • Mileage- the total mileage of the Object in km;

  • Current mileage- the vehicle's mileage for the reporting period;

  • Maintenance and repair - data on maintenance and work performed;

  • Fuel costs - fuel expenses;

otchet-o-napominaniyakh:

temperatura:
This section contains reports for analyzing readings from temperature and humidity sensors installed on vehicles and other monitored objects. They help you track changes in readings, detect when the temperature goes outside the permitted limits and compare sensor data with the Object's location.

With these reports you can:

— view temperature and humidity readings for the selected period

— analyze changes in readings as tables and charts

— check that the temperature stays within the permitted range

— configure the data display interval

— compare readings from several sensors

The set of indicators and available parameters depends on the selected report, the installed sensors and the Object settings.
otchyet-po-temperature-diskretnyj:
The “Discrete Temperature Report” contains readings from the temperature and humidity sensors of monitored objects at a set time interval.

Before building the report, select the reporting period and Objects, then enter a value in the Min. time (sec) field.

The Min. time (sec) field defines the interval between the temperature readings shown in the report. The value is specified in seconds.

For example:

  • 900 — temperature readings are shown at 15-minute intervals

  • 1800 — temperature readings are shown at 30-minute intervals

What the report shows

  • Date — the date and time the reading was recorded

  • Temperature or humidity sensor — the value recorded by the sensor
otchyet-po-temperature:
The “Temperature Report” shows how temperature sensor readings changed over the selected period. A separate chart is built for each day and each monitored object.

The horizontal axis shows time, and the vertical axes show temperature and humidity. Sensor readings are shown as lines of different colors, and the horizontal gray lines show the boundaries of the permitted temperature range.

When you hover over the chart, a pop-up window appears with the date, time and sensor readings at the selected moment.

If you open the map panel and select a point on the chart, the map shows the Object's location at that moment. This way you can trace the relationship between temperature changes and the route.

How to configure a temperature sensor

Configuring a temperature sensor helps you get accurate data on the condition of equipment or vehicles. Correct sensor configuration and specifying operating ranges helps automatically filter out invalid values so that you see only reliable information.

A temperature sensor is added in the same way as any other sensor. For more information on adding sensors, see this article.

Here we go through the parameters you need to specify for a temperature sensor so that reports are built correctly.

To configure a temperature sensor:

1. Add a sensor

2. Specify the name and description

3. In the drop-down list, select the sensor type

4. Specify the data field. Select which parameter to take the data from (for example, engine_temp). It is important to select exactly the field in which the system receives temperature values.

5. Set the minimum and maximum threshold

Configure the sensor's operating range — the permitted value limits within which the sensor operates normally. If the readings go outside this range, the system records a deviation.

On the chart, this range is highlighted with gray lines, so you can immediately see when the temperature was within the norm.

6. Configure the minimum and maximum value filter

Set the minimum and maximum values so that the system ignores erroneous data (for example, if the sensor returned an error or an invalid value). Such values are automatically excluded from reports.
otchyet-po-temperature-2:
The “Temperature Report No. 2” contains temperature sensor readings for the selected period. Use it to track temperature changes, check that the temperature stays within the permitted range, and determine the Object's location and speed at the moment the reading was recorded.

What the report shows

  • Object — the name of the monitored object for which the report was generated

  • Date — the date and time the temperature reading was recorded

  • Event — the event associated with the recorded reading

  • Temperature — the temperature value according to the sensor data

  • Temperature Name — the name of the temperature sensor

  • Temperature Status — the status of the recorded temperature value

  • Temperature High — the upper limit of the permitted temperature range

  • Temperature Low — the lower limit of the permitted temperature range

  • Location — the Object's coordinates at the moment the reading was recorded

  • Speed — the Object's driving speed at the moment the reading was recorded

  • Location — the Object's address at the moment the reading was recorded
otchyet-po-temperature-3:

otchyet-po-temperaturnomu-intervalu:

The report on speed violations in geofences and on roads helps you monitor where and when vehicles exceeded the speed limit, both on ordinary roads and inside geofences (for example, on the territory of a warehouse, a construction site or in a particular district).

This report combines data from two modules: “Violations Control” and “Geofences”. As a result, you see all cases of speeding both on ordinary roads and inside the specified geofences in one common report.

When building the report, select the required Object and geofence to see all cases of speeding.

How to set a speed threshold for a geofence

You can set a separate speed threshold for each geofence:

  • Open the card of the required Object

  • Go to the “Geofences” tab

3. Set the geofence speed threshold for this Object:

  2. Use the arrows to set the speed limit for this zone

If a vehicle is in a geofence, the limit set for that zone is applied.

If the threshold is not set, speeding will not be recorded, and the report may be empty.

Once you have set the speed threshold, the system tracks all trips on its own and flags cases of speeding.

The report shows:

otchyet-ob-avariyakh:
The report is available if the “Accident Detection” module is enabled. It helps you analyze in detail what happened to a vehicle: when and where the incident occurred, how fast the vehicle was moving, from which direction the impact came, and which trips took place during this period.

The top part of the report contains the main information about the event:

  • Report period — the dates for which the report was generated

  • License plate (garage number) — the vehicle identifier

  • Crash (Event type) — the event description, in this case an accident

  • Time — the exact time of the incident

  • Device type — the name of the device that sent the data

  • Coordinates — the point on the map where the event occurred (you can open the location on the map).

Acceleration graph (Accelerometer Graph)

The central part of the report contains a graph showing which forces acted on the vehicle at the moment of the accident:

  • X axis (blue line) — forward/backward motion (acceleration, braking, head-on impact)

  • Y axis (purple line) — right/left motion (turning, side impact)

  • Z axis (green line) — up/down motion (a bump, hitting an obstacle)

  • Red line — the vehicle's speed

Sharp spikes or drops on the graph indicate the moment of the collision.

Vehicle diagram

Next to it is a vehicle model with a red arrow that indicates the direction of the impact during the accident.

Trips and parking

At the bottom of the report is a list of the vehicle's trips and parking for the selected period.

The table shows:

  • Status — moving or parked

  • Start / End — the start and end time of the trip or parking

  • Maximum speed — the highest speed during the trip

  • Duration — how long the trip or parking lasted

  • Distance (km) — the total mileage of this trip

  • Start / Stop — the address where the trip started and ended

  • Coordinates — the exact GPS coordinates

    After an accident, the device may send “Crash” tags many times. In the report, if more than a minute has passed between such signals, it is considered a new accident event. Therefore, there may be several records for one vehicle in the report.

    If you click a row with a specific accident, the system tries to load the vehicle's track for that time and show it on the map (the panel at the top). If there is no track data, the map simply does not change.

The report builder is a tool that lets you create your own reports in the monitoring system to suit your tasks.

It helps you configure which data to show, how to display it, and which blocks the report consists of.

You configure the report form once, save it, and then reuse it whenever you need the information in a convenient format.

kak-rabotat-s-konstruktorom:
The report builder lets you create your own report form with the columns, filters and calculation logic you need.

In this article you will learn:

  • How to create a report — step-by-step configuration of the report form

  • How to run a report — running a report from the builder

  • Report grouping — how to combine data by groups

  • Interface overview — what the builder consists of

  • Report configuration — how to configure a report further

  • Import and export — how to transfer reports between accounts

How to create a report

1. Go to the “Reports” section

2. Find the “Builder” button

3. Click it — the builder window opens

In the builder:

4. Click “Add”

5. Select the report type

6. In the “Name” field, enter the report name

7. In the “Columns” block, click “+” and add the required fields

8. Specify the data, formulas, filters and other column parameters

9. If necessary, fill in the “Configuration” field

10. Click “Save”

After saving, the report becomes available in the “Reports” section.

Report example

For example, you can create an Idle – Summary Table report.

Report type: “Summary table”

Added columns:

  • Vehicle — the Object for which the report is built

  • Idle time — the idling duration

  • Total number of idles — the number of events

  • Fuel at start — the fuel balance at the start

  • Fuel at end — the fuel balance at the end

In the “Configuration” field you can set a filter so that only the data you need appears in the report.

For example, only Objects with idling:

{"filter":[{"key":"total_idle_events_number","rule":">","value":0}]}

After the report is created and saved in the builder, it becomes available in the “Reports” section.

How to run a report

1. Go to the “Reports” section

2. Select an Object (select its checkbox in the list)

3. Select the required report created in the builder

4. Specify the period and additional parameters

5. Click “Build report”

The system generates the report according to the specified form.

You can do the following with the finished report:

— view and analyze it

— export it to CSV, Excel, PDF —

— print it

Report grouping

The data of a report created in the builder can be combined into separate blocks using grouping. Depending on the report type, the following options are available:

  • by drivers

  • by dates

  • by Objects

  • by Object groups

To configure grouping:

1. Go to the “Reports” section

2. Select a report created in the builder

3. In the “Grouping” field, select the suitable option

4. Select Objects and, if necessary, other data for building the report

5. Click “Build report”

For example, with grouping by Object groups, a separate block with the data related to it is generated for each selected group.

Builder interface overview

On the left is the “Reports” panel with a list of reports that have already been created.

It contains the list of created reports and control buttons:

The control buttons are also located here:

— create a new report

— import or export a report

— refresh the list

On the right is the configuration area for the selected report:

  • Type — the report builder type

  • Name — the report name

  • Total — the main indicator for the summary

  • Sorting — the order in which data is displayed

  • Desc — descending sort

  • Columns — configuration of the report contents

  • Configuration — additional report configuration in JSON format. It lets you control how data is displayed in the report.

Report configuration

The “Configuration” field is intended for additional report settings. Parameters are specified in JSON format and define how data is processed and displayed.

Splitting data by hours

To split the data into hourly intervals, specify:

{"split": "hour"}

When the report is built, the data for each hour is displayed in a separate block.

Splitting data by shifts

Report data can be split by work shifts. For each shift, the system generates a separate interval and calculates indicators only from the data that belongs to it.

To configure the split, specify the start and end time of each shift in the split parameter, for example,

{
  "split": ["08-20", "20-08"]
}

In this example, two shifts are configured:

  • from 08:00 to 20:00

  • from 20:00 to 08:00 the next day

If the show parameter is not specified, the report displays all configured shifts.

Example of a report for all shifts

In the example, the “Loader Operation Timeline” report is split into day and night shifts. For each shift, a separate block is displayed with the Object, the start and end time of the interval and the equipment operation indicators.

The night shift is displayed as one continuous interval from 20:00 of the current day to 08:00 of the next day.

Since the selected report period starts at 00:00, the remaining part of the night shift — from 00:00 to 08:00 — is also displayed at the beginning of the report.

Displaying one shift

To include only one of the configured shifts in the report, add the show parameter:

{
  "split": ["08-20", "20-08"],
  "show": 1
}

The parameter value corresponds to the shift's sequence number in the list:

  • show: 1 — show the first shift, from 08:00 to 20:00

  • show: 2 — show the second shift, from 20:00 to 08:00

Example of a report for one shift

The example specifies the show: 1 parameter, so the report contains only day shifts from 08:00 to 20:00. A separate block is generated for each day. Night shifts are not displayed in the report.

Splitting a shift at midnight

By default, the shift from 20:00 to 08:00 is treated as one continuous interval. To split it at the calendar day boundary, add the split_days parameter:

{
  "split": ["08-20", "20-08"],
  "split_days": 1
}

The night shift will be split into two intervals:

  • from 20:00 to 00:00

  • from 00:00 to 08:00

The day shift remains one block from 08:00 to 20:00.

The show parameter is not specified because the report includes both the day and night shifts.

All parameters can be used at the same time:

{
  "split": ["08-20", "20-08"],
  "show": 1,
  "split_days": 1
}

In this example, the report displays only the first shift, and shifts that cross midnight are split by calendar day.

Filtering data

The configuration lets you define which data should appear in the report.

For example, for an Idle – Summary Table report you can add the following columns:

  • Vehicle

  • Idle time

  • Total number of idles

  • Fuel at start

  • Fuel at end

To include in the report only Objects for which at least one idle was registered, specify:

{"filter":[{"key":"total_idle_events_number","rule":">","value":0}]}

As a result, rows in which the value of the “Total number of idles” field is zero are not displayed.

Merging rows

To merge several rows within one split period into a summary row, specify:

{"merge": true}

The merged row shows the values of the configured columns, and the intermediate rows are hidden. Configure the columns that should be included in the report and save the changes.

Example of merging rows

In the example, the report is grouped by drivers and split by day. A separate block is created for each driver, and their data for each day is merged into one row. The row shows the vehicle, the date, the start time of the first trip and the end time of the last trip, the total driving and idling time, and the total mileage for the day.

Importing and exporting reports

Reports from the builder can be transferred between accounts. To do this, use the “Export” and “Import” buttons

How to export a report

1. Click “Export”

2. Select a location on your device

3. Save the file

How to import a report

1. Click “Import”

2. In the window that opens, if necessary, turn on the Remove existing reports option if you need to delete existing reports in the builder

3. Select the report file

4. Click “Import”

The report will be uploaded to the account.

When creating a report, you first select the report builder type.

It determines:

— which data will be used

— which fields will be available in the “Columns” section

— what the final report will look like

Available report types

The following types are available in the system:

  • Summary table — summary data: totals, sums, the number of events and other aggregated indicators

  • Work — the activity of an Object or sensors during the selected period

  • Eco events — events related to economical and uneconomical driving and fuel consumption

  • Chart — data visualization as charts

  • Trips table — a list of trips with parameters: time, mileage, start and end

  • Geofences table — geofence data: entries, exits, time spent

  • Current state — the state of the Object at the moment the report is generated

  • Sensor operation — sensor operation data for the period

  • Sensor events — triggers, state changes and threshold events

  • Connection loss — information on connection outages

  • Notifications — a list of system notifications

  • Cards — data on fuel cards and transactions

  • Driver behavior — events related to driving style

  • Fleet summary — general information on all Objects

  • RFID tags — RFID data

  • Refuel and fuel drain events — fuel operations

  • PTM — specialized reports for the PTM module

How report data is generated

1. You select the report type

2. The system loads the categories and fields available for it

3. In the “Columns” section, you select the data you need

4. The report displays only the selected columns

The set of available columns depends on the selected report type

The builder has:

  • universal (basic) fields — available in most report types

  • specialized categories — appear only for certain types

Example 1. The “Current state” type

Data on the current state of a vehicle is available for this type.

In addition to the basic data (for example, make, model, speed), a “Services” category appears, where you can add maintenance fields:

  • Last TO motohours — engine hours at the last maintenance

  • Next TO motohours — engine hours at the next maintenance

  • Mh until next TO — engine hours until the next maintenance

  • Last TO date — the date of the last maintenance

  • Last TO number — the number of the last maintenance

  • Next TO date — the date of the next maintenance

  • Last TO mileage — the mileage at the last maintenance

These fields help you monitor the current state and maintenance of a vehicle.

Example 2. The “Cards” type

Data on fuel cards and transactions is available for the “Cards” type.

A CardTransactions category appears in the columns, where you can select, for example:

  • Transaction Type — the operation type

  • Transaction Location — the location

  • Transaction Time — the time

  • Card number — the card number

  • Distance Previous-Current — the distance between values

  • Current — the current value

  • Transaction Amount — the amount

This type is used to analyze card operations.

Examples of report types

The builder offers several report types, each solving its own task. Below are a brief description and examples to make it easier to find your way.

Summary table

A summary table helps you get summary data on Objects for the selected period.

You configure:

  • which columns will be in the report

  • which indicator to use for the total

  • how to sort the data

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

  • Name — the report name

  • Sorting — the order of rows

  • Total — the main indicator for the summary

  • Desc — descending sort

  • Columns — which data to show

  • Configuration — additional settings

An example of a report built from the builder

The “Total” field sets the main indicator on which the report is built.

The “Sorting” field determines the order of rows.

For example, if you select sorting by Vehicle, the rows in the finished report will be sorted by vehicle.

With Desc enabled, the data is sorted in descending order.

Work

The “Work” report shows the activity of Objects or drivers during a period.

With this report you can see:

— when the event occurred

— on which Object

— where it was recorded

— the parameter values

The report can include the values of discrete, two-state and multi-state sensors. The required sensor is selected by the label assigned to it when configuring the column.

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

  • Name — the report name

  • Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered

  • Desc — descending sort

  • Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report

  • Configuration — additional parameters and filters

The example in the screenshot creates an Overspeed CAN general report — a speeding report based on CAN data. A filter is set in the “Configuration” field — the report will include only events where the sensor value is greater than 85.

{"filter": [ { "key": "sensor", "rule": ">", "value": 85 } ]}

Chart

A chart is a report type that builds a visual representation of data as graphs. It is designed to analyze how indicators change over time: speed, fuel consumption, temperature, mileage, equipment operation and other parameters.

You can add several data groups:

  • Speed — a graph of the Object's driving speed

  • ODO — a mileage graph

  • Fuel — fuel level and consumption

  • Temperature — the temperature of various sensors (you can select specific ones).

  • Special sensors — special sensors

  • Hardware — data from hardware

  • Eco Pies — eco events and violations (harsh braking, turns, collisions, unfastened seat belt, etc.).

For each group you can:

  • Turn its display on or off.

  • Select specific sensors or event types

  • Configure “Show axis” — whether to display a separate Y axis for this group

  • Configure “Single axle” — use one common Y axis

    For Eco Pie you can select additional settings:

  • Show per hour — show the number of events per hour

  • Show duration — show the duration of events

After the report is saved and built in the “Reports” section, the system displays an interactive chart:

  • The X axis shows time

  • The Y axis shows the values of the selected parameters (there may be several axes)

  • Each parameter is assigned its own line color

  • When you hover over the chart, a tooltip appears with the exact time and the values of all parameters at that point

  • A legend at the bottom of the chart shows which lines correspond to which parameters

  • You can zoom, pan and analyze individual time segments of the chart

Eco events

The “Eco events” type is used to build reports on events related to:

— economical or uneconomical driving style

— fuel consumption

— the environmental behavior of the vehicle

Such a report helps you analyze when and where eco events occurred and what type of event was recorded.

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

  • Name — the report name

  • Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered

  • Desc — descending sort

  • Summarize — the summary mode of the report

  • Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report

  • Configuration — additional parameters and filters

Trips table

A trips table is a report type used to view vehicle trips during the selected period.

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

  • Name — the report name

  • Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered

  • Desc — descending sort

  • Columns — the set of data that will be displayed in the report

  • Configuration — additional parameters and filters

After the report is built, the system displays a table with trips for the selected period.

Geofences table

A geofences table is a report type for analyzing geofence visits and equipment operation inside them. The report can display entries and exits, the length of stay in a zone, sensor operation periods and other related data.

When creating a report, configure the following parameters:

  • Name — enter the report name

  • Rows — select how rows are formed:

  • Geofence visits — one row corresponds to one geofence visit

  • Equipment work periods — one row corresponds to a separate operating period of the selected sensor inside a geofence

  • Sorting — select the field by which the data will be ordered

  • Descending (Desc) — turn on descending sort

  • Columns — configure the data that should be displayed in the report

  • Configuration — if necessary, specify additional parameters and filters

The set of available data and columns may depend on the selected row formation mode.

To build a report using a form from the builder:

1. Go to the “Reports” section

2. Select the report type

3. Specify the required Objects

4. Select the required geofences

5. Set the report period and click “Build report”

After that, the system generates a table for the selected geofences.

Current state table

A current state table is a report type that shows the current state of an Object at the moment the report is built.

The example shown displays service data, but depending on the selected report configuration, the set of data may be different.

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

The “Sensor groups” field lets you limit the report to the sensors you need.

Notifications is a report type used to view events created by the notification system.

Such a report helps you analyze, for example:

When creating a report of this type, you can set:

  • Sorting — the field by which the data will be ordered

  • Configuration — additional parameters and filters

Notification type

kak-nastroit-kolonki-otchyeta:
For a report to contain the data you need, you must add and configure columns in the builder. Each column determines what information will be displayed in the report and how it will be processed.

To add a column:

1. In the report builder, click the button in the “Columns” block

2. Fill in the parameters of the new column

Column parameters

1. Name

Enter the column name that will be displayed in the report header.

2. Data

Select from the drop-down list the data field that will be used in the column

3. Sensor groups

Select the sensor group whose values should be shown in the column. When the report is built, the system automatically displays the values of the sensors from the selected group.

Reports support output of the values of discrete, two-state and multi-state sensors.

4. Total Functions

This parameter determines how the system calculates the totals at the bottom of the table (in the summary row).

  Value
  What it does
  None
  The total for the column is not calculated
  Sum
  Adds up all values in the column
  Average
  Calculates the arithmetic mean (sum ÷ number of Objects)
  Max.
  Shows the maximum value in the column
  Min.
  Shows the minimum value in the column
  Formula
  Lets you set your own calculation formula

You can select several functions at once for one column.

Example of using totals in a mileage report:

  • CAN mileage — Sum, Max.

  • GPS mileage — Min.

  • CAN mileage at start — Sum

  • CAN mileage at end — Average

In the built report, total rows appear at the bottom of the table showing the values calculated according to the selected functions.

5. Units

Specify the unit of measurement of the data (km, L, km/h, °C, hours, etc.).

6. Formula

Lets you use mathematical expressions, for example, (%odometer_end% - %odometer_begin%) / 100

7. Filter

For any column with numeric values you can configure filtering of report rows. In the “Filter” field, specify one of the conditions:

  • > X— the value is greater than X

  • < X— the value is less than X

  • = X— the value is equal to X

For example, if you enter > 25 for the “Speed” column, the report will show only events recorded at a speed above 25 km/h.

8. Formatting function

Lets you set special formatting of the value (rounding, date conversion, unit conversion, etc.). It is used to bring data to the required form.

9. Hide

Select the checkbox if the column is needed only for calculations (for example, for a formula) but should not be shown in the final report.

How to delete a column

Click the column and click .

How to configure the columns table

Configure the columns table the way that suits you. Select which columns with parameters to display.

1. In the header of any column, click the arrow . A menu with column settings appears:

  • Sorting data in ascending or descending order

  • Selecting columns to display

    2. To configure which columns to show:

  • Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display in the table column opens

  • Select the checkboxes next to the parameters you want to see

How to use formulas in report columns

The report builder has two ways of adding formulas:

1. A formula for an existing field — adding a formula to an already existing data field

2. A standalone formula — creating a new column based on a formula using several fields

A formula for an existing field

This method is used when you need to modify the data of an already existing field.

How to configure:

1. Add a column with an existing data field (for example, “Idle time”).

2. In the “Formula” field, enter the expression to be applied to this field

For example, a Fuel Consumption While Driving report with an “Idle time” column. The “Formula” field contains =%te%-%ts% — this expression calculates the difference between the end time (te) and the start time (ts) of the idle

A standalone formula

This method is used when you need to create a new column based on several data fields.

How to configure:

1. Add a new column

2. In the “Data” field, select “Formula”

3. In the “Formula” field, enter an expression using data field identifiers

For example, a Fuel Consumption While Driving report with a “Consumption while driving” column:

  • In the “Data” field, Formula is selected

  • The Formula field contains =%fuel%/((%te%-%ts%)/60/60) — this expression calculates fuel consumption per hour:

    — %fuel% — fuel consumption according to the sensor

    — (%te%-%ts%)/60/60 — time in hours (the difference between the end and start time of the event, divided by 3600 seconds)

After the report is saved, the system automatically calculates the value for each row using the specified formula.

For more information on formula syntax, see the separate article.

moduli-1:
Modules are separate components of the PILOT system, each responsible for specific functions.

Thanks to the modular organization, you can:

— configure the system for your company's specific tasks

— pay only for the features you really need

— add new modules depending on your needs

How modules are connected

Modules are connected by the Contract administrator in the Admin panel. Some modules have their own settings that must be activated correctly.

If you have difficulties connecting a module, contact the support service.

Module Reports

When you enable a module, additional Reports appear to help you analyze operations.

You can find them in the “Reports” section.
video-i-cms:
The “Video” and “CMS” modules let you connect different types of video devices to the system: dash cams, vehicle cameras, and body cameras. They give you access to online streams, archived recordings, and telematics data.

The “Video” and “CMS” modules let you connect different types of video devices to the system: dash cams, vehicle cameras, and body cameras. With them you can view online streams and archived recordings, as well as receive telematics data. Mettax cameras can also send driver face recognition results to PILOT.

These modules work together: to connect cameras and dash cams correctly, you need to activate both modules.
nastrojka-modulej-v-paneli-administrator:
For dash cams and cameras to work in the system, you need to enable two modules: “Video” and “CMS”.

They work together:

  • “CMS” connects the devices and receives the data stream

  • “Video” shows streams, stores the archive, and provides access to the player

If you enable only one of them, the connection of cameras and dash cams will be incomplete.

Enabling the modules

If you have administrator access:

1. Log in to the admin panel

2. Go to the “Contracts” tab

3. Select the contract you need

4. Right-click the contract and select “Edit”

5. Go to the “Modules” tab

6. Select the check boxes next to the “Video” and “CMS” modules

After that, the modules will be activated for the selected contract.

Configuring CMS

1. Go to the “Module settings” tab

2. Select the “CMS” module

3. Find the “Configs” section; it is empty by default

4. Specify the keys:

  • url: video.pilot-gps.com

  • account: login

  • password: password

    To get the login and password, contact technical support. For security reasons they are not published in this guide.

After that, the CMS module will be configured.

When everything is set up, the PILOT system will:

  • receive video online

  • save recordings from dash cams and cameras

  • combine telemetry (speed, location, events).
kakie-ustrojstva-mozhno-podklyuchat:
The PILOT system supports different types of video devices. Each type has its own connection parameters:

Howen

  • Server 1 (telematics): Server URL, port 20009

  • Server 2 (video): video.pilot-gps.com, port 33000

    Howen uses a separate key, url_howen, in “Module settings”

    No password is required to connect.

CMS

  • Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com

  • Port: 6608

Cipia

  • Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com

  • Port: 1883

Teltonika DualCam

  • Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com

  • Port: 20233

Hikvision

How Hikvision devices are connected depends on the specific model.

Some models use the standard connection to the video.pilot-gps.com server.

For example, for Hikvision G40:

• Server address (Host): video.pilot-gps.com

• Port: 6608

Other Hikvision models that can be connected to PILOT:

  • DS-MCW407 (BWS): a body camera for video and audio with online transmission.

  • AE-MN5043 (DVR): a mobile dash cam with GPS for vehicles.

  • AE-VC583I-IS/P(H): a high-resolution vehicle IP camera (license plate recognition).

Different Hikvision models may use different connection parameters. Contact support to find out which ones apply.
