podklyuchenie-videoustrojstva-v-kabinete:
After the administrator has configured the modules “Video” and “CMS” in the admin panel, the user needs to create an object and set up the cameras.

Creating an object

1. Log in to the user account

2. Go to the “Main” section

3. Click “Create object”

4. Fill in the data in the object card:

  • Vehicle number or object name

  • Device ID

    5. In the “Device type” field, select:

  • CMS, if you have a CMS device

  • Howen, if you have a Howen device

  • or other types

1 — Device type

2 — Template. For CMS, the system already has ready-made global templates (settings for quick connection)

Other devices have no templates, so simply select the device type.

6. Click “Save”. The settings are applied and the object appears in the list.

Setting up cameras for an object

After saving the object, you need to specify how many cameras are connected and how they will work.

1. Open the object card by double-clicking the object in the list

2. Go to the “Video” tab

3. Click “Add camera”

4. Specify:

  • Camera name

  • Device type

  • Channel number

    If you select the Main stream check box, the camera transmits high-quality video (a sharper picture with more detail), but internet traffic consumption is higher.

If you leave the check box cleared, the sub-stream is used: the picture quality is lower, but traffic is used more economically.

5. Click “Save”

6. Repeat for all the cameras you want to add

Connecting an additional video device

In PILOT you can add an additional video device to an object if you already have a primary device (for example, Teltonika).

This is useful, for example, when:

  • Teltonika collects telemetry (speed, tracks, sensors),

  • while CMS or Howen handles video.

This way, one object can work with both GPS data and a video stream at the same time.

Adding an additional device

1. Open the object card

2. Go to the “Additional IMEI” field and click

3. In the window that opens, click the “Add” button

4. Select the device type from the list

5. When adding the device, you can select parameters:

  • Ignore coordinates

    Coordinates from the additional video device will not be used, since the primary device already transmits coordinates.

  • Ignore Retrans

    Data retransmission from the additional device will be disabled so that data is not duplicated and does not interfere with the primary telematics.

6. Click “Save”, and do not forget to also save the changes in the object card.
onlajn-video-s-kamer:
After you have saved the cameras in the object card, they become available in the system.

In the object list, a camera icon is displayed next to the vehicle name:

  • Green camera: the device is active, video is available

  • Gray camera: the device is inactive

How to view online video

1. In the object list, click the camera icon

2. A video player with a real-time stream opens

The player shows all available camera channels (for example: road, cabin, side or rear views, depending on the hardware).

The video displays:

  • the duration of the current online stream

• recording date and time

• channel number

• GPS coordinates: latitude and longitude

• driving speed in km/h

Streaming time limit

For online video, you can set the stream to stop automatically after a specified time. This lets you limit viewing duration and control how long live video runs.

To set the limit, click the settings icon in the upper-right corner of the video player.

The “Streaming time limit” window opens. In it you can enable automatic stopping and specify the stream duration.

To enable automatic stopping, select the “Automatically stop streaming” check box.

Then specify:

• Duration: how long the stream runs before it stops

• Unit: the unit of measurement, for example minutes or hours

After setting it up, click “Save”.

The video player header will show the duration of the current online stream in the format:

Live duration: current time / set limit

For example, Live duration: 00:03:15 / 00:30:00 means that the stream has been running for 3 minutes and the set limit is 30 minutes.

If automatic stopping is enabled, the system ends the online video after the specified time.

Controlling the video player

In the player you can use the following functions:

Start / Stop: start or stop the stream

Sound: adjust the volume or mute it

Screenshot: capture the current frame

🔲 Full screen: expand the player to full screen

Two-way communication

In the upper-right corner of the player there is an intercom icon . With this function you can communicate with the driver in both directions: hear the driver and speak to them.
kak-rabotat-s-mediafajlami:
All recordings and photos from devices are available for viewing in your account, either in the “History” section or on the “Media” tab of the selected object.

Media files in “History”

In the “History” section you can not only view an object’s tracks but also work with video: watch recordings, download clips, or review recorded violations.

1. In the top panel, go to the “History” section

2. Select the object you need from the list by selecting its check box

3. Specify the time period

4. Click the “Search” button

5. In the search results, select the check boxes next to the track records you want to view

6. A “Media” tab appears in the bottom panel (next to “Events”)

The “Media” tab is divided into two parts:

  • Device: recordings stored on the device itself (a dash cam or camera)

  • Storage Server: recordings stored on the server (for example, DMS/ADAS events: seat belt not fastened, fatigue, smoking, and so on)

Device tab

This tab shows everything that is still stored on the device.

How to view a recording:

1. Click the icon next to the recording in the list

2. A player opens with the video for the selected time interval

The video shows basic information:

  • channel number

  • date and time

  • vehicle speed and/or coordinates

In the player you can use the following functions:

Play / Pause: start or pause playback

Stop: end playback

Seek: move through the recording

Screenshot: capture a frame from the video

Sound: adjust the volume (if the recording contains audio)

Playback speed: slow down or speed up the recording

Full screen: expand the player to full screen

How to download a video:

1. Click the download button

next to the recording

2. A window for downloading the video opens

3. You can download either the entire video or only the segment you need.

  • To select a segment, specify the start and end time in the calendar

3. Click “Start”

Wait while the system prepares the file (the device must be turned on and the recording must still be on the memory card).

While the file is being prepared, a progress indicator is displayed in the window. It contains:

— the amount of data already transferred and the total file size

— the completion percentage

— the current data transfer speed

— the estimated time to completion

For example, the value 7.5 MB / 136.3 MB (5.5%) • 266 KB/s • 8 min means that 7.5 MB of 136.3 MB has been transferred, the download is 5.5% complete, the current speed is 266 KB/s, and about 8 minutes remain.

3. Once the file is prepared, you can download it to your computer: click “Save”

If the device has already overwritten the video recording, you will not be able to download it.

Storage Server tab

This tab contains recordings from the server. Safety-related events (DMS and ADAS) are uploaded to the server, for example:

  • the driver was not wearing a seat belt

  • smoking while driving

  • lane departure

  • signs of fatigue

A description is stored for each event, for example: “Seat belt not fastened”, “Driver fatigue”

How to work with media on the server

To view the photo of an event, click the icon .

Video is also available for some recordings: just click the play icon .

To save a media file (photo or video) to your computer, use the download button .

Where violations in Storage Server come from

All violations you see on the Storage Server tab are detected by the device itself.

When you create an object and apply a global settings template (for example, for CMS devices), a multi-position Alarm sensor appears in the object.

The device sends violation codes, and PILOT automatically maps these codes to the sensor’s calibration table of values.

The table translates technical codes into clear statuses, for example:

  • talking on the phone

  • unsafe following distance

  • smoking while driving

  • fatigue

  • lane departure

  • and other violations

When the driver commits one of these violations, the device sends the code to the system along with a photo or video. A basic set of violation codes is already built into the calibration table, so the main events are recorded right away, with no additional setup.

Media files in the object menu

The object menu has a separate “Media” tab.

To open it:

1. Find the object you need in the list

2. Right-click it

3. In the menu that appears, select “Media”

The “Media” tab is divided into two parts:

  • Device: recordings stored on the device itself (a dash cam or camera)

  • Storage Server: recordings stored on the server (for example, recordings of violations)

For details on what these sections contain and how to work with video, see above.
prosmotr-kamer-na-paneli-dashcam:
The Dashcam section in the main menu lets you watch the cameras of several objects at the same time. For example, you can display images from the cabins of different vehicles on one screen and quickly switch to the camera you need.

You can open up to 64 video streams on the panel. The cameras of each object are grouped into a separate block.

In this article:

  • Panel interface: the main areas and controls of Dashcam

  • Selecting cameras and building the panel: selecting objects and starting the video streams you need

  • Adjusting the zoom: changing the size of all video blocks

  • Viewing a camera in full screen: enlarging the image and returning to the general grid

  • Controlling the video player: starting and stopping the stream, controlling sound, and taking snapshots

  • Hiding and restoring cameras: temporarily turning off unneeded video streams and reopening them

  • Closing an object’s video block: stopping all streams of the selected object

  • Streaming time limit: automatically stopping viewing after a set time

Panel interface

On the left is the Camera management area with a list of objects and the cameras connected to them. On the right is the Dashcam workspace, where video blocks are opened.

The top of the panel provides:

  • : refreshes the list of objects and cameras

  • : opens the selected cameras on the panel

  • : changes the size of all open video blocks

  • Camera counter : shows the number of open video streams

  • : shows the duration of the current viewing session

  • Streaming time limit: configures automatic stopping of streams

Selecting cameras

The Camera management list shows all objects with cameras.

To see an object’s cameras, expand its row. The connected cameras appear under the object name with their names.

Building the panel

To open cameras:

1. Go to the Dashcam tab

2. In the Camera management area, expand the folder you need and find the object

3. Expand its row and select the check boxes next to the cameras you want to open

You can select individual cameras or all available cameras of the object.

4. Check the number of selected cameras at the top of the panel

5. Click Build dashboard

Separate blocks for the selected objects appear in the workspace. Each block shows the selected cameras.

The total number of cameras open at the same time cannot exceed 64.

If the panel is already built, you do not need to create it again to add another object. Double-click the row of the object you need in the Camera management area. Its cameras are added to the workspace, and previously opened streams continue to run without restarting.

Adjusting the zoom

With the Zoom slider you can change the size of all open video blocks at once:

— zoom out to fit more objects on the screen

— zoom in to see the image in more detail

Viewing a camera in full screen

To take a closer look at the image, double-click the camera you need. It expands to full screen.

To return to the general camera grid:

— double-click the image again

— or press Esc

Controlling the video player

The main actions are available at the bottom of each video player:

Start / Stop: start or stop the stream

Sound: adjust the volume or mute it

Screenshot: capture the current frame

Full screen: expand the player to full screen

Hiding a single camera

If you do not need the image from a particular camera for a while, you can hide it. To do this, click the × icon in the upper-right corner of the corresponding video stream.

After hiding:

— the camera is no longer displayed in the block

— its active stream stops

— the other cameras of the object continue to work

— the size and layout of the block do not change; a static area takes the camera’s place.

Stopping unneeded video streams helps reduce internet traffic consumption and the load on your computer.

Restoring hidden cameras

To bring back a hidden camera:

1. Click the settings icon in the object block header

2. Find the camera you need in the list of hidden cameras

3. Select it to start displaying it again

To restore all hidden cameras of the object at once, select Show All.

If the block has no hidden cameras, the menu displays the message No hidden cameras.

Closing an object’s video block

To close a video block completely, click the × icon in its header.

The block is removed from the workspace, and all its active video streams stop. The cameras of other objects continue to work.

Streaming time limit

To keep streams from staying on longer than necessary, you can configure them to stop automatically.

1. Click the settings icon on the right

2. The “Streaming time limit” window opens

3. To enable automatic stopping, select the “Automatically stop streaming” check box.

Then specify:

• Duration: how long the stream runs before it stops

• Unit: the unit of measurement, for example minutes or hours

4. Click “Save”

After saving, the current viewing time and the set limit are displayed next to Live duration:

When the set time runs out, PILOT automatically stops the streams.

If you do not need automatic stopping, clear the Automatically stop streaming option and save the settings.
voditeli-3:
The “Drivers” module is used to work with drivers in the system.

With it you can:

— create and edit driver cards

— assign drivers to vehicles

— configure drivers’ access to vehicles

— view which vehicles a driver worked on and during which period
kak-sozdat-voditelya:
To add a new driver, go to the “Drivers” tab in the “Main” section.

1. Click “Add driver”

2. The driver card opens, where you need to fill in the data. The driver card has two tabs: “Main” and “Vehicle”

“Main” tab

This is where you enter the driver’s personal data:

  • Driver name: full name or the name that will be displayed in the system

  • Date of birth

  • Gender

  • Driving start date

  • Driver’s license: number and expiration date

  • iButton: authentication key (if driver identification is used). For example, the iButton field is used to automatically identify the driver by face ID received from a Mettax camera

  • Email: email address

  • Phone: contact number

  • Group: the group the driver belongs to

  • Description: any additional information

  • For all users: if selected, the driver becomes available to all users of the system

  • Labels: tags for searching and grouping drivers

  • Photo: the driver’s photo. To upload a photo, click the icon under the image. The icon becomes available after the card is saved for the first time.

After filling in the data, click “Save”.

“Vehicle” tab

On this tab you can:

— assign the driver to a vehicle

— configure access to objects

— enable or disable alerts

Assigning a driver to a vehicle

1. Select the “Assign driver to vehicle” check box

After that, the “Object” and “Date” fields become active.

2. In the “Object” field, select the vehicle the driver will be assigned to

3. Specify the date and time from which the assignment takes effect

If a driver is already assigned to a vehicle, they are not unassigned automatically. The system can have several drivers for one vehicle at the same time. This is designed for real-life scenarios, for example, when two drivers work in one vehicle or drivers change by shift or on the road.

If you need a vehicle to have only one active driver at all times, enable the Single_Driver configuration in the contract in the admin panel.

In this mode, when a new driver is assigned, the previous one is automatically unassigned. The system will not have two active sessions for one vehicle.

If the driver uses an iButton, all previous drivers are automatically unassigned when the new driver authorizes.

Show history

The “Show history” button opens a window with the driver’s work history:

— which objects the driver worked on

— during which periods the vehicle changed

Access to objects

The “Access to objects” field lets you select which objects the driver will have access to in the system.

If you select objects, access is limited to those specific objects; if you leave the field empty, access is open to all objects.

Alerts

If you enable the “Send alerts” option, the system sends notifications related to this driver.

If you disable the option, such notifications are not sent.

Finishing work with the card

After configuring all parameters, click “Save” to apply the changes.

The “Delete” button removes the driver card from the system completely.

“Files” tab

After the card is saved for the first time, the “Files” tab appears.

You can store the driver’s documents there, for example:

— driver’s license

— medical certificates

— contracts

— other files

How to add a file

1. Click the button

2. In the window that opens:

— enter a description of the file

— click “Choose file” and upload a file from your device

3. Click “Save”.

The file then appears in the list on the “Files” tab.

Working with files

To download a file, click it in the “File” column.

To delete a file, click the trash icon next to it.

After adding or deleting files, do not forget to click “Save” in the driver card to apply the changes.
kak-rabotat-s-voditelyami-1:

You can customize the driver list: select the columns you need and enable sorting and filters.

1. In the header of any column, click the arrow to open the settings menu

2. The menu offers:

— sorting data in ascending or descending order

— filtering by the selected column

— selecting the columns to display

3. To choose which columns to show:

— click “Columns”

— select the check boxes next to the parameters you need; the table updates automatically

How to open the driver card

To open the driver card for viewing or editing:

2. Double-click the row with the driver’s name

The driver card opens in a separate window.

Driver groups

When you add a driver, you specify the group the driver belongs to.

Groups are created on the “Online” tab (these are object groups), but you can also use them to organize drivers.

The main actions are at the top of the list:

Driver assignment: bulk configuration of driver assignment to vehicles

Export drivers: export the list to a file

Import drivers: load drivers from a file

Add driver: create a new driver

Refresh list: refresh the data

How to configure driver assignment to vehicles

To link drivers to vehicles, open the DriversLink window. To do this, on the “Drivers” tab, click the “Assign driver to object” button at the top of the list.

In this window you can:

— assign drivers to vehicles

— configure access to vehicles by ID / iButton

DriversLink lets you not only link a driver and a vehicle but also create an assignment group.

Such a group stores:

— the list of vehicles

— the list of drivers

— the selected access mode

1. Select the access mode

At the top of the window, select the mode you need:

[0] Off

ID control is disabled. The vehicle is available without driver identification.

[1] Only authorized ID can unlock the vehicle

Only assigned drivers can use the vehicle.

4. Create an assignment group

After selecting vehicles and drivers:

  1. Click “Save”.

  2. In the window that appears, enter a group name and click OK.

The group appears in the list on the left. It stores:

— the selected access mode

— the list of vehicles

— the list of drivers

For the selected vehicles, the group name appears in the “Group” column.

5. Click the “Save” button at the bottom of the window.

The selected settings are then applied to all vehicles in the group.

opredelenie-voditelya-po-face-id:
Mettax cameras can recognize the driver’s face and send the driver’s identifier to PILOT. After successful recognition, PILOT automatically assigns the driver to the object on the same principle as for iButton and RFID tags.

This function lets you determine who is operating the vehicle when several drivers use the same object.

Preparing drivers on the device

First, drivers must be registered on the Mettax device. After registration, the device creates a faceId identifier for each driver.

How drivers are added depends on the camera model and settings. If you do not know how to register drivers on the device, contact the specialist who installed or configured the camera.

After a driver is registered, the device must:

1. Recognize the driver’s face

2. Send the created faceId to PILOT

3. Send the recognition result in the faceRecogn parameter

The faceId identifier is created by the Mettax device. The value received from the device is linked to the card of the corresponding driver in PILOT.

Recognition data

During a face check, the device sends the following parameters to PILOT:

  • faceId: the driver identifier created on the device

  • faceRecogn: the recognition result

  • alarm: the type of check performed

The faceRecogn parameter can take the following values:

  • 1: the face was successfully recognized

  • 0: the check was unsuccessful

  • 2: the face could not be detected

  • 3: the comparison ended with an error

For automatic driver assignment, the device must send faceRecogn=1.

The camera can send the following check events:

  • alarm=647: periodic driver check

  • alarm=648: driver check when the ignition is turned on

Data display in raw points

During a face check, the Mettax camera sends the alarm, faceId, and faceRecogn parameters in the object’s raw data.

The highlighted row in the example shows the following values:

alarm=647; faceId=1; faceRecogn=1;

Here:

  • alarm=647: the camera performed a periodic driver check

  • faceId=1: the device sent driver identifier 1

  • faceRecogn=1: the face was successfully recognized

In the rows above, the camera sent:

faceId=20210301001; faceRecogn=0;

The value faceRecogn=0 shows that the face could not be recognized.

In the row with alarm=648, the check was triggered when the ignition was turned on. The value faceRecogn=0 also means the face was not recognized.

For automatic driver assignment, the faceId identifier and a successful faceRecogn=1 result must arrive in the same point at the same time. The received faceId value must match the value in the iButton field of the driver card.

Setting up the Face ID sensor

For PILOT to use the received faceId to identify the driver, you need to create a special sensor with the iButton purpose on the object.

1. Add a new sensor to the object

2. Specify the following parameters:

  • Purpose: iButton

  • Type: Special

  • Name and description

  • Field: for example, faceId

  • Conversion formula: *%faceRecogn%. It multiplies the faceId value by the recognition result. When recognition is successful (faceRecogn=1), the faceId value does not change, and PILOT can match it with the identifier in the driver card. With other values, the formula result does not match the original faceId.

  • Maximum value: a value that allows the faceId identifiers in use to be stored

5. If necessary, enable “Close driver session when ignition is turned off”. After the ignition is turned off, the assigned driver is no longer considered active for the object

6. Save the sensor

Checking the formula

Before saving the sensor, check the formula on test data.

1. Click “Test” next to the conversion formula

2. In the window that opens, find the faceid and faceRecogn parameters

3. In the faceid parameter, enter a test driver identifier, for example: faceid=20210301001

The value 20210301001 is an example of a faceId created by a Mettax device.

4. Replace the automatically filled-in faceRecogn value with 1: faceRecogn=1.

The parameter faceRecogn=1 corresponds to successful face recognition.

5. Click Test

If the check is successful, the result should match the faceid value: Success: 20210301001

The formula *%faceRecogn% multiplies faceid by the recognition result. With faceRecogn=1 it returns the original driver identifier. With other values, the formula result does not match the original faceId.

The automatically filled-in test values are not device data. Before checking, replace faceRecogn with one of the values supported by the Mettax camera: 0, 1, 2, or 3.

Linking Face ID to a driver

When a driver is registered, the Mettax device creates a unique faceId identifier for the driver. For PILOT to identify the driver automatically, this identifier must be entered in the driver card.

1. Find out the faceId assigned to the driver by the Mettax device

2. Copy the faceId value

3. Open the card of the corresponding driver in PILOT

4. Go to the “Main” tab

5. Paste the faceId value into the iButton field

6. Save the changes

The value in the iButton field must exactly match the faceId identifier sent by the camera. A separate identifier is used for each driver.

After successful recognition, the camera sends faceId and faceRecogn=1. PILOT matches the received faceId with the value in the iButton field and assigns the corresponding driver to the object.
logbook:
LogBook is a portal that provides drivers with all data about their trips, events, and fuel expenses, as well as information about their driving style.

Through this portal, drivers can track both business and private trips and receive reports on fuel and toll road expenses.
kak-podklyuchit-logbook:
To connect LogBook, you need to complete two steps:

  • Activate the LogBook module in the admin panel

2. Connect LogBook in the user interface

Connecting the LogBook module in the admin panel

  • Log in to the admin panel with your login and password

  • Select the contract to which you are connecting the module

  • Right-click the contract to open the context menu

  • In the menu, select “Edit”

  1. In the contract settings window that opens, select the “Module settings” tab

6. Select the drivers module and set the key for it: logbook = 1

7. After adding the key, click “Update” and save the contract settings.

Connecting LogBook in the user account interface

  • Go to the user account

  • In the “Main” section, go to the “Drivers” tab

3. Select the driver you need and open the driver card by double-clicking the driver in the list

4. Enable the LogBook module for the selected driver by selecting the LogBook Acces check box

5. Set the login for the driver’s access to the portal

6. Click the “Send to driver” button. An email with a link to access the LogBook portal is sent to the address specified in the driver card.

The driver must have a real email address, otherwise they will not be able to receive the email.
To set up the password and the driver’s access to the portal correctly, we recommend contacting technical support.
kak-vojti-v-logbook:
To log in to LogBook:

  • Follow the link: logbook.pilot-gps.com

2. Enter your login credentials: login and password

3. Click Continue. You will then enter the system and can start using all its functions

If you need to change your password

If you forgot your password or want to change it, follow these steps:

1. Click Reset password

2. Enter your email address and click Reset password again

3. An email with a password reset link is sent to your address

4. Follow the link, enter a new password, repeat it, and click Continue.
obzor-interfejsa-portala:
After logging in to LogBook, you land on the main page.

Let us identify the main interface elements:

  • Left panel with the summary and filters

  • Top panel with the section menu

Left panel: filters and summary

1. Trip period
At the top of the screen, select the period for which you want to view trips. To do this:
  • Specify the date and time using the calendar icon
  • Click the Refresh button
2. Main information
The Main section displays:
  • Timezone – the time zone in which trip times are displayed
  • Driver – the name of the driver whose data is shown
  • Current vehicle – the vehicle number or ID
  • Vehicle – a drop-down list for selecting the vehicle you need if several vehicles are assigned to you
3. Mileage summary
The Summary section shows the total mileage for the selected period:
  • Total km – total mileage
  • Business km – kilometers marked as business trips
  • Private km – kilometers marked as private trips
4. Toll roads
This section displays information about toll road expenses:
  • Total Toll – total toll road expenses
  • SANRAL / NON-SANRAL – toll roads split by operator type (if applicable)
  • Business Toll – toll road amount for business trips
  • Private Toll – toll road amount for private trips
5. Driver statistics
The Driver statistic section displays driving style and safety indicators:
  • Harsh Acceleration – number of hard accelerations
  • Harsh Brakes – number of hard braking events
  • Excess Idling – long stops with the engine running
  • Over Speeding – cases of exceeding the set speed.
  • Max speed – the highest recorded speed
  • Driver score – the overall driving style score as a percentage: the higher it is, the more careful and economical the driving

Top panel

The main portal sections are at the top of the screen:

  • Trips – a list of all trips for the selected period

  • Events – individual driving events (hard braking, speeding, and so on)

  • Fuel – data on refuels and fuel consumption

  • Tolls – detailed information on each toll section

  • Media – photos or videos associated with trips

The upper-right part of the screen contains:

  • Email – the current user

  • Settings – access to account settings

  • Logout – log out of the system
kak-rabotat-s-nastrojkami-v-logbook:
This article explains how to use settings in the LogBook portal. You will be able to:

— configure a calendar with days off for working time tracking

— go to and view the portal user guide

— change your password

— view the user’s action history on the portal

Setting up days off and holidays

So that LogBook correctly identifies trips on days off (for example, marking them as private), you can configure the calendar.

Importing a production calendar

1. Go to the Settings section and select Holidays.

2. In the window that opens, select Import to automatically load the calendar for the year you need

3. Enter the following data:

  • Year: specify the year for which you want to load the list of holidays

  • Country code (2 letters): for example, ZA for South Africa

4. Click Save to save the data

Adding a day off manually

1. Open Settings and select Add

2. Enter information about the day off:

  • Date: select the date of the holiday

  • Name: specify the official name of the holiday

  • Local Name: what the holiday is called in your language or in your company

  • Type: the type of holiday (national, regional, corporate, and so on)

  • Launch Year: specify the year from which this holiday is taken into account

    3. Click Save

User guide

If you need information on working with the LogBook portal, you can read the user guide.

Changing your password

To change your password for logging in to the LogBook portal:

1. In Settings, select Change password

2. Enter a new password and repeat it for confirmation

3. Click Save to save the new password

Viewing the action history

With the Audit function, you can view the history of actions on the portal.

How to view the action history:

1. In the Audit window, select:

  • Start Date: specify the date from which to show events

  • End Date: select the date up to which to show events

  • Driver: select the driver or user whose activity you want to track.

    2. Click Show

You will then see a list of all actions in the specified period:

  • Date: when the event occurred

  • Driver: who performed the action

  • Login: which account the action was performed under

  • Operation: what exactly was done

  • IP: which IP address the action was performed from

  • Browser: which browser was used to perform the operation
kak-rabotat-s-razdelami:
The main portal sections are at the top of the screen:

  • Trips – a list of all trips for the selected period

  • Events – individual driving events

  • Fuel – data on refuels and fuel consumption

  • Tolls – detailed information on each toll section

  • Media – photos or videos associated with trips

Trips

The “Trips” section displays all of the driver’s trips.

Functions in the section:

  • Auto Process  – automatically sorts trips into business and private
  • Show current position – displays the object’s location on the map
  • Edit locations – helps you correct or refine the addresses of trip start and end points
  • Reports – creates reports on trips and expenses for the selected period
  • Check boxes Business and Private – use these check boxes to filter trips: show only business trips, only private trips, or all trips

Automatic trip processing

The Auto Process function helps automatically split trips into business and private.

How to set up automatic processing:

  • Click Auto Process in the “Trips” section

2. In the window that appears, select the period to which you want to apply automatic processing:

  • Current Month: if you select this option, the system automatically processes trips for the current calendar month

  • Select date range: if you want to process trips for a specific period, select the dates using the calendar.

Specify:

  • Start Date: the date from which to start automatic processing

  • End Date: the date up to which to apply it

3. Specify the standard working hours in the fields:

  • Start Work: specify the time from which trips are considered business trips. For example, 08:00.

  • End Work: specify the time after which trips are considered private. For example, 19:00.

All trips that take place between Start Work and End Work are automatically marked as Business

The “Control room” module is designed for monitoring and managing object parameters in the system. It helps you track events related to objects and simplifies working with notifications and event-handling algorithms. With this module you can not only receive notifications about events but also configure exactly what the system should do when such an event occurs.

The module was previously called GARM. This name may still appear in some places in the interface.
The new name, “Control room”, is now in use and will eventually replace the old one completely.

Main functions of the module:

Event monitoring

The system tracks events related to objects and notifies you about them, for example, when parameters deviate or a state changes.

Event-handling algorithms

You can configure action scenarios that the system performs automatically when an event occurs, for example, sends a notification, records data, creates a command, and so on.

Notification management

You define which events trigger notifications, who they are sent to, and which handling algorithm is used.
kak-sozdat-algoritm:
The “Control room” module helps the system respond to events automatically. It uses event-handling algorithms: predefined sequences of actions that run when certain conditions are met.

For example, you can configure the system to:

— immediately notify the operator and mark the event as critical when speed or temperature is exceeded

— create a task for the dispatcher and send the driver a reminder in case of a long idle period

— record the arrival time and send an SMS to the customer when the vehicle enters the customer’s geofence

Creating an algorithm

  • Go to the “Algorithms” section in the top interface menu

2. Create a new algorithm

On the “List” tab, click the “Add” button . The builder workspace opens

3. Assemble the algorithm from blocks

In the workspace you can drag blocks and arrange them into a scenario.

Each block is a separate step that the system performs when the event is triggered.

Available blocks:

  • Start block: the starting point of the algorithm

  • Text: displays a message or comment

  • Command: a system action (for example, sending a notification)

  • Command template: a ready-made action for reuse

  • Webhook: sends an HTTP request to an external system. The block lets you pass event data to a third-party service, for example a CRM, a dispatch system, or a corporate application

  • Condition: a logical check (for example, if the temperature exceeds a threshold)

  • Choice: a fork with several action options

  • End: completes the algorithm

Additional blocks may also be available, depending on the system configuration.

4. Arrange the blocks and connect them

An algorithm usually starts with the “Start block”, followed by condition checks and actions, and ends with the “End” block.

Connect the blocks by dragging branches between them.

For example, branches are set from the “Condition” block to the “Text” block:

  • “Yes”: if the condition is met

  • “No”: if the condition is not met

Place the Webhook block in the branch where data must be sent to an external system. If the request must be sent regardless of the check result, add a separate Webhook block to both branches.

At this stage only the structure of the algorithm is defined. Parameter values (conditions, message texts, request parameters, and other settings) are specified later, when you link the algorithm to a notification.

5. Save the algorithm

When the diagram is ready, click “Accept”.

In the window that appears, enter a name for the algorithm and click “OK”. The algorithm is saved in the list and becomes available for use.

Example of a simple algorithm

Task: record an event if the cargo temperature exceeds the allowed value.

How to build the algorithm:

1. Add the “Start block”

2. Add the “Condition” block, which checks that the temperature is above normal

The “Temperature” parameter and the threshold are set later, when linking to a notification.

3. From the “Condition” block, place “Text” blocks and draw the “Yes” and “No” branches to them

4. Complete the algorithm with the “End” block and make sure all blocks are connected

This is a basic algorithm that can be used as a foundation for automatic event handling.

A created algorithm does not run on its own. To make it work, you need to link it to a notification.

You can read how to do this in the next article.

This article explains how to set up algorithms to work through notifications.

You will learn:

— how to link an algorithm to a notification so that it runs automatically when events occur

— how to create a notification with an algorithm for manual event generation

For an algorithm to start working and respond to events, it must be linked to a notification.

For linking to work, the “Notifications” module must be enabled in the contract.

Linking an algorithm to an event

Such an algorithm runs automatically when the conditions are met and arrives in the “Control room”.

1. In the top panel, click the icon and open “Contract settings”. Go to the “Notifications” tab.

2. Click “Add” to create a new notification

3. Link the algorithm

  1. In the notification settings window, click “Algorithm linking”

  1. Select the algorithm you need from the list

  1. Click the algorithm; its diagram with blocks opens

4. Configure the algorithm blocks

  1. Double-click the block you need

  1. Fill in the text and select event tags

  1. Click “OK”

How to create a tag for a block

Tags help you quickly understand the essence of an event and visually highlight it in the list.

If the tag you need does not exist:

1. In the “Tag” field, click

2. In the tags window, click to add a new tag to the list

3. Enter the tag name and select a color

4. Save; the tag appears in the list and becomes available for selection

Configuring the Webhook block

The Webhook block passes event information from PILOT to an external system, for example a CRM, a dispatch system, or a corporate application. The request is sent when algorithm execution reaches this block. For more on how Webhook notifications work and how to configure them, see this article.

If the algorithm uses a Webhook block:

1. Select the Webhook block in the diagram

2. Double-click it to open its settings

3. Click the edit icon next to the block name

4. Fill in the parameters in the Webhook Details window

URL

Specify the address of the external system to which PILOT should send the data. You need to get the address from the administrator or developer of the receiving system.

Header

Specify the request headers. By default, data is sent in JSON format:

[
  "ContentType: application/json"
]

Change the headers only if the receiving system requires a different data format or additional parameters.

Body

Specify the data to send. By default, the following template is used:

{
  "agent_id": "%AGENTID%",
  "vehiclenumber": "%VEHNUM%",
  "ts": "%TS%",
  "lat": "%LAT%",
  "lon": "%LON%",
  "speed": "%SPEED%",
  "data": "%DATA%",
  "zone": "%ZONE%",
  "driver": "%DRIVER%"
}

Instead of the variables enclosed in % signs, the system automatically substitutes information from the event. For example, %SPEED% is replaced with the object’s speed, and %VEHNUM% with the vehicle number.

You can change the request body: remove unneeded fields, add your own fields, or use other available variables.

Keep the JSON format valid:

"field_name": "%VARIABLE%"

If the JSON structure or a variable is written incorrectly, the external system may not receive or process the request.

Allowed variables

  Variable
  What it passes
  %ACCOUNTID%
  Account ID
  %AGENTID%
  Object ID
  %VEHNUM%
  Vehicle number
  %TS%
  Timestamp
  %DATETIME%
  Date and time
  %LAT%
  Latitude
  %LON%
  Longitude
  %SPEED%
  Speed
  %ODO%
  Mileage (from the sensor)
  %DATA%
  Notification data
  %ZONE%
  Geofence
  %ZONE_ID%
  ID of the first geofence
  %ZONE_NAME%
  Name of the first geofence
  %DRIVER%
  Driver
  %MAXSPEED%
  Maximum speed (for speeding notifications)
  %DUR% 
  Duration of the speeding
  %SPEEDLIMIT% 
  Set speed limit (Speed control)

The set of available variables may depend on the notification type. For example, the variables %MAXSPEED%, %DUR%, and %SPEEDLIMIT% are intended for speeding notifications.

After filling in the parameters, click “Save”, then confirm the block configuration with the “OK” button. If different branches of the algorithm use different Webhook blocks, configure each of them separately.

Configuring the event processing window

You can configure how the event processing window looks for the operator:

  • In the algorithm linking window, click “Settings”

2. Click to add elements:


What you can configure:

  • Element type: the kind of block (for example, plaintext is plain text)

  • Text: information for the operator

For example:

To add a section with vehicle information, click the car icon. A new block of the vehicle type appears, where you can set the title and text.

After configuring, click “OK”; the operator will see the form exactly in this form when processing the event.

Completing the notification setup

  • Notification name

  • Object

  • Notification type: Control room (GARM)

  • Group

  • Notification conditions (for example, the “Temperature” parameter and its threshold)

2. Click “Save”

3. The notification with the linked algorithm appears in the list and is sent to the “Control room” when the conditions are met

Algorithm for manual event generation

Manual generation is needed when an event does not arrive automatically, for example, for non-routine situations, testing, or an operator recording an event manually.

After you choose:

— the algorithm ends

— the event is considered processed

— the result is saved in the history

If the algorithm has no fork, a “Finish” button appears instead of “Yes / No”.

How to work with the event processing window

In the processing window, click the map icon ; a built-in map opens at the bottom.

On the map you will see:

  • the object’s position at the time of the event

  • the track of movement before and after the event

  • the address and coordinates

Click the icon in the processing window to open an additional panel with detailed data on the object and the event.

It has three blocks:

1. Sensors

— sensor values at the time of the event

— current values now

2. Processed events

— the date of previous events for this object

— which operators processed them

— processing time, group, and event text

3. Task information

— task number and status

— time of status changes

— route and actual times

On this panel the operator sees the full context of the event without leaving the processing window.
kak-nastroit-parametry-sobytij:
You can configure how events are displayed in the “Control room”: set groups, colors, and processing statuses.

1. Go to “Contract settings”

2. Open the “Control room” tab

In the interface it may currently be called GARM, which is the module’s former name.

Event group settings

On the left is the list of event groups coming from the “Control room” (for example: Observation, Arming/Disarming, RFID Antenna, and others).

Each row is a separate event group. For it you can configure:

  • Group color: select a color from the list. The color helps you identify the event type, for example, blue for observation, red for alarms

  • “Alarm” type: select the check box if events of this group should be considered alarms

The trash icon deletes a group if it is no longer needed.

How to add an event group:

  • Click the “Add” button at the bottom of the event list

  • Select a color for the new group

  • If necessary, select the “Alarm” type

After saving, the new group immediately appears in the list and starts being used in the “Control room”.

Stage color settings

On the right you choose the color used to show the event state. The color helps you understand what is currently happening with the event.

  • In progress: the event is being processed

  • Unprocessed: a new event

  • Processed: events that the algorithm and the operator have already handled

  • Unprocessed (timer expired): the event was not processed in time

To set a color, select it from the drop-down list.
klimat:
The “Climate” module is designed to monitor temperature and humidity on monitoring objects where temperature and humidity control is important, for example, residential premises, warehouses, offices, and cold rooms.

In standard mode of the “Climate” module, you can:

— view the current sensor values

— see the date and time of the last update

— track changes in readings

— display sensors on the room plan

When the Velavu integration is connected, the “Climate” module can also be used for indoor positioning — tracking objects inside buildings.

In this mode, the module displays Velavu objects, their location on the plan, status, and movement history.
kak-rabotat-s-modulem-klimat:
The “Climate” module helps you monitor temperature and humidity at monitored objects.

In it you can group sensors into a structure of rooms, view their current values, follow updates, and display sensors on an object plan.

In this article we will cover:

  • What to do before you start

  • How the module interface is organized

  • How to create a room

  • How to add nested elements

  • How to add a sensor

  • How to work with sensors in the list

  • How to upload a room plan

  • How to place sensors on the plan

  • Which actions are available for a room

Before you start

For the “Climate” module to work correctly, temperature or humidity sensors must be set up in advance on the monitored objects.

The module works only with sensors that are already added to the system and linked to monitored objects.

Therefore, before you start, make sure that:

1. A monitored object has been created

2. A temperature or humidity sensor is set up on the object

Example

Suppose you want to monitor the temperature in a residential space. Then:

1. First, create an object named Home in the monitoring system. To learn how to create a monitored object, read here.

2. Then add a temperature sensor to it. To learn how to set up a sensor on an object, read here.

3. After that, open the “Climate” module and link the sensor to a room

Module interface

The module interface is divided into two main parts:

List of rooms and sensors

On the left is the main workspace with a list of:

  • Names of buildings, floors, and rooms

  • Sensors linked to each room

  • The current value of each sensor

  • Time of the last update

  • A mini-chart of reading changes

Tools are located at the top of the list:

Search: a field for quickly finding the object or sensor you need

Filter: to select items by conditions

“Add” button: to add a new room

Refresh button: to refresh the data

Room plan

If an SVG plan has been uploaded for the room, the plan with sensor markers is displayed on the right.

How to work with the module

1. Create a room

To start monitoring the climate, you need to create a structure: a building, a floor, or a room

  • Go to the “Climate” section

    2. Click the button at the top of the list

    3. In the window that appears, enter the room name

4. Click OK

The new room appears in the list. You can now work with it through the context menu.

If you want to change a room you created:

1. Right-click it

2. In the menu, select “Edit”

3. In the window that opens, change the name

4. If necessary, select the room type: building, floor, room

5. Click “Add”

2. Add nested elements

If your room consists of several zones, you can make the structure more detailed. For example, add floors to a building and rooms to a floor.

1. Right-click the room you need in the list

2. In the menu, select “Add room”

3. Specify the name of the new element

4. Select the room type: building, floor, or room

5. Click “Add”

The new element appears inside the selected room. You can repeat this process to build the structure you need.

3. Add a sensor

After creating a room, you need to link a sensor to it:

1. Select the room you need in the list

2. Right-click and select “Add sensor”

3. A settings window opens where you need to select:

  • Monitored object: the object the sensor is linked to

  • Sensor: the temperature or humidity sensor you need from the list

4. Click “Add”

After saving, the sensor appears in the “Climate” module list.

It displays:

  • Name: the sensor name in the system

  • Current value: the temperature or humidity right now

  • Update time: when data was last received

  • Mini-chart: how the value changed over time

If a plan has been uploaded, the sensor is also displayed on it.

How to work with sensors in the list

Sensor tooltip

If you hover the cursor over a sensor in the list, a tooltip appears.

It shows:

  • sensor name

  • sensor ID

  • sensor type

  • current value

  • current status

The following statuses can be used for sensors:

  • In range: the value is within the allowed range

  • Out of range: the value has gone beyond the allowed limits

  • Offline: no current data is arriving from the sensor

Mini-chart

A mini-chart of the sensor’s operation and reading changes may be displayed next to the sensor in the list. It helps you quickly see how values changed over time.

If you hover the cursor over the chart, you can see a tooltip with additional information, for example, the value at a specific point and the time the reading changed.

How to delete a sensor

1. Right-click the sensor

2. Select “Delete sensor”

3. Confirm the deletion

How to upload a room plan

A room plan is an SVG file with a plan of your object. After uploading the plan and adding sensors, you can:

— see sensors directly on the plan

— compare values between rooms and see the temperature difference in different zones

— monitor the situation visually

How to upload

1. Select the room you need in the list

2. Right-click and select “Upload SVG”

3. Select the SVG file with the room plan

4. Specify the width and height of the plan; these are the dimensions at which the plan is displayed in the interface

5. Save

After that, the plan appears on the right side of the module window.

How to place sensors on the plan

After you upload an SVG plan, the added sensors appear on it automatically.

You can drag the sensors with the mouse and place them according to their actual location in the room.

When you hover the mouse over a sensor on the plan, a tooltip with its name and current value appears.

Room actions menu

To open the actions menu, right-click the room.

Through this menu you can:

Edit the element

Add room: create a nested structure element

Upload plan: add an SVG file so that the plan appears on the right side of the window

Add sensor: connect a temperature or humidity sensor

Delete element: delete the room
kak-rabotat-s-integratsiej-velavu:
Velavu is an indoor positioning system that lets you track the location of objects inside buildings. It uses fixed positioning points — anchors — and mobile tags to determine the location of equipment, vehicles, assets, or personnel on a building or floor plan.

The Velavu integration with PILOT lets you work with this data in the system interface.

With the Velavu integration in PILOT, you can:

— load the structure of sites, buildings, and floors from Velavu

— see the location of objects inside buildings

— open detailed information about devices

— track movement history
kak-podklyuchit-integratsiyu-velavu:
The Velavu integration is configured at the partner account level through configuration parameters.

Integration setup is available only to users with main administrator rights. If you do not have the appropriate access level, contact support.

1. In the admin panel, go to the “Partners” section

2. Double-click the partner you need; the partner card opens

3. Go to the “Configuration” tab

4. Click the “Add” button

5. In the drop-down list, select the Velavu key. In the parameter value, paste the Velavu configuration in JSON format.

Example of a Velavu JSON configuration

[
 {
 "broker": "iot.velavu.com",
 "port": "8883",
 "customer_id": "YOUR_CUSTOMER_ID",
 "api_token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN",
 "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nYOUR_CERTIFICATE\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
 "key": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nYOUR_PRIVATE_KEY\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
 }
]
  Parameter
  Description
  broker
  Velavu MQTT broker address
  port
  Connection port
  customer_id
  Customer ID in the Velavu system
  api_token
  Velavu API access token
  cert
  SSL certificate for the connection
  key
  SSL private key
You obtain all the data (customer_id, api_token, certificate, and key) from your Velavu account.

6. Save the configuration. After that, the integration becomes available for the accounts that belong to this partner
kak-rabotat-s-obektami-velavu:
With the Velavu integration in PILOT, you can track the location of objects inside buildings in real time: which floor, room, or zone equipment and personnel are in.

In this article we will cover:

  • How to switch to Velavu mode

  • How to get started with Velavu

  • How to synchronize

  • How to interact with devices

  • How to view device details

  • Object and device menu

  • Velavu geofences

How to switch to Velavu mode

After the Velavu integration is connected, the “Climate” module lets you switch between two modes:

  • Standard — the regular “Climate” module mode for working with temperature and humidity sensors

  • Velavu — the mode that displays Velavu objects

    1. Open the “Climate” module

2. On the “Climate” tab, use the drop-down list to switch the mode from “Standard” to “Velavu”

3. The interface switches to Velavu mode

In Velavu mode, the Velavu object tree is displayed instead of the usual temperature and humidity sensors.

Each element in the tree usually shows:

  • the object name, for example, Velavu-00Q6N

  • the type, for example:

    — ANCHOR — anchor

    — TAG — tag

    — Device — device

In Velavu mode, the following are available at the top of the window:

Filter — to select the elements you need

Search — to quickly find a device, floor, or site

Synchronization button — to load or update the structure from Velavu

Add button — lets you manually add a room if you need to extend the structure

How to get started with Velavu

For Velavu objects to appear in the “Climate” module, you first need to prepare the objects in the system.

1. Create a monitoring object. To learn how to create an object, read the separate article.

2. In the object card, enter the object identifier from the Velavu system

3. After that, you can configure the object further, for example:

— select an icon

— specify a color

— fill in other parameters

4. Run synchronization

Once the objects are prepared, go to the “Climate” module and synchronize the structure.

Synchronizing the Velavu structure

Synchronization is needed to load the object structure from Velavu and display it in the “Climate” module:

1. Open the “Climate” module

2. Switch to Velavu mode

3. Click the synchronization button

4. The system loads buildings, floors, and devices from the Velavu API

After synchronization, the entire structure appears in the object tree, grouped by account, building, and floor.

How to interact with Velavu objects

  • If you click an object in the tree on the left, the corresponding object on the plan is highlighted.

  • If you click an object on the plan, it is automatically selected in the object list.

Which objects are displayed in Velavu

The module can display different types of objects:

  • Anchors — fixed reference points used to calculate the position of other devices

  • Tags — tags that are usually attached to equipment, people, or other objects. Once the anchors are configured, their position is calculated automatically.

  • Proximity Tags — tags that are detected within the radius of another object

Color coding of Velavu objects

Velavu objects are displayed on the plan as colored circles. The color indicates the object type and its status:

  Color
  Object type
  Description
  Blue
  Anchor (Anchor )
  Fixed positioning point installed in a room
  Green
  Tag (Tag)
  Moving object — equipment, vehicle, or personnel
  Yellow
  Proximity Tags (Proximity Tags)
  Tag located within the range of another object
  Red
  Offline
  The object is not transmitting data or is outside the coverage area

Tooltip on hover

If you hover over an object in the list or on the plan, a tooltip with brief information about the object appears.

The tooltip shows:

  • Name — the object name in the system

  • Agent ID — the internal object identifier

  • Device ID — the Velavu device identifier

  • Location type — the object placement type

  • Coordinates — the current coordinates of the object

  • Site — the name of the site the object belongs to

  • Floor — the floor where the object is located

  • Status — the current state of the device: online or offline

This tooltip helps you get the main information about an object without opening the device card.

Viewing device details

A detailed card with full information is available for each Velavu device. To open it, click the view icon next to the object in the tree.

The device card opens as a separate window with several tabs:

Basic information

This tab shows general information about the device: where it is located, what it is attached to, and its status.

  • Device name — the device name in the Velavu system, for example, Velavu-Sp8mv

  • Device ID — the unique device identifier, for example, Sp8mv

  • Site — the name of the site where the device is installed, for example, GARGASH

  • Floor — the floor where the device is located, for example, Level 1 - GR001

  • Connection status — the current state of the device: online or offline

Below is the “Assignment” block, which may show information about the asset:

  • Asset name — the asset the device is attached to

  • Asset group — the group the asset belongs to

  • Asset category — the asset category

  • Operation — the current action or state of the asset

At the bottom of the tab, the following field is displayed:

  • Last update — the date and time when data was last received from the device

Location

The “Location” tab shows data about the device location.

Here you can see:

  • Floor name — the floor where the device is located

  • Site name — the site where the device is placed

  • Location type — the way the device is placed

  • Latitude — the current latitude value

  • Longitude — the current longitude value

  • Nearest device ID — the identifier of the nearest device

  • Distance to device — the distance to the nearest device

Device status

The “Device status” tab shows the current technical state of the device.

Battery status

This block may show:

  • Charge level — the battery charge percentage, for example, 90%

  • Battery charging — whether the device is connected to a charger

Connection

This block shows:

  • Connection status — online or offline

  • RSSI — signal level

  • Gateway ID — the identifier of the gateway the device is connected through

  • Signal level — connection quality

Movement and activity

In this block you can see:

  • Motion detection — whether the object is moving or stationary

  • Last activity — the date and time of the device's last activity

Environment

This tab shows environmental sensor data if the device supports measuring temperature, humidity, or pressure.

Here you can see:

  • Temperature — the current value in °C

  • Humidity — the current value in %

  • Pressure — the current value in kPa

Below is the “History charts” block.

If data is available, charts of temperature, humidity, and pressure changes are displayed here.

Above the charts you can select the viewing period: 1h — 1 hour, 6h — 6 hours, 1d — 1 day, 7d — 7 days, 30d — 30 days, All — the entire available period

Assignment

The “Assignment” tab shows which asset the device is associated with.

Here you can usually see:

  • Asset name — the asset the device is attached to

  • Asset group — the group the asset belongs to

  • Asset category — the asset category

  • Operation — the current action or state of the asset

If the asset data is not filled in, the fields may show N/A.

Technical data

The “Technical data” tab shows additional service information about the device.

Depending on the device, the following may be available here:

  • Firmware / model

  • Beacon interval

  • Heartbeat frequency

  • State update frequency

  • Temperature and humidity update frequency

  • Beacon transmit power

  • Site ID

  • Floor ID

Velavu object menu

A context menu with additional actions is available for Velavu floors and sites. To open the object actions menu, right-click the Velavu object.

Through this menu you can:

Edit — change the name and type of the room

Add room — create a nested element of the structure

Show anchors — show the fixed positioning points on the object plan.

Anchors are hidden by default.

To show the anchors, select “Show anchors” in the menu. They will appear on the plan and in the list.

To hide the anchors, select “Hide anchors” in the menu.

Add object — link a Velavu monitoring object to a room

Delete element — remove a room from the structure

Velavu device menu

For an individual Velavu device, the following action is available in the context menu:

  • Delete object

This action removes the link between the device and the Velavu room.

Velavu geofences

Velavu geofences are loaded into the system automatically from Velavu. You do not need to create them manually in PILOT.

It is enough to configure the sites and buildings in Velavu and then click the synchronization button in Velavu mode in the “Climate” module. The system will automatically import the geofences, the structure of sites and floors, and the related devices.

After that, the Velavu geofences will appear in the “Geofences” section in a separate folder.
kak-prosmotret-istoriyu-obektov-velavu:
On the “History” tab, you can view the history of Velavu objects for a selected period.

You can:

— see where an object was at a specific moment

— see which room it was in

— trace the movement of the object on the map

How to open the Velavu history

1. Go to the “History” tab

2. In the “View” field, select Velavu mode

3. Specify:

  • Period from

  • Period to

    4. In the “Objects” field, select one or more Velavu objects whose history you want to view

After that, records for the selected objects appear in the table below.

The following columns are usually displayed for each record:

  • Name — the Velavu object name

  • RFID — if RFID data is available

  • Type — the object type, for example: Anchor (ANCHOR) or tag (TAG)

  • Date — the date and time of the record

  • Building — the building the record relates to

  • Floor — the floor where the object was located

  • Duration — how long the object stayed in this state or place

  • Sensor — related sensor data, if any

  • Actions — buttons for viewing and playback

You can customize which columns are displayed:

1. In the header of any column, click the arrow . A menu with column settings appears, where you can:

• Sort the data in ascending or descending order

• Choose which columns to show on the screen

2. To choose which columns to show:

  • Click “Columns” — a list of parameters available for display in the list opens

  • Select the check boxes next to the parameters you want to see

What you can do in the history

1. View records by object

The history is grouped by each selected object.

For each object, you can expand the list of records and view its history over time.

2. View the object on the map

If you select a record in the list, a map is displayed on the right. On the map, you will see the position of the object at the time of the record

3. Play back movements

Next to each device there is a player — a play button and a slider.

With the player, you can see how the device moved around the site over time

4. View the device card

Next to each record there is an icon . Click it to open the Velavu device card.

The card opens with exactly the data that was present when the record was created.
rfid-metki-2:
The “RFID tags” module is designed for creating and managing RFID tags, which are used for automatic identification of objects in the monitoring system.

Tags help the system determine which object a vehicle interacted with. For example, they can be used to determine which container a garbage truck serviced or which checkpoint a vehicle visited.

In the module, you can:

— add RFID tags and combine them into groups

— check the time of the last read

— view the location of a tag on the map

— view the read history

How RFID tags work

RFID requires two elements:

— RFID reader — a device on the vehicle that detects nearby tags

— RFID tag — a device with a unique identifier, installed on a container, trailer, equipment, or another object

When a tag comes within range of the reader:

1. The RFID reader on the vehicle detects the tag

2. The reader receives the tag's unique identifier and transmits it to PILOT

3. PILOT looks for a tag with this identifier in the RFID tag directory

4. If the tag is found, the system updates the information about its last read

5. If automatic actions are defined for the tag or its associated object, the system performs them

Where RFID tags are used

Automatic trailer linking

An RFID tag is installed on the trailer and a reader on the tractor unit. When the trailer comes within range of the reader, PILOT recognizes the tag and can automatically link the trailer to the vehicle.

Route control

RFID or BLE tags are installed at checkpoints: at stops, warehouses, company premises, and other locations. When a vehicle is near a tag, PILOT records the visit to the checkpoint.

Container servicing control

RFID tags are installed on containers, and readers on garbage trucks or other service machinery. On each read, PILOT saves information about the container, the time and place of service, and the vehicle that performed the work.

Vehicle identification

RFID tags help recognize vehicles when entering company premises, passing checkpoints, and performing production operations.

Driver identification

A personal RFID tag can be assigned to a driver. After the read, PILOT identifies the driver and can link a trip, events, or completed work to them.
kak-podgotovit-rfid-metki-k-rabote:
Before you start, install an RFID reader, connect it to the tracker, and set up the transmission of identifiers to PILOT.

1. Install the hardware

1. Install the RFID reader on a vehicle or other machinery

2. Connect the reader to the tracker that transmits data to PILOT

3. Attach RFID tags to the objects you need to recognize. Tags can be attached, for example, to containers, trailers, equipment, checkpoints, and stationary and movable objects

2. Configure the RFID reader in PILOT

1. Add an RFID sensor to the object's sensors

2. Select the device field in which the reader transmits the tag identifier

3. Save the settings

After configuration, PILOT starts receiving identifiers from the hardware and looking for matching records in the RFID tag directory.

If the reader transmits an identifier that is not in the RFID tag directory, the system cannot match it with an existing record. Such a tag may be displayed as Unknown.

Once an RFID tag with the corresponding identifier is added to the system, PILOT will recognize it correctly on subsequent reads.

4. Add the RFID tags used on your objects to the directory.

For each tag, specify its unique ID and other required parameters. After saving, PILOT will be able to match the identifiers received from the reader with the tags you created. For detailed instructions, see the article “How to manage RFID tags”.

RFID in the object card

The object card has an RFID field. In it, you can specify the identifier of the tag associated with this object.

For example, if the monitoring object is a container with an RFID tag, enter the identifier of the installed tag in the field. PILOT uses this information in the RFID module and when generating reports.
kak-upravlyat-rfid-metkami:
In the “RFID tags” module, you can add and edit tags, combine them into groups, search for the records you need, and load data from Excel.

How to add an RFID tag

To create a new RFID tag:

1. Go to the “RFID tags” tab

2. Click the “Add” button

The RFID tag creation card opens.

Fill in the required fields:

  • ID — the unique identifier of the RFID tag. It is usually entered manually, using the identifier that the RFID reader transmits when it reads the tag. In some cases, the ID may be assigned automatically after the hardware reads the RFID tag for the first time.

  • Name — the name of the RFID tag under which it will be displayed in the system

  • Group — the group the tag belongs to

  • Description — additional information about the tag

  • Latitude and longitude — approximate coordinates of the RFID tag location. For example, if the RFID tag is attached to a container site, a checkpoint, or another stationary object, you can save its coordinates in the system

  • Fixed tag — enable this parameter if the tag is in a permanent location and does not move. A stationary RFID tag can be linked to a geofence, to a route point, or to a bus stop. In this case, PILOT will take the tag read into account when determining visits to these zones

    3. Click “Save”. After saving, the tag appears in the general list

How to create an RFID tag group

If the group you need does not exist in the system yet, you can create it when adding or editing a tag.

1. In the “Group” field, enter the name of the new group

2. Fill in the other tag parameters

3. Click “Save”

The new group is created automatically and becomes available when you add subsequent RFID tags.

How to edit an RFID tag

1. Double-click the tag in the list

2. Change the required parameters

3. Click “Save”

How to find an RFID tag

To search, use the group filter or the search bar.

1 — Search by group

Select a group above the list. After you select it, the table is updated and only the records that belong to this group remain.

2 — Search by name or ID

Enter a known value in the search bar. Only the records that match the query remain in the list.

To show all tags again, clear the search bar.

Toolbar commands

The top panel of the module provides commands for creating, updating, importing, exporting, and displaying RFID tags.

Add — create an RFID tag

Export to Excel — save the tag list to an XLSX file

Import from Excel — load RFID tags from an XLSX file to add or update the tag list. Before importing, make sure the file structure matches the Excel template

Download Excel template — download a file template for importing RFID tags. Fill in the required fields in the template and save the file, then use “Import from Excel” and upload the completed file

Refresh — refresh the RFID tag list without reloading the page

Icon color settings — configure the color display of RFID tags on the map depending on when the latest data was received

Show on map — display the selected RFID tags on the map. Before using it, select one or more tags in the list

Clear map — remove all displayed RFID tags from the map

RFID tag actions

Additional actions are available for RFID tags in the list.

Show on map — view the last known location of the RFID tag on the map

Tag history — view the usage history of the RFID tag

Delete tag — delete the RFID tag from the system
kak-proverit-mestopolozhenie-i-istoriyu-:
In the “RFID tags” module, you can check the last read, show a tag on the map, and view its usage history.

How to check the last read

When a vehicle detects an RFID tag, PILOT automatically updates the information in its row.

The list shows:

1 — Updated: the date and time of the last information update

2 — Last update: how much time has passed since the read

3 — Vehicle: the monitoring object that last read the tag

The vehicle appears in the row after the tag has actually been read. Physical contact between the reader and the tag is not required. It is enough for the tag to be within range of the hardware.

How to show one tag on the map

1. Find the actions menu in the tag row

2. Select “Show on map”

The map moves to the last known location of the tag and shows a marker.

Click the marker to open a tooltip. It shows:

— the date and time of the last update

— the tag name

— the tag ID

— coordinates, which you can copy

— the address

To close the tooltip, click the cross in its upper-right corner or select another marker.

How to show several tags

1. Select one or more tags in the list

2. On the toolbar, click “Show on map”

Markers for the selected tags appear on the map.

How to view the history of an RFID tag

With it, you can:

What is a geofence?

A geofence is a designated area on the map that you create to monitor the movement of objects.

A geofence can have any shape:

  • Polygon — for example, the territory of a company or an entire city

  • Circle — a zone with an arbitrary radius

  • Line — for example, a specific street or road section

You can configure automatic notifications about entering or leaving a geofence, and view reports on all geofence-related events in the “Reports” section.

To create and work with geofences, you must have the appropriate access rights.

3. Configure additional parameters:

  • Idle control — specify the time in minutes after which staying in the zone is considered idle time. For example, if you specify 15 minutes, the system records an idle period if the object stays in the zone longer than this time. If you specify 0, idle time in this zone is not counted (this is the default value). Idle data can be viewed in the dedicated idle reports and in summary reports

  • Speed control — set a speed limit for objects within this geofence

  • Zone type — choose whether the zone is a working zone or a restricted zone:

— working geofence — an area where the object should be and perform its tasks (for example, a warehouse, a construction site, a route)

— restricted geofence — an area the object must not enter (for example, private property, hazardous or closed areas, military facilities)

  • Alert type — configure the alert type in this zone:

— idle in zone — the system sends an alert if the object stays in the zone longer than the set time

— border crossing — the system sends an alert when the object enters or leaves the geofence

— idle in zone and border crossing — the system sends an alert on either of these events

  • Recalculate geofences for (number of days)

If you changed the geofence parameters or have just created a new one, you can recalculate the events for this zone for a past period (for example, the last 7 days).

To do this, select the “Recalculate geofences for” check box and choose the number of days. The system recalculates all events (entries, exits, idle periods, and so on) for the selected period using the new settings.
