A stationary RFID tag can be linked to a geofence. PILOT takes its read into account when determining a visit and records the event even when the object's GPS coordinates are temporarily inaccurate.

RFID tag management is available if:

— you have administrator rights

— the RFID tags module is connected for the account

— the geofence belongs to the account and is available for editing

How to prepare an RFID tag

Before linking, add the RFID tag to the system:

1. Open the “Main” section and go to the “RFID tags” tab

2. Create a new tag or edit an existing one

3. Specify the tag ID. It must match the identifier transmitted by the RFID reader

4. Specify the latitude and longitude. The tag coordinates must be inside the geofence you want to link it to

5. Enable the “Fixed tag” parameter

6. Click “Save”

If the tag coordinates are outside the geofence, PILOT does not allow linking. In this case, check the tag coordinates or the geofence boundaries.

How to link an RFID tag

  • Open the “Main” section and go to the “Geofences” tab

2. Select the check box next to the geofence you need to display it on the map

3. Make sure the RFID tag is inside the geofence

4. Right-click the geofence and select “Manage RFID tags”

5. Find the tag you need and select it in the link column.

To search for a tag by name or identifier, use the “Search” field.

To show only the tags already linked to the selected geofence, click “Linked”

6. Click “Save”

The RFID tag is linked to the geofence. If the tag coordinates are outside it, PILOT does not allow linking.

How a visit is determined

When an object detects an RFID tag linked to a geofence, PILOT takes this read into account regardless of the current GPS coordinates. Therefore, a visit can be recorded even if, according to GPS data, the object is outside the geofence.

A geofence visit is the period between entry and exit, not each individual tag read.

An exit is recorded when both conditions are met:

— the object no longer detects the linked RFID tag

— according to GPS data, the object is outside the geofence

Therefore, several RFID tag reads do not always create several visits. For example, if an object moved away from the tag and then detected it again, but according to GPS stayed inside the geofence all this time, the current visit does not end.

How to view tag details on the map

Click the RFID tag on the map to open a tooltip.

The tooltip shows:

  • the date and time of the last read

  • the tag name

  • the tag identifier

  • coordinates

  • the address

The tooltip header shows the object that last detected the RFID tag. If the tag has never been read, there is no object information.

kak-rabotat-s-platnoj-dorogoj:
A special menu is provided for configuring a toll road.

Left-click the toll road you need, and you will see the following functions:

  • Gates — configure entry and exit points

  • Scheduler — set conditions and rates for the toll road

  • Delete — delete the toll road

    How to add toll gates

Gates are points on a toll road that record the moment an object enters and exits the tolled section. Thanks to gates, the system determines exactly when an object started and finished driving on the toll road.

For accurate accounting of the start and end of the tolled section, add entry and exit points — gates.

How to add gates:

1. Open the toll road menu and select “Gates”

  1. Click to add a new point

3. Enter the gate name

4. Select the gate type:

  • Entry — marks the place where vehicles enter the toll road

  • Exit — marks the place where vehicles leave the toll road

  • Composite (or complex) — can be both an entry and an exit

    5. A gate marker appears on the map. You can move it to the right place.

    6. After the gates are added, click “Save”.

Depending on the structure of the toll road and the traffic patterns, the system supports different gate configuration options. This lets you account for all trips accurately and correctly calculate the toll for any route.

As examples, let us look at two main scenarios: using simple gates and complex gates.

Simple gates

Simple gates are the option where the entry and exit points are located on the same line (the same section of the toll road). In this case, you simply mark the start and end of the tolled section, and the system records all trips between these two points.

For example, a vehicle enters the toll road through “Gate 1” and exits through “Gate 2” on the same section.

Even if GPS is temporarily lost on the road (for example, in a tunnel), the system still remembers where the entry and exit were and correctly calculates the toll.

Complex gates

Complex (or composite) gates are the option where the entry and exit can be on different lines (different sections of toll roads). You can link one line as an entry with another line as an exit, and there can be several such combinations. Such gates are convenient for complex traffic layouts, when a toll road has several routes, interchanges, entries, and exits. They let you account for trips between different sections of toll roads.

For example, a vehicle enters the toll road through “Gate A” (on one section) and exits through “Gate B” (on another section). You can create several such links, for example: “Entry 1” — “Exit 1”, “Entry 2” — “Exit 2”, and so on.

How to create complex gates:

  1. Create toll roads on the map

Draw the first section of the toll road on the map as a polyline, set its width, and give it a clear name, for example, Polyline_North.

Draw the second section of the toll road and name it, for example, Polyline_South

2. Go to the settings of one of the toll roads, for example, Polyline_North

3. In the toll road menu, select “Gates”

4. Click to add gates

5. Enter the gate name, for example, North_to_South

6. Select the gate type — composite (complex)

7. In the Link zone field, select the second toll road you want to link these gates to, for example, Polyline_South. In the “Location” field, the coordinates are filled in automatically.

8. Click “Save”

9. Configure rates and schedule

For this composite pair of gates, you can open the “Scheduler” and set individual rates and a schedule for the route between, for example, Polyline_North and Polyline_South

10. If necessary, create the reverse direction for the second toll road

This way, if a vehicle enters the toll road through the gate on Polyline_North and exits through the gate on Polyline_South, the system determines that this is the North_to_South route and applies the corresponding rate and schedule.

How to work with the scheduler

The scheduler is a tool for configuring the conditions of travel on a toll road.

How to configure the scheduler:

1. Open the toll road menu

2. Select “Scheduler”

3. In the “Scheduler” window, configure the parameters

  • Traffic periods:

    For each day of the week (weekdays, Saturday, Sunday), set the time intervals you need:

    — normal

    — high

    — peak

    For each period, specify its own time frame, for example, 08:00–10:00 — high traffic.

  • Rates for different vehicle types:

    For each time period, specify the toll for:

    — motorcycles and passenger cars

    — buses and trucks

    — trucks with trailers

  • Tolerance

    Click the tolerance button and specify the allowed delay or deviation time so that the system does not treat minor lateness as a violation.

4. After filling in all the parameters, click “Save” at the bottom of the window. The conditions of travel on the toll road are taken into account automatically according to your settings.

How to delete a toll road

To delete a toll road, open the toll road menu and select “Delete” — after that, the toll road disappears from the zone list and is no longer displayed on the map.

With it, you can configure:

— on which days and hours an object may operate

— how long continuous driving is allowed

— how long rest should last during the day, at night, and over 24 hours

— the maximum time on a route, in a zone, or between zones

Based on these settings, the system generates violation notifications — for example, about overwork, insufficient rest, or staying on a route too long.

How to configure the working time of an object

1. Go to the “Online” tab

2. Select the object you need in the list

3. Double-click it to open the card

4. In the left panel, select the “Working time” tab

The tab consists of several blocks:

Days of the week

Select the check boxes for the days on which the object may operate

Schedule

  • Weekdays (Mon–Fri)

  • Saturday

  • Sunday

To set the time:

1. Click the icon next to the row you need

2. In the window that opens:

  • Click

  • Specify the working interval

  • If necessary, add several intervals

    3. Save the changes

Night time

The “Night time” block defines the period of the day that is considered night.

Specify:

— the start time of the night period

— the end time of the night period.

These settings are used to calculate night rest and generate the corresponding notifications.

Alert settings

This is where you set the threshold values; when they are exceeded, the system generates notifications.

Available parameters:

  • Driving duration (min.) — the allowed time of continuous movement without a break

  • Rest time — day (min.) — the daytime rest standard

  • Rest time — night (min.) — the nighttime rest standard (within the night period)

  • Rest time per 24 hours (min.) — the minimum total rest per 24 hours

  • Max. driving time between zones (min.) — the maximum travel time between geofences

  • Max. parking time in zone (min.) — the maximum allowed parking time in a geofence

  • Max. time on route (min.) — the maximum allowed time on a route from the start to the end of the trip.

The object's actual figures are compared with these values. If a violation is recorded, the system can create a notification.

How to configure the working time of a driver

  • Saturday

  • Sunday

To set the time:

1. Click the icon next to the row you need

2. In the window that opens:

  • Click

  • Specify the working interval

    5. Save the changes

If you try to assign a driver to a vehicle outside working hours, the system shows a warning and prevents the operation.

Default working time settings at the contract level

In the admin panel, you can set default working time settings and restrictions for the Time control module at the contract level.

These parameters are used as a template:

— when adding new objects

— for objects that have never had their own settings saved on the “Working time” tab

That is, you configure the settings once in the contract — and when an object is created, these values are automatically filled into its card. If necessary, they can be changed at the level of a specific object.

You can specify only the parameters you want to make defaults. The remaining fields use system values or are filled in manually.

The “Violation control” module automatically tracks speeding by a vehicle.

While the vehicle is moving, the system compares its actual speed with the speed allowed on the current road section. If the speed exceeds the allowed value by more than the set threshold, the system registers a speed violation.

How to configure violation control

1. Open the object card — double-click the object in the object list

2. Go to the “Violation control” tab

  1. Select the “Speed violation” check box to enable speeding control

4. Set a value in the “Allowed speed excess threshold” field

  1. If necessary, select the “Send alerts” check box to receive notifications about registered violations

6. Click “Save”

After saving, the system starts tracking speeding according to the specified settings.

Configuration parameters

Speed violations

Enables or disables speeding control for the selected object.

If the check box is selected, the system tracks the driving speed and records violations according to the specified settings.

Allowed speed excess threshold

Determines by how much the vehicle's speed must exceed the allowed speed on the road for the system to register a violation.

For example, if:

  • the allowed speed on the road section is 80 km/h;

  • the set threshold is 20 km/h,

a violation is registered only when the vehicle's speed exceeds 100 km/h.

Send alerts

If you select this check box, the system sends a notification each time a violation is registered.

Data on recorded speed violations is available in the “Events” module

Speed limits

When detecting speeding, the system uses the speed limits for each road section.

By default, this data is taken from the OpenStreetMap (OSM) mapping service. The system stores an allowed speed value for each road type, which is used when calculating violations.

If necessary, these values can be changed. To do so, click “Change speed limit values”.

A table of speed limits for various road types and vehicle categories opens.

The first column shows the road types used by OpenStreetMap. The names are displayed as internal OSM identifiers. For example: AT:rural — rural roads in Austria, DE:urban — urban roads in Germany, bus_guideway — a road intended for bus traffic.

For each road type, you can set separate speed limits for different vehicle categories:

  • General — the default value

  • Trucks — for trucks

  • Buses — for buses

  • Passenger cars — for passenger cars

If a vehicle category has its own value set, the system uses exactly that value when detecting a violation.

How to change a speed limit

1. Click “Change speed limit values”

2. Find the road type you need

3. Double-click the cell with the vehicle category you need

4. Enter the new speed limit value.

5. Click “Save”

6. Close the window and click “Save” in the object card

The recalculation module reprocesses an object's data for a selected period and updates information about trips and geofence visits if settings have changed or information was displayed incompletely.

Two types of recalculation are available:

  • Trips — the system regenerates the object's trips

  • Geofences — the system reprocesses data on the object's presence in geofences

How to start a recalculation

1. Go to the “Main” section → “Online” tab

2. Find the object you need in the list

3. Right-click it

4. Select “Data recalculation”

5. In the “Recalculation type” field, select which data to update:

  • Trips — the system recalculates the object's trips

  • Geofences — the system reprocesses data related to the object's presence in geofences

    6. In the “Number of days” field, specify the recalculation period

    7. Click “Start”

After the start, the request is queued for processing.

Recalculation does not run immediately. Processing time depends on the selected period and the amount of data. The longer the period, the longer the recalculation may take.

After processing is complete, the results are available in the recalculation history.

How to view the recalculation result

To check the status of a recalculation, click “History” in the “Data recalculation” window.

A list of all recalculations that were run for the selected object opens. Here you can check the recalculation parameters, its status, and the processing result.

The table shows:

  • Object — the object the recalculation was run for

  • Recalculation type — trips or geofences

  • Days — the number of days selected at launch

  • Requested — the date and time the request was sent

  • Processed — the date and time of processing or of the last status update

  • Result — the current status and information about the recalculation

If the “Processed” and “Result” fields are not yet filled in, the recalculation may be queued or in progress. Open the history later to check its status.

After a trip recalculation, the result may show:

  • Run time — the processing duration in seconds

  • Agents — the number of processed messages from the object

  • Points — the number of processed points

  • Tracks — the number of generated trips

  • Parkings — the number of generated parkings

After a geofence recalculation, the result may contain service records, execution time, and the number of processed geofences. This information is used mainly for diagnosing the system. For normal operation, it is enough to make sure the recalculation completed successfully.

If the recalculation did not start, finished with an error, or no data appeared after it, contact support.

The “Trailers” module is designed for creating, configuring, and managing trailers used together with monitoring objects.

A trailer can be used in two ways:

— as an information object — it stores trailer data and can be linked to a vehicle

— as a monitoring object — it has its own GPS tracker and sensors and transmits data to the system

After a trailer is linked to a vehicle, the system displays them as a single combination and lets you track information about both the tractor unit and the trailer itself.

In this article, we will explain how to:

— create a trailer

— configure trailer parameters

— link a trailer to a vehicle

— view trailer information on the map and in the object list

— work with the link history

— delete a trailer

How to create a trailer

1. Go to the “Trailers” tab

2. Click the Add button

The trailer creation card opens.

Fill in the required parameters and click “Save”.

Trailer parameters

  • Trailer name — the name under which the trailer is displayed in the system

  • Associated object — select the monitoring object from which the trailer receives location data, sensor states, and other parameters.

The associated object is not the vehicle the trailer will be attached to, but the monitoring object whose data relates to this trailer.

Type — select the trailer type

If the type you need is not in the list, contact technical support to have it added.
  • Width — specify the trailer width and select the unit of measurement: millimeters, centimeters, meters

  • Group — select the group the trailer will belong to

  • RFID — the RFID code transmitted by the vehicle's RFID sensor when a trailer is connected. Using this identifier, the system automatically determines which trailer is connected to the vehicle.

  • Description — additional information about the trailer.

Additional parameters

  • Exclusive — determines the order in which trailers are linked.

If the parameter is enabled, when this trailer is connected, all other trailers previously linked to the vehicle are automatically unlinked. Use this parameter if only one trailer can be connected to a vehicle at a time.

  • Agro — used together with the agriculture module (Agro). Enable this parameter only for objects that work with the agro module functionality.

  • Send alerts — enables sending notifications about events related to this trailer

Access to objects

Select in the list the objects for which this trailer will be available. If you leave the field empty, the trailer is available to all objects.

How to link a trailer

You can link a trailer to a vehicle in two ways.

Through the trailer card

At the bottom of the card, open the “Objects” section.

Select with check boxes one or more vehicles to which you need to grant access or link the trailer.

To find the object you need, you can use:

  • the filter

  • search with match highlighting — the characters found are highlighted in yellow

After selecting the objects, click “Save”.

Through the object card

1. Select the object in the list

2. Right-click it

3. In the context menu, select “Trailers”

4. Do one of the following:

  • Link — to connect a trailer

  • Unlink — to disconnect a previously linked trailer.

Working with trailers

After a trailer is linked:

— the object icon on the map changes to a vehicle-with-trailer icon

— the name of the connected trailer appears in the “Trailer” column of the object list

Information on the map

You can view the object's tooltip on the map with information about the trailer.

To open the object's tooltip, left-click its icon.

If trailer display is enabled in the settings, the object's tooltip shows information about the connected trailer. If there is an associated object, you can view the data coming from the trailer's GPS tracker.

To enable trailer display in the tooltip:

1. Go to “Contract settings”

2. Open the “Personalization” tab

3. In the “Tooltip elements” section, select the “Trailer” check box

4. Save the changes

Information in the object list

To view trailer information in a tooltip, hover over the object in the list.

For the tooltip to be displayed in the object list, in “Personalization” select the “Show object tree tooltips” option.

Trailer history

A link history is available for each trailer.

To open the history:

1. Right-click the trailer on the “Trailers” tab

2. Select “Show history”

The history shows:

  • the RFID code

To delete a record from the history, click the icon .

1. Right-click the trailer on the “Trailers” tab

2. Select “Delete”

The dashboard is a screen with visual data in the form of diagrams and charts.

How to work with the dashboard:

  1. Expand the dashboard to full screen to work with the analytics
  • Find the button

  • Click it — the dashboard opens in full-screen mode, and you can focus only on the charts

The dashboard includes a pie chart with the number of service reminder statuses.

This chart shows how many vehicles are in each service reminder status:

  • Active

  • Overdue

  • Completed

  • Service needed soon

The dashboard also has a chart with maintenance costs. It shows information about the cost of service maintenance by month.

Object analytics

To view the analytics of a specific object:

1. Find the “Analytics” column in the object list.

2. Click the chart icon

You will go to the detailed analytics, where you can calculate:

  • Life cycle estimate

  • Maintenance cost estimate

  • Fuel cost estimate

In the analytics of a specific object, you manage the data yourself and customize the analytics to your needs. You can change the parameters at any time and immediately see the updated calculations.

Analytics chart

The chart shows how the cost of owning the object changes over the years.

All data on the chart is calculated based on the values you enter in the sections:

  • Life cycle estimate

  • Maintenance cost estimate

  • Fuel cost estimate

When you change these parameters, the chart is updated automatically.

What is shown on the chart:

  • Bars show expenses by year:

    — maintenance costs

    — fuel costs

    — planned and actual values

  • The TCO line shows the total cost of ownership of the object for each year

  • The depreciation curve helps you see how the value of the object decreases over time

  • Cost per km shows the average cost of one kilometer of mileage, planned and actual

Life cycle estimate

Fill in the following fields:

  • Estimated service life (in months)

Specify the service life of the object or equipment in months. For example: 60 months for a car.

  • Expected purchase price.

    This is the price you expected to spend on the object.

  • Disposal cost estimate

How much you plan to spend on disposing of or writing off the object at the end of its service life.

  • Estimated annual mileage (in miles)

If it is, for example, a car, specify how many miles it travels per year.

  • Actual purchase price

The real amount that was spent on the purchase.

  • Estimated residual value

How much the object will be worth at the end of its service life.

  • Fuel consumption (l/km)

Specify how many liters of fuel are consumed per kilometer.

Depreciation method

Choose the depreciation calculation method that suits your object:

  • Accelerated or double-declining balance method

Writes off the value quickly in the first years. A doubled straight-line depreciation rate is applied to the residual value.

For example:

A car costs $10,000, service life is 5 years

Straight-line rate = 1/5 = 20%

Doubled rate = 40%

Year 1: 10,000 × 40% = $4,000

Year 2: (10,000 – 4,000) × 40% = $2,400

This method is usually used for assets that lose value quickly or provide more benefit at the beginning of their service life.

  • Sum of years' digits

A smoother way of writing off value than the accelerated method. First, all years of the service life are summed, then each year's share of this sum is calculated.

For example:

Service life: 5 years

Sum of years: 1+2+3+4+5 = 15

Year 1: 5/15 of the value

Year 2: 4/15

Year 3: 3/15 and so on

The method is suitable for assets with uneven wear but without a sharp drop in value.

Maintenance cost estimate

Enter planned and actual values by year. This shows how closely expenses match expectations.

Fuel cost estimate

Similarly, set the plan and actual for each year.

3. Confirm the action

The “Transactions” tab displays operations made with fuel cards. Here you can find the operation you need, view refuel details, and check whether the object's location matches the gas station coordinates.

How to find transactions

1 — Transaction period

2 — Fuel card selection

After you select the parameters, operations for the specified period appear in the table.

How to view operation details

Select the transaction you need in the table. The “Operation details” area opens on the right side of the screen.

It shows:

  • the company — the data provider

  • the fuel card number

  • the date and time of the operation

  • the gas station

  • the object's location

  • the odometer reading

  • the fuel type

  • the fuel quantity

  • the price

  • the total amount

  • the refuel volume according to the sensor

  • the coordinate matching result

  • a map with the object's location

Coordinate matching check

PILOT compares the object's location at the time of the operation with the saved coordinates of the gas station. The coordinates are considered matching if the distance between the object and the gas station does not exceed 100 meters.

The result is displayed in the “Coordinate match” field:

  • green “Match” status — the object was near the specified gas station

  • red “No match” status — the object was more than 100 meters from the saved gas station coordinates

A lack of a match does not always mean an incorrect operation. The cause may be inaccurate gas station coordinates, an error in determining the object's location, or missing data.

If the fuel card is not linked to an object, PILOT cannot determine its location for the check. In this case, a message appears saying that the card is not linked to an object.

If no coordinates are specified for a gas station, contact technical support. Provide the name or identifier of the gas station, the address, latitude, and longitude.

Table settings

To change how the transactions table is displayed, click the arrow in the header of the column you need. In the menu that opens, you can:

— sort records in ascending or descending order

— select the columns to display

— group records by the selected parameter

— enable the grouped data view

To select columns:

1. Open the menu in the header of any column

2. Select “Columns”

3. Select the check boxes next to the data you want to see in the table

The “Composite objects” module is designed to combine several fuel objects and sensors into one logical object and track them as a single fuel accounting system.

It helps you build a clear fuel flow scheme — from source and storage to dispensing — and correctly calculate receipts, consumption, and balances.

The module is useful in the following scenarios:

— if a tanker truck with several compartments is used

— if there is a stationary gas station or fuel depot

— if you need to account for receiving, storing, and dispensing fuel within a single scheme

In the module, you can:

— create and configure composite objects

— add elements (objects) and sensors to them

— use them in reports and monitoring for fuel calculations

How to create a composite object

  1. Before creating a composite object, make sure the following are already configured in the system:

— the required objects (vehicles, tanks, and other elements that will be part of the scheme)

— the corresponding sensors

All objects and sensors must be added and configured correctly in advance — only after that can they be combined into a composite object.

2. Go to “Main” → “Composite objects”

3. Click the button to add an object

4. Enter the name of the composite object

5. It appears in the list on the “Composite objects” tab

How to add elements to a composite object

2. Click the button to add an element

3. Specify:

— object — an element of the composite object (select from the list)

— sensor (select from the list of the object's sensors)

— date

— element type — its role in the fuel scheme:

  • Tank — a container for storing fuel, for example, a tanker truck compartment, a stationary reservoir, a generator tank.

  • Input flow meter — measures the volume of fuel entering the system, for example, receiving at a fuel depot, filling a stationary tank, recording receipts before storage.

  • Flow meter — measures the volume of fuel leaving the tank, for example, refueling a vehicle, dispensing fuel to customers, supplying fuel to equipment.

  • Input tank — an external fuel source, for example, a large external supplier reservoir.

4. Click “Save”

The element becomes part of the composite object and appears in the list. Click it — it is displayed on the diagram.

Add all the required elements.

A notification is an automatic message that the system sends when a certain event defined in the settings occurs.

Notifications let you receive information about events, for example:

— engine start or stop

— speeding

— fuel level change

— refuel or fuel drain

— entering or leaving a geofence

— loss of connection with the device

— the need for maintenance

With notifications you can respond to events quickly and keep track of the state of objects in the system.

The “Notifications” module lets you set up:

— the conditions under which a notification is triggered

— the objects it applies to

— the delivery method, for example by email, SMS, Telegram, as a message in the system, or as a Push in the mobile app
kak-sozdat-uvedomlenie:
After the “Notifications” module is activated, a new “Notifications” tab appears in the contract settings.

Through this tab, you can configure the events for which the system sends notifications to users.

1. Go to “Contract settings” and open the “Notifications” tab

2. Click the button

3. The notification settings window opens

Basic notification parameters

1. Template

Select a notification template if you want to use ready-made settings.

A template is created after you configure a notification — to do this, fill in all the parameters and click “Save as template”. After that, you can reuse it.

2. Selection by objects or tags

Specify which objects the notification applies to:

  • By objects — select specific vehicles or equipment

  • By tags — use this if you need to apply the notification to a whole group of objects at once

3. Type and name

Set the notification name — it helps you quickly find it in the list and understand which event it is responsible for.

Select how you want to receive notifications:

  • SMS — a message to your phone

  • Push — a notification in the mobile app

  • Email — an email message

  • Alert — a pop-up notification in the interface of the system

  • Control Room — the event is displayed in the “Control Room”

  • Webhook — sending data to an external service

  • Command to device — sending a command to the tracker

  • Command template — sending a preconfigured command from a template to the device

  • Telegram — a notification through the Telegram bot

To receive notifications by Email, confirm your email address in your personal settings in advance.

If necessary, you can set an alternative message text — it is sent when the notification is triggered.

If the “Control Room” module is connected, the “Algorithm binding” button becomes available. With it, you can configure automatic event handling scenarios — for example, define a sequence of actions that runs when a certain event occurs.

4. Notification time

In the “Notification time” block, you can set the conditions under which the notification works:

— select the time zone

— specify the days of the week

— set time intervals

5. Additional information

Select the parameters you need — they are added to the notification text:

— driving speed

— the object's driver

— the geofence the object is in (if the “Geofences” module is connected)

— map link (Google)

— direct link to the event

— the event address

The direct link to the event opens the object on the map from the notification. After following it, you will see the object's current position and its main parameters.

The link is valid for a limited time, after which it becomes unavailable.

6. Notification types and conditions

When creating a notification, select the event on which it should be triggered.

For example:

— speeding

— sensor triggering

— parking or movement

— loss of connection

— other system events

Each notification type has its own trigger conditions. For example:

— speed threshold

— event duration

For more about notification types and conditions, read the separate article.

7. Geofence parameters
This setting is available if the “Geofences” module is connected.

In the notification settings, you can specify in which geofences the notification should be triggered.

To do this, select one or more geofences from the list or select all of them at once with the button .

Then select where exactly the notification should be triggered:

  • Everywhere — the notification is sent regardless of where the object is located

  • In selected zones — the notification is sent only if the object is inside the selected geofences

  • Outside selected zones — the notification is sent only if the object is outside the selected geofences

After configuring all notification parameters, click “Save”.

If you want to save the configured notification as a template so you can later use it as a template when configuring a new notification, click “Save as template”.
If you enable the “For all users” parameter, the notification is sent to all users of the account.

All created notifications are displayed on the “Notifications” tab in “Contract settings”. To learn how to work with this tab, read the article “How to work with the notification list”.

Watch an example of notification setup in a short YouTube video:
https://youtu.be/O4y0YhNp6b4

When you create a notification, you select the type of event the system will monitor and set up its trigger conditions.

The conditions determine when the notification is sent — for example, when a speed limit is exceeded, during a long parking stop, or when a sensor reading changes.

All available notification types are listed below.

Movement and route

  • Speed

  • Movement

  • Parking

  • Mileage

  • Routes

  • Scheduler

System and device status

  • Connection loss

  • Device problems

Sensors and events

  • Sensor events

  • Ignition operation

  • Ignition event

  • Sensor operation

  • Sensor value change

  • Multi-sensor events

  • Complex sensor event

  • Sensor faults

Indicators

  • Temperature

  • Humidity

  • Pressure

  • Fuel level

  • Refuels and fuel drains

    Geolocation and object events

  • Geofences

  • Proximity to an object

Advanced scenarios

  • Formula

  • Event media files

  • iButton duplication

  • Blocking for exceeding limits

How to set up conditions

1. Select the notification type

The notification type determines which event the system monitors — for example, speeding, parking, or a sensor trigger.

2. Set the parameters — for example, the speed threshold or duration

3. Add extra conditions if needed

To add another condition, click the button

To remove a condition, use the button

You can also change the order of conditions with the arrows

If a notification has several conditions, you can select a logical rule between them:

  • AND — the notification is triggered if all conditions are met at the same time

  • OR — the notification is triggered if at least one of the conditions is met

Main notification types

Speed

The notification is triggered if the object's speed meets the specified condition.

You can set the following conditions:

If the speed is:

— greater than the specified value

— less than the specified value

— equal to the specified value

You can also specify how long the condition must be met:

— seconds

— minutes

— hours

— kilometers of travel

For “Speed” notifications you can set a repeat interval. This helps you avoid a large number of identical notifications.

For example: if the speed exceeds 60 km/h for more than 60 seconds, the system sends a notification. The next notification appears only after the specified interval (for example, 5 minutes) if the speeding continues.

Ignition events

The “Ignition events” notification type is used to receive messages when the ignition state of an object changes.

Available conditions:

  • On — a notification is sent when the ignition is turned on

  • Off — a notification is sent when the ignition is turned off

  • On and off — a notification is sent for both events

  • Moving without the sensor on — a notification is sent if the object started moving but the ignition sensor is not on

If needed, you can enable the “Failure trigger” option. It helps you track recurring errors or unstable sensor operation.

When the option is enabled, additional fields become available:

  • Number of errors — how many times the error must repeat for the notification to be triggered

  • Reset time — after how many minutes the error counter is reset

Ignition operation

This notification type lets you monitor how long an object stays with the ignition on or off.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

  • Longer than — a notification is sent if the ignition stays on or off for longer than the specified value. Enter a number for the duration and select the unit: seconds, minutes, hours, kilometers of travel

  • Break duration — a setting that counts only events separated by a break of the specified length. For the break you also need to specify a value and a unit

Sensor events

The “Sensor events” notification type lets you receive notifications when the state of the selected sensor changes.

Available conditions:

  • On — a notification is sent when the sensor switches to the “on” state

  • Off — a notification is sent when the sensor switches to the “off” state

  • On and off — a notification is sent on any change of the sensor state

  • Moving without the sensor on — a notification is sent if the object started moving but the selected sensor is not on.

If needed, you can enable the “Failure trigger” option. It helps you track recurring errors or unstable sensor operation.

When the option is enabled, additional fields become available:

  • Number of errors — how many times the error must repeat for the notification to be triggered

  • Reset time — after how many minutes the error counter is reset

  • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to.

Sensor operation

With this notification type you can monitor how a sensor value changes and how long the sensor stays in a given state.

After selecting the type, set the conditions:

• No change for longer than — the notification is triggered if the sensor value does not change for longer than the specified time. You need to specify a numeric value and a unit.

• Longer than — the notification is triggered if the sensor stays in a certain state, or its value exceeds the condition, for longer than the specified time. You also need to set a value and a unit.

• Break duration — a setting that defines how long a break in sensor operation must be to end the current event.

• Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to.

If a sensor with the specified tag is on, the system starts counting its operating time. When the duration reaches the “Longer than” value, an event is created and a notification is sent.

After the notification is sent, no repeated notifications are sent for the same event while the sensor keeps working continuously.

If the sensor turns off, the system starts counting the break duration. If the sensor turns on again before the “Break duration” time has elapsed, the event is considered ongoing and no new notification is created.

If the sensor stayed off for at least the time specified in “Break duration”, the current event ends. The next period of the sensor being on is counted as a new event.

For example: if “Longer than” = 10 minutes and “Break duration” = 2 hours, a notification is sent after the sensor has been working for 10 minutes. A repeat notification appears only after the sensor has been off for at least 2 hours, then turns on again and works for more than 10 minutes.

Sensor value change

The “Sensor value change” notification type lets you track how much the value of the selected sensor has changed over a certain period of time.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

  • Difference greater than — enter a numeric value: how much the sensor value must change for the notification to be triggered. For example: 5 — if the value changes by more than 5 units.

If you enable the “by modulus |x|” option, the system takes a change in either direction into account — both an increase and a decrease.

  • Over a period — specify the time interval over which the change is analyzed: enter a number and select a unit (seconds, minutes)

  • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to.

Multi-sensor events

The “Multi-sensor events” notification type is used for sensors that work with a state table (for example, equipment status, device operating mode, switch positions).

Such a sensor can have several possible values, and the notification is triggered when its state changes.

Then set the conditions:

  • Changes only — if you enable this option, a notification is sent only when the sensor value changes

  • Ignore values outside the table — if you enable this setting, the system takes into account only the values listed in the sensor's table. All other values (not described in the table) are ignored, and no notification is sent for them

  • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to

Complex sensor event

The “Complex sensor event” notification type lets you set up a single notification for several sensor events at once.

Select the groups of sensors the condition applies to.

The “Reset time” field sets the period after which the system resets the event state.

Sensor faults

The “Sensor faults” notification type is designed to detect possible problems in sensor operation and to monitor that sensors work correctly.

This notification also works as a fault indicator:

— when a fault is detected, a yellow indicator appears next to the object status

— when a sensor goes into the failure state, a red indicator appears

You can enable one or several conditions at the same time:

  • Outside the calibration table — a notification is sent if the sensor value goes outside the calibration table for the specified period of time

  • No changes — a notification is sent if the sensor value does not change for the specified time

  • Number of changes — a notification is sent if the number of changes of the sensor value is greater or less than the set threshold over the specified period of time.

You can also take into account:

  • Geofence enter — sensor changes are counted only when entering a geofence

  • Geofence exit — sensor changes are counted only when leaving a geofence

  • Additional rule — lets you set an extra condition for detecting a fault. You need to specify:

— the sensor field name

— the condition: >, <, =

— the value

Handlers and formulas can be used.

  • Failure trigger settings — if a fault repeats several times, the sensor can go into the failure state.

The trigger settings define:

— Number of errors — how many faults must occur for the sensor to go into the failure state

— Reset time (min) — the error-free period after which the failure status is cleared automatically

  • Trigger reset rules — how long the object must stay parked or drive without errors for the fault status to be cleared automatically. You can set up the conditions under which the trigger is reset:

— parking time (in minutes)

— driving time (in minutes)

— if needed, set a formula

  • Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to

Device problems

The “Device problems” notification type is designed to detect incorrect tracker operation or data transmission errors.

You can enable one or several conditions at the same time:

  • Coordinates change without speed (Coords change without speed) — the notification is triggered if the object's coordinates change but its speed is zero. You need to specify a threshold and a unit

  • Speed without coordinates change (Speed without changing coords) — the notification is triggered if the device transmits a speed but the coordinates stay the same

  • Coordinates change — a notification is sent on a sudden or abnormal change of coordinates. You can set the parameters above which the event is considered a problem.

  • Additional rule — lets you set an extra condition for detecting a fault. You need to specify:

— the sensor field name

— the condition: >, <, =

— the value

  • Failure trigger settings — if the problem occurs several times, the device can go into the failure state. The trigger settings define:

— Number of errors — how many times the problem must repeat

— Reset time (min) — after how many error-free minutes the failure status is cleared

  • Trigger reset rules — you can set up the conditions under which the trigger is reset:

— parking time (in minutes)

— driving time (in minutes)

— if needed, set a formula

Pressure

The “Pressure” notification type is used to monitor pressure sensor readings. The notification is triggered if the pressure value meets the specified condition.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

• Condition — select how the system compares the pressure value:

— Greater than — the notification is triggered if the pressure becomes greater than the specified value

— Equal to — the notification is triggered if the pressure equals the specified value

— Less than — the notification is triggered if the pressure becomes less than the specified value

• Value — enter the numeric pressure value the sensor reading is compared with

• Longer than — specify how long the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered. Enter a number and select a unit:

— seconds

— minutes

— hours

— kilometers of travel

• Repeat interval — sets the pause between identical notifications if the condition continues to be met

For example: if the pressure is below the set value for more than 10 seconds, the notification is sent once. The next notification appears only after the specified interval if the condition still persists.

• Sensor groups — select the group of sensors the condition applies to

Temperature

This notification type is used to monitor temperature from the selected sensor, for example in a refrigerator unit, an engine, or other equipment.

Then set the conditions:

  • If the temperature — sets the main rule by which the system compares the sensor readings with the specified value in degrees Celsius (°C). Available options:

    — Greater than — the notification is triggered if the temperature exceeds the specified value

    — Equal to — the notification is triggered if the temperature is exactly equal to the specified value

    — Less than — the notification is triggered if the temperature drops below the specified value

    — Out of range — the notification is triggered if the temperature goes outside the set range (for example, below +2°C or above +8°C)

  • Longer than — lets you set the minimum time the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered. This helps filter out short and insignificant fluctuations (for example, when the refrigerator door is opened). In the “Units” field you can select the unit of this duration: seconds, minutes, hours.

  • No change for longer than — a separate condition that helps detect possible sensor faults when its readings “freeze” at one value. The notification is triggered if the temperature does not change for longer than the specified period of time.

  • Sensor groups — select which temperature sensors this rule applies to

Humidity

The “Humidity” notification type is used to monitor humidity from the selected sensor, for example in a cargo compartment or a refrigerator unit.

After selecting the type, set the conditions:

  • If the humidity:

— Greater than — the notification is triggered if the humidity is above the specified value

— Less than — the notification is triggered if the humidity is below the specified value

— Equal to — the notification is triggered if the humidity equals the specified value

— Out of range by — the notification is triggered if the humidity deviates from the set range by the specified value

  • Enter the numeric humidity value the system compares the sensor readings with. The value is set in percent (%).

  • Longer than — specify how long the condition must be met for the notification to be triggered:

— Seconds — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of seconds

— Minutes — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of minutes

— Hours — the condition is met for longer than the specified number of hours

  • No change for longer than — this setting lets you control situations when the humidity does not change for a set time. The notification is triggered if the humidity value stays unchanged for longer than the specified period

Connection loss

The “Connection loss” notification type is used to monitor loss of connection with an object. The notification is triggered if no data is received from the device within the specified time or distance.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

  • Longer than — specify how long the connection loss must last for the notification to be triggered:

— Seconds — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of seconds

— Minutes — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of minutes

— Hours — the notification is triggered if the connection loss lasts longer than the specified number of hours

— Kilometers — the notification is triggered if the object has traveled the specified distance without a connection

Mileage

The “Mileage” notification type is used to monitor an object's mileage by the odometer. It lets you receive notifications if the mileage is greater or less than the set value over the selected period.

After selecting the type, set the conditions:

  • If the mileage:

— Greater than — the notification is triggered if the object's mileage is greater than the specified value

— Less than — the notification is triggered if the object's mileage is less than the specified value

— Monthly limit exceeded — the notification is triggered if the mileage for the month has exceeded the set value

  • Units — enter the numeric mileage value the system compares the odometer data with. The value is set in kilometers.

  • Period — select the period over which the condition is checked:

— Total — the condition is checked for the entire period since the notification was created

— Per month — the condition is checked within the current month

— Per day — the condition is checked within the current day

Movement

The “Movement” notification type is used to monitor object movement. The notification is triggered if the object is moving for longer than the set time or covers the specified distance.

Set the conditions:

  • Longer than — specify how long the object must be moving for the notification to be triggered. Enter a number and select a unit:

— Seconds — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of seconds

— Minutes — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of minutes

— Hours — the notification is triggered if the movement lasts longer than the specified number of hours

— Kilometers — the notification is triggered if the object has traveled more than the specified distance

  • Break duration — this setting counts only movement events separated by a break of the specified length. If the break between two movement segments is shorter than the specified value, the system treats them as one continuous movement. For example, if you set a break of 10 seconds, a stop shorter than 10 seconds does not interrupt the movement event.

Parking

The “Parking” notification type is used to monitor object stops. The notification is triggered if the object stays still for longer than the set time.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

  • Longer than — specify how long the object must stay still for the notification to be triggered:

— Seconds — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of seconds

— Minutes — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of minutes

— Hours — the notification is triggered if the parking lasts longer than the specified number of hours

Geofences

The “Geofences” notification type is used to monitor geofence-related events. It lets you receive notifications when an object enters a geofence, leaves it, stops inside it, or passes through it without stopping.

Available conditions:

  • Entry — the notification is triggered when the object enters the selected geofence

  • Exit — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the selected geofence

  • Entry+Exit — a notification is sent both on entering and on leaving the geofence

  • Stop in geofence — the notification is triggered if the object stops inside the geofence

  • No stop in geofence — the notification is triggered if the object enters the geofence, does not stop in it, and then leaves it

  • Min. speed — for conditions related to a stop or no stop, you can specify a minimum speed. This parameter helps determine whether the object is considered moving or stopped inside the geofence

Fuel level

The “Fuel level” notification type is used to monitor the fuel level from the selected sensor on the object. The notification is triggered if the fuel level meets the specified condition.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

  • If the fuel level:

— Greater than — the notification is triggered if the fuel level is above the specified value

— Less than — the notification is triggered if the fuel level is below the specified value

— Equal to — the notification is triggered if the fuel level equals the specified value

  • Units — enter the numeric fuel level value the system compares the sensor readings with

Refuels and fuel drains

The “Refuels and fuel drains” (Fuel Refuelings & Drainings) notification type is used to monitor events related to changes in fuel level. It lets you receive notifications about refuels and fuel drains on an object.

After selecting this type, check which events should trigger the notification:

• Refuels — the notification is triggered when the system detects a refuel

• Drains — the notification is triggered when the system detects a fuel drain

• Refuel start — the notification is triggered at the moment a refuel starts

• Drain start — the notification is triggered at the moment a fuel drain starts

Proximity to an object

The “Proximity to an object” notification type is used to monitor the situation when one object approaches another within a set distance.

In this notification type, one object is treated as a moving geofence, and the system tracks when another object enters or leaves this zone.

After selecting this type, set the trigger condition:

If the distance to the object is:

  • Less than — specify the distance at which an object is considered to be near another object. The value is set in meters.

  • Longer than — specify how long an object must stay within the range of another object for the notification to be triggered. The value is set in seconds.

  • Enter — if you enable this option, the notification is triggered when the object enters the range of another object

  • Exit — if you enable this option, the notification is triggered when the object leaves the range of another object

  • Objects — select from the list the objects for which proximity will be tracked

The system compares the objects from the list and determines when one object is at the set distance from another. The object being approached is treated as a moving geofence. For example, if a vehicle from the selected list gets closer than 100 meters to another object and stays nearby for more than 30 seconds, the system sends a notification.

Formula

The “Formula” notification type is used to check a custom condition set as a formula. The notification is triggered if the formula result is true or false.

In the “Formula” field, enter the expression to check. You can use raw data fields, sensor values, handlers, and formulas in it.

The notification is triggered if the check result is:

• true — the condition is met

• false — the condition is not met

Blocking for exceeding limits

The “Blocking for exceeding limits” notification type is used to send a notification if an object was blocked because of a violation of the set limits.

If the system detects such a block, the notification is sent through the selected channel.

After selecting this type, specify the delivery method, for example:

• Email

• SMS

• Webhook

• Telegram

• Push

If Email is selected, notifications are sent to the specified email address.

This notification type is applied automatically to all existing objects and to all new objects created after it is set up.

Scheduler

The “Scheduler” notification type is used to monitor object movement during working and non-working hours according to its work schedule settings.

After selecting this type, set the trigger conditions:

• At the scheduled time — the notification is triggered if the object moves within the set working hours

• Outside the scheduled time — the notification is triggered if the object moves outside the set working hours

  • Longer than — specify how long the object must be moving for the notification to be triggered

  • Break duration — this setting takes breaks between movement events into account. If the break is shorter than the specified value, the system treats the movement as continuous. For example: if you set a break of 10 seconds, a short stop of less than 10 seconds does not interrupt the movement event.

Event media files

The “Event media files” notification type is used to send a notification when the device successfully uploads to the storage server a media file associated with a recorded event. This notification is triggered not at the moment of the event itself, but only after the file has been successfully transferred and saved on the server.

For example, a notification can be sent when the device uploads a photo of a violation, a video clip of the event, a snapshot from the driver's cabin or of the road situation, or another file created after the event was recorded.

Such a notification can be used for events related to ADAS / DMS violations and warnings, for example driver distraction, phone use, smoking while driving, fatigue, collision risk, lane departure, or harsh braking.

The “Repeat interval” parameter lets you set a pause between identical notifications if the device uploads several media files in a row for the same event.

iButton duplication

The “iButton duplication” notification type is used to detect situations when the same iButton is registered on more than one vehicle within a set period of time.

Such a notification helps detect incorrect driver identification. For example, if a driver used the same iButton on one vehicle and then on another, the system may assume that the driver switched to the other object and update the assignment. As a result, trip, driver, and report data may become incorrect.

After selecting this type, set the condition:

  • Over a period — specify the time during which the system checks whether the same iButton was used on more than one object. The notification is triggered if the same iButton is detected on several objects within the specified time.

For this notification type to work correctly:

— an iButton sensor must be set up on the objects

— the drivers module must be used

— the notification must be linked to the objects you want to monitor

Routes

The “Routes” notification type is used to monitor events on routes already assigned to an object. In the settings of this notification you select which route events you want to be notified about.

After assigning the vehicle to a route, the system starts comparing the object's trips with the assigned route:

— records entering and leaving the route

— takes passing checkpoints into account

— includes trips in route reports

In the settings of this notification type, you select which route events should trigger notifications:

  • In stop zone — the notification is triggered when the object is in the zone of a checkpoint or stop. The radius of this zone is set on the map when configuring the route.

  • Outside stop zone — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the zone of a checkpoint or stop. The zone boundary is also defined by the radius set when editing the route

  • Route entry — the notification is triggered when the object enters the route boundaries. The route boundaries are defined by its width set on the map

  • Route exit — the notification is triggered when the object leaves the route boundaries.

All created notifications are displayed on the “Notifications” tab in the “Contract settings”.

Here you can:

— view the list of all created notifications

— create new ones

— edit existing notifications and delete the ones you no longer need

— work with notification templates

— apply notifications to new objects automatically

Notification list

The table shows all notifications available in the current account.

For each notification the table shows:

  • ID — the internal notification identifier

  • User — the user who created the notification

  • Name — the notification name

  • Type — the type of event the notification works on

  • Date — the date and time the notification was created

  • Vehicle — the objects the notification is linked to

The following actions are available on the right of each row:

Edit — open the notification for editing

Delete — delete the notification

Notification templates

The tab provides notification export and import functions. You can use notifications that are already set up as templates and transfer them to another account.

1 — Export notifications

2 — Import notifications

Exporting notifications

When you export, the current list of notifications is saved to a JSON file.

1. Click “Export notifications”

2. The system creates a file in JSON format

You can use this file as a template — for example, to quickly set up notifications in another account.

During export, the following are automatically excluded from the file: vehicles, geofences, phone numbers, email addresses. This is because another account may have different objects and contacts. After import, you will need to specify this data manually.

Importing notifications

Import lets you load previously saved notifications from a JSON file.

Before importing, choose the suitable option:

  • Do not delete old notifications — the new ones are added to the existing ones

  • Delete old notifications — the current settings are replaced with the imported ones

How to import:

1. Select the file to upload

2. Click “Import”

Automatic notification assignment

The “Enable automatic notification assignment” option determines whether notifications are applied automatically to new objects.

If the option is enabled, all created notifications are automatically assigned to new objects that you add to the account.

If the option is disabled, you will need to add new objects to notifications manually.
kak-rabotat-s-webhook-uvedomleniyami:
A webhook is a way to automatically pass event data from the system to an external service or to your server.

For example, if a vehicle exceeds the speed limit, the system sends a request to the address you specified and passes the event information.

How webhook notifications work

1. You specify a URL — where to send the data

2. When the notification is triggered, the system sends a POST request with JSON

3. Your server receives the data and processes it as needed

Before you start, make sure that:

— the URL is correct and reachable

— the server responds with code 200 (OK)

— if the server does not respond or returns an error, the address is temporarily blacklisted

How to set up a webhook

1. Go to creating or editing a notification

2. In the “Type and name” block, select the webhook sending method

3. To set up webhook notifications, click the edit field — the Webhook Details window opens, where you set the data sending parameters.

In the Webhook Details window you will see three fields:

1. URL

Specify the address the data will be sent to.

2. Header

This is where the format of the transmitted data is specified. The required value is already set by default:

["ContentType: application/json"]
3. Body (request body)

This is the data that will be sent. The following template is used by default:

{
 "agent_id": "%AGENTID%",
 "vehiclenumber": "%VEHNUM%",
 "ts": "%TS%",
 "lat": "%LAT%",
 "lon": "%LON%",
 "speed": "%SPEED%",
 "data": "%DATA%",
 "zone": "%ZONE%",
 "driver": "%DRIVER%"
}
4. Variables for the request body
You can modify or extend the request body using the allowed variables from the list on the right.
Keep to the format — "value":  "%VALUE%". If the syntax is broken, the webhook will not work.

Allowed variables

  Variable
  What it passes
  %ACCOUNTID%
  Account ID
  %AGENTID%
  Object ID
  %VEHNUM%
  Vehicle number
  %TS%
  Timestamp
  %DATETIME%
  Date and time
  %LAT%
  Latitude
  %LON%
  Longitude
  %SPEED%
  Speed
  %ODO%
  Mileage (from the sensor)
  %DATA%
  Notification data
  %ZONE%
  Geofence
  %ZONE_ID%
  ID of the first geofence
  %ZONE_NAME%
  Name of the first geofence
  %DRIVER%
  Driver
  %MAXSPEED%
  Maximum speed (for speeding notifications)
  %DUR% 
  Duration of the violation
  %SPEEDLIMIT% 
  Set speed limit (Speed control)

How to insert a sensor value

If you need to pass the data of a specific sensor:

1. Open the “Sensors” tab

2. Copy the exact sensor name

3. Return to the webhook settings window and in the Body field insert the variable in the format %Sensor name%. For example, if the sensor is called Fuel sensor status, write %Fuel sensor status%.

How to get raw data

You can pass data directly from the device:

1. Go to the “Points” tab

2. Find the parameter in the “Raw data” column

3. Insert it into the Body field in the Webhook window in the format %Parameter name%. For example, if the parameter is called Valid, write %Valid%.

Request example

When the notification is triggered, your server receives data that looks roughly like this:

{
 "agent_id": 4328,
 "ts": 1545254055,
 "data": ["У286НМ 67", "Parkingdur", "2", "1", "мм"]
}

The data set depends on which variables you specified in the request body and which notification type is configured.

To start receiving notifications:

1. Go to “Contract settings” and open the “Privacy” tab

2. Find the “Notification settings” section

3. Check the notification types you want to receive:

  • Speed

  • Refuels

  • Connection loss

  • Idle time

  • Violation control

  • Drivers

4. For each selected notification type, choose how you want to receive it:

  • Email — notifications by email
To receive notifications by email, you need to confirm your email address.

  • Alert — a pop-up notification in the system

  • SMS — a message to your phone

  • Telegram — a message in Telegram

  • Push — a notification in the mobile app

5. Click “Save”
kak-prosmatrivat-uvedomleniya:
When an event configured in the system occurs, you receive a notification. It appears in the “Notifications” window.

The first time you sign in, this window may open automatically. If you closed or minimized it, open it again by clicking the notifications icon on the top bar.

kak-dobavit-ostanovki:
A stop is a geographic zone that a vehicle must visit while performing a trip along a route.

1. Go to the lower part of the workspace — this is where the list of all stops is located

2. Click the button to add a new stop

3. In the window that opens, specify:

  • Name and description

  • Coordinates: manually with the arrows or by moving the marker on the map

  • Stop radius (m) — the zone within which arrival is recorded

    If needed, check the boxes:

    — technical stop — not counted in boarding and alighting, but used in route calculation

    A technical stop is a point on the route that:
    — is not shown in the schedule of passenger trips
    — does not take part in boarding and alighting records — no passengers are recorded at it
    — takes part in building the route — for example, it helps lay out the path correctly
    — can be used to monitor bus movement — for example, as a checkpoint
    — does not affect passenger flow reports — its data does not go into boarding/alighting statistics

    — terminal stop — the point where the route ends and the return journey begins

    If you check the “Terminal” box for a stop, the system treats it as the last stop on the route:
    — the system truncates the route — all stops after this one are not used in the trip
    — the bus starts moving in the opposite direction — that is, it switches to the return schedule (if the trip is bidirectional)
    — only the stops up to and including this terminal stop are counted in the schedule and reports

4. Click “Save” — the stop appears in the list

The list shows all added stops with their ID, radius, type, and description.

To edit a stop, double-click it in the list and make the changes in the window that opens.

To delete a stop from the list, use the icon .

Once you add trips, the list shows all created trips and the number of stops in each of them.

Click the arrow next to a trip to expand its list of stops.

Each stop entry has an arrow — click it to open the menu and configure the route:

  • Forward / Back — change the order of the stop in the route

  • U-turn — specify that the vehicle turns around at this stop and starts moving in the opposite direction

To delete a stop from a trip, right-click it in the list and select “Delete”.

How to link an RFID tag to a stop

A stop visit can be detected by an RFID tag. When the vehicle reads the tag linked to a stop, the system processes the received data as a visit to that stop within the assigned bus line.

Before linking, add and configure the necessary tags in the “RFID tags” module. The tag must be within the stop radius.

To link RFID tags:

1. Create a stop or select an existing one

2. Click the tag icon next to the stop

3. In the “Stop RFID tags” window, find the tag you need by name or identifier

4. Check the box next to the tag

5. Select other tags if needed

6. Click “Save”

Several RFID tags can be linked to one stop. In this case the system can process a visit when any of them is read. To show only the tags that are already linked, check the “Linked” box.

If the tag you need is not in the list, check that it has been added and configured in the “RFID tags” module. Also make sure the tag is within the stop radius.

After linking, add the stop to a bus line, and then assign this line to a vehicle. Only after all these steps are completed can the system match the read RFID tag to the stop and process its visit.

raspisanie:
The “Schedule” module is used together with the “Trips” module. A schedule specifies the time at which a vehicle must pass the checkpoints of a trip or start the next pass along the route.

The “Trips” module defines the vehicle's route, and the “Schedule” module defines the planned travel time along this route.

How to create a schedule

To create a schedule:

3. Fill in the schedule parameters:

  • Name — enter the schedule name

  • Time — specify the planned time of passing the stops of the selected trip. Enter the time and click the button . Each value is added separately and appears in the list at the bottom of the form.

For example, for a trip with three consecutive stops you can add:

— 07:15 — the time of passing the first stop

  • Link to lap start — check the box if the added values should mark the start times of new laps

For example, if you add 07:12, 08:12, and 09:12, the vehicle must:

A new lap means the vehicle starting another pass along the selected route from its starting point.

4. Click “Save”
udobnyj-marshrut:
The integration passes data on trips and fare payments from the “Convenient Route” system to PILOT. Based on this data, you can analyze passenger flow and generate bus reports.

The setup consists of three stages:

1. The contract administrator enables the required modules

2. The server administrator sets up API access

3. The user links payment terminals to buses

Before you start the setup, prepare:

  • the login and password for API access

  • the API address

  • the Terminal ID of each payment terminal

Terminal ID is the identifier of the payment terminal installed in a bus. PILOT uses this identifier to determine which bus the trip and payment data belongs to.
  • the list of buses with terminals installed
Before the setup, prepare the API address, login and password, and the terminal identifiers for the buses. If you do not have this data, contact the contract administrator or PILOT support. The specialists will tell you where to get it.

  • access to the PILOT admin panel

  • access to the config.php file on the server

1. Enable the module

This stage is performed by the PILOT administrator

1. Open the admin panel

2. Go to the Contracts tab.

3. Select the contract you need and right-click it

4. Select “Edit”

5 In the contract card, go to the “Modules” tab and enable the “Convenient Route” and “Passenger flow” modules

6. After enabling the modules, go to “Module settings” in the contract card

7. Find and select the “Convenient Route integration” module

8. In the “Configs” block, add the parameters

   Key
  Value
  Purpose
  version
  2

  For example, Terminal ID, gosNum
 Defines the field the integration uses to match data to a bus

9. Click “Save”

2. Set up the API connection

This stage is performed by the server administrator.

Open the config.php file on the server and add the parameters:

// Удобный маршрут 2.0

Instead of the placeholders, enter the login and password received for your organization.

3. Specify the bus Terminal ID

marshruty-3:
The “Routes” module is designed for creating, editing, and monitoring route completion by vehicles.

With the module you can:

— create routes of any complexity

— set up checkpoints
