— analyze route completion in reports
kak-sozdat-marshrut:
To create a route in the system, you need to fill in the main parameters in the builder and add route points that will be displayed on the map. In this article we explain how to create a route and set its parameters so that the route is ready for use in the system.

How to create a route

1. Go to the “Routes” tab

2. Click the button — the “Build route” form opens

3. Fill in the route parameters

Main settings

1. Name

Enter a clear route name, for example: “Route No. 5”, “Downtown delivery”, “Warehouse — Customer”.

2. Detection range (km)

This parameter defines how far from the route line a vehicle is still considered to be on the route.

Simply put, the system creates a “corridor” around the route. For example, if you enter 0.3 km, this means 300 meters on each side of the route line.

As long as the vehicle moves inside this corridor, the system considers that it follows the route. If it leaves the corridor, a deviation from the route is recorded.

The value can be a fraction (for example, 0.3). A value that is too small (for example, 0.05 km) can cause false triggers because of GPS error. A value that is too large (for example, 5 km) will count serious detours as part of the route.

3. Geocoder

Select the service that automatically fills in the address from the coordinates of route points.

Control time

This is the planned time for completing the entire route.

For example, if the route usually takes 2 hours 30 minutes, enter 2 hours and 30 minutes.

This value is used in reports:

— to compare plan and actual

— to see whether the driver meets the standard

Route completion percentage

This parameter defines what percentage of points must be visited for the route to be considered completed.

For example, if 10 points are set and the percentage is 90%, the driver can skip one point and the route is still considered completed. This allows for force majeure on the road — for example, an accident or a traffic jam when the driver has to bypass part of the route.

  • “Active” check box

If you want the percentage rule to actually apply:

1. Enter the required percentage (for example, 80)

2. Check the “Active” box

3. Save the route builder

How to add route points

A route point is a checkpoint where the passage of a vehicle is recorded.

1. Go to the “Points” section below the route settings

2. Click the button

3. Select the place on the map or enter the address manually. The point appears on the map

4. If needed, drag the marker to the exact place

On the map, a point is shown as an icon with a number surrounded by a circle — the detection radius. This radius, which looks like a red dashed line on the map, determines when a vehicle has entered or left the checkpoint. If the vehicle enters the point radius, the system records the visit.

To change the point radius, click it with the left mouse button and drag it to the size you need.

The radius affects detection accuracy: the larger it is, the greater the allowed error in detecting a visit. A radius that is too large may count an arrival before the vehicle actually stops, and one that is too small may cause a point to be missed.

If the vehicle did not cross the checkpoint radius, the system does not record its visit — this is counted as a deviation from the route.

5. Repeat the process for the other route points and click “Save”

If you add two or more points, the system automatically builds a route between them.

How to link an RFID / BLE tag to a route point

A BLE tag is a small physical device (Bluetooth Low Energy) installed at a specific place, for example at a terminal stop or on a customer's premises.

When a vehicle approaches this point, the tracker detects the tag and sends its unique identifier (the IButton parameter) to the system.

Why this is needed:

— if GPS is unstable or jammed

— if accurate recording of arrival at a specific place is important

— if you need route completion to be counted correctly

Tags can be linked to route points only when the RFID tags module is enabled. First you need to set up the tags in this module. To learn how to create a tag, read this article.

If you use BLE tags:

1. Open the route

2. Select a specific point

3. Click the tag icon next to the point you need

4. In the window that opens, select the tag you need and link it to the point

The tag must be within the point radius.

5. Click “Save”

You can link several tags to one point.

After linking the tag to the point, save the route.

When a vehicle drives the route, the system works as follows:

1. Checks whether a BLE tag is linked to the point

2. Looks for an IButton event within ±5 minutes of the passage time

3. If a tag is detected — the point visit is recorded via BLE

4. If no tag is detected — the standard GPS geofence check is used

This way, even if GPS is unstable, the route is counted correctly — based on the actual arrival at the point.

How to view or edit a route

1. Go to the “Routes” tab

2. Find the route you need

3. Right-click it

4. Select “Edit”

5. The route builder opens, where you can make changes or just view the settings

In this article we explain how to work with a route in the system, what actions you can perform, and which tools are available for them.

Route menu

Route actions

Move the map to the route center

Edit route

Viewing a route and points

In PTM you can:

panel-upravleniya:
The task dashboard is a section in PTM where you can see all created tasks and work with them. This panel is a window for viewing and managing tasks that have been assigned or are in progress.

In this article we cover:

— how the task table is organized and what information its columns show

— buttons and functions for quick task management

— how to create, upload, and export tasks using templates

— which actions are available when you right-click a task row

— how to switch between workspaces

Task table

The center of the panel shows a table of created tasks. Each row in the table is a separate task. The table columns show task data, for example:

  • Task ID — the unique task number in the system

  • Received at — when the task was created

  • Task type — planned execution time or estimated task time

  • Order type — the task category (for example, "Delivery", "Booking", etc.)

  • Execution status — the current task status

  • Date and time (planned) — planned date and time of arrival/departure

  • Start in, min — defines how many minutes before the planned start time the task can automatically move to processing

  • Finish after, min — defines the time after the planned task end, after which the system can finish it automatically

  • Mark time, sec — the minimum time the vehicle must stay inside the geofence for a visit to be recorded. The check is performed both when entering and when leaving the geofence

  • Enable cyclic routes — allows correct processing of routes where a vehicle repeatedly moves between the same points and then returns to the base.

  • Completion function — defines the condition for automatic task completion. The following options are available:

— Return to base — the task is completed after the vehicle appears in the base geofence again.

The following can be used as the base:

  • the first route point

  • the last route point that matches the first

  • a point with the “Base” subtype

  • an alternative geofence created in the PILOT system

— Finish by shift — the task is completed after the estimated execution time ends: Planned end time + the value of the “Finish after” parameter

— Last waybill address (entry) — the task is completed after entry into the geofence of the last route point is recorded

— Last waybill address (exit) — the task is completed after exit from the geofence of the last route point is recorded.

Additional task handling rules let you configure automation and refine task processing rules:

  • Enable task auto-completion — forcibly completes tasks the specified number of minutes after the planned end time. Not recommended for use together with auto statuses

  • Task execution time — used when calculating the planned end time if the execution time field cannot be edited manually

  • Allow sending unassigned tasks to all drivers — lets drivers pick tasks themselves from the common queue in the mobile app

  • Enable editing tasks in the table for the current day only — limits editing of tasks in the table to the current day. Works together with user permissions only for the dynamically generated task table (the table is generated dynamically based on all task templates).

  • Enable task autofill by key fields — the system automatically fills in data from previously created tasks based on the values entered by the user

  • Disable selection of system task types — hides service task types when creating new tasks

  • Enable color highlighting of task statuses — highlights status cells in the table according to the current task status

  • The current user is the initiator by default — when a task is created, the initiator is automatically set to the current user

  • Enable tooltips for table rows — brief task information is displayed when you hover the cursor over a row

  • Close task after signing — the task is closed automatically after the entire approval and document signing chain is completed

  • Enable waypoint building bypassing auto statuses — creates waypoints based on the route regardless of how the auto status mechanism works

  • Enable geofence priority on points — if a route point is linked to a PILOT system geofence, that geofence is used to record the visit

  • Do not use the first point as the last point — disables automatic route closing and affects waybill generation

  • Enable selection of a replacement vehicle — lets you assign a backup vehicle without changing the main vehicle assigned to the task

  • Enable synchronization of address editing with the address classifier — when an address is changed in a task, the changes are automatically saved in the address reference book

Integrations

Integration with external services allows the system to exchange data with other platforms. You can:

1. Connect external services

2. Set up automatic data import and export via API, email, or webhooks

3. Specify which events and data must be passed to the system and back

Integrations are used for:

  • creating notifications

  • automatically importing tasks from email using a specified template (for example, for the “Magnit” system)

To connect an integration, you need to:

1. Select the integration group

2. Select the integration system

3. Fill in the connection parameters

If only the notification mechanism is used, for integration with the “Magnit” system it is enough to specify the email address without a password.

Webhook settings

The following parameters are available for each integration:

  • Webhook URL — the address for sending webhooks

  • Webhook headers — additional HTTP headers, for example an authorization token

  • Webhook parameters — the payload sent in the webhook

Special functions are used for automatic data substitution:

  • fn[getApiKey] — get the API key from the configuration (for the ERP Sarmix system only)

  • fn[getAgentId] — get the vehicle ID from the PILOT system

  • fn[getCurrentAgentLocation] — get the current vehicle location

  • fn[getCurrentUTC] — get the current time of the vehicle packet in seconds

  • fn[getCurrentZoneId] — get the ID of the geofence the vehicle is in

  • fn[getTaskId] — get the ID of the task the vehicle is performing

  • fn[getErpOrderId] — get the request ID (for the ERP Sarmix system only)

  • fn[getCurrentSpeed] — get the current vehicle speed

  • fn[getVehicleNumber] — get the vehicle number

Webhook parameters configuration example

The “Webhook parameters” field contains a JSON object with the data to be passed to the external system. Special functions are used for automatic value substitution.

{
  "access_token": "fn[getApiKey]",
  "agent_id": "fn[getAgentId]",
  "geolocation": "fn[getCurrentAgentLocation]",
  "time_event": "fn[getCurrentUTC]",
  "zone_id": "fn[getCurrentZoneId]",
  "pilot_task_id": "fn[getTaskId]",
  "erp_order_id": "fn[getErpOrderId]",
  "speed": "fn[getCurrentSpeed]",
  "vehiclenumber": "fn[getVehicleNumber]"
}
 

As a result, the system automatically substitutes the actual values, for example:

{
  "access_token": "123456789abcdef",
  "agent_id": "4521",
  "geolocation": "55.751244,37.618423",
  "time_event": "1750054800",
  "zone_id": "125",
  "pilot_task_id": "98765",
  "erp_order_id": "ORD-4567",
  "speed": "68",
  "vehiclenumber": "А123ВС777"
}

Additional integration parameters

  • Algorithm ID — the identifier of an algorithm created in the PILOT system for processing notifications by an operator

Algorithm data — the payload passed to the PILOT algorithm when a notification is triggered. It is configured by technical support when needed. The composition and structure of the data depend on the specific algorithm and processing scenario.

Algorithm data configuration example

{
  "-6": {
    "text": "Выполните действия",
    "options": [
      "Действие 1",
      "Действие 2",
      "Действие 3"
    ]
  }
}

  • Algorithm timer — the algorithm execution wait time in seconds

  • Sensor ID — the sensor identifier from the PILOT system

  • Emails — the list of email addresses for sending notifications

Account settings

Here you can configure the main system parameters for your account:

1. Queue for the mobile app:

Enable the task queue for drivers and define whether they pick tasks from the common queue themselves or tasks are assigned automatically.

2. Integration and profile settings:

— Set the login and password

— Specify the time zone and default language for the whole system

— Enable the ExactFarming integration and configure the token for this integration

3. “Logistician – Dispatcher” workflow chain:

Enable the workflow chain and select the permission template that will be used for logisticians and dispatchers.

4. Phone interface:

Enable the new interface for mobile devices, and also configure automatic generation of completion certificates.

5. Sending messages:

Configure the system to send notifications to requesters and drivers when needed

6. Event notifications:

Configure notifications about various errors, such as geocoding problems, missing vehicle or track, incorrect time intervals, geofence overlaps, and track gaps.

ehkodrajving-kachestvo-vozhdeniya:
The “Driving quality” module helps you assess drivers' driving style and identify dangerous or uneconomical maneuvers.

The system automatically analyzes data received from the device installed on the vehicle and records various events, for example:

— sharp acceleration

— harsh braking

— sharp turns

— speeding

— prolonged idling

— other events configured in the rules

For each recorded violation the system can assign penalty points. Based on this data, Eco-driving reports are generated, which let you assess the driving quality of each driver or vehicle.

Driving quality events are generated from data transmitted by the device installed on the vehicle. The available events depend on the device model and the parameters it supports.

The overall driving quality score is calculated taking into account the recorded events, the assigned penalty points, the selected penalty type, and the configured ECO weights.
nastrojka-pravil-kachestva-vozhdeniya:
Driving quality rules define which driver actions the system treats as violations and how they are taken into account when assessing driving quality.

Each rule monitors a specific parameter received from the device installed on the vehicle, for example speed, acceleration, or idling duration. If the value meets the specified conditions, the system records a driving quality event.

For each rule you can set:

— the parameter to monitor

— the event recording conditions

— the event type

— the message displayed in reports

— the number of penalty points and how they are assigned

You can create any number of rules and configure them to suit your vehicles, the installed equipment, and your company's requirements.

How to open the driving quality settings

1. In the user account, double-click the vehicle you need in the object list

2. In the object card, open the “Driving quality” tab

On this tab you can create and change the rules by which the system detects violations.

Control rules

The center of the window contains the rules table. Each row is a separate rule by which the system analyzes data received from the device. If the value meets the specified conditions, the system records a driving quality event.

You can create any number of rules and configure them to suit your vehicles and equipment.

Rule parameters

  Column
  Description
  Field
The sensor or parameter to be monitored. For example, speed, acceleration, ignition, or another parameter received from the device
  Formula
An additional mathematical or logical expression for processing the value before the check
  Type
The type of driving quality event that is recorded when the condition is met. The system uses the type to classify the event and calculate “Eco-driving” indicators. You can use the built-in types or create your own
  Message
  The text displayed in reports when the event is recorded. For example: Harsh Braking or Speeding
  Min.
  The minimum value from which the rule starts to trigger
  Max.
  The maximum value at which the event is still considered a violation. For example, if you specify the range 132–250 km/h, a violation is recorded at a speed within this range
  Period
  The interval in seconds during which several identical triggers are counted as one event. For example, if you specify 600 seconds for idling, a new violation is recorded only 10 minutes after the previous one
  Penalty
  The number of penalty points assigned for the event. It can be 0 — in this case the event is recorded, but no penalty points are assigned
  Penalty type
  Calculation method for penalty points

Main control types

“Eco-driving” reports most often use four main event types:

  • Acceleration — sharp vehicle acceleration

  • Braking — harsh braking

  • Cornering — a sharp maneuver when taking a turn

  • Speed — exceeding the set speed threshold

If needed, you can create your own event types.

Penalty types

For each rule you can choose one of three ways of assigning penalty points.

Simple

A fixed number of points specified in the “Penalty” field is assigned.

For example, if the penalty is 5, 5 points are assigned for each violation.

Weighted

The penalty is calculated taking the severity of the violation into account. The more the violation exceeds the set threshold, the greater the total number of penalty points.

This type is used when you need to consider not only the fact of the violation but also its seriousness.

Multiplier

The number of points is calculated by the formula: Violation value × Penalty

For example:

  • violation value — 5

  • penalty — 2

The total number of penalty points is 10.

This mode is convenient when the size of the penalty should depend on the magnitude of the violation.

How to create a rule

You can create any number of control rules yourself.

To do this:

1. On the “Driving quality” tab, click the “Add rule” button

2. A new row appears in the table

3. Fill in the rule parameters

Specify:

1. Field — the sensor or parameter to be monitored

2. Formula, if needed

3. Event type — select from the list. If the type you need is not there, you can create it yourself

4. The message that will be displayed in reports

5. The minimum and maximum values that define the range in which the event is considered a violation

6. The period for merging repeated events

7. The penalty size and penalty type

After filling in the parameters, click “Save”.

After saving, the rule starts being used when processing data received from the device.

To change a rule, change the parameters you need in the corresponding fields of the rule row.

To delete a rule, click the icon in the row of the rule you need, then save the changes.

Additional penalties

At the bottom of the window there are penalty settings that apply independently of individual rules.

The following parameters are available:

  • Penalty for entering a restricted geofence — assigned when the vehicle enters a restricted geofence

  • Penalty for an unauthorized driver — assigned if the vehicle is driven by a driver who is not permitted to operate this object

  • Penalty for speeding per minute / unit — additional points for exceeding the set speed limit

Enter the required values and save the settings.
shablony-pravil:
A rule template is a saved set of driving quality settings. With a template you can apply ready-made rules to a vehicle without configuring each rule manually. You can pick a template by device type and vehicle type, apply it to an object, or create your own.

In this article:

  • Ready-made templates

  • How to apply a template

  • How to create a template

  • How to set up template applicability

  • Importing and exporting rules

Ready-made templates

To open the template list:

1. Open the vehicle card

2. Go to the “Driving quality” tab

3. Expand the “Template” list

The list shows the suitable templates and a separate “Universal templates” group.

Universal templates are not tied to a specific device or vehicle type, so they can be applied to different vehicles.

The system also provides ready-made templates for certain telematics equipment models:

  • CIPIA

  • FLEX — for devices working over the Flex protocol, for example Smart 2333

  • GB100 ECO — for Queclink GB100

  • GV65 ECO — for Queclink GV65

  • Ruptela

  • Teltonika

Choose the template that matches the equipment and vehicle type.

How to apply a template

1. Open the “Driving quality” tab

2. In the “Template” field, select the template you need

3. Click “Apply”

4. The rules from the template are loaded into the table. Check them and click “Save” at the bottom of the vehicle card.

When a new vehicle is created, PILOT selects templates by device type and vehicle type. If the vehicle type is not specified, the “Passenger car” type is used for selection, but the field in the card is not filled in automatically.

How to create your own template

First set up the driving quality rules. To add a rule:

1. Click the plus icon

2. Fill in the rule parameters

3. Click “Save” in the rule row

To save the configured rules as a template:

1. Click the save icon next to the “Template” list

2. In the “Save as template” window, specify:

  • Template name

  • Device type — optional

  • Vehicle type — optional

3. Click “Save”

If you leave the device type or vehicle type blank, the template can be used with any value of that parameter.

The created template appears in the list of available templates.

How to set up template applicability

Applicability defines which devices and vehicles the template will be available for.

Template scope

A template can be linked:

— to a device type and a vehicle type

— to a device type only

— to a vehicle type only

  • — to neither type — such a template is considered universal
If the device type is not specified, the template can be used with any device. If the vehicle type is not specified, the template suits all vehicle types.

To set up applicability:

  • In the upper right part of the window, find the tools for managing eco-driving settings

  1. Click the icon

at the top of the “Driving quality” tab

3. In the “Template applicability” window, select:

  • Device type

  • Vehicle type

  • Template

  • Device type

  • Vehicle type

  • Template

    3. Click “Link”

In the “Device type” field you can select a specific equipment model.

In the “Vehicle type” field you can select a specific vehicle type or leave the value “For all vehicle types”.

In the “Template” field, select the template for which applicability is being set up.

For example, a template can be linked to a FleetGuide device and the “Passenger car” vehicle type.

To clear the selected value, click the cross icon in the corresponding field.

After linking, PILOT takes the device type and vehicle type into account when selecting available templates. A template is not applied automatically: you choose it and confirm the application.

After a template is applied, its rules are copied into the vehicle settings.
If you change the rules manually, the settings will differ from the original template. Later changes to the template itself also will not change the settings of vehicles it was applied to earlier.

Importing and exporting rules

Import and export let you transfer rules between vehicles or save a copy of them.

At the top of the “Driving quality” window, find the export and import tools.

**Export ** — saves the current rules to a JSON file

To do this:

1. Click the export button

2. Save the file to your computer

All rule parameters are saved to the JSON file.

**Import ** — loads a previously saved JSON file

To do this:

1. Click the import button

2. Select the file

3. The settings are loaded into the table automatically

Imported rules replace the current set of rules in the table. If needed, save the existing settings with export before importing a new file.
tipy-kachestva-vozhdeniya:
Driving quality types are event categories that the system uses to classify violations and generate “Eco-driving” reports.

Each driving quality rule is linked to a specific event type. When the rule is triggered, the system records an event of the selected type.

For example:

  • Acceleration — sharp acceleration

  • Braking — harsh braking

  • Turn — sharp turn

  • Speed — speeding

  • Seat Belt — seat belt violation.

Event types are stored in a separate reference book.

When you create or change a rule, you select the type you need from this reference book in the “Type” field.

If the standard types are not enough, you can create your own. After creation, the new type becomes available when setting up rules.

How to open the driving quality types reference book

1. Open the “Driving quality” tab

2. In the upper right part of the window, find the tools for managing “Eco-driving” settings

3. Click the “Driving quality types” button

The event types reference book opens.

These are the types used when selecting a value in the “Type” column (Acceleration, Braking, Turn, Speed, Seat Belt)

How to create a new type

1. In the event types reference book, click “Add”

2. Enter the event name

3. Click “Save”.

After saving, the system automatically assigns the new type a unique identifier (ID). The system uses it to identify the event type unambiguously, and it does not need to be set manually.

To change a type name, double-click the row, make the changes, and save them.

To delete a type, use the “Delete” button .

Delete types only if they are no longer used in rules. If a type is already in use, first replace it in the existing rules, and then delete it.
ehko-vesa:
ECO weights (importance coefficients) define how strongly different types of violations affect the overall driving quality score.

When the system records a driving quality event, it assigns penalty points. When the overall score is calculated, these points are taken into account using ECO weights.

The higher the ECO weight, the more strongly violations of this type affect the overall driving quality score.

Changing ECO weights does not affect event recording or the number of penalty points assigned. Only their influence on the overall score in Eco Driving reports changes.

ECO weight settings apply to the whole account and are used when generating Eco Driving reports.

Indicators

The system uses the following indicators.

  Indicator
  Meaning
  Speeding
  Exceeding the speed limit
  Excess Idle
  Prolonged engine idling
  Harsh Brake
  Harsh braking
  Harsh Accel
  Sharp acceleration
  Harsh Corner
  Sharp turn

The following are shown for each indicator:

  • Numeric coefficient — the value the system uses when calculating penalty points

  • Slider — lets you change the importance of the corresponding violation type

  • Percentage — shows the contribution of this violation type to the overall score

The total sum of all weights must be 100%.

Example

If you increase the ECO weight for Speeding, speeding affects the overall driving quality score more than the other violation types. The events themselves and the assigned penalty points do not change.

How to set up ECO weights

1. Open the “ECO weights for driving” window

2. Change the values with the sliders

3. Make sure the sum of all ECO weights is 100%

4. Click “Save” to apply the current ECO weight values. They are saved as working settings that the system will use when calculating driving quality

The weights most often changed are Harsh Brake and Harsh Accel, when you need to increase or reduce the influence of sharp maneuvers on the overall driving quality score.

Additional commands are available at the bottom of the eco weights window:

  • Update Defaults (Save as defaults) — saves the current values as defaults

  • Load Defaults (Load defaults) — loads previously saved defaults

  • Reset Defaults (Restore standard defaults) — returns the standard system settings:

— Speeding — 58.3%

— Excess Idle — 10.4%

— Harsh Brake — 6.9%

— Harsh Accel — 13.9%

— Harsh Corner — 10.4%
takhograf-2:
The “Tachograph” module helps you track and analyze driver work based on data from the hardware. All data comes directly from the tachograph and cannot be changed manually.

Use the module to track driver activity statuses: driving, rest, work, availability.

Based on the activity data you can:

  • understand how busy each driver is

  • check whether work and rest regulations are observed

  • analyze how the schedule was actually worked

How to configure data for the module

1. Go to the admin panel, open the “Machines” tab and find the Object the tachograph works with

2. Right-click the selected Object — the context menu opens

3. Select “Edit” in the menu

4. In the Object settings window that opens, select the “Configuration” tab.

5. Add the module configuration with the button and click “Save”

Which Sensors are required

For the module to display reliable information, certain Sensors must be added to the Object card:

  Sensor purpose
  What it shows
     Sensor setup example
  Driver state
Position of the driver mode switch: driving, rest, work, availability
  Card state
Status of the driver card in the slot (inserted or not, in use or not)
  Tachograph mode
Changes in the tachograph operating states

For details on how to add Sensors, see the section “Sensors”

How to view tachograph data

1. In the User account, go to the “Tachograph” section

2. Select the Object you want to analyze

3. Specify the period in the calendar — the days or hours you need data for

4. Click “Search”

5. You will see an activity summary: when the driver was driving, resting, available or working. The data is displayed as a clear interactive report on driver work and rest regimes for the selected period, broken down by days and weeks.

How the system works internally

The module receives data directly from the tachograph. This is “raw” technical data that the system converts into understandable states. This data is used to calculate driver activity statuses: driving, rest, work.

How to decode tachograph data

Let's look more closely at the tables with data received directly from the tachograph's digital interface — for example, via the CAN bus or another data transmission channel.

This data is processed by the monitoring system and helps determine:

  • Which driver card was installed (Table 1)

  • What the status of each driver is — resting, working, driving the vehicle — as well as the current card state in each slot (Table 2)

These parameters are generated as codes and bit values, so to be interpreted correctly they must be handled either by the system or by a specialist when configuring the hardware.

Below is the decoding of this data according to the tachograph specification.

Table 1

This table describes the structure of the packet that transmits the identification number of the driver card installed in the tachograph:

0x02 – driver card 1 or 2. The card number depends on the type of event for which this packet is generated.

The codes of the events for which the packet is generated help determine exactly which card was installed and in what situation.

Table 2

The table describes a data byte from the tachograph interface with ID: 98.

This byte contains compressed information about the following parameters:

  • The activity of each driver — rest, readiness for work, driving the vehicle, etc.

  • The state of the card slots — whether a card is inserted or not, whether it is authorized or not.

The byte is divided into bit fields — 8 bits in total, split into 4 groups of 2 bits, each responsible for a specific parameter.

The information from this byte helps you:

  • Connect external hardware to the tachograph

  • Get accurate data on driver activity

  • Configure the system so that it understands what exactly the driver is doing

For example: if the value of bits 0–1 = 3, driver No. 1 is driving the vehicle.

Calibration tables are also often built on the basis of this data. They are needed to convert the “raw” numbers from the tachograph data byte into understandable states. Instead of “raw” values such as 2 or 3, you will see “Rest” or “Card authorized”.

One byte (8 bits) is split into four pairs of bits — each 2 bits are responsible for one state:

  Bits
  Parameter
 Values
  0–1
 Driver 1 activity
 0, 1, 2, 3
  2–3
 Driver 1 card slot
 0, 1, 2, 3
  4–5
 Driver 2 activity
 0, 1, 2, 3
  6–7
 Driver 2 card slot
 0, 1, 2, 3

Therefore you need to configure calibration tables to convert the values into an understandable driver activity and card state.

Calibration table examples

The “Driver state” calibration table. You use this table to decode bits 0–1 and 4–5 (driver activity).

The “Card state” calibration table. You use this table for parameters 2–3 and 6–7 (driver card state).

To learn how to configure a calibration table, read here.

The module generates a driver activity Report that helps you track:

— periods when the driver is at the wheel

— rest, availability and work time

The accident detection module shows and processes “accident” events received from the vehicle.

What the module consists of

  • Notification settings — enabling the “Accident detection” Notification type in the “Contract settings”

  • Event display in History — accident Events are saved in History and displayed on the Map and in charts

How to enable Notifications

1. Go to the “Contract settings”

2. Open the “Notifications” tab

3. Click

4. In the list of Notification types, enable “Accident detection”


5. Click “Save”

Once enabled, the system will monitor incoming Crash tags from the vehicle and send Notifications

How Notifications are sent

When an accident signal (a Crash tag) arrives from the vehicle, the system checks it:

— if the data can be decoded (Crash_id), you will see the details in the Notification

— if decoding is not possible, a standard message arrives: "Crash detected!"

After an accident, the device may send the same Crash tag many times. So that you do not receive a stream of identical Notifications:
1. The system reacts only to the first signal and sends a Notification
2. Repeated signals are ignored until the first “clean” point without the accident tag arrives
3. If a new Crash tag arrives after that, you will receive a new Notification
This way you get only one Notification per accident, not a stream of repeats.

Accident history

To find and view an accident Event:

  • Go to the “History” section
For accident Events to be displayed in “History”, enable them in “Contract settings” → “Map and geocoding” tab → “Displaying events on the map” section → “Accident detection” event

2. Select the dates of the suspected accident

3. Select the History Tracks

4. Open the “Events” tab in “History”

5. Find the Event address on the Map — it will be marked with a marker

6. Click the marker to see the Event chart

What the chart shows

The chart shows how the loads on the vehicle changed during the accident. The data comes from the accelerometer — a device that records acceleration and sudden changes in motion.

The chart has three lines:

  • Blue (X) — forward and backward movement of the vehicle (for example, acceleration, hard braking or a frontal impact).

  • Purple (Y) — movement to the right and left (for example, a side impact or a sharp turn).

  • Green (Z) — movement up and down (for example, hitting an obstacle, a bump or an impact from below).

Sharp peaks and dips are the moment of impact. You can use them to see the nature of the collision: frontal, side or combined.

  • Y axis (vertical) — shows the strength of acceleration / deceleration (in arbitrary accelerometer units)

  • X axis (horizontal) — time (in milliseconds)

    What you can see on the chart

In this example, before the accident the lines fluctuate around 0 — the vehicle is moving smoothly, without sharp acceleration.

In the center there is a sharp dip downward (blue X and purple Y) — this is the moment of collision: strong braking with a lateral shift component.

After the impact the lines return closer to zero, but a slight “ripple” remains — these are oscillations after the collision.

Purpose of the module

  • Sensors are installed in containers and signal the PILOT platform when the container is filled up to the Sensor level.

  • The Sensor is installed at a height of about 80% of the full tank, so that there is still time for the garbage truck to arrive.

  • The waste removal company's operator sees in real time on the PILOT platform that several waste containers are approaching the upper mark, and creates a task to build an optimal route so these overflowing containers are collected sooner.

  • The garbage truck Driver receives a task in the app to pick up specific containers, along with the optimal route to them.

  • The operator sees the task being completed online in real time.

In an emergency, for example a fire in a waste container, the operator also receives a Notification on the PILOT platform (as well as by SMS, push or e-mail, depending on the method they prefer) about the incident and the need to respond.

Moreover, on the PILOT platform you can set up in advance a response scenario for emergencies

(a fire in a waste bin, an accident involving a garbage truck, a vehicle leaving its route), and then any operator of the waste removal service company will know what to do when a particular situation occurs.

The “Fines” module helps you track unpaid and overdue fines associated with vehicles and Drivers.

After the module is connected, fine data is received in PILOT automatically through the ELPAS service.

ELPAS is an external service that obtains fine data from government sources and passes it to PILOT. Once configured, the module automatically requests new data and displays the fines found in the system.

All fines are collected in one window, so you do not need to check each vehicle separately.

Here we will explain:

— how to connect and configure the “Fines” module

— what data is needed to search for fines

— how to view the fines found

— how to work with the list of fines
kak-podklyuchit-modul:
The module is connected by the system administrator or the servicing Partner.

If you have access to the admin panel, configure the module yourself using the instructions below. If you do not have access, contact your Partner or technical support.

To find fines, PILOT uses an integration with the ELPAS service. The service checks charges by the organization's details, vehicle data and driver's licenses.

1. Enable the module

Enable the “Fines” module:

  • for the Partner

  • for the sub-Partner

  • for the Contract

The module must be enabled at all levels. If it is disabled at even one of them, the system will not be able to receive fine data.

2. Add the ELPAS configuration

1. Go to Contract settings → Configs

2. Click “Add”

3. In the “Key” field, enter fine_api

4. In the “Value” field, enter elpas

5. Click “Save”

The configuration must be enabled for the Partner, the sub-Partner and the account. Only then will the system be able to receive fine data.

3. Set up the tariff

The module is paid, so a tariff must be set up for it to work.

1. Go to the Contract settings, “Services” tab

2. Click “Add”

3. In the list of services, select “Fines module”

4. Select the tariff for the module

5. Click “Save”

If you do not know which tariff to use, contact technical support.

4. Fill in the organization's details

In the Contract card, enter:

  • TIN (ИНН)

  • KPP (КПП).

The ELPAS service searches by the combination of TIN and KPP, so both fields must be filled in.

5. Fill in the vehicle data

For each vehicle you must enter the vehicle registration certificate (STS) number.

To do this:

1. In the User account, open the Object card

2. Go to the “Info” tab

3. Enter the series and number of the vehicle registration certificate

4. Save the changes

Repeat these steps for each vehicle.

Copy the series and number exactly as they appear in the certificate. Even one wrong digit can prevent the fine from being found and linked to the right Object.

6. Fill in the Driver data

Open each Driver's card and enter the driver's license number.

Without the driver's license number, the ELPAS service will not be able to check fines issued to that Driver.

Four identifiers are used to search for fines:

TIN (ИНН) — identifies the organization that fines may be issued to

KPP (КПП) — clarifies the organization's data and is used together with the TIN

STS (СТС) — helps find fines for a specific vehicle

DL (ВУ) — helps find fines by driver's license

When fines appear

After the setup is complete, wait for the next data update.

Every night, once a day, the system automatically contacts the ELPAS service, receives information about new fines and updates the list.

Each update loads fine data for the last 30 days.

If the service finds new fines, they will automatically appear in the User account after the update completes.

To transfer data from the Wialon system, use the “Import from Wialon” module. Data is transferred through the migration wizard — select the Objects you need and transfer them to PILOT.

Before transferring data, make sure your Wialon account has export rights — access to the Import/Export function. If you do not have these rights, “Import from Wialon” will not be able to export Objects.

For a clear understanding of how to work with the migration wizard and transfer data from Wialon to PILOT, watch the video “How to transfer data from Wialon to PILOT”.
https://youtu.be/TMAA7MX-EQU

How to transfer data:

1. Connect the “Import from Wialon” module in the admin panel. After that, the “Import from Wialon” button appears on the “General” tab

2. Click the button

3. The migration wizard window opens, divided into two parts:

On the left — the list of migration jobs

On the right — the list of Wialon Objects that will be transferred

4. Create a new migration job:

  1. Click the “Add job” button

  2. In the window that appears, fill in the fields:

  • Wialon login — your Wialon login

  • Wialon password — your Wialon password

  1. Click the “Load Objects from Wialon” button

  2. A list of Objects that can be transferred appears below. Check the ones you want to import.

Objects marked processed have already been selected in other jobs and are not available for selection.

  1. Click “Save”

5. The new job appears in the list on the left in the migration wizard window. All of its statuses will be empty — this means the job has not been run yet.

6. To start the data transfer, click the job in the list and click “Run job”

Once started, the job cannot be changed.

7. After the job is started, the data transfer begins automatically

The stage statuses will be updated in the migration wizard window — this usually takes no more than a minute.

Wait for the process to finish: you will see the statuses change and new data appear.

To follow the migration process and see current statuses, click the “Refresh” button .

In this example, after the job with id: 322 was completed, the only Wialon Object was fully and successfully transferred to PILOT.

Migration stages

The migration stages are displayed for each Object:

  Stage
  Description
  start 
  The job has started. Migration has begun, the system has started executing the job
  auth
  Authorization in the Wialon API. The system connects to Wialon to gain access to the data
  wlp
Export of Object parameters.
The main Object parameters are exported from Wialon (number of successfully processed files with Wialon Object parameters / total number of Wialon Objects in this job)
  wln
  Export of Object Events.
  Object Events are exported from Wialon (number of successfully processed files with Wialon Object Events / total number of Wialon Objects in this job)
  veh
Creation of Objects in PILOT
(number of successfully created PILOT Objects / total number of Wialon Objects in this job)
  sns
  Sensor import. Transfer of data about the Sensors installed on Objects
  evt
  Event import. All Events related to Objects are imported (for example, speeding, refuels, alarms)
  rc
  Data recalculation:
  rc1 — Tracks: recalculation of routes and movement Tracks
  rc2 — binary sensors: recalculation of data for Sensors with two states (for example, on/off)
  rc3 — sensors: recalculation of data for all Sensors
  rc4 — odometer: Mileage recalculation
  rc5 — eco: recalculation of driving style data (eco-driving)
  r6 — multi-sensors: recalculation of data for complex (multichannel) Sensors

Migration stage statuses

The status field values can be as follows:

  Value
  Description
  empty
  The migration stage was not run
 
  The stage completed successfully
 
  The stage completed with errors
  1001
  Wialon API error code
  no data
  Wialon API error message (no data)

moduli-2:
System modules are separate components that together form a complex system, providing its functionality and interconnected operation.

Each module performs specific tasks or functions, and they can be developed and updated independently of each other.

Only the system administrator can manage activation, through the admin panel.

The list of modules in a Contract may vary depending on the Partner's settings.

CMS and Video - a system component that lets you monitor the state and behavior of the driver and passengers inside the cabin.

Drivers module - a system component used to manage and track the work of Drivers in the system.

Counterparties module (Sales representative) - intended for managing information about counterparties, including clients, suppliers, Partners and sales representatives. This module helps organize interaction with counterparties and improve the quality of service.

Control room - a system component for tracking the location of a vehicle and scanning its condition.

Climate control - a system for automatically regulating climatic conditions in an enclosed space, for example in a vehicle, office or living space. The main goal is to maintain comfortable conditions for people, including optimal levels of temperature, humidity and air quality.

RFID tags module - a module intended for monitoring the reading of RFID tags; a narrowly focused module created to control waste collection (there is a tag on the bin and a reader on the vehicle).

Analytics module (Dashboard)- a system component that provides capabilities for collecting, processing and analyzing data from monitored Objects in order to obtain valuable information about them.

Engine blocking module - a system component intended to prevent unauthorized access to and starting of the engine.

Geofence module - intended for territorial control of monitored Objects. It lets you record the fact that an Object is in a given zone, exceeding the permitted idle time in the zone, and leaving the zone.

Commands module - a system component that includes a set of commands that Users can send to devices.

Time control module - a system component intended for tracking, recording and managing working time.

Violation control module - a system component used to track and detect violations using a set of predefined rules.

Logistics module - a system component intended for managing and optimizing logistics operations within the supply, storage and transportation of goods or services.

Recalculation module - a system component used to perform recalculations and transformations of data in the system. Recalculation is possible for two types: Zones and Trips.

Trailers module - intended for monitoring the state of trailers and semi-trailers attached to main vehicles. This module lets you track the location, state and movement of trailers, as well as view the history of connections and disconnections with the vehicle.

Retranslation module - a system component used to forward data from one source to another or to several other sources at once. It acts as an intermediary between the sender and the recipient of the data.

Service module - a system component intended for convenient planning or recording of vehicle technical inspections.

Events module - a system component intended for tracking and recording the various Events configured in the system. It plays a key role in monitoring Objects and analyzing User actions.

Fuel cards module - the choice of fuel depends on specific requirements, operating conditions and environmental factors.

Notifications module - a system component intended for sending Notifications to Users about various Events, changes or states. It provides prompt information to the User and allows timely response to important Events.

Trips module- a system component intended for automating and optimizing the operation of bus routes, improving passenger service quality and ensuring the efficiency of the vehicle fleet.

Routes module - a system component intended for passenger flow control.

PILOT task manager - a module intended for monitoring, managing and coordinating the execution of tasks or processes in the system. It gives Users the ability to observe and manage current processes

Schedule - a module used to create, manage and optimize work schedules for vehicles and Drivers.

Eco-driving - a component of the vehicle management system intended for monitoring, analyzing and improving driving style.

Tachograph module - intended for monitoring and recording data on the work and rest regimes of Drivers, driving speed and other important parameters related to vehicle operation. Tachographs play a key role in ensuring road safety and compliance with regulatory requirements.

Crash detected - a component of the vehicle management system intended for automatically detecting road accidents involving vehicles. The module uses various Sensors to monitor movement parameters.

Rent Сar - a module intended for managing and automating vehicle rental processes.

Waste collection module - intended for planning, optimizing and monitoring waste collection and removal operations.

Agro module (Trailers module)- intended for automating and optimizing the management of agricultural machinery and resources in the agro-industrial complex.

Hardware health monitoring module - a system component intended for monitoring the state of various components and systems of vehicles. This module helps identify faults, prevent breakdowns and optimize Maintenance.

LogBook module - a portal for Drivers where they can track their Trip statistics, eco-driving data, fuel costs, toll costs and their ratings.

Each Driver can access the portal and see only their own statistics, which are analyzed based on all Trips in all vehicles they have used.

The field editor is a tool that lets Users change or manage data fields. For example, in a text type or a table, the field editor can be used to change field properties such as its size, the type of data it contains, or how it is displayed.

The view according to the settings in the User interface.

When editing a field, you can change its type by selecting the one you need from the list provided.

Be careful: when editing a field, the text for the name property must be entered only in lowercase Latin letters.
For example, if the field name (fieldLabel) has the value "fieldLabel":"MVA Number", then in name you can write: "name":"mvanumber".
If you need to make a field required, copy and paste "allowBlank":false:
{"fieldLabel":"MVA Number","name":"mvanumber","xtype":"numberfield","allowBlank":false}
Text field (Text field) {"fieldLabel":"AS400 Status","name":"as400_status","xtype":"textfield"}
Number field (Number field) {"fieldLabel":"MVA Number","name":"mvanumber","xtype":"numberfield","allowBlank":false}
Drop-down field (Combobox) {"fieldLabel":"Vehicle Colour","name":"colour","xtype":"combobox","store":[["0","Unknown"],["1","White"],["2","Black"]]}
Date field (Date field) {"fieldLabel":"Vehicle Installation date","name":"vehinsdate","xtype":"datefield","format":"d.m.Y"}
Checkbox (Checkbox) {"fieldLabel":"Example text","name":"exampletext","xtype":"checkbox"}

  • fieldLabel - the field name;

  • name - the form element identifier;

  • xtype - the field type;

  • allowBlank - a required field;

  • format - the date format;

  • store - the list items, where "1" is the item identifier in the list and "White" is the item name in the list;

Contracts

Add payment

Manually add a credit to the Partner's balance.

  • Specify in the form:

  • External payment identifier

The message includes:

— the amount of the debt

— the Contract number

After the template is applied, the Partner will see a Notification, for example: “You need to pay off the subscription fee debt of … Otherwise all Objects will be disconnected from monitoring starting on the 1st of next month.”

If the balance becomes negative:

  • 5 days before the expected zero balance, a warning will start to be displayed on sign-in to the admin panel

  • the number of days is calculated based on average daily charges

  • after 5 days, access to the admin panel is blocked until a positive balance is restored

If an error appears when calculating the blocking. This means that:

1. One of the Partner's machines has a tariff in another currency.

The system cannot correctly calculate the total time until blocking when charges are in different currencies.

Solution: sign in as an administrator, open the corresponding AgentID and assign the correct price list.

2. The Contract has “incorrect” tariffs.

To fix this:

  • Open “Contracts” and call the context menu with a right click

    2. Select “Finance” → Incorrect tariffs

• SMTP Login — the login for authorization on the mail server

• SMTP Passw — the password for authorization

• SMTP Email — the e-mail address on whose behalf e-mails will be sent

• SMTP security — selection of the connection type (no encryption, SSL, TLS — depending on the server settings)

Please check the entered data carefully — the delivery of e-mails depends on the correctness of these settings.

Checking the SMTP server

After entering the parameters, you can run a connection check.

The system uses the SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) protocol to test the connection and authorization.

The check is performed as follows:

1. The system gets the SMTP server address from the request and checks whether it is specified

2. It gets the connection port. If no port is set, the standard port 25 is used

3. An SMTP client instance is created, and the connection timeout and debug level are configured

4. An attempt to connect to the server is made:

— if SSL is selected, the prefix ssl:// is automatically added to the address

— when connecting over SSL, certificate verification is temporarily disabled

5. After a successful connection, the EHLO command (the extended SMTP greeting command) is sent

6. The system gets the list of ESMTP extensions supported by the server

7. If TLS mode is selected and the server supports STARTTLS, the system:

— initiates a secure connection

— sends the EHLO command again

8. If the server supports authentication, a sign-in attempt is made using the specified login and password

Error handling

If an error occurs at any stage:

— the information is written to the error log

— HTTP code 400 is returned

— an error message is output in JSON format

Regardless of the result of the check, the connection is closed properly with the QUIT command.

Finally, the function returns the connection parameters and the result of the check.

This procedure helps make sure that the server is available, supports the selected encryption type and accepts the specified credentials.

If the check fails, we recommend double-checking the server address, port, security type and sign-in data.

SIM cards in monitoring systems are used to provide communication between monitoring devices and the server. They play a key role in systems that require remote tracking and data transmission.

SIM cards are used in GPS trackers for vehicles to transmit location data in real time. This makes it possible to control routes, monitor schedule compliance and respond to deviations from the route.

SIM cards allow monitoring devices (for example, GPS trackers and Sensors) to connect to mobile networks to transmit location, status and other parameter data to the monitoring server.

This is especially important for devices that are in motion or in remote locations without access to Wi-Fi or wired networks.
