retranslyatsiya-2:
The “Retransmission” section is used to send monitoring object data to external systems.

For example, data can be sent to:

— city platforms

— integration services

— monitoring systems such as Wialon

— servers that work over the EGTS protocol

— REST API

— other external systems that accept telematics data

Retransmission works as follows:

1. Create a data transmission destination (endpoint)

2. Specify the connection parameters for the external system

3. Connect one or more objects to this endpoint

After that, the system automatically starts sending the data of the selected objects to the external system.

This approach lets you set up a connection once and use it for any number of objects, without re-entering the server address, port, authorization parameters and other settings.

The “Retransmission” section consists of three tabs:

  • Endpoints — destinations for data transmission to external systems. This is where you configure the connection parameters for the external system: server address, port, protocol, authorization data and other parameters.

  • Statistics — data transmission statistics, error information and transmission status. Here you can check for errors, see the number of sent and received packets, assess the state of the queues and make sure that data is reaching the external system successfully.

  • Objects — objects connected to retransmission. Any number of objects can be connected to one endpoint. If necessary, you can disconnect an object from retransmission or connect it to another endpoint.

Key retransmission concepts

Below are the main terms used in this section.

Endpoint

— a destination for data transmission to an external system.

An endpoint specifies the connection parameters:

  • server address

  • port

  • data transmission protocol

  • path, if required

  • authorization parameters

  • additional settings

One endpoint can be used by several objects at once. For example, if all objects must send data to the same Wialon account, it is enough to create one endpoint and connect the required objects to it.

An object is a vehicle, device or any other monitoring object whose data is sent through the selected endpoint. Each object can have its own retransmission parameters, such as an external identifier or a data transmission schedule.

Partner

— the partner contract that the endpoint belongs to.

Depending on access rights, a user can work only with their own endpoints or can also see the endpoints of child partners.

Contract

— the end-user contract that the monitoring object belongs to

Auto-add objects (Auto add

) — this function lets you automatically connect new objects of the selected contract to an endpoint. For example, all of a customer’s objects must send data to the same external system. After the rule is set up, every new object created in the selected contract is connected to the endpoint automatically, with no extra user action.

External ID

— the object’s identifier in the external system. By default, the device IMEI is usually used as the External ID, but you can change it if necessary.

The external system uses this identifier to recognize the object and match the data it receives.

Uspw

— authorization data for sending data to the external system. Depending on the protocol, this may store a login, password, token or other access parameters. If the protocol requires additional authorization parameters, they are specified in the Json config field.

Access rights

The available data and actions depend on the user’s role in the admin panel.

Administrator

An administrator has full access to the section and can:

— view all endpoints

— manage all retransmission objects

— create, edit and delete endpoints

— view overall statistics for all retransmissions

— work with test endpoints

User

A partner user sees only the data that belongs to their partner structure.

They have access to:

— their own endpoints

— endpoints of child partners

— objects of contracts that belong to the accessible partner branch

— statistics for the available endpoints

A partner cannot view or change data that belongs to other partner structures
endpoints:
This article describes how to work with data transfer destinations (endpoints): from creating and configuring a connection to connecting Objects and automating the retranslation process.

Here you will learn:

  • What an endpoint is

  • How to work with the list of endpoints

  • How to create endpoints

• How to connect Objects to an endpoint

  • How to set up automatic connection of new Objects

What an endpoint is

An endpoint is a destination for transferring data to an external system. It holds the connection parameters: the server address, port, data transfer protocol and authorization parameters.

After an endpoint is created, one or more Objects can be connected to it.

List of endpoints

To open the list of endpoints, go to the “Retranslation” → “Endpoints” section.

This tab shows all available data transfer destinations and their current state.

Here you can:

— create new endpoints

— change the settings of existing endpoints

— connect Objects

— set up automatic connection of new Objects

— view data transfer statistics

— enable, disable and delete endpoints

Top panel

The following actions are available on the top panel:

1. Add — create a new endpoint

2. Statistics — select the period for displaying statistics

3. Search — search for an endpoint in the table

4. Clear filters — reset all filters

Selecting the statistics display period

The Statistics parameter affects the display of the mini-charts in the columns:

  • Err — errors

  • Send — sending of data

  • Ack — acknowledged packets

The mini-charts help you quickly assess the state of retranslation for the selected period.

The chart shows:

— the dynamics of the indicator

— the total number of events for the selected period

When you hover the cursor, information about the selected point of the chart is displayed.

The following periods are available:

  • 12 hours — the last 12 hours

  • Day — the last 24 hours

  • Week — the last week

  • 2 weeks — the last two weeks

  • Month — the last month

Endpoints table columns

Actions — available actions for the endpoint

ID — the unique identifier of the endpoint

Partner ID — the identifier of the Partner that owns the endpoint

Partner name — the name of the Partner that owns the endpoint

Host — the IP address or domain name of the external server

Port — the port for connecting to the external server

Format — the data transfer protocol used

Statistics / Objects — the number of Objects connected to the endpoint

Statistics / Active — the number of active Objects that are currently transmitting data and are online

Statistics / Auto — the number of Contracts for which automatic adding of Objects is enabled

Statistics / Queue — the number of packets in the send queue

Statistics / Err — a mini-chart of errors for the selected period

Statistics / Send — a mini-chart of send attempts for the selected period

Statistics / Ack — a mini-chart of accepted packets for the selected period

On/off — the endpoint state (enabled or disabled)

Status — the endpoint state: active, disabled or no active Objects

Uspw — authorization data (hidden by default)

Testing — the test endpoint flag. Available to the administrator only

TimeZone — the time zone

Comment — additional information

Speed Limit — the maximum speed transmitted to the external system

Schedule — the retranslation schedule

Mapping fields — field mapping settings for special formats

You can configure which columns with parameters to display in the table.

To do this:

1. Click the arrow in the header of any column

2. Select the Columns item

3. Check the columns you need

4. Uncheck the columns you do not want to display

The same menu also offers:

— ascending sort

— descending sort

— data filtering

Endpoint actions

The following actions are available in the “Actions” column:

On or off — enable or disable the endpoint

Edit — open the form for editing the endpoint. You can also double-click a table row to open the endpoint settings

Auto add — set up automatic connection of Objects

Statistics — open the statistics for the selected endpoint

Machines or Objects — open the list of connected Objects

Delete — delete the endpoint

How to create an endpoint

1. Click “Add” on the top panel

2. Fill in the connection parameters

Main parameters

Name — the name of the endpoint

Host — the address of the external server to which data will be sent

Port — the port of the external system connection

Format — the data transfer protocol or format

Path — an additional path or URL route, if required by the protocol used

Uspw — authorization data for connecting to the external system

Time zone — the time zone that will be used by default for the Objects of this endpoint

Speed Limit — the maximum speed that will be transmitted to the external system

“Enabled” checkbox — enables or disables the endpoint

Testing — lets you create a test endpoint. The parameter is available to administrators only

Json config — additional connection settings in JSON format

Comment — a free-form comment for system Users

Mapping fields — field mapping settings for special data transfer formats

Schedule — the schedule during which data transfer through this endpoint is allowed

3. Click “Save”

After saving, the endpoint becomes available for connecting Objects.

How to edit an endpoint

1. Click the “Edit” button in the actions column or double-click the endpoint row

2. Change the necessary parameters

3. Click “Save”

The changes are applied automatically to all Objects that use this endpoint.

If the system finds an endpoint with the same parameters, it will offer to merge them. Check the settings carefully before confirming.

If you do not confirm the merge, the changes will not be saved.

How to enable or disable an endpoint

To temporarily stop or resume data transfer:

1. Click the enable button or the disable button in the actions column

If an endpoint is disabled, all Objects connected to it stop transmitting data to the external system.

How to delete an endpoint

1. Click the delete button in the actions column

2. Confirm the deletion

Before deletion, the system will show the number of Objects that use this endpoint.

After deletion, data transfer through the endpoint will be stopped completely.

Endpoint Objects

To view the Objects connected to an endpoint:

1. Find the endpoint you need

2. Click the “Machines/Objects” button in the actions column

A list of Objects that transmit data through the selected endpoint opens.

From this window you can:

— connect new Objects

— change the retranslation parameters of individual Objects

— temporarily disable data transfer

— remove Objects from the endpoint

Object list columns

Agent ID — the Object identifier

Machine — the name of the monitored Object

IMEI — the unique device identifier

Contract — the Object's Contract

External ID — the Object identifier in the external system

On/off — whether retranslation of the Object is enabled or disabled

Err — a mini-chart of errors for the Object

Send — a mini-chart of send attempts for the Object

Ack — a mini-chart of accepted packets for the Object

Actions with Objects:

and — enable or disable the Object in this endpoint

— remove the Object from this endpoint

How to add Objects

1. In the “Objects/Machines” window, click the “Add” button

2. Select one or more Objects

3. If necessary, change the External ID. By default, the device IMEI is used as the External ID

4. Click “Add” to connect the selected Objects to the endpoint

If the list of Objects is long, use the search at the top in the “Search” field — enter the name or number of the Object.

How to edit an Object

1. Double-click the Object in the list

2. Make changes in the Object editing form

In the form you can change the Object-level retranslation parameters:

  • Endpoint — the data transfer destination through which the Object sends information to the external system

  • External ID — the Object identifier in the external system

  • “Enabled” checkbox — enables or disables data transfer for the selected Object only

  • Speed limit — the maximum speed that will be transmitted to the external system for this Object

  • Time zone — the time zone used for transmitting this Object's data

  • Uspw — authorization data for this Object

  • Json config — additional retranslation settings in JSON format

  • Schedule — the data transfer schedule for the Object.

The Host, Port, Format and Path parameters cannot be changed in this form. They are inherited from the endpoint.

If you need to change the connection to the external system, open the endpoint settings or select another endpoint.

3. Save the settings

Automatic connection of Objects to an endpoint

The Auto add function lets you automatically connect new Objects to an endpoint.

This function is used when all Objects of a particular Contract must automatically transmit data to one external system. After the rule is set up, new Objects will be connected automatically without additional User actions.

How to set up Auto add

1. Click the Auto add button in the actions column

2. A window opens with the list of Contracts for enabling automatic adding of Objects. Click “Add”

3. Select one or more Contracts

4. Click “Add”

After saving, all new Objects of the selected Contracts will be connected to this endpoint automatically.
statistika:
The Statistics tab shows data transfer statistics and information about possible retranslation errors.

To open the statistics, go to the “Retranslation” → “Statistics” section.

The page lets you monitor retranslation, track the success of data transfer, analyze errors and identify problem Objects or transfer destinations.

The statistics are generated from the retranslation service data and are displayed according to the current User's access rights.

The administrator can view global statistics for the whole system or statistics for individual endpoints.

A Partner user sees statistics only for their own endpoints and the endpoints of Partners below them in their hierarchy.

Statistics view modes

The Scope filter is available to the administrator:

  • Global — statistics for the whole retranslation system.

  • Endpoints — statistics for individual data transfer destinations.

Users with the Partner role work only in Endpoints mode.

Statistics filters

At the top of the page there are filters that let you select the data you need for analysis.

Scope (Statistics scope)

Defines the source of the statistics:

  • Global — statistics for the whole system;

  • Endpoints — statistics for individual endpoints.

Available to administrators only.

Protocol

A filter by data transfer protocol. It lets you display statistics only for the selected protocol.

Metric

Defines which events will be displayed in the charts and tables.

The following values are available:

  • All metrics — all metrics

  • OK only — only successfully accepted packets

  • Errors only — only errors

  • Spooled only — only packets placed in the queue

  • Dropped only — only dropped packets

Endpoint

Lets you select one endpoint or a group of endpoints for analysis.

The list of endpoints is grouped by Partner.

Loop threshold/hour (Cyclic transmission threshold per hour)

Used to find Objects with a suspiciously large number of transmitted packets.

If the number of packets exceeds the specified threshold, the Object may appear in the Loop suspicion table.

From and to

The start and end of the analyzed period.

Time on the charts is displayed in the User's local time zone in 24-hour format.

Statistics charts

At the top of the page, charts are displayed that help you quickly assess the state of retranslation.

Traffic over time

Shows the change in the number of packets over time.

The chart helps you identify:

— periods of high activity

— a sharp increase in load

— the moments errors appear

— periods with no data transfer

Outcome

Shows the distribution of data transfer results.

From the chart you can quickly assess:

— how many packets were successfully accepted

— how many packets ended with an error

— how many packets were placed in the queue

— whether there are problems with data transfer

By protocol

Compares statistics across different data transfer protocols.

The chart lets you determine:

— which protocol is used most often;

— which protocol has more errors

— which protocols create the main load

By endpoint

Compares statistics between endpoints.

From the chart you can quickly determine:

— the most active endpoints

— endpoints with an increased number of errors

— the transfer destinations with the highest load

If you click any endpoint on the By endpoint chart, the system automatically:

— selects this endpoint in the filter

— updates the other charts

— updates the statistics tables

— shows information only for the selected endpoint

Metrics

The following indicators are used in the statistics.

Accepted / Ack

The number of packets successfully accepted by the external system. The higher this indicator, the more successfully retranslation is working.

Send

The number of packet send attempts. Shows the total volume of outgoing data transfer.

Errors

The number of sending or connection errors. A rise in this indicator usually points to problems with the connection, the endpoint settings or the availability of the external system.

Spooled

The number of packets placed in the send queue. Such packets will be sent later, when transfer becomes possible.

Dropped

The number of packets that were dropped by the service and will not be transferred.

Queue

The current size of the endpoint queue. If the value keeps growing, this may indicate problems sending data to the external system.

Statistics tables

Tables with information are located below the charts.

Top endpoints

A list of endpoints with the largest number of transferred packets for the selected period.

Lets you quickly identify the most active data transfer destinations.

Recent endpoint errors

A list of the latest retranslation errors.

The table helps you quickly understand the cause of data transfer problems and identify the endpoint where the error occurred.

Top vehicles for endpoint

A list of Objects that generated the largest volume of traffic for the selected endpoint.

Used to analyze load and find the most active Objects.

Loop suspicion

A list of Objects that exceeded the set threshold of packets per hour.

This situation may indicate cyclic data transmission, a hardware configuration error or incorrect operation of the integration.

If Objects appear in this list, it is recommended to check the retranslation settings and the data source.
obekty-2:
The “Objects” tab shows all Object retranslations available to the current User.

List of Objects

To open the list of Objects, go to the “Retranslation” → “Objects” section.

Here you can:

— find the Object you need

— see through which endpoint data is transmitted

— enable or disable retranslation of an Object

— open the retranslation settings

— view the data transfer statistics for the Object

Top panel

The following actions are available on the top panel:

  • Configs — retranslation configuration settings

  • Export — export the list of Objects

  • Statistics — select the period for displaying the mini-charts

  • Search — search the table

  • Clear filters — clear the filters

Table columns

  • Actions — available actions for the Object's retranslation.

  • ID — the identifier of the retranslation record.

  • Agent id — the Object identifier.

  • Host — the IP address or domain name of the external server.

  • Port — the port of the external server

  • Format — the data transfer protocol used.

  • Statistics / Err — a mini-chart of errors

  • Statistics / Send — a mini-chart of send attempts for the selected period

  • Statistics / Ack — a mini-chart of accepted packets for the selected period

  • Last id — the identifier of the last processed packet.

  • Uspw — authorization data

  • Time zone — the time zone of the Object's retranslation

  • — the state of the Object's retranslation (enabled or disabled).

Actions with an Object

The following actions are available in the Actions column:

— enable or disable retranslation of the Object

Edit — open the Object's retranslation settings. You can also open the editing form by double-clicking the Object row.

In the editing form you can change the parameters that apply only to the selected Object:

If you need to change the server address, port, data transfer protocol or connection path, open the settings of the corresponding endpoint on the Endpoints tab.

Working with retranslations from the “Machines” section

You can manage retranslations not only through the “Objects” tab in the “Retranslation” section, but also directly from the list of Objects in the “Machines” section.

To do this:

1. Go to the “Machines” section

2. Select one or more machines

3. Right-click

4. In the context menu, select the “Retranslations” item

Retranslations of a single machine

If one machine is selected, the retranslations window of the selected Object opens.

The window consists of two sections:

Configuration — contains the list of the Object's configured retranslations.

Here you can:

— add a new retranslation

— change an existing one

— delete a retranslation

— enable or disable data transfer

Resend requests — contains requests to resend historical data for the selected period.

Retranslations of several machines

If several machines are selected, the menu item is displayed as “Retranslation (N)”, where N is the number of selected Objects.

After the window opens, you can create the same retranslation for several machines at once.

In this case, the system will create a separate retranslation record for each selected Object using the one selected endpoint.

How to add a retranslation

1. In the “Machines” section, select one or more Objects

2. Open the context menu with a right click

3. Select the “Retranslations” item

4. In the “Configuration” section, click the button

The retranslation creation form opens.

Fill in the required parameters:

  • Endpoint — the data transfer destination

  • External ID — the Object identifier in the external system

  • Speed limit — the transfer speed limit

  • Time zone — the time zone

  • Uspw — authorization data

  • “Enabled” checkbox — enables or disables retranslation

  • Json config — additional parameters in JSON format

  • Schedule — the data transfer schedule

The host, port, format and path fields are determined by the endpoint settings and cannot be edited in this form. To change these parameters, change the settings of the corresponding endpoint.

After saving, the Object will start transmitting data through the selected endpoint.

Resend requests

The Resend requests section is intended for resending previously saved data for a specified period.

This function is used if data was not transferred to the external system for some reason or a repeated export of historical information is required.

How to create a request:

1. In the Resend requests section, click the button

2. Specify the period start date

3. Specify the period end date

4. Click “Add”

After creation, the request appears in the table.

Resend requests table columns

  • Start time — the start of the resend period

  • Stop time — the end of the resend period

  • Create at — the date and time the request was created

  • Update at — the date and time the request was last changed

  • Status — the current state of the request:

  • New — the request has been created and is waiting to be processed

  • In Process — the data is being resent

  • Complete — processing is complete

After the request is completed, the data for the specified period will be retransmitted through the selected retranslation.
chastye-problemy-i-ikh-reshenie:
No data in the external system

If data does not appear in the external system, check:

— whether the endpoint is enabled

— whether retranslation of the Object is enabled

— whether External ID is filled in correctly

— whether the endpoint settings are correct (host, port, format, path)

— whether the authorization data (Uspw) is specified correctly

— whether there are errors on the Statistics tab

— whether the queue (Queue) is growing

A new Object was not connected automatically

Check:

— whether the Auto add rule is enabled for the Object's Contract

— whether the Object was created after the rule was set up

— whether the endpoint is enabled

— whether the Object belongs to the Contract for which the Auto add rule is set up

— whether the User has access rights to this Contract

Queue is growing

If the Queue indicator is increasing, packets are accumulating in the queue and cannot be sent.

This usually happens if:

— the external server is unavailable

— incorrect connection parameters are specified

— the receiving side rejects the connection

Check the Host, Port and Uspw settings, the availability of the external system and the latest errors on the Statistics tab.

The number of errors (Err) is growing

If the Err indicator is increasing, check:

— the availability of the external system

— the correctness of the authorization parameters

— whether the selected data transfer protocol is correct

— the schedule settings

— restrictions or requirements of the receiving side

There is Send, but no Ack

If the Send indicator is growing while Ack stays at zero, this means the system is sending data but does not receive an acknowledgment of receipt.

Check:

— the protocol settings

— External ID

— Json config

— the authorization data

— error messages on the Statistics tab

Statistics are not displayed

Possible reasons:

— no data has been transferred through the endpoint yet

— the display period selected is too short

— the endpoint was created recently

— the statistics have not had time to be generated yet

Recommendations

  • Create a separate endpoint for each external system

  • Set up Auto add if all new Objects of a Contract must automatically transmit data to one system

  • Before deleting an endpoint, check the number of connected Objects

  • When problems occur, first open the Statistics tab and check the Queue, Err, Send and Ack indicators

nastrojka-retranslyatsii-tripia:
Tripia is a data retranslation protocol designed for transmitting vehicle telematics information to the external Tripia system in JSON format.

The Tripia protocol can transmit:

— vehicle coordinates and speed

— Trip data

— vehicle status

— Sensor data

— GPS, ADAS and DMS Events

— CAN bus data

— Driver identification information

Data is transmitted in real time.

How to add a retranslation

1. Go to the admin panel

2. Go to the “Machines” tab

3. Find the Object you need, right-click it and select “Retranslation” in the menu

  1. In the window that opens, click the button for adding a retranslation

5. In the “Configuration” window, fill in the fields to set up the retranslation

Connection parameters

When creating an endpoint, specify the following parameters:

  Parameter
  Value
  Format
  Tripia
  Host
  64.225.12.166
  Port
  3000
  Protocol
  TCP
  Data format
 JSON

Data transfer frequency

Data is transmitted automatically:

— every 30 seconds when the ignition is on

— every 1 minute when the ignition is off

Transmitted data

Provider information

The data of the organization that owns the vehicle is transmitted:

  • provider name (Provider Name)

  • provider code (Provider Code)

Vehicle information

The following is transmitted:

  • vehicle identifier

  • license plate number

  • dispatcher data

Event registration data

The following is transmitted:

  • event time (Event Timestamp)

  • data sending time (Sent Timestamp)

GPS data

The main navigation parameters are transmitted:

  • latitude (Latitude)

  • longitude (Longitude)

  • speed (Speed)

  • heading (Heading)

  • altitude (Altitude)

  • number of satellites (Satellites)

  • HDOP

  • PDOP

Connection data

Mobile network parameters are transmitted:

  • signal level

  • mobile operator (MCC/MNC)

  • connection type

  • Cell ID

Vehicle status

The following is transmitted:

  • ignition

  • movement

  • odometer

  • engine hours

  • battery voltage

GPS Events

The following Events are transmitted:

  • battery disconnection

  • signal jamming (Jamming)

  • loss of satellites

  • vehicle towing

  • loss of communication signal

  • restoration of communication signal

  • harsh acceleration

  • harsh turn

  • harsh braking

  • accident (Crash)

GPS Sensor data

Transmission of data from the following Sensors is supported:

  • Temperature Sensors

  • Door and body state Sensors:

    — driver door

    — passenger door

    — side cargo door

    — rear cargo door

    — engine hood

  • Additional Sensors:

    — panic button (Panic Button)

Telemetry

Flags indicating the presence of the following subsystems are transmitted:

  • ADAS

  • DMS

  • Refrigerator

  • CAN Bus

  • Driver ID

ADAS Events

Driver assistance system Events are transmitted:

  • FCW (forward collision warning)

  • LDW (lane departure warning)

  • LDWL

  • LDWR

  • PCW

  • PROX

DMS Events

Driver monitoring system Events are transmitted:

  • blocking

  • face lost (Face Lost)

  • distraction

  • frequent yawning

  • looking aside

  • smoking

  • talking on the phone

  • drowsiness

  • seat belt not fastened

CAN bus data

The following is transmitted:

  • fuel level (%)

  • fuel volume (liters)

  • fuel load

  • fuel consumption

  • speed

  • odometer

  • engine hours

  • driver door state

  • passenger door state

Driver identification (Driver ID)

The following is transmitted:

  • identifier type

  • identifier code

  • Driver ID

  • Driver name

dopolnitelnye-json-konfiguratsii-retrans:
Some retransmission protocols support additional settings through the Json config field. With a JSON configuration you can change the composition of the transmitted data, use processed sensor values, rename fields, filter packets and set up special data transmission scenarios.

The supported parameters depend on the selected retransmission protocol.

Specify the JSON configuration in the Json config field when you create or edit a retransmission.

Wialon Retranslator

Sending processed sensor values

Lets you send sensor values to the retransmission after they have been processed in PILOT.

For example, you can send the fuel level sensor value after calibration has been applied.

Example

{
  "sensors_use": {
    "fuel_1": 135785,
    "NameSensor": 228
  }
}

  • sensors_use — list of sensors whose values must be taken from the object’s configured sensors

  • fuel_1 — name of the parameter that will be sent to the retransmission

  • 135785 — ID of the object’s sensor in the system

You can find the sensor ID in the object’s sensor settings.

Notes:

  • For fuel level sensors to work correctly, calibration must be set up.

  • Values that fall outside the calibration range are sent as is.

  • For example, a raw value of 65530 may be sent instead of liters.

Sensor filtering and processing

Example

{
  "sensors_use": {
    "temp_1": 1370805,
    "temp_2": 1370806
  },
  "tags_rewrite": {
    "temp_2": "temp2",
    "temp_01": "temp1"
  },
  "sensors_filter": {
    "temp_1": {
      "max": 130,
      "min": 1,
      "type": "int"
    },
    "temp_2": {
      "max": 100,
      "min": 1,
      "type": "int"
    }
  },
  "sensors_notuse": {
    "temp_1": 1,
    "temp_2": 1
  }
}

  • sensors_use — lets you use the values of the specified object sensors.

  • tags_rewrite — lets you rename parameters before sending.

Example:

{
  "tags_rewrite": {
    "temp_2": "temp2"
  }
}

In this case, the temp_2 parameter will be sent as temp2.

  • sensors_filter — lets you filter sensor values.

Supported parameters:

  Parameter
  Description
  type
  Data type. Currently, int is supported
  min
  Minimum allowed value
  max
  Maximum allowed value

Example:

{
  "sensors_filter": {
    "temp_1": {
      "min": 1,
      "max": 130,
      "type": "int"
    }
  }
}

Filtering works for sensors that send integer values.

  • sensors_notuse — lets you exclude sensors from transmission.

Example:

{
  "sensors_notuse": {
    "temp_1": 1,
    "temp_2": 1
  }
}

This configuration excludes the specified sensors from the data being sent.

Sensor settings made in PILOT do not affect retransmission through this mechanism. All transmission parameters must be specified in Json config.

Packet filtering

Lets you skip sending packets that match certain conditions.

Example

{
  "packet_filter": {
    "Valid": "0"
  },
  "keys_to_skip": [
    "HardVersion"
  ]
}
  • packet_filter — does not send a packet if the specified parameter has the given value.

Example:

{
  "packet_filter": {
    "Valid": "0"
  }
}

If the Valid parameter equals 0, the packet will not be sent.

You can specify several conditions.

  • keys_to_skip — does not send a packet if it contains the specified key.

Example:

{
  "keys_to_skip": [
    "HardVersion"
  ]
}

If the packet contains the HardVersion field, it will be skipped.

You can specify several keys.

Wialon IPS and Wialon IPS v2

Renaming parameters

Lets you replace a parameter name before sending.

Example

{
  "params": {
    "Vsourse": {
      "name": "pwr_ext",
      "type": "int"
    }
  }
}

In this example, the Vsourse parameter will be sent as pwr_ext.

Sending IButton in the packet body

Example

{
  "params": {
    "IButton": {
      "type": "tcp_box"
    }
  }
}

How it works

If the IButton parameter has the tcp_box type, the identifier value is sent in the packet body. If the parameter is missing, IButton is not added to the packet and an empty value is sent.

This setting is used to send the driver identifier outside the standard parameter block.

The inputs block

Lets you generate additional inputs based on sensor values.

Example

{
  "inputs": {
    "DIN1": {
      "max": 1,
      "min": 1,
      "value": false,
      "myval": false
    }
  },
  "params": {
    "DIN1": {
      "name": "DIN1",
      "type": "int"
    }
  }
}

Parameters of the inputs block

  Parameter
  Description
  min
  Minimum allowed value
  max
  Maximum allowed value
  value
If set to true, the actual sensor value is sent in the packet. If the parameter is missing or set to false, the standard packet-building logic is used
  myval
  Lets you substitute your own value for the sensor value when the condition is met

Simplified configuration example

{
  "inputs": {
    "DIN1": {
      "max": 1,
      "min": 1
    }
  },
  "params": {
    "DIN1": {
      "name": "DIN1",
      "type": "int"
    }
  }
}

If the sensor value falls within the range from 1 to 1, the value 1 is sent in the packet.

This mechanism is used to duplicate the sensor state in bit form.

For example, to send the door state through the inputs block.

Wialon Retranslator, Galileo and EGTS

Renaming fields

Example

{
  "tags_rewrite": {
    "temperature": "galileo_temp_0",
    "digital": "galileo_in_2"
  }
}

Lets you replace field names before sending.

For example:

  • temperature → galileo_temp_0

  • digital → galileo_in_2

Saving retransmission logs

Example

{
  "save_data_for_report": "1"
}

Enables saving of retransmission data for later report generation and diagnostics

Generating temperature data

Example

{
  "temperature_data_generator": {
    "DOS": "galileo_in_2",
    "closed_value": 0,
    "temperature_sensors": [
      "galileo_temp_0"
    ]
  }
}

This setting is used for special scenarios.

When the specified condition is met, the system can automatically generate temperature sensor values.

Parameters

  Parameter
  Description
  DOS
  Monitored sensor
  closed_value
  Value at which the condition is met
  temperature_sensors
  List of temperature sensors

This functionality is implemented for special integration scenarios and is used only when the receiving system requires it.

Raw data can come, for example, from a temperature, humidity, pressure or speed sensor, and others.

Raw points are data in their original form, without any changes or processing.

Each raw point usually comes with a timestamp, which lets you track and analyze how parameters change over time.

  • Direction - GPS compass heading relative to the object.

  • Satellites - number of satellites the object sees.

Security settings are located in the admin panel, in the settings section.

Two types of verification can be set up:

  • TOTP (via QR code)

  • Verification by e-mail.

TOTP authentication is a “time-based one-time password” and is a form of two-factor authentication.

It is a secure method in which, in addition to their standard password, the user enters a one-time password generated every 30 seconds by an authentication app on the user’s mobile device.

1. How to set up TOTP authentication:

Download an authentication app.

Install an app that generates one-time passwords, such as Google Authenticator or Authy, on your mobile device.

2. Scan the QR code.

Use the authentication app to scan the QR code provided by the service.

This links your account to the app and lets it generate unique codes.

3. Enter the code you received.

Enter the current code shown in the app into the confirmation field on the web site or in the application to complete the process.

  1. How to use TOTP authentication to log in.

- Enter your user name and password. Start by entering your credentials.

- Open the authentication app. On your mobile device, open the app you used to set up TOTP.

- Enter the one-time password. Look at the current one-time password in the app and enter it to complete the login process.

5. Benefits of using TOTP.

Security

Even if someone knows your password, they cannot access your account without the one-time password.

Convenience

The authentication app does not need an internet connection to generate the code.

Versatility

Many services support TOTP, so you can use a single app to access different accounts.

E-mail authentication

To authenticate by e-mail, you need to:

  • Set up SMTP in the partner settings.

  • Add the 2FA_EMAIL configuration.

After the settings are added to the partner configuration, a code entry window appears on the main login screen once you enter the login and password for the admin panel.

AI assistant

Chats are saved in the history — you can return to previous conversations to continue the discussion or view an answer again.

Additional login protection

kak-ustanovit-i-vojti-v-prilozhenie:
This article explains how to start using the PILOT mobile app. You will learn:

— how to install the app on your smartphone

— how a regular user logs in

— how an administrator logs in and works with user accounts

— how to log in to the app with two-factor authentication

— which login settings are available

Installing the app

To start using the mobile version of PILOT, install the app on your smartphone.

Method 1. Through the app store

1. Open the app store on your phone:

  • Google Play, if you have an Android phone

  • App Store, if you use an iPhone

    2. In the search bar, enter: ПИЛОТ

    3. Find the app with the brand icon and tap “Install”

Method 2. Via a direct link

You can go straight to the app store using a link from your smartphone:

Go to Google Play

Go to App Store

After following the link, install the PILOT app.

When installation is complete, the PILOT icon appears on your smartphone screen — tap it to open the app.

Logging in to the app

To log in to the app, make sure you have:

  • A smartphone with the PILOT mobile app installed

  • An internet connection

  • The login and password for your PILOT account

How to log in

1. Open the PILOT app

2. On the start screen, enter the login and password for your web account

3. Tap “Log in”

4. If you want your details to be saved so you don’t have to enter them every time, select the “Remember me” checkbox

5. Select the server to log in to

After a successful login, you will go to the app’s main screen with its sections.

Logging in as an administrator

Administrators can log in to the app with their own login and immediately see the profiles of all users under the contract. You can quickly switch between accounts, help colleagues and manage settings in the mobile app.

1. Enter the administrator login and password

2. Tap “Log in”

3. Select the server to log in to

4. The app shows a list of contracts assigned to the administrator

5. Tap the contract you need

6. Select a specific user within the contract and go to their user account

Logging in to the app with two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds extra protection to your PILOT account. To log in, you need not only a login and password but also a one-time code. Even if someone else learns your password, they cannot log in to the account without this code.

PILOT offers two ways to confirm a login:

  • Code from an authenticator app (TOTP) — the code is generated in a connected app, for example, Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator

  • Code by e-mail (Email 2FA) — the system sends a code to a verified e-mail address

Before logging in to the mobile app, you must enable the chosen 2FA method in the user profile in the PILOT web interface.

Both two-factor authentication methods can be enabled for an account at the same time. In this case, you must complete both verification steps in order when logging in: enter the code from the authenticator app, then the code received by e-mail.

Logging in with a code from an authenticator app (TOTP)

This verification method uses a six-digit code from the authenticator app.

To learn how to enable TOTP authentication in the web interface, read here.

To log in to the mobile app:

1. Open the PILOT app

2. Enter your login and password

3. Tap “Log in”

4. Open the authenticator app and find the code for your PILOT account

5. Enter the six-digit code on the login confirmation screen

6. Tap “Log in”

After the code is verified successfully, the app opens

The code is refreshed every 30 seconds. If the code has expired, wait for a new one to appear and enter it.

Logging in with a code by e-mail (Email 2FA)

With this method, after your login and password are checked, PILOT sends a one-time code to the e-mail address specified in the user profile.

To learn how to enable e-mail login confirmation in the web interface, read here.

To log in to the mobile app:

1. Open the PILOT app

2. Enter your login and password

3. Tap “Log in”

4. Check your e-mail and find the message with the code

5. Enter the code you received on the login confirmation screen

6. Tap “Log in”

After the code is verified successfully, the app opens.

If the message does not arrive, check your “Spam” and “Junk” folders and make sure the correct address is specified in your profile. Do not share the one-time code with other people.

Here you can:

Register using the

device QR code

This article explains how to work with the “Objects” section. You will learn:

— how to work with the object list

— how to get information about each object

— how to use the object menu

Object list

The “Objects” section shows the list of all monitoring objects. Here you can see the status of objects and the time of last communication.

To find the object you need, use the “Search” field and enter the object’s name or number.

Tap the button to configure how the object list is displayed. You can choose which objects to show, as well as how objects are grouped — for example, by groups, geofences or tags.

The object list shows a short summary for each object. From it you can tell where the object is, whether it is moving, and how much fuel and mileage it currently has.

For example, the summary shows:
  • Object name — for example, “VAZ 2106”
  • Date and time of the last message — when the device in the vehicle last sent data
  • Number of satellites — how reliably the location is determined
  • Current fuel volume in the tank — in liters (for example, 359.14 l.)
  • Total mileage — how far the vehicle has traveled in total (for example, 1,918,896.25 km)
  • Engine hours / working time — total engine running time (for example, 34526 h. 16 min.)
  • Address of the last point — country, region, locality and the exact address where the vehicle is now
  • Current speed — speed at the moment (for example, 74 km/h)
  • Time in the current state — how long the object has been moving or stationary (for example, “Upd: 00 sec” — just updated)

When you tap an object in the list, you go to the “Info” and “History” tabs with detailed information.

“Info” tab

The “Info” tab shows all the main information about the object:

  • Location on the map

  • Statistics: data for the selected day — time in motion, mileage, maximum and average speed, fuel consumption and average consumption per 100 km.

  • Sensors: current state of the sensors and the time of their last update.

  • Additional information: vehicle model, current status, time of last communication, speed and mileage.

The “Show on map” button opens a map with the object’s current location.

The “Get directions” block lets you build a route:

  • In PILOT — the route opens right in the app

  • On another map — an external map service opens

“History” tab

The “History” tab shows exactly how the object moved during the selected period.

The top of the screen shows a map with the object’s position and its track for the day.

Below the map is a short summary for the selected day: total mileage, maximum and average speed.

Just below is a date switcher — select the day you need, and the map, statistics and event list update for that date.

Next comes a detailed list of events for the selected day, in chronological order.

An event includes:

— start time

— event type (movement or parking)

— duration

— for movement events, the distance covered and the average or maximum speed

— the address where the movement started or ended, or the parking location

If you tap an event, the corresponding route appears on the map, and you can view it in the player.

Date filter

Select the dates you need to view the movement history for exactly that period.

Actions menu

Tap the three dots to open additional functions:

  • Current track — shows the object’s current location and its recent movement. The map shows where the vehicle is and the route it has taken

  • Show on map — return to displaying the object

  • Create link — get a token that lets a third party view the object on the map

  • Events — view notifications and events for the object: time, place, event type. With the settings you can select the objects for which events and notifications are shown, configure the types and specify the period — the dates and times for which you want to view the list of events that occurred.

If you tap a specific notification or event, it is shown on the map with a marker.

  • Video — go to the “Video” tab with image previews from connected cameras

  • Blocking — block or unblock the engine (commands are available when the “Engine blocking” module is connected)

  • Rename object — enter a new name and tap “Apply”

  • Points — view the object’s raw points

Object menu

Additional functions are available for each object. Tap the three dots next to the object to open the menu:

  • Information — go to the “Info” tab with the main information about the object

  • History — go to the “History” tab, which shows how the object moved during the selected period

  • Current track — shows the object’s current location and its recent movement. The map shows where the vehicle is and the route it has taken

  • Show on map — display the object on the map in real time

  • Follow — watch the object’s movement in real time. While following, the selected object is not merged with other objects into a cluster and stays visible on the map regardless of zoom level

  • Create link — get a token that lets a third party view the object on the map

  • Events — view events and notifications for the object: time, place, type

  • Rename object — enter a new name and tap “Apply”

  • Points — view the object’s raw points

Additional functions may appear in the menu depending on the modules connected to your account.

kak-prosmatrivat-uvedomleniya-i-sobytiya:
In the “Events” section, information is divided into two tabs:

  • “Notifications” — triggered rules that were set up in advance in the web interface. A notification is generated when the condition of a configured rule is met. For example, the system creates a “Speed control” notification if an object exceeded the specified speed and kept moving at that speed for longer than the set time.

  • “Events” — changes in the state of objects and sensors registered by the system, for example, ignition on, door opened, prolonged idling, sensor triggered.

How to view notifications

Open the “Events” section and go to the “Notifications” tab.

Notifications are grouped by date. Each card shows:

— the object the notification relates to

— the time it was triggered

— the notification name

— a description of what happened

For example, a “Speed control” notification may contain the set limit, the maximum recorded speed and the duration of the violation.

Tap a card to open the map and see the place where the notification was triggered.

If push notifications are allowed for the account, the app alerts you about new triggers on your mobile device.

How to configure the notification list

1. Go to the “Notifications” tab

2. Tap the settings icon in the upper right corner

3. In the “Objects” block, select groups or individual objects

4. In the “Notification types” field, select one or more configured notifications, or leave the “All types” option

5. Specify the start and end of the period

6. Tap “Apply”

The list will show only the notifications that match all the selected conditions.

To clear the conditions you set and return to the initial settings, tap “Clear”.

How to view events

Go to the “Events” tab. It shows the events that the system registered for objects and their hardware.

Each card shows:

— the object

— the event time

— the event type

— the description

For example, the list may show ignition on, idling, door opened or a service reminder.

Tap an event card to open the map and see the place where it was registered.

How to configure the event list

1. Go to the “Events” tab

2. Tap the settings icon

3. In the “Objects” block, select the objects to display events for

4. In the “Event types” field, select the categories you need, for example, “Route events”, “Agro”, “Battery” or “Complex events”. To avoid limiting the list by category, leave the “All types” option

5. Specify the start and end of the period

6. Tap “Apply”

To reset the selected conditions, tap “Clear”.

The set of available notification and event types depends on the account settings, connected modules and user rights.
menyu-i-nastrojki-polzovatelya:
The “Menu” section contains the user profile, financial information and the main settings of the mobile app. Here you can switch between profiles, check the account status, top up your balance, configure address display, app parameters and the interface theme.

In this article:

  • User profile — switching between saved profiles and logging out of the account

  • Finance — information about the organization’s account and balance top-up via Stripe

  • Address display — choosing the address components displayed in the app

  • Settings — language, object refresh, map parameters and layer visibility

  • Appearance — choosing the light, dark or system theme

The set of tabs depends on the connected modules and the user’s rights.

The menu may also include “Geofences”, “Drivers”, “Inspections”, “Analytics”, “AI support”, “Commands” and “Video”. Working with them is described in separate articles.

User profile

The “User profile” block shows your name or login.

If you want to switch to another account, tap your login — a list of profiles you have previously used in the app opens. If the “Remember” option was selected for these accounts, you can quickly switch to the profile you need without entering your details again.

If you want to log out of the current account, go to the “Profiles” tab, where you will find the logout button.

Finance

The “Finance” tab shows information about the organization’s account status:

  • Organization — name of the organization

  • Account number — identifier of the settlement account in the system

  • Deposit — amount of the deposit made

  • Balance — current account status

  • Available balance — amount available for use

  • SMS balance — number of available SMS messages

How to top up your balance via Stripe

Stripe is a payment service for secure payment by bank card and other available methods. If Stripe payment is enabled for your account, you can top up your balance in the mobile app:

1. Open the “Finance” tab

2. In the “Pay via Stripe” block, enter the amount

3. Tap “Pay”

4. On the Stripe page, select a payment method and confirm the payment

5. After the payment is processed successfully, return to the app and check your balance

Address display

On this tab, you can configure which parts of the address are displayed in the system, for example, in object cards, reports or history.

Go to the “Address display” tab and use the switches to select the address components you want to see. After configuring, tap the “Save” button at the bottom of the screen.

You can turn the following elements on or off:

  • House number

  • Street

  • City

  • Postal code

  • Region

  • Country

  • Suburb

  • Info

  • Geofences

  • Hide address if there is a geofence — if enabled, when an object is inside a geofence, the system shows only the geofence name instead of the full address

  • Reverse address order — when this option is enabled, the address is displayed in reverse order — from the country down to the house number.

Settings

On the “Settings” tab, you can configure how the app works and looks, including map and refresh parameters.

Main settings:

  • Language — select the app interface language

  • Object refresh period — set how often object location data is refreshed (for example, every 20 seconds)

  • High location accuracy — enable this option so the app uses more accurate location methods

  • Show the “Change scale” button — if you enable this option, a separate zoom button is displayed on the map.

  • Group objects on the map — enable this setting if you want objects located close to each other to be grouped into “clusters” for easier viewing

  • Show geofence names — when this function is enabled, geofence names are displayed on the map

Layer visibility:

  • KML layer visibility — turn on or off the KML/KMZ layers uploaded in the web version (for example, additional outlines, objects or boundaries) that are displayed on the map

  • Tile layer visibility — this switch turns additional map layers on or off

Account management:

At the bottom of the screen you will find the button for deleting your account. However, to delete the account completely, you need to contact technical support.

Appearance

In the “Appearance” section, you can choose how the app interface looks:

  • Light theme — the app is displayed in light tones

  • Dark theme — the app is displayed in dark tones. This theme is often used for working at night or in low light

The appearance follows the device theme if you select “Same as system”.
